(99cd-100ab) (The fifty Bhairavas are): AsitāSga (Black Body) (A) and SitāSga (White Body) (Ā), Kāpālin (Skull Bearer) (I), Bhrku˜in (Knitted Eyebrows) (Ī), Krta (Created) (U) along with Krodha (Anger) (Ū) and Unmatta (Madman) (¬), Karāla (Fierce) (­) (and the one the wise) know (as) BhīnaSa (Horrific) (ŀ), Maheśvara (Great Lord) (Ŀ), Mahākāya (Big Body) (E),91 A˜˜ahāsa (Loud Laugh) (Ai), and Tumburu (O), Mahākāya (Big Body) (Au) and Nrsiˆha (Man Lion) (¤), Vijaya (Victory) (Ö), and Paśupati (Lord of the Creatures) (Ka), Kha˜vāSgin (Staff -bearer) (Kha), Õāmara (Warlock) (Ga), µa‰ka (Axe) (Gha), CaSÆīśa (Lord of Wrath) (¥a), and PracaSÆavat (Wrathful) (Ca), MuSÆadhārin (Bearing a Severed Head) (Cha), Śiva (Ja), Śambhu (Jha), UÆÆāma (Beyond Control) (na), Õāmara (Warlock) (µa), Ardhanārin (Hermaphrodite) (µha), Vrddha (Aged) (Õa), Śukra (Sperm) (Õha), Kāla (Death) (¦a), CaSÆa (Wrath) (Ta), Kuleśvara (Lord of Kula) (Tha), Lambon˜ha (Long Lip) (Da), Gharghara (Jar) (Dha), Kāladaˆn˜ra (Death's Teeth) (Na), Ugrarūpin (Horrific Form) (Pa), Bhīmanāsa (Terrific Nose) (Pha), Vajrakāya (Lightning Body) (Ba), Kaulīśa (Lord of Kaula) (Bha), Go (Cow) (Ma), Vrna (Bull) (Ya), Dhvaja (Banner) (Ra), Raktāmbaradhara (Red Clothed) (La), Śūlin (Lancer) (Va), Vyagrogra (Agitated and Fierce) (Śa), Pi‰gala (Tawny) (±a), Bhrgu (Sa), Trailokya (Triple World) (Ha) and Bhāsura (Shining One) (K±a). Such are the fifty Bhairavas, mentioned in due order. (100cd-105) Recalled at all times (they are) the bestowers of accomplishment. (Their names) should be uttered with the (preceding honorific) ` śrī '92 and they should be worshipped with effort. They are all subject to (the goddess's) Command and worship the goddess's feet. One should know (these gods) of great fame to be the attendants in PūrSagiri. (106-107) The Three Goddesses, Maids and Attendents In the same way, O Śambhu, there are said to be three Kula goddesses (in PūrSagiri), namely, Kha˜˜ikī and the rest.93 These three are (together engaged) in service and they are called the triad (trikasaˆjñā).94 (108) Vijayā (Victory), Damanā (Control) and Mahimā (Glory), the third - these three are the three maids (cellakā)95 corresponding to (the three) beginning with Kha˜˜ikī. (109)

sanskrit: 124 ४०४ •४०५ कुमारिकाखण्डः •४०६ विक्रमं डोबिकं सद्य तेषां संज्ञात्रयं विदुः । ४०८ प्रतिचाराः स्मृता ह्येते परिकर्मे ँ उदाहृताः अन्येषां” प्रतिचारीणां देवगन्धर्वयोषिताम् । ४११ ४१२ ।। ११० ।। परिसंख्या न विद्यते मण्डलाग्रे वरानने ॥ १११ ॥ ।। ।। एवं देव्या:१३ स्वरूपेण पूर्णपीठमुदाहृतम् । पूर्णाव्वा प्रकटा ज्ञेया गुप्तपीठमतः शृणु ४१७ ४१६ ४१८ खेचरं नाम पीठं तु शवरीदेवतालयम् । ४१९ ।। ११२ ।। माता च”” मङ्गलाव्वा च षष्ठदेवः स्वयं प्रभुः ।। ११३ ॥ ४२१ पद्ममुद्रा पुनस्तत्र ध्यानपीठमुदाहृतम् ४२२ । एवं भैरवपीठं तु श्मशानं २३ कथयामि ते ।। ११४ ॥ नाम्ना उड्डामराख्यं तु सभयं योगिनिर्भयम् । समय४ संस्थितं तत्र २५ कौलभेदं तु भूतले ।। ११५ ।। •४२७ तेन कष्टतरं रौद्रं कालं तत्र व्यवस्थितम् । । सिद्धिभाजनवीराणां योगज्ञानप्रबोधकम् ।। ११६ ॥ योगिनां४२८ सिद्धिदातारं ४९ अन्येषां न कदाचन । ४३० श्मशानपालकस्तत्र नाम्ना च विकृताननः ।। ११७ ।। एवं चोत्तरपीठं तु दक्षसिंहासने स्थितम् । •४३२ दिव्यवर्षशतं सार्धं ४३१ स्थित्वा सा गगनं गता ।। ११८ ।। सिद्धनाथेनानुष्ठानं बहुकालं कृतं स्वयम् ।
english: CHAPTER SIX 125 The wise know the names of the three to be Vikrama (Valour), Õobika (Washerman) and Sadya. These three are said to be the (male) attendants (paricāra) said to be (engaged) in the service (of the goddess).96 O fair faced lady, the other attendants in front of the maSÆala, that is, gods, celestial musicians (gandharva) and women, are innumerable. (110-111) Thus, PūrSa(giri), the sacred seat of the goddess, has been described according to (its true) nature. One should know PūrSāvvā (Mother PūrSā) to be clearly visible (praka˜ā) (there). (112abc) Khecara - the Hidden Sacred Seat Listen then (to the teaching concerning) the hidden sacred seat (guptapī˜ha).97 (This) sacred seat, called Khecara (the Skyfarer), is the abode of the deity Śavarī. (112d-113ab) And the mother98 (here) is MaSgalāvvā (Auspicious Mother), while ±an˜hadeva99 is himself the lord. Again, the Gesture of the Lotus (padmamudrā) is there and it is called the sacred seat of meditation (dhyāna). (113cd-114ab) UÆÆāmara - the Cremation Ground In the same way, I will now tell you about the cremation ground that is Bhairava's sacred seat (bhairavapī˜ha).100 It is called UÆÆāmara. (Although) frightening (for common people), it frees yogis from fear (yoginirbhaya). (114cd-115ab) The Rule (samaya) is present there.101 It is the Kaula division (kaulabheda) (here) on the surface of the earth. Thus Death (kāla), who is extremely severe and fierce (raudra), resides there. (115cd-116ab) It awakens the heroes endowed with accomplishments (siddhi) to the knowledge of Yoga. It bestows accomplishment to yogis, never to anyone else. (116cd-117ab) The guardian of the cremation ground there is called Vikrtānana (Deformed Face). And so, the Northern Seat (uttarapī˜ha) is on the lion throne on the right (daknasiˆhāsana).102 (117cd-118ab) Having resided (there) for one hundred and fifty divine years103 (the goddess) went (up into) the sky (leaving) Siddhanātha (who) for a long time performed the rites himself (svayam). (118cd-119ab)

sanskrit: 126 कुमारिकाखण्डः दिव्यज्ञानप्रभावेण ४३४ तत्रैवान्तरधीयत ४३५ ।। ११९ ॥ द्विपञ्च४३६ ऋषयस्तेन शिष्यपुत्राः कृतान्वये । ४३७ । वरुणं४३८ च तथागस्ती वृद्ध शुक्रं जनार्दनम् ॥ १२० ॥ •४४० यमं च नारदं केतुं राहुश्चैव द्विपञ्चकम् ४२ । पूर्णपीठावतारं तु संजातं द्वापरे युगे ।। १२१ ॥ जालन्धराद् विनिष्क्रान्तं तृतीयं पीठनायकम् ४४५ चतुर्थं संप्रवक्ष्यामि अवतारं यथा भवेत् ।। १२२ ।। द्वीपान्ते दिव्यमस्तीति स्थानं सिद्धाश्रमं महत् । •४४७ क्वचिद् देश¨¨ महारम्यं दिव्यं चातिमनोरमम् ॥ १२३ ॥ सान्निध्यं भवते तत्र योगिनीनां गृहे गृहे । समयं सर्वभूतानां“ शास्त्रोऽयं श्रीकुजामतम् ।। १२४ ।। भगाख्या कामरूपेण तत्र कामेश्वरी स्थिता । रससिद्धास्तु५२ पञ्चाशत् कामेच्छाक्रीडनिर्भराः ५३ ।। १२५ ।। तेन सिद्धाश्रमं ५४ प्रोक्त५५ शवरी५६ दृढयौवना । ४५७ स्वयंभूजीयते भूमौ शून्यदेवकुलोत्तरे ।। १२६ ।। मातरीसप्तसहिता५९ अष्टमी तत्र देवता । ४६२ देवागारे ४६० भ्रमेन्नित्यं कदम्बाख्य ४६९ त्रिलोचन १२ ॥ १२७ ॥ •४६३ तेन वृक्षं‍ समाख्यातं कदम्ब४४ कामरूपके ।
english: CHAPTER SIX 127 The Ten Sages (He) became invisible there itself by the power of divine knowledge (i.e. the Command), and he made ten sages (his) disciples, that is, sons belonging to the lineage. (They were): VaruSa and Agastī, Vrddha (Aged), Śukra (Sperm), Janārdana (Castigator of the People), Yama, Nārada and Ketu with Rāhu, the tenth. (119cd-121ab) PūrSapī˜ha descended (into this world) in the Dvāpara Age. (This), the third leader of the sacred seats, emerged out of Jālandhara.104 (121cd-122ab) Kāmarūpa Kāmeśvarī, Her Attendents and the Kadamba Tree Now I will tell (you) about the fourth descent. There is a place on the Island (of the Moon) called `Divine'. It is the great hermitage of accomplished yogis (siddhāśrama).105 This place, which is somewhere (in the higher spheres of reality),106 is very comfortable, divine and extremely beautiful. There (yogis enjoy) the intimate presence (sānnidhya) of the Yoginīs in every house.107 (122cd-124ab) The Rule (samaya) of all living beings is this scripture, the venerable Kujāmata. Kāmeśvarī (the Mistress of Passion), called the `Yoni' (bhaga) resides there in the form of passion (kāma). (124cd-125ab) Fifty accomplished alchemists (rasasiddha) (reside there) full of desire to play love games. Thus it is said to be the hermitage of accomplished yogis (siddhāśrama) (where the goddess) Śavarī,108 in the full vigour of youth, (resides). (125cd-126ab) Self-generated (svayambhū) (she) arose in the world, in the Northern Kula of the Lord of the Void (Śūnyadeva). (She is) the deity there who, accompanied by the seven Mothers,109 is the eighth one. (126cd-127ab) O Three-eyed one, the (Point - bindu - otherwise) called Kadamba, should rotate constantly in (the centre of the triangle) the abode of the deity (devāgāra).110 Thus the tree in Kāmarūpaka is said to be the Kadamba.111 (127cd-128ab)

sanskrit: 128 कुमारिकाखण्डः कामरूपी च भगवान् श्वेतरूपधरो महान् ।। १२८ ॥ मित्रदेवः स्वयं सिद्धः शापानुग्रहकारकः । स्वामिभक्तिवशात् तत्र अवतारं करोति सः ।। १२९ ।। •४६८ ४७० पादुकाब्जं नमस्कृत्वा प्रविष्टो योगिनीगृहे । कलकलरव मुञ्चति‍ देव्याः ४७४ ।। मुञ्चति७२ देव्या: ४७३ पादाग्रस्मरणात् ॥ १३० ॥ मण्डलं स्थापयेद् दिव्यं निर्दिष्टं यत् कुलान्वये । ४७६ चिन्तामणिमहापुष्पैः सुरा कादम्बरी शुभा ॥ १३१ ॥ ४७७ शावरी पूजिता सिद्धैर्यया सृष्टं चराचरम् ४८० ४७८ दिव्योल्का ९ निर्गता वक्रा सिद्धनाथस्य पश्चिमे ।। १३२ ।। कुलज्ञानं तथा प्राणं सर्वस्वं च निवेदितम् । प्रदक्षिणशतं कृत्वा साष्टाङ्गं तु नमस्करेत् ।। १३३ ।। ४८५ प्रसन्ना शवरी३ तस्य आज्ञां ददति पुष्कलाम् । वदते ६ मित्रदेवेश उत्तिष्ठ जगतारक ४८७ ।। १३४ ।। विचरस्व“ यथाशक्त्या कामरूपें कलौ युगे । सृष्टिसंहारकतीर त्वमेकः कुलशासने ।। १३५ ॥ गुटिकासिद्धिस्ते दत्ता विचरस्व यथासुखम् । पूजयित्वा नमस्कृत्वा सर्वे तत्र समागताः ।। १३६ ॥ ततो हृष्टमना भूत्वा देवी वचनमब्रवीत् । ४९५ ४९६ युष्मदुपार्जितं किञ्चित् गुटिकादि महायशाः तत् सर्वं “ मत्प्रसादेन सफलं च भविष्यति । ४९७ ।। १३७ ।।
english: CHAPTER SIX 129 Bhairava receives the Alchemical Pill (There) the nature of the Blessed One (bhagavat) is Passion (kāmarūpin). He is great and his form is white.112 (He is) Mitradeva himself, the accomplished one (siddha) who (both) curses and bestows grace. (128cd-129ab) Swayed by (his) devotion to (his) lord (svāmin) (the goddess),113 he descended there (into the world) and having saluted the lotus of (the goddess's) sandals (pādukābja), he entered the House of the Yoginī.114 (129cd-130ab) By recollecting the fore part of the goddess's feet he let out a loud noise and generated a divine maSÆala in the manner taught in the (spiritual) family of the Kula (kulānvaya).115 (130cd-131ab) Śāvarī,116 the auspicious (goddess of) Kādambarī wine (surā)117 who has emitted the moving and immobile (universe) was worshipped by accomplished yogis with wish-granting gems (offered as) great flowers. (131cd-132ab) The (goddess) Vakrā, the divine fire falling from heaven (divyolkā),118 emerged to the west (paścima) of Siddhanātha119 (who) offered (her) the knowledge of Kula, (his) vital breath (prāSa) and all (he) possessed (sarvasva).120 (132cd-133ab) He circumambulated (her) a hundred times and then saluted, prostrating fully (before her). Pleased with him, Śavarī gave him (her) powerful Command. (133cd-134ab) She said: "Arise, O Mitradeva, saviour of the universe, move (freely) in Kāmarūpa during the Age of Strife according to (your) power. (134cd-135ab) According to Kula doctrine you are the sole creator and destroyer.121 The Accomplishment of the Pill (gu˜ikāsiddhi)122 has been given (to you). (Now) wander (freely) as you please". (135cd-136ab) Once they had worshipped and saluted (the goddess), they all came there. Then the goddess, delighted, said: "O greatly famed ones, whatever you have earnt (including the Accomplishment of) the Pill and the rest, will all be fruitful by my grace." (136cd-138ab)

sanskrit: 130 कुमारिकाखण्ड: •४९९ ५०० ५०१ एव लब्धवरा भूत्वा तत्रैवान्तरसंस्थिताः ।। १३८ ।। ५०२ प्रतिचाराः स्मृताः सर्वे पञ्चाशाज्ञाविधेयिका: ५०८ ५०९ ५०३ अकुल ४ विमलं योगी आनन्दं कमलेश्वरम् ॥ १३९ ॥ बहुल पुलिन भूतिर्मदनः कङ्कराट् ” शिशुः । कुमुदं चपलं श्यामं तमाल गदकोंकणम् ।। १४० ॥ कौलीशं कमलं कान्ति २ दमथ अटवीमुखम् । •५१० -५१४ •५१३ अमृतं कुम्भकेशश्च कालनाम तु घुघुरम् ।। १४१ ॥ अमोघं सुन्दर चैव संवर्तं प्रभुरव्ययम् । •५१६ ५१९ क्रोधीश नयनं कान्ति आकाशं परमं शशि : ।। १४२ ।। कौबेरं कुलवागीश कुबेरं विरजं विदुः । नित्यानन्दं तथा श्वेतं योगेश्वर ° गणेश्वरम् ॥ १४३ ॥ सोमेश्वर २२ कुलाधारं नक्त २३ धूर्जटि २४ संख्यया । एवं पञ्चाशत् सिद्धाश्च मातृकादेरनुक्रमात् ५ ।। १४४ ॥ ५२६ सिद्धा रसकृषा देव स्थिता आस्थानमण्डपे । ५२९ प्रतिचारी७ तथा सप्त तत्रैव १२८ च व्यवस्थिताः ।। १४५ ।। -५३२ त्रीणि बाह्ये समुद्दिष्टा: ३१ शिल्पिनी चक्रिणी द्वयम् । -५३३ ५३५ । मातङ्गिनी तृतीया च त्रयेते तृतीया च त्रयेते'४ प्रतिचारिकाः ।। १४६ ॥ गुप्तसंज्ञा भवेत् तेषां यथा शास्त्रे निगद्यते । ५३६ सुनन्दिनी च भद्रा च च्छिंच्छा देवी तृतीयका ।। १४७ ।। ५३९ •५४० •५४९ चेल्लका: ५३८ प्रतिचाराश्च' प्रतिचाराश्च ता तार४० वज्रधर कुलम् ।
english: CHAPTER SIX 131 The Fifty Rasasiddhas When they had received (their) boon in this way, they stood there within (the maSÆala of Kāmarūpa). Executors of the (goddess's) Command, all fifty are said to be (her) attendants. (138cd-139ab) (They are): Akula (A), Vimala (Pure) (Ā), Yogin (I), Ānanda (Bliss) (Ī), Kamaleśvara (Lord of the Lotus) (U), Bahula (Abundance) (Ū), Pulina (Sandy Shore) (¬), Bhūti (Wealth) (­), Madana (Inebriation) (ŀ), Ka‰karā˜ (Lord of the Herons) (Ŀ), Śiśu (Child) (E), Kumuda (Lotus) (Ai), Capala (Fickle) (O), Śyāma (Dark Blue) (Au), Tamāla (Palm Tree) (¤), Gada (Mace) (Ö), Ko‰kaSa (Ka), Kaulīśa (Kha), Kamala (Lotus) (Ga), Kānti (Beauty) (Gha),123 Damatha (Self- control) (¥a), A˜avī (Grove) (Ca), Mukha (Face) (Cha), Amrta (Nectar) (Ja) and Kumbhakeśa (Lord of the Jar) (Jha), the one called Kāla (Death) (na), Ghurghura (Worm) (µa),124 Amogha (Unfailing) (µha) and Sundara (Beautiful) (Õa), Saˆvarta (Doomsday Fire) (Õha), Prabhu (Lord) (¦a), Avyaya (Imperishable) (Ta), Krodhīśa (Lord of Wrath) (Tha), Nayana (Eye) (Da), Kānti (Beauty) (Dha), Ākāśa (Space) (Na), Parama (Supreme) (Pa), Śiśi (Moon) (Pha), Kaubera (Ba), Kulavāgīśa (Lord of the Speech of Kula) (Bha), (and the one the wise) know (as) Kubera (Ma), Viraja (Shining) (Ya), Nityānanda (Eternal Bliss) (Ra) and Śveta (White) (La), Yogeśvara (Lord of Yoga) (Va), GaSeśvara (Lord of Hosts) (Śa), Someśvara (Lord of the Moon) (±a), Kulādhāra (Foundation of Kula) (Sa), Nakta (Night) (Ha) and Dhūrja˜i (Dredlock) (K±a). Such, according to (their) number, are the fifty Siddhas, corresponding in due order to (the fifty) energies of the alphabet (mātrkā) and the rest. (139cd-144) O god, the accomplished Yoginī (siddhā), Rasakrnā (Thin with the Alchemical Potion) resides in the pavilion of the assembly and seven female attendants (praticārī)125 (also) reside there. (145) The Six Female Attendents and the Three Male Servants It is taught that three are on the outside, namely, the two, Śilpinī (the Sculpteress) and CakriSī (the Mover of the Wheel) along with MātaSginī (the Sweeper) as the third. These are the three female attendents. They have secret names, as taught in the scripture. (146-147ab) Sunandinī (Well Praised) and Bhadrā (Auspicious) with the goddess Cchiˆcchā126 (Tamarind) as the third, are the maids (cellakā). Again, the (male) servants are Tāra (Saviour), Vajradhara (Bearer of the Thunderbolt) and Kula.127 (147cd-148ab)

sanskrit: 132 कुमारिकाखण्डः त्रयेते४२ स्मृतास्तत्र‍ प्रतिचाराश्च भैरव ॥ १४८ ॥ ०५४४ एवं सिद्धाश्रमं ह्युग्रं देव्या आज्ञाप्रभावतः ५४६ । तेन पीठं समाख्यातं नाम्ना वै कामरूपकम् ।। १४९ ।। कामुकत्वे यदा देवो कामरूपं तदुच्यते । -५४७ श्वेतं ४८ वर्णं भवेत् तस्मिन् श्वेतरूपेण नायकी ॥ १५० ॥ उभयोर्योगभावेन बालिका पीठदेवता । भगाग्रे तु विजानीयात् पीठेद कामरूपकम् ॥ १५१ ॥ कामार्थाीय समायुक्तं गुप्तयुग्मं ब्रवीम्यहम् । -५५३ ५५४ उच्छुष्मपीठ वरारोह“ शावरस्य तु शावरी ।। १५२ ॥ नाम्ना सा कोङ्कणा देवी कोंकणात् देवी कोंकणात्““ तु विनिर्गता । ५५५ तथा च भवते सिद्ध: मित्रदेवेति नामतः ॥ १५३ ॥ ।। योनिमुद्रा विजानीयात् योन्यग्रे मातृमण्डले । ५६० तत्रैवान्तरमार्गस्थं श्मशानमटवीमुखम् ।। १५४ ॥ ५६१ नायकस्तत्र विख्यातः शङ्खपाल: कृतान्तवत् । ५६२ ५६३ राक्षसास्तस्य सेवन्ते तथा गगननायका: ।। १५५ ।। ५६५ रात्रौ प्रज्वलिते ६४ दीपे क्रीडते योगिनीगणम् । यमचक्रं स्थितं तत्र योगिनीवीरसंगमम् ५७० ।। १५६ ॥ रौद्रदिने सुऋक्षे च मेलाप भवते ततः ।
english: CHAPTER SIX 133 O Bhairava, these are the three servants who are said to be there. Thus, by the power of the goddess's Command, the Hermitage of Accomplished Yogis (siddhāśrama)128 is terrific (ugra). (148cd-149ab) Kāmarūpaka, Ucchunma, the secret seat, the secret couple, the Siddha and the Gesture Thus it is called a sacred seat, Kāmarūpaka by name. When the god is in a passionate state (kāmukatva), that is said to be Kāmarūpa. (149cd-150ab) Within it is the colour white and the mistress (nāyakī) whose form is white.129 Bālikā (the Girl) is the deity of the sacred seat by virtue of the state of union (yogabhāva) of both. Know that this sacred seat, Kāmarūpaka, is at the front of the Yoni (bhagāgra). (150cd-151) I will (now) explain the secret couple (guptayugma), united in order to (fulfil their) passion (kāma). O fair-hipped one, (this is) the sacred seat (called) Ucchunma.130 The Śāvarī of the Śāvara (here) is the goddess Ko‰kaSā by name who has come forth from Ko‰kaSa. (151cd-153ab) And in the same way, the accomplished yogi (who resides here) is called Mitradeva.131 Know that the Gesture of the Yoni (yonimudrā) is located at the front (agra) of the Yoni in the Circle of the Mothers (mātrmaSÆala).132 (153cd-154ab) A˜avīmukha - the Cremation Ground, the Field and the Seat There, located on the inner (antara) path, is the cremation ground (called) A˜avīmukha. The leader there, (as formidable) as (the Lord of) Death (krtānta), is called Śa‰khapāla (Protector of the Conch). (154cd-155ab) Demons (rāknas) and the Leaders (of the deities and Siddhas) in the Sky (gagananāyaka) serve him and at night a troupe of Yoginīs plays (there) (in the light of a) lighted lamp. (155cd-156ab) The congregation (cakra) of Yama (the lord of the dead) is present there (where) Yoginīs and heroes meet. Then union (melāpa) takes place (between them) on Rudra's day at an auspicious time (surkne). (156cd-157ab)

sanskrit: 134 कुमारिकाखण्डः विषय कुलकौलं तु योगिनीवीरमेलकम् ॥ १५७ ।। सिद्धनाथः৺२ स्थितस्तत्र अन्तर्धीने ५७३ स्थितस्तत्र अन्तर्धीने महाप्रभुः । ५७४ एवं तदग्रपीठं तु पीठदेव्या समन्वितम् ॥ १५८ ॥ संस्थिता दिव्यरूपेण “ कामभोगसुखे रता । ५७५ •५७७ ५७६ दत्वा सिद्धस्य पीठं त गता सा खेचरीक्रमे ॥ १५९ ॥ ।। ।। ततः सिद्धान्वय ँ“ जातं अनेकास्तत्र दीक्षिताः । ५७९ चित्रसेनो नासिकस्तु शुकस्त्रैलोक्यपालकः ।। १६० ।। कपाली डामरश्चैव विघ्नेशं कालपाशकम् । ५८२ ऋषयोऽष्टौ स्मृता ह्येते दीक्षिता: सिद्धनायकाः ।। १६१ ।। कामरूपावतारोऽय^३ संजात ४ च कलौ युगे । -५८५ पूर्णपीठाद् विनिष्क्रान्तं भुक्तिमुक्तिफलप्रदम् ।। १६२ ।। एवं कृतयुगारभ्य पीठाम्नायं चतुष्टयम् । यो वेत्ति स किलाम्नाये अन्यथा नामधारकः ।। १६३ ।। तस्मिन् कलियुगस्यान्ते श्रीमत्कामाख्यमण्डले -५९० ५९२ । तस्मिन् सिद्धाश्रमे पूर्वे अटव्यां” तिस्रसंज्ञकम् ॥ १६४ ॥ नदीस्रोतत्रये ९३ मध्ये विघ्नेशं क्षेत्रपालकम् । देवताश्रम” तत् स्थानं तिस्रपीठेति सूचितम् ।। १६५ ।। भक्तिहीने शठे लोके मन्दाज्ञा संप्रवर्तते ।
english: CHAPTER SIX 135 The field (vinaya) is Kulakaula that engenders the union of heroes and Yoginīs. Concealed, the great lord Siddhanātha resides there. (157cd-158ab) In this way, that sacred seat which is situated in the front (i.e. the lower corner of the triangle) (agrapī˜ha) has a goddess of the seat (pī˜hadevī). She resides (there) in a divine form, devoted to the bliss of the enjoyment of passion (kāmabhoga). (158cd-159ab) Once bestowed that sacred seat on the accomplished one, she entered the Transmission of the Skyfaring (Goddesses) (khecarīkrama).133 Thus a lineage of Siddhas (siddhānvaya) came into being and many were initiated there. (159cd-160ab) The Eight ¬nis Citrasena (Whose Army is Diverse), Nāsika (Nose), Śuka (Parrot), Trailokyapālaka (Guardian of the Triple World), Kāpalin (Skull Bearer), Õāmara (Warlock), Vighneśa (Lord of Obstacles) and Kālapāśaka (Bond of Death). These are said to be the eight sages (rni) (of this seat, all of whom) are initiates and leaders of accomplished yogis. (160cd-161) This is Kāmarūpa's descent (into this world) that has taken place during the Age of Strife. It has emerged from PūrSapī˜ha134 and bestows the fruit of (both) worldly benefits and liberation. (162) Thus, starting from the Krta Age, this is the four-fold tradition of the sacred seats. He who knows (this) is indeed in the tradition (āmnāya) otherwise (he is so only) by name. (163) Tisra - The Sacred Seat of the Future At the end of that Age of Strife,135 (the sacred seat) called `Tisra' will136 be (located) in the region (maSÆala) of the venerable Kāmākhya, in that Hermitage of Accomplished Yogis (siddhāśrama)137 in the eastern grove. (Situated) in the midst of the current of three rivers, the guardian of the field (there) is Vighneśa (the Lord of Obstacles). (164-165ab) That place is the hermitage of the deity. It is called Tisrapī˜ha. The Command that operates in (this) deceitful world devoid of devotion is weak.138 (165cd-166ab)

sanskrit: 136 कुमारिकाखण्डः द्वीपान्ते चोत्तरे भागे त्रिकूटभुवनेषु च ।। १६६ ॥ ५९७ ५९८ माया मातङ्गिरूपेण त्रिषु स्रोतसु मध्यतः । तिस्रनद्यां गतं स्थानं यक्षकन्दरमागतम् ॥ १६७ ॥ ६०२ कृतं तत्रावतारं तु पीठ तिस्राख्यसंभवम् पीठî॰३ ६०४a । ६०४b कृत: पूर्वतनुर्देव ६०६ गोपितो ६०५b मत्यलोकतः ।। १६८ ॥ ६०८ कलावर्धे ततो देव प्रकटं पञ्चमं भवेत् । ६०९ तत्रारभ्य क्रमायातं ततः संवर्तकं भवेत् ।। १६९ ॥ आज्ञायास्तमन”° भूयः वर्तते मत्यलोकत: ११ । त्वया सार्धमनुष्ठानं १२ मया १३ पूर्व४ कृतं ततः ।। १७० ।। त्वं च तत्र मतङ्गीश संजात चान्तिमे युगे । अन्त्यजाज्ञाप्रसूतिस्तु पुनः सन्तानमर्हति ।। १७१ ।। पुनः स्थितिक्रमादाय तिस्रपीठाद् विनिर्गतम्¨¨ । उघं गुरुगृह१९ देव१२° तैलिकाक्रममण्डलम् ॥। १७२ ।। प्रकटं तद् भविष्येत सद्योज्ञानं २२ प्रवर्तते । महासान्निध्यमतुल१२३ एव २४ पीठान्वयं २५ भवेत् ॥। १७३ ।। तस्मिन् युगे१२६ ह्यह९२७ वृक्षं त्वया ह्यकुलकन्दरे । ६२८ एतद् युगान्तिमं पीठं पञ्चमं •६२९ पीठनायकम् ।। १७४ ॥ चतुर्थे कलियुगे प्राप्ते म्लेच्छराज्ये तु उत्तरे । ६३० ३१ इतरे गुरुशिष्ये तु लोभमोहवशं गते ।। १७५ ।। आज्ञावेशे २ गते १३ क्षीणे अधिकारे क्षयं गते । ६३४ समयभङ्गसंप्राप्ते गुरोराज्ञा च लङ्घने ।। १७६ ।। पुनः सृष्टि करिष्यामि अवतारं तु पञ्चमम् ।
english: CHAPTER SIX 137 (The goddess) Māyā, in the form of MātaSgī (the Sweeper Woman), (resides) on the Island (of the Moon)139 in the northern part amidst the worlds of the Triple Peak (trikū˜a)140 in the middle of the three currents. (166cd-167ab) 'The Descent of the Lord and the Goddess into the Sacred Seat and the Establishment of a New Transmission' (The Lord) reached the Ravine of the Tree Spirits (yaknakandara), which is a place on the river Tisra and having descended there (into the world) the sacred seat called `Tisra' came into being. 141 (167cd-168ab) O god, having fashioned a body (like the) previous one (he lay) hidden in the world of mortals. Then, at the end of the Age of Strife, the fifth god should become manifest. (168cd-169ab) Then, beginning from there, is the Doomsday Fire (saˆvartaka)142 that has come in due order. Once again, the (divine) Command disappears in the world of mortals. (169cd-170ab) Formerly, I worshipped along with you and then you became Mata‰gīśa there in the last (of the four) ages. (170cd-171ab) The last born progeny (prasūti)143 of the Command should have a lineage (santāna) again. (So), taking up again the sequence of emanation,144 it has emerged from the seat (called) Tisra. (171cd-172ab) O god, the current (of the lineage) (ugha) is the Teacher's House, that is, the KramamaSÆala of the Oilpresser Girl (tailikā).145 That will become manifest and the instantaneous knowledge (sadyojñāna)146 (of ultimate reality) will operate (in the world). (172cd-173ab) In this way the tradition (anvaya) of the sacred seat will be one of great proximity (to the deity) (mahāsānnidhya) and it will have no equals. In that age I am the Tree along with you in the Ravine of Akula.147 That is the sacred seat of the end of the age148 and the fifth leader of the seats. (173cd-174) When the fourth age, that of strife, comes and there will be a barbarian kingdom (mleccharājya) in the north (of India).149 When the teacher and disciple of (every) other (tradition) come under the sway of greed and delusion; when the penetration of (the divine) Command has waned and authority is no more; when the Rule (samaya) has been broken and the Command of the teacher is disregarded, I will again bring about (a new) emanation, namely, the fifth incarnation (avatāra). (175-177ab)

sanskrit: 138 कुमारिकाखण्डः ६३७ ६३८ तिस्राख्ये तु महापीठे सर्वपीठपरीवृते ।। १७७ ।। ६३९ सर्वेषामुत्तरे ९ घोरे सद्योनिग्रहकारके ६४० । पुनः स्थितिं क्रमौघस्य तस्माद् वै४२ पीठपञ्चमात् ।। १७८ ।। तत् चाष्टाविंशमं भेद पूज्यमानं भविष्यति । ६४६ कुब्जिका अधिकारिणी तथा सिद्धो मतङ्गकः ।। १७९ ॥ द्वावेतौ सृष्टिकर्तारौ कलिस्यान्ते ४९ न संशयः । ६४८ एवं पीठं भवेत् तिस्रं गुप्तं वै पीठनायकम् ॥ १८० ॥ तिस्रपीठे तु तिस्राव्वा त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुता । ६५० ६५२ गुप्तसंज्ञा भवेत् तत्र बिन्दुतत्त्वे व्यवस्थितम् ।। १८१ ॥ ६५३ ·६५४ ६५५ ६५६ कुचन्द्र पीठसिद्ध च अव्वा सा वक्रिका स्वयम् । क्रमसंज्ञा तथा मुद्रा भवते तु कदम्बिनी ।। १८२ ॥ ६५७ ताडनात् ताडिवृक्षं तु दह्यमानं भवेत् ततः । ६५८ दिव्यज्ञानप्रभावेण ८ सिद्धनाथे प्रकाशितम् ६६१ पञ्चमं चोत्तमं पीठं कलिस्यान्ते न संशयः । ।। ॥ १८३ ॥ तिस्रपीठात् समारभ्य पूजाक्रिया प्रवर्तते ॥ १८४ ॥ ॐकारादितः‍ पीठाना उक्ता ये प्रतिचारकाः । ६६७ ६६५ प्रतिचार्यश्च६६ ताः सर्वाः भविष्यन्ति च पञ्चमे ।। १८५ ।। भविष्यन्ति न संदेहो तिस्राख्ये पीठनायके । श्मशानानामघोर ६८ तु सुरसिद्धनमस्कृतम् सुरसिद्धनमस्कृतम्” ।। १८६ ।। •६७० नायक घोरनामानां ससिद्धामरवन्दितम् । ६७३ अर्धचन्द्रोत्तरे पीठं भगमूर्ध्नि विनिर्गतम् ।। १८७ ।। तत्रस्था परमा काली दिव्यज्ञानप्रकाशक । ६७४
english: CHAPTER SIX 139 (This will occur) in the great sacred seat called `Tisra'. Surrounded by all the sacred seats, it is the highest of all (uttara) and, horrific (ghora), immediately chastises (nigraha) (the wicked).150 (177cd-178ab) By virtue of that, the fifth sacred seat, the current of the Transmission (kramaugha) will again be stable and that, the twenty-eighth division,151 will be worshipped. (178cd-179ab) Kubjikā (will have) authority (here) and the accomplished yogi (will be) Mata‰gaka (the Sweeper). At the end of the Age of Strife these two are certainly the creators (srn˜ikartr). (179cd-180ab) Such is the sacred seat Tisra, the hidden leader of the seats. Tisrāvvā,152 famous in the three worlds, resides in Tisrapī˜ha. (180cd-181ab) There, her name is secret and she is established in the Principle of the Point (bindutattva).153 The accomplished yogi of the seat is Kucandra154 while the mother (avvā) is Vakrikā herself. (181cd-182ab) The name of the transmission (krama) and the gesture is Kadambinī. The tree is the TāÆī155 (so called) because it `beats' (tāÆanāt) and so should be burnt. (182cd-183ab) Without a doubt, this, the fifth and best seat, (will be) revealed to Siddhanātha by the power of divine knowledge at the end of the Age of Strife. (183cd-184ab) Ritual action (pūjākriyā) starts from Tisrapī˜ha. The attendants, male and female, said be those of the sacred seats from O¤ onwards, will all be in (this), the fifth one.156 They will certainly be (there), in the leader of the seats called `Tisra'. (184cd-186ab) Saluted and praised by the gods and accomplished yogis, (this sacred seat is) the leader, (in itself) not terrible (aghora), of those (beings) called `terrible' (ghora) and of the cremation grounds. (186cd-187ab ) (This is the) sacred seat above the Half Moon that has emerged on top of the Yoni (bhagamūrdhni). The supreme Kālī, who illumines divine knowledge, resides there.157 (187cd-188ab)

sanskrit: 140 कुमारिकाखण्डः •६७६ पारम्पर्ये ७५ क्रमं ज्ञानं शास्त्रोऽयं विमलं मतम् ।। १८८ ।। ६७७ • ६७८ भविष्ये प्रकट नाथ कलिस्यार्थे न संशयः । इदं पीठावतारोऽयं कथितं तव सुन्दर ।। १८९ ॥ भविष्यं च विभाव्यते पञ्चमं तिस्रपीठकम् । ६८० बालक्रमं च कामाख्ये खेचरं जालपीठके ॥ १९० ॥ कौमारं पूर्णपीठे तु ओडियाणे २ तु वृद्धकम् । । एवं पीठक्रमं ज्ञात्वा पारम्पर्यक्रमागतम् ८३ ।। १९१ ॥ यस्तु संपूजयेन्नित्यं स साक्षाद् भैरवः स्वयम् । ६८६ ६८७ पीठान् ८५ पर्यटते यो वै आचार्यः साधकोऽपि वा ।। १९२ ।। ६८८ स मुक्त: स शिवः साक्षात् साम्नायी देशिकोत्तमः । ६९० ब्रह्महत्यासहस्रैक गोहत्यामयुतं तथा ।। १९३ ॥ सर्वपापा९२ विनश्यन्ति असंख्या:३ पीठसेवनात् । पूजयेन्नित्यमेव हि सदा पीठचतुष्टयम् ।। १९४ ॥ तस्येच्छा भवते सिद्धिर्योगिनीनां प्रियो भवेत् । श्रीपूर्वान् भाषयेत् सर्वान् पीठान्ते यान् ” व्यवस्थितान् M तेभ्यो” लब्धवरो भूत्वा रुद्रलोके महीयते । ६९९ ७०० ॥ १९५ ॥ उडियाणे ०३ प्रविष्टो यो वीरो दर्प करिष्यति ।। १९६ ॥ दारिद्र्य॰॰६ मरणं तस्य मासमेकं स जीवति । ७०७
english: CHAPTER SIX 141 This scripture (śāstra) is the pure doctrine (mata), which is the knowledge and the Transmission (krama) (handed down) through the series (of teachers pāramparya). O lord, it will certainly become manifest in the future at the end of the Age of Strife. (188cd-189ab) O handsome one, I have told you this, the descent (into the world) of the (four) sacred seats and the sacred seat Tisra that is considered to be the fifth, future one. (189cd-190ab) Conclusion: in praise of the four sacred seats and admonitions The Transmission of the Child is in Kāmākhya, (that of) the Skyfarer (khecara) in the sacred seat of Jāla, that of the Youth in the seat of PūrSa (and that of) the Aged in OÆiyāSa.158 (190cd-191ab) He who constantly worships the transmission (krama) of the sacred seats that has come down through the sequence of the series (of teachers) (pāramparyakrama), having known it thus, is himself Bhairava directly apparent. (191cd-192ab) He who does the round of the sacred seats, whether he be a teacher (ācārya) or an adept (sādhaka), is liberated. He is Śiva directly apparent (sāknāt), he is (a true) member of the tradition and the best of teachers. (192cd-193ab) By resorting (sevana) to the sacred seats, all (one's) countless sins are destroyed, whether one has committed brahminicide a thousand times (or even if) one has killed a myriad cows. (193cd-194ab) (Thus) one should always and constantly worship the four seats in this way. The desire of one (who does) so becomes an accomplishment (siddhi) and he is dear to the Yoginīs. (194cd-195ab) (The names) of all those who reside in a sacred seat should be uttered with a preceding (honorific) `śrī'.159 Once obtained a boon from them, he waxes mighty in Rudra's world.160 (195cd-196ab) The Kaula adept (vīra) who has entered UÆiyāSa and cultivates pride (there) becomes poor and dies; (indeed) he lives (barely) for a month. (196cd-197ab)

sanskrit: 142 कुमारिकाखण्डः ७१ ० जालन्धरे तु यो दर्पं” मूढात्मा च करिष्यति ।। १९७ ।। तस्करो हनते ? तस्य३ नदी वा व्याधिदारुणा ७१२ । षण्मासं जीवितं तस्य म्रियते बान्धवैः सह ॥ १९८ ॥ अथवा पूर्णपीठे” तु द्वेष संचरते तु यः ७१९ ७१८ । अहंकारं च कुरुते अग्निदाहाद् विनश्यति ।। १९९ ।। अथवा विषसंग्रामे৺२१ म्रियते मासपञ्चमें ७२३ ७२२ । कामरूपे सुखासीनः कश्चिद् दर्पं करिष्यति ।। २०० ।। अदृष्टमुद्गराघातः पतते तस्य मूर्धनि । । शुष्यते स्वशरीरेण म्रियते पक्षमध्यतः ।। २०१ ।। दर्प” कृत्वा तु सुभग स गुरुर्नरकं व्रजेत् । ७३० ७३३ ७११ तस्मात् तस्य न भुक्तिः स्यात् परत्र च न विद्यते ।। २०२ ।। ७३४ ७३६ तस्माद् दर्पं न कर्तव्यं विद्वेष३५ न समाचरेत् M १७३७ । विनयाद् भवते भुक्तिर्मुक्ति विनयाद् भवेत् ।। २०३ ।। तस्माद् विनयकौलोऽयं विनयं तु समाचरेत् । ७३८ ७३९ वीरभोज्यं प्रकर्तव्यं ओजापूकाचतुष्टये ।। २०४ ।। कृत्वा पूजा यथाशक्त्या पीठजान् ? पूजयेत् तदा । साधकः सिद्धिमाप्नोति इहलोके परत्र च ॥ २०५ ।। रुद्राश्च भैरवा॰४३ वीरा:॰॰॰ सिद्धा:४५ पूज्याश्चतुष्टये । चतुष्पीठावतारोऽय निर्णीतं तु चतुर्युगे ।। २०६ ।। अटते॰४७ यो हि सत्येन आचार्यः स कुले भवेत् । ७४८ त्रिमात्रं ज्योतिसंकाश वह्निमण्डलमध्यतः श्री — उद्यानमह ५२ वन्दे कौलिकाज्ञाप्रवर्तकम् ७५१ ।। २०७ ।। ।
english: CHAPTER SIX 143 A thief, river or terrible disease kills the deluded soul who is given to pride in Jālandhara. He lives for (only) six months and dies along with his relatives. (197cd-198) Or again, he who despises (others) in the sacred seat (called) PūrSa and is proud dies by fire or else dies in the fifth month in a fierce battle. (199-200ab) A blow by an invisible hammer falls on the head of whoever, seated comfortably in Kāmarūpa, acts proudly. (200cd-201ab) He dries up along with his body and dies in the middle of the lunar fortnight. O handsome one, the teacher who has been proud goes to hell. (201cd-202ab) Thus, he neither has (any) worldly benefit (bhukti) (in this world nor) is it found in the other (paratra). Therefore one should not be proud or hate (others). (202cd-203ab) By right conduct (vinaya) (one attains worldly) benefits (bhukti), by right conduct (one attains) liberation. Thus, this is the Kaula (tradition) of right conduct (vinayakaula) and one should practice right conduct. (203cd-204ab) One should eat heroes' food (vīrabhojya)161 in the four sacred seats, OÆiyāSa, Jālandhara, PūrSagiri and Kāmarūpa (ojāpūkācatun˜aya). Once one has worshipped (the seats) to the best of one's ability, one should then worship those born of them. (204cd-205ab) The adept (sādhaka) attains accomplishment in this world and the next. The Rudras, Bhairavas, heroes and accomplished yogis should be worshipped in the four (sacred seats).162 (205cd-206ab) This has been explained namely, the descent (into the world) of the four seats in the four Ages. He who wanders (from one to the other) in accord with truth (satyena) is a teacher in the Kula.163 (206cd-207ab) In Praise of the Sacred Seats I praise the venerable Udyāna, the propagator of the Kaula Command which, in the centre of the Circle of Fire, is of three measures (trimātra) and is (as brilliant) as light. (207cd-208ab)

Divine, it is located in the fore- part of that (Triangle). Extremely subtle and half a measure, its nature is supreme bliss.165 (210cd-211ab) I salute the propagator of the Kaulika Command located at the End of the Twelve (finger space). sanskrit: 146 -८१० कुमारिकाखण्डः ८१२ कृत्वा च भारते वर्षे आत्मकीर्ति कुलाम्बिके ।। २२० ।। तेन कौमारिकाखण्डं संजातं पुण्यपावनम् । पूर्वसन्तानदेवेन यदुक्तं भारतं व्रज ।। २२१ ।। ततः प्रभृतिर्देवेश”” उभाभ्यां मेलक त्विह । तत्” कृत”“ सकलं देव्या आज्ञानन्दावबोधनम् ।। २२२ ।। आगता तु पुनस्तत्र पूर्वरूपानुयायिनी ” । ८२० ८२३ ८२४ देवोऽपि पूर्वसन्ताने” शिष्यः सुरवरार्चितः ।। २२३ ।। श्रीमदोड्डुमहेशान५ कृत्वा चाज्ञां ददेत्२६ तु सा—७ । ८३१ इत:“” ८२७ ८३२ तदा च२८ भारते २९ वर्षे इतः प्रभृत्यनुग्रहम् उडुपीठपुरारभ्य कुरु सृष्टिमनेकधा । .८३६ । ।। २२४ ।। इत्याद्यावतारे' महामन्थानभैरवयज्ञे अन्वये सप्तकोटिप्रमाणे मेरुमार्गविनिर्गते लक्षपादाधिके विद्यापीठमार्गे विमलषट्कनिर्णये कादिभेदे आज्ञापारमेश्वरे स्वमिनीमते श्रीचतुर्विंशत्सहस्रसंहितायां ” अव्वाक्रमभाषिते ८४० श्रीनाथाज्ञापीठव्याप्तिनामानन्दः ॥ ६ ॥
english: CHAPTER SIX 147 O mother of Kula, (the goddess thus) established her fame in the land of Bhārata and so the meritorious and holy Region of the Virgin (goddess kaumārikākhaSÆa)174 came into being. (220cd-221ab) O lord of the gods, the union with (us)175 both is taking place here (in this world) from when176 the god of the previous lineage (santāna) said (to me): "Go to (the land of) Bhārata".177 (221cd-222ab) Once the goddess had done all that namely, brought about the awakening of the bliss of the Command, she returned there in accord with her previous form. (222cd-223ab) The god also in the previous lineage (pūrvasantāna) (was her) disciple, worshipped by the best of the gods. And having made (him) the venerable and great lord (maheśāna) OÆÆu, she gave (him) the Command (again).178 (223cd-224ab) Then from that time onwards (there will be) grace in the land of Bharata. In order to reside again in the seat of UÆu179 bring about the emanation (of the universe) countless times (anekadhā).180 (224cd-225ab) This is the (sixth) chapter called the Pervasion of Śrīnātha's Sacred Seat of the Command (ājñāpī˜ha). It belongs to the primordial descent into the great sacrifice of the Churning Bhairava in the tradition (anvaya) that consists of seventy million (verses) that has emerged on the Path of Meru and (extends) for a hundred and twenty-five thousand (verses). It is on the path of the Seat of Knowledge (vidyāpī˜ha) and is the ultimate purport of the Pure Six (Thousand Verses vimalana˜ka) in the division beginning with `Kā' in the venerable scripture of twenty-four thousand (verses) (known as) the Svāminīmata of the Supreme Lord's command as uttered within the Tradition of the Mother (avvākrama).

sanskrit: सप्तमानन्दः श्रीनाथ उवाच किमेतत्' पश्चिमं वेश्म अधिकारं तु तस्य किम् । कथं दिव्यतनुर्मुद्रा' तथा चैव कुलक्रमम् ॥ १ ॥ संकेत मूलभाषा च तथा चैव कुलागमम् । उपदेश न मे ज्ञातं सर्वं कथय क्रिके ॥ २ ॥ श्रीवक्रा उवाच ७ मन्थानस्य तु भेदस्य भैरवस्य तु संग्रहम् । कादिभेदं' प्रवक्ष्यामि सहस्रज्येष्ठकौलिकम् ।। ३ ॥ वक्रिकाक्रमसिद्धस्य आज्ञाशास्त्रं क्रमोदयम् । श्रीनाथ ते प्रवक्ष्यामि मेरुमार्गविनिर्गतम् ॥ ४ ॥ चतुर्थे तु युगे प्राप्ते आद्यपीठावतारितम् । पश्चिमस्य गृहस्यैव अवतार कलौ युगे ॥ ५ ॥ तस्योद्धारोपदेश” तु संप्रदाय तु कौलिकम् । आदिकादिसमायुक्तं सर्वसंहारमन्त्रितम् ।। ६ ।। भैरवं भैरवीसार्ध तस्योध्वे तु कुलक्रमम् । सप्ताविंशतिभिर्भेदैः” संस्थितं तु विभेदतः ॥ ७ ॥ १६ गृहमित्यवतारोऽयं° पश्चिमामुखमुत्तमम्” । -२३ तस्योपदेशमपरं” अवतार च सिंहकम् ॥ ८ ॥ षोडशैः २४ षोडशैश्चैव अपरे चैव षोडश ।
english: CHAPTER SEVEN The Authority of the Goddess in the Venerable City of the Moon Śrīnātha said: What is that Western House (veśman)? What is its authority? How is the Gesture (mudrā) (endowed) with a divine body and similarly, what is the Kula tradition (kulakrama)? (1) (What) is the teaching (saˆketa)? (What) is the Root Language (mūlabhānā) and the Kula scripture (kulāgama)? O Vakrikā, I have not known the teaching (concerning these matters) tell me everything. (2) The Descent of the Scripture The venerable (goddess) Vakrā said: 1I will expound the collection (saˆgraha) (of teachings) of the division of the Churning (manthāna) Bhairava, the Kaulika (scripture) of the Thousand Elders (sahasrajyen˜ha) which is the division beginning with KĀ (kādibheda).2 (3) I will expound for you, O Śrīnātha, the scripture of the Command (ājñāśāstra). It is the dawning of the transmission (kramodaya) that has emerged from Meru. (It belongs to) the one who is accomplished in Vakrikā's transmission (krama) and was brought down (to earth) in the first seat (ādyapī˜ha)3 during the fourth Age.4 (4-5ab) It is the descent (into this world) of the Western House that has taken place during the Age of Strife. The teaching concerning the formation of its mantras (uddhāra) is a Kaulika tradition (saˆpradāya). Endowed with (all the letters in the series) beginning with `A' (i.e., the vowels) and (those) beginning with `Ka' (i.e., the consonants), it is consecrated (mantrita) with universal destruction.5 Following after (tasyordhve) is the Kula Transmission divided into twenty-seven divisions6 that belongs to Bhairava accompanied by Bhairavī. (5cd-7) The Western House The House is this descent (of the teaching into the world).7 It is the Western Face,8 the best (of all). Its teaching is the other (apara) descent (into the world), namely, that of the Lion (siˆhaka). (It takes place) along with sixteen (Siddhas) and with sixteen (more) and in the other (group there are) sixteen.9

sanskrit: 150 कुमारिकाखण्डः एवं त्रितयसंयोगात् श्लोकानि द्वादशानि वै ।। ९ ॥ गजेन्द्रं प्रथमं नाम विद्याकूटं च षड्विधम् । तद् २७ वर्णं” तच्छिवाकाशं तल्लिङ्ग” तच्छिवेति च ॥ १० ॥ तदासौ आपबीज” तु देव्यात्मान ं तथैव च । । पदैकमष्टधा प्रोक्तं अंशश्लोकानि ” द्वादश ॥ ११ ॥ चन्द्रसूर्यशिवेच्छया” कृत्वा” वर्णगमागमम् । परस्परसमायोगादेतत्” क्षेत्रपरिग्रहम् ॥ १२ ॥ अमृतादिविसर्गीन्ताः कलाषोडशरश्मयः” । तिर्यगा सा स्मृता रेखा कतान्ता ” वामदेवता ।। १३ ॥ उन्नता दक्षिणे रौद्री थसान्तामित्यनुक्रमात्” । ज्येष्ठा वामा च रौद्री च ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेश्वराः ॥ १४ ॥ एकीभावं त्रिभिर्यस्मात् तदासौ“ योगिनीगृहम्” । ४९ ५० अमृताद्यश्च जीवन्ति” ये लिङ्गा योनिमण्डले ं ॥१५ ॥ तेषां सिद्धाञ्च योगिन्या उपर्युपरि योजयेत् । स्वरचक्रेश्वरी रेखा द्वितीया कादितान्तगा ।। १६ ।। ५४ थादिसान्ता'' तृतीया च त्रिभिः ४ रेखै: सुरेश्वरी । पञ्चाशत् सिद्धयोगिन्यो ं अत्र ये ते वदाम्यहम् ।। १७ ।।

sanskrit: CHAPTER SEVEN 151 Thus the Twelve Verses (are generated) by the conjunction of the three (groups of sixteen). The first (letter) is called the Lord of Elephants (gajendra) (Ca) 10 and the six-fold (seed-syllable called) the Peak of Knowledge (vidyākūṭa) (AIM). (9cd-10ab) That is the Letter (varṇa). That is Śiva's Void. That is the Linga and that is Śiva. That is the seed-syllable of Water and the (very) Self of the goddess.13 (10cd-11ab) The verses that are the sections (aṁśa) (of the Twelve Verses) are twelve and one part (pada) (of each section) is said to be eight-fold. 14 (11cd) This, the enclosure of the field (kṣetraparigraha) (is generated by) the mutual conjunction (of the letters) when the (energy of the) letters has been made to go and come impelled by the Moon, the Sun and Siva's will. 15 (12) The sixteen rays of energy (kalā) 16 are (the vowels) starting with Nectar (amṛta) (i.e. the letter A) and ending with Emission (visarga - H) (the last vowel). That is said to be the slanting line (which is) the deity on the left (vāmadevatā) and has the letters Ka and Ta at its extremities (katāntā).18 Raudrī is elevated (unnatā) on the right and is (the line of letters) ending (at the extremities with) Tha and Sa, in due order. (13-14ab) (The three goddesses) Vāmā, Jyeṣṭhā, and Raudrī (correspond to the gods) Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśvara. As a unity (is formed) by (these) three that is this, the House of the Yogini (yoginīgṛha). (14cd-15ab) 19 And the Siddhas of those Lingas namely, the (series of letters) beginning with Nectar (A), that live within the Circle of the Yoni (yonimaṇḍala) 20 should be conjoined at progressively higher levels (within the Triangle of Letters and along the sides)21 with (their corresponding) Yoginī. (15cd-16ab) The Mistress of the Wheel of Vowels (svaracakreśvarī) is (the first) line. The second begins with Ka and ends with Ta. Again, the third begins with Tha and ends with Sa. Sureśvarī (the Mistress of the Gods is formed with these) three lines. (Now) I will tell (you) who the fifty (pairs of) Siddhas and Yoginīs are here. (16cd-17)

english: CHAPTER SEVEN 155 This, the group of Siddhas and (their) wives, is the pure enclosure (parigraha) of the goddess.24 The Siddhas correspond to the letters in the deity's Circle of the Yoni. This indeed is said to be the sequence of the Siddhas (corresponding to the letters of the alphabet that come) at the beginning of the Aggregate of (Twelve) Verses (ślokarāśi). Having placed the Five PraSavas at the beginning, `avvāpāda' is at the end.25 O god, one should worship the Western House according to this procedure (vidhi). (32cd-34) Mahāntārikā the Vidyā and Kaulinī the Command in the Centre of the Triangle O fair faced one, Śiva and Śakti are these, (the letters) Ha and K±a, that are within the House.26 These two, the venerable Maitreya (otherwise) called Kucandra27 and the venerable goddess (śrīmān devī)28 Kubjikā, established in the Five (PraSavas) should be conjoined together simultaneously (yugapat)29 in the House of the Peak syllables (kū˜aveśman).30 (35-36ab) The Five (PraSavas) at the beginning along with (the same) five at the end and the Vidyā between the two is (the goddess) Mahantārikā (the Great Saviour) in the Triple World31 and she, the Command, is the sign of realisation (pratyaya) in (this) world. (36cd-37ab) Whoever she looks at also goes to the supreme abode and, once the supreme has been reached, O god, he then certainly attains accomplishment (siddhi).32 This is said to be the oral teaching (mukhāmnāya) in the hermitage (of the transmission) with (its) three divisions. (37cd-38) Above is the Command of sixteen Siddhas. Sixteen Siddhas are in the north (i.e. on the left of the Triangle) and sixteen are in the south (i.e. on the right). Śiva is the deity in the centre. Once the (individual) soul (ātman), seated in the centre of the Yoni (bhaga), has penetrated through the Yoni, he attains the supreme (paraˆ vrajet).33 (39-40ab) The Command of the Wheel of the Krama (kramacakra) rests between (the Wheels called) Self supported (svādhi) and the Filler (of Jewels) (pūraka).34 Her form crooked (tiryagākrti), facing downwards,35 she is the Knot of Brahmā.36 (40cd-41ab) The energy Kaulinī is the Transmental (unmanā) who brings about (karoti) the most excellent penetration (āveśa).37 Her Wheel above is the maSÆala that has been divided in half (ardhakrta).38 (41cd-42ab)

english: CHAPTER SEVEN 157 The Tree internalised within it is the Kadamba which is the union of the male and female seed (kuSÆagolaka).39 Within that is the subtle, plough-shaped Wick of the Command (ājñāvarti).40 (42cd- 43ab) That Command rests facing downwards within the Yoni (bhaga).41 That is the supreme and horrific (bhīmā) (goddess) Vakrikā. Once known, (the Wheels) are perforated.42 (43cd-44ab) In a moment, by merely recollecting the Command, (the yogi experiences) shaking (dhunana), possession (āveśana), trembling (kampa) and the slanted, upward movement (of kuSÆalinī), or else entry into the lower regions (pātāla).43 (44cd-45ab) The City of the Moon conjoined with the Twelve Verses and the Path of the Moon First the Twelve Verses of Meru are extracted (uddhrta) from amongst the fifty Rudras beginning with ŚrīkaS˜ha and are (then) deployed in the Half Wheel (ardhacakra). In the middle of that is the Wheel of Emanation (srn˜icakra) that has emerged from the Goddess of the Path (mārgadevī).44 (45cd-46) O Great Lord, I will establish your authority along with you. This is the City of the abode of the Siddhas, the abode of the House of the Gesture of the Yoni (yonimudrā).45 Of (all) the seats beginning with that of Yoga (yogapī˜ha),46 (this is) the Western (tradition) of Sadyojāta. (47-48ab) That is said to be the City conjoined with the Twelve Verses. The Vidyā is located there in the middle, encapsulated by the two groups of the five (praSavas).47 O Lord of Kula, the path of the Path of the Sequence of the Full Moon (pūrSimākramamārga) is that of the goddess. (48cd-49) I am she who, facing downwards, halts there in the First Seat (ādyapī˜ha)48 and exercises authority (there) by (my) anti-clockwise rotation. When the end of the Nameless (anāmānta) has been attained the accomplishment of the Command (is realised) in the Kulakrama.49 (50-51ab) (The goddess's Vidyā) beginning with the letter BHA and ending with the letter CA has emerged above and below. The Vidyā of Form (rūpavidyā) shines (beautifully) in the shape of the flame of the lamp of energy (śakti).50 (51cd-52ab) Then, the light of the energy of the Moon is Mālinī who (sits in union) close by (to the god) Kucandra.51 This is the Moon with full authority (pūrSādhikāra) that has emerged from the centre of Śiva. (52cd-53ab)

sanskrit: 158 कुमारिकाखण्ड: एव९ एवं ते द्वादश श्लोका एवं सा क्रमदेवता ।। ५३ ।। १९० संयोगेन क्रमाच्छम्भो सन्तान मेरुमार्गयो : १९९ । विनिष्क्रान्तं महादेव कौलिकं गुणवत्तरम् ॥ ५४ ॥ १९३ शक्त्याधार पुरं प्रोक्तं पुरं क्षेत्रपरिग्रहम् । तस्यान्तरगता देव्या कुब्जिकाहं च चन्द्रमा १९५ १९४ १९७ ॥ ५५ ॥ सा च लिङ्गं कुलाधारं अधिकार तु चिञ्चिणी । क्षेत्रलिङ्गाश्रमयोगाद्”” गृह चन्द्रपुरं भवेत् ॥ ५६ ॥ २०१ २०३ चन्द्रपूर्णगृहारभ्य” अन्वयस्य त्वनुक्रमम् । २०४ प्रकटं मत्यलोके तु अवतारं कलौ युगे ॥ ५७ ॥ उलिसिद्धाश्रमं मत्ये°५ चन्द्रपुर्याद् विनिर्गतम् ँ । २०८ २०९ •२१० २११ । ओकारश्च षकारश्च तथा त्वं” मित्रसंज्ञकः ।। ५८ ॥ मुद्रितं तेषु तज्ज्ञानमाख्यातं १२ उडपीठके २१३ । २१६ तदावतारित”४ शिष्यैर्नवभिः १५ पुण्ड्रवर्धने ॥ ५९ ॥ त्रिभिश्चैवाधिकार१७ स्यात् कोङ्कणे पूर्णगिर्यके २१८ । त्रिभिः सिद्धैश्च”” पाताले अन्तरिक्षे त्रिभिः पुनः ।। ६० ।। २२० चन्द्रपूर्णपुरे तत्र चिञ्चिणीनाम” वृक्षकम् २२२ । भञ्जितं तत्४ त्वया नाथ तेन त्वं २५ चिञ्चिणी २६ स्मृतः कीर्तिदेवेति विख्यातस्तस्मिन् ” वै चन्द्रपुर्यके । २३३ २२९ २३० २३१ २२७ सिद्धानां षोडश: २३२ पुत्राः ३ स्थिता ये ताननुग्रहेत् ।। ६२ ।। २३५ २३६ ख्यातं गुरुत्वाम्नाय ै५ वै तेषामनुक्रमेण तु । .२३७ २३८ उन्मनादिक्रमेणैव यावत् श्रीनाथचिञ्चिणी ॥ ६३ ॥ पुष्पसंकेतक शम्भो” अज्ञात्वा नैव मुक्तिभाक् । ।। ६१ ।।
english: CHAPTER SEVEN 159 Such are your Twelve Verses. Such is she, the deity of the Krama. O Śambhu, by the sequential union (of these) two paths of Meru the Kaulika lineage (santāna), the most excellent (of all), O Great God, has come forth.52 (53cd-54) The City (pura) is said to be the foundation (ādhāra) of Energy (śakti). And the City (pura) is the enclosure of the field (knetraparigraha). I am Kubjikā and the Moon (candramā) who is the goddess within it. And she is the Li‰ga, the foundation (ādhāra) of Kula, while authority is (me the Tamarind goddess) CiñciSī. The House, that is, the City of the Moon (candrapura), is (generated by) the union of the field and the Li‰ga.53 (55-56) The Lineages of Siddhas The geneology (anukrama) of the lineage (anvaya) commences with the House full of the Moon (candrapūrSa). Manifest in the mortal world, the descent (avatāra of the Siddhas) takes place during the Age of Strife (kaliyuga). The Hermitage of the Siddhas of the lineages (ulisiddhāśrama) has come forth into the mortal (martya) (world) from the City of the Moon.54 (57-58ab) The Three Siddhas (The first Siddhas are those denoted by) the letter O (for OÆÆīśanātha)55 and ±A (for ±an˜hanātha) as well as you who are called Mitra.56 Stamped (mudrita) within them57 is that knowledge that has been explained in the sacred seat of UÆa (uÆapī˜ha).58 (58cd-59ab) The Nine Siddhas It was brought down into (the city of) PuSÆravardhana by the nine disciples. Authority (was established) by three (of them) in PūrSagiryaka (in the land of) KoˆkaSa.59 (It was established) by three Siddhas in the subterranean region (pātāla) and by three again in the sky (antarikna). There is a tamarind tree (ciñcinī) there, in the city of CandrapūrSa. You bent it, O lord, and so it is that you are said to be CiñciSī (nātha - the Lord of the Tamarind). Therein, in the City of the Moon (candrapuryaka you are) known as Kīrtideva (God of Fame). May he grace the sixteen (spiritual) sons of the Siddhas. (I have thus) explained, in due order, their preceptorial lineage (gurutvāmnāya). (59cd-63ab) The Convention of the Flowers - the Eighteen Siddhas O Śambhu, without having known the Convention of the Flower (punpasaˆketaka) that extends in due order from the Transmental (unmanā) up to Śrīnātha and CiñciSī, one is not liberated.60 (63cd-64ab)

sanskrit: 160 कुमारिकाखण्डः २४१ उन्मनाद्यादिनाथान्तं गुर्वोघं पुष्पसंज्ञकम् ॥ ६४ ॥ कोङ्कणे तु त्रिधाभिन्नं नाथादौ तत् कलौ युगे ४२ । २४३ २४४ न दीक्षा न परत्वं च पारम्पर्यक्रमं न हि ॥ ६५ ॥ क्रमस्य क्रमणं नास्ति पुष्पसंकेतवर्जिते ५ । २४५ । बीजोज्झिते ६ यथा क्षेत्रे सस्यं नैव प्ररोहति पुष्पसंकेतहीनेषु मुक्तिर्नैव च विद्यते । २५१ २४८ ।। ६६ ।। आदिनाथस्त्रयोलीनां वृक्षनाथेति विश्रुतः ।। ६७ ॥ तस्य ते नव पुत्राश्च वर्तमाने २५२ कलौ युगे २५३ । संजाताः २५४ कोङ्कणे मत्ये २५५ अधस्त्रीणि ६ त्रयोध्वतः २५९ २६० २५७ निर्वंशाश्च गताः षट् च सवंशास्त्रीणि कोङ्कणें । २६२ तेषां संज्ञा? मुखाम्नाये २ श्रीदेशे गोत्रमण्डले ॥ ६९ ॥ गगनः कुमुदस्तथा ६३ पद्मो देवश्च भैरवः । २६४ २६६ कमल: शिवरामश्च कृष्णानन्दस्त्रिलोचन ।। ७० ।। एवं क्रमेण ते जाताः संकेतेन पृथक् पृथक् । २६७ २६८ ।। द्वितीयं च चतुर्थं च पञ्चमं च अधस्त्रयः ॥ ७१ ॥ सप्तमं चाष्टनवमं त्रीण्येते ऊध्वगाः २७२ क्रमात् २७४ २७५ २७६ २७३ । ।। ६८ ।। खेचरास्ते पुरा सर्वे दिव्याज्ञायाः सर्वे दिव्याज्ञायाः प्रभावतः ।। ७२ ।। पाताले ये गतास्त्रीणि भोगान् भुञ्जन्ति चापरे । । अधिकारे २१ स्थितास्त्रीणि प्रथमं च तृतीयकम् ।। ७३ ।। षष्ठमाज्ञा स्वरूपेण अधिकारक्रमे २८३ स्थिताः ' २८४
english: CHAPTER SEVEN 161 The Current of Teachers (gurvogha), called (the Convention of) the Flower extends from the Transmental up to Ādinātha (the First Nātha). O lord, in the Age of Strife it was initially divided into three in (the land of) Ko‰kaSa.61 (64cd-65ab) There is no initiation, no supreme condition (paratva), no transmission through the series (of teachers) and no transmission (kramaSa) of the teaching (krama) in the absence of the Convention of the Flower. (65cd-66ab) Just as no crop grows in a field devoid of seed,62 so too there is no liberation for those devoid of the Convention of the Flower.63 (66cd-67ab) The Nine Siddhas 64The First Nātha (ādinātha) of the three lineages (oli) is famous as Vrknanātha (Lord of the Tree).65 He has these nine (spiritual) sons in the present Age of Strife. (67cd-68ab) Three (of them) arose below in the mortal (land of) Ko‰kaSa and three above. Six had no (spiritual) descendants left and the three that had descendants (remained) in Ko‰kaSa.66 (68cd-69ab) Their names within the assembly of the clan (gotramaSÆala), according to the oral tradition (mukhāmnāya) in Śrīdeśa are, O Three-eyed One: 1) Gagana (Sky) and 2) Kumuda (Moon Lotus), 3) Padma (Lotus) and 4) Deva along with 5) Bhairava, 6) Kamala (Lotus), 7) Śiva, 8) Rāma and 9) KrnSānanda (KrnSa's Bliss). They have thus arisen successively, each individually, according to the convention (saˆketa). (69cd-71ab) The second (Kumuda), the fourth (Deva) and the fifth (Bhairava) are the lower three. The seventh (Śiva), eighth (Rāma) and ninth (KrnSānanda) - these three, in due order, are above. All of these (last three) are Skyfarers of old by the power of the divine Command while those three who have gone to the lower regions enjoy worldly benefits (bhoga) on the inferior (level). (71cd-73ab) Three are established in authority namely, the first (Gagana), the third (Padma) and the sixth (Kamala).67 They are established in the transmission of authority (adhikārakrama) as the (very) nature of the (divine) Command. (73cd-74ab)

sanskrit: 162 कुमारिकाखण्डः २८९ २८७ तेषां२८५ सन्तति: संजाता पुरुषाणीह षोडश ।। ७४ ।। १९४ २९१ २९२ तेषां नामानि”° वक्ष्यामि पूजासंकेतकेन तु । सूरस्तीव्रश्च खेचर्यो गर्भमुक्तश्च सिंहकः ।। ७५ ।। जयो विजयमित्रश्च वीरो विमलपञ्चकम् । २९८ २९७ रत्नकेशवमुन्मत्तमुद्रास्रोतावहं ततः ।। ७६ ।। इत्येते षोडश:”” सिद्धा भविष्यन्ति कलौ युगे । ३०२ द्विचतुष्कं च यत् पूर्वं पञ्चमोज्झितं सुव्रत ।। ७७ ।। गदेवस्य सुता ज्ञेया विज्ञेया ज्येष्ठ – ओलिगा: ३०६ ३०५ । पञ्चमो मध्यमोल्यां तु पदेवस्य सुतः स्मृतः ॥ ७८ ॥ ३०९ नवादिषोडशान्तास्तु ँ विज्ञेया“ बाल–ओलिकाः' । कदेवस्य सुता ज्ञेया एवं ते सिद्धषोडश ।। ७९ ।। •३१३ परान्वय तु प्रथमं द्वितीयं वक्रिकान्वयम् । सिद्धान्वयं ततः पश्चात्” भविष्यति कलौ युगे ॥ ८० ॥ ३१५ द्वापञ्चाशद् भवेज्ज्येष्ठे सप्ताविंशति६ मध्यमे । ३१७ ३१८ बालक्रमे भविष्यन्ति चतुराशीति संख्यया ।। ८१ ।। एषां वै सिद्धसन्तानमसंख्यानं”” भविष्यति । आज्ञा चण्डतरा° तेषां भविष्यति १ महेश्वर ३२३ ३२२ नवानां षोडशानां च पूजास्थानान् वदाम्यहम् ।। ८२ ।। ३२४ ।
english: CHAPTER SEVEN 163 The Sixteen Siddhas Their lineage (santati) (also) arose, consisting of sixteen men. I will tell (you) their names according to the ritual convention (pūjāsaˆketaka). 1) Sūra (Brave) and 2) Tīvra (Sharp), 3) Khecarya (Skyfarer) and 4) Garbhamukta (Free from the Womb), 5) Siˆhaka (Lion), 6) Jaya (Victory), 7) Vijayamitra (Friend of Victory), 8) Vīra (Hero), 9-13) the Five Pure Ones (vimalapañcaka), 14) Ratnakeśava (Jewel Hair), 15) Unmattamudrā (Gesture of Frenzy), and 16) Srotāvaha (Bringer of the Current). These are the sixteen Siddhas who will live in the Age of Strife. (74cd-77ab) The Three Lineages of the Sixteen Siddhas O one of good vows, the (first) two groups of four with the fifth, as before, missing, should be known to be the (spiritual) offspring of Gadeva (i.e. Gaganadeva). One should know that they belong to the Lineage of the Eldest (jye- n˜holi). (77cd-78ab) The fifth is in the Middle Lineage (madhyamoli) and is said to be the (spiritual) son of Padeva (i.e. Padmadeva). (78cd) The ninth to the sixteenth should be known to belong to the Lineage of the Child (bāloli). One should know that they are the (spiritual) sons of Kadeva (i.e. Kamaladeva). Such, then, are those sixteen Siddhas.68 (79) The first (group constitutes) the Supreme Lineage (parānvaya), the second Vakrikā's Lineage. After that there will be the Lineage of Siddhas (siddhānvaya) in the Age of Strife.69 (80) Fifty-two belong to (the Lineage of the) Eldest, twenty-seven to the Middle (Lineage), while eighty-four will belong to the Lineage of the Child.70 Their lineage of Siddhas will be innumerable and, O Great Lord, their Command will be extremely powerful. (81-82) The Locations of the Nine Siddhas in the Body I will tell (you now) the places where the (groups of) nine and sixteen (Siddhas) are worshipped. (83ab)

sanskrit: 164 कुमारिकाखण्डः प्रथमं च भ्रुवोर्मध्ये १२५ द्वितीयाधारमण्डले' ३२७ ३२८ ३२६ तृतीयं मणिपूरे तु चतुर्थं पञ्चमं तथा । ३३० ३१ ॥ ८३ ॥ पुनराधारे” संपूज्य षष्ठं वै स्वाधिष्ठानगम् ३३५ सप्ताष्टनवमं३३ देव' तुयतीते तु पूजयेत् । ३३२ एवं ते नवसिद्धानां शरीरे पूजनक्रमम् ॥ ८५ ॥ षोडशानां महादेव श्रूयतां स्थाननिर्णयम् । ३३७ ॥ ८६ ॥ अष्टौ कपालमालायां नवमं नाभिमण्डले द्विपञ्चात् षोडशं यावत्” भगमालां प्रपूजयेत् । ३४२ तेषां सन्तति:३४९ संजाता संसारे कलिवर्तमनि स्थानमेकादशं ै३ यावत् ओलिशुद्धिरिह क्रमे । ।। ८४ ।। ।। ८७ ।। । पारम्पर्यन्वयं ह्येतत् गुरुशिष्यक्रमं तथा ॥ ८८ ॥ ३४७ ३४८ भविष्यति कुलनाथ निःशेष तु कलौ युगे । ३५४ । स्व–उल्यां४९ गुरु– ओघ तु निर्बीजं पूजयति यः संसारे ५२ वर्तते भूय: ३५३ संसारान्न निवर्तते वृक्षनाथं विना यस्तु श्रीनाथं पूजयति यः संसारे वर्तते भूयः संसारान्न“ निवर्तते । ३५५ ३५९ ३५१ ॥ ८९ ॥ ।। ९० ।। ओलित्रितयमार्ग तु कथितं तव मण्डले ॥ ९१ ॥ •३६० नाख्यातं निर्णय चात्र आख्यातमिह संहिताम् सिद्धानां५२ षोडशः पुत्राः ६३ संजाता मित्रयोनिषु ३६६ ३६१ ३६४ प्रथमा ज्येष्ठ - ओली ३६५ च क्रमभेदे समासतः । ३६७ । ।। ९२ ।। पुरमध्ये समाख्याता' तत्रारभ्य क्रमार्चनम् ।। ९३ ।।
english: CHAPTER SEVEN 165 The first is between the eyebrows. The second is in the Circle of the Foundation (ādhāramaSÆala).71 The third is, along with the fourth and the fifth, in MaSipura. Having worshipped in the Foundation again, the sixth is present in (the Wheel of) the Self-supported (svādhin˜hāna).72 O god, the seventh, eighth and ninth should be worshipped (together as a group) in (the centre corresponding to the state that is) Beyond the Fourth (turyātīta). (83cd-85ab) The Location of the Sixteen Siddhas in the Body Such is the order of worship (pūjanakrama) of your nine Siddhas in the body. (Now) O Great God, hear the teaching concerning the location of the sixteen (Siddhas). (85cd-86ab) One should worship (the first) eight in the Garland of Skulls (kapālamālā). The ninth in the Circle of the Navel and the tenth up to the sixteenth in the (Wheel that has) Yonis as a Garland (bhagamālā).73 (86cd-87ab) Their lineage (santati) has come into existence in the world of transmigration on the path of the Age of Strife. The purification of the lineages (oli) here in the transmission (krama) (should done) up to the eleventh place (sthāna).74 (87cd-88ab) This is the lineage of the serial transmission (of the tradition) (pāramparyānvaya) and the sequence of teachers and disciples. (All this) without exception will take place, O lord of Kula, in the Age of Strife. (88cd-89ab) He who worships the current of teachers within his own lineage (uli) without seed,75 continues to remain in the world of transmigration. He does not leave it. He who worships Śrīnātha without (worshipping) Vrknanātha continues to remain in the world of transmigration.76 He does not leave it. (89cd-91ab) The Three Lineages I have told you the Path of the Three Lineages in the maSÆala, (however I) have not told you the teaching (concerning it) here. It is explained (elsewhere) here in this scripture (saˆhitā). (91cd-92ab) The sixteen (spiritual) sons of the Siddhas are born in Mitra's wombs.77 The first lineage (olī) is that of the Eldest and is (established) in (its appropriate) division of the Transmission. In brief, it is said to be in the centre of the City. The worship of the Transmission (kramārcana) (takes place) having begun there. (92cd-93)

english: CHAPTER SEVEN 167 The second is the Middle Lineage (located) in the southern and northern corners (of the Triangle). The third, in due order, is the Lineage of the Child and is (located) in the corner in the forepart (of the Triangle). There, (the goddess) is called Mudrā (Gesture)78 and is the Command of the Tradition (anvayājñā) here within (the Siddhas who are) the wombs (that receive her fertilising seed). (94-95ab) O (OÆÆīśa), ±A (±an˜hanātha) and Mitra(nātha) are famed as the (founding) Siddhas in the three lineages (oli).79 He who explains the Hermitage of the House of the City of the Moon in another way and who, O god, does not know the three lineages, the teaching concerning the Twelve Verses, the Seat of Yoga, the three Siddhas, the Transmission (krama), the Vidyā and the maSÆala, O lord of the gods, will not be worthy of worship. He is not a disciple in the Kula and Kaula and has no authority in this scripture (śāstra). (95cd-98ab) Conclusion This is the sūtra of the City of the Moon It is the introductory sūtra (of this scripture) (pratijñāsūtra). It is the first in this Kula scripture (śāstra). (What) follows is its subsequent (continuation) (uttara). The First Gesture (ādimudrā), along with (its) three divisions,80 the Twelve Verses, the Siddhas of the House and the goddesses as well as the goddess of the Vidyā, the Full Moon, the Siddhas of the Lineages (oli), the three persons and the sixteen Siddhas81 - O god, having first known these (things) after that one may set up (udāharet) the Transmission (krama). (98cd-101ab) This is the (seventh) chapter which is the emergence of the transmission (kramodaya) concerning a Description of the Authority (of the Goddess) in the Venerable City of the Moon. It belongs to the primordial descent into the great sacrifice of the Churning Bhairava in the tradition (anvaya) that consists of seventy million (verses) that has emerged on the Path of Meru and (extends) for a hundred and twenty-five thousand quarter (verses). It has been brought (down to earth) into the first sacred seat along the path of the Seat of Knowledge (vidyāpī˜ha) in the teaching of the Pure Six (Thousand Verses vimalana˜ka) belonging to the division beginning with `Kā' in the venerable scripture of twenty-four thousand (verses) (known as) the Svāminīmata of the Supreme Lord's command as uttered within the Tradition of the Mother (avvākrama).

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER ONE 1. These verses are discussed in the summary of contents of the KuKh in chapter nine of the introduction to which the reader is referred. Both the ±a˜sāhasrasaˆhitā and the KumārikākhaSÆa open with the following verses set in the metre sragdharā. Called the SaˆvartāmaSÆalasūtra, they are an expanded version of the first verse of the KMT which reads: Within (the centre) of SaˆvartāmaSÆala is the power of bliss (ānanda- śakti). Present in (every) part (pada) of the Transmission (kramapadanihitā), she is pleasingly horrific (subhīmā). Once emitted the first quaternary present in (both) Akula and Kula the pentad (follows) and another, the sextet, (again) the four, another pentad and then again the four. This, in reality, is the maSÆala. Bow to him by whom (all this) has been emitted, the best of teachers, Bhairava, the venerable Kujeśa. saˆvartāmaSÆalānte kramapadanihitānandaśaktiƒ subhīmā saˆsrjyādyaˆ catunkaˆ akulakulagataˆ pañcakaˆ ca anyana˜kam | catvāraƒ pañcako‘nyaƒ punar api caturas tattvato maSÆaledaˆ saˆsrn˜aˆ yena tasmai namata guruvaraˆ bhairavaˆ śrīkujeśam || The first line of this verse is the same as the corresponding line in the ±SS and the KuKh. In the KMT the second quarter of the third line ends with tattvato maSÆaledaˆ ('this, in reality, is the maSÆala') instead of noÆaśājñābhinekaˆ ('the Consecration of the Sixteenfold Command'). According to Schoterman's numbering, which I have adopted, the last quarter of the verse in the KMT corresponds to the second and the last quarter of the half verse numbered four in the version here. Mukunda, the author the SaˆP, also notices that the version in the KMT is embedded in the first part of the sūtra, and refers to it as the short one (laghusaˆvartārthaƒ). After he has commented on it, drawing most of his material from chapter two of the KuKh, he goes on in the same way to comment on the rest of the sūtra which he refers to, along with the first part, as the long version (brhatsaˆvartā). Whether it is the short or the long version, knowledge of the meaning of this sūtra is particularly important for adepts of the Kubjikā cult. Thus, the ŚM concludes its commentary on the short version by saying that: Those who do not know (the meaning of the) Saˆvartā (sūtra) do not know the Śrīmata (the root Tantra and teachings of the Kubjikā cult). O goddess, without (knowing) the Śrīmata (all) effort (to acquire) knowledge is in vain. saˆvartāˆ [g, ‰, ch: saˆvartā] ye na jānanti na te jānanti śrīmatam ||

The fifteenth and sixteenth names are feminine as are their dependent ordinals. The remaining names are all neuter and their dependent ordinals are in concord, even though it is clear that a masculine proper name is intended. This change from masculine to neuter of male proper names is common in the Sanskrit of such texts and need not detain us. Although the KnT presents all the names as masculine, it is clear that in order to do so the

36 NOTES OF THE SANSKRIT TEXT OF CHAPTER TWO author has had to take recourse to expedients, such as suffixing - akhyaḥ to the names that are clearly feminine. Although belonging to the main period of development of the Kubjikā Tantras, the KnT is a derived work by a self- proclaimed author. It is not surprising, therefore, that the Sanskrit of a passage such as this one, drawn from the Tantras, has been polished up. The SM is closer in this respect to the passage we are examining. The mixed genders and loose concord there encourages us to accept the same here as part of the orginal basic text and not the result of simply scribal error. The editor is faced here with a dilemma. Should this passage be extensively emended to the correct Sanskrit on the lines of the version found in the KnT? One wonders to what degree scribes may commit errors. It is likely that this passage is not orginal to the Kukh and was drawn from another source where the same confusion of genders existed. The redactor(s) of the Kukh sought to overcome this problem by labelling each member of the series abstractly as a 'division' of the Divine Current irrespective of gender (see 2/26ab). Thus one could think of the neuter forms as agreeing with which is normally treated as neuter in this text (see above, note to 1/2b). 103. कु, खः त । 104. घ्, च्, छ्: व्याप्तिर्; KnT: समनाख्यस्तृतीयञ्च; ŚM: तृतीयं च पराव्याप्तिर् । 105. Above in 2/28 the sequence is Mitranātha (MI), Sasthanātha (SA) and Oddīśanātha (O). It is as follows: 1) Oddīśanātha (O) – Oddiyāna (O) – Krta Age 2) Caryānātha (CA) - Jalandhara (JĀ) - Tretā Age 3) Sasthanātha (SA) - Purnagiri (Pū) – Dvāpara Age 4) Mitranātha (MI) - Kāmarūpa (KA) - Kali Age. english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER TWO 1. According to Monier-Williams, the common, non-technical sense of the noun saˆvitti (f.) is: 'knowledge, intellect, understanding; perception, feeling, sense of; mutual agreement, harmony, recognition, recollection'. Here it has the special sense the technical term pratyaya conveys. The SKh (4/22ab) explains: saˆvitti (means), by secondary ascription, a sign of attainment (pratyaya), such as the explosion of a tree and the like (brought about by the yogi's will) (saˆvittir upacāreSa vrknaspho˜ādipratyayam). According to Monier-Williams the word pratyaya means: 'belief, firm conviction, trust, faith assurance or certainty; proof, ascertainment'. In our texts, and the Tantras in general, this word possesses an added technical sense derived from these primary meanings. Pratyaya denotes those signs that indicate the yogi's degree of accomplishment and hence inner level of attainment. When used in this sense, I therefore normally translate the term pratyaya with the phrase 'sign of attainment'. Most of these signs are externally perceptable. They include what would be understood in India as signs of possession by the deity (āveśa) such as bodily tremours or fits. They also include powers to perform magical-cum-yogic feats. Although the outer signs are more numerous, there are inner signs also. As one would expect, the most important is a powerful experience of bliss (ānanda) and what is here called saˆvitti which I translate as the 'realisation (of attainment)'. Saˆvitti may also mean simply 'consciousness' as in the two following examples. The god is explaining the deeper meaning of a set of mantras called the Five Jewels. The first Jewel, this passage tells us, is one's own transcendental consciousness, which within Śiva, realises his true nature: That is said to be (the highest) sense organ (āknā), which devoid of mind (citta), is constantly (present) in the being of the mind. Again, the dissolving away of the mind is said to be (the condition) devoid of mind. (The state) devoid of mind, established above non-self (nairātmya), is due to that. The most excellent teachers say that that is the Jewel which is one's own consciousness (svasaˆvitti) (present) within Supreme Śiva by means of meditation. cittahīnā tu sāknā [k gh: sāknī] yā cittibhāve [k ‰: vitī-; all MSs: -bhāva] sadā smrtā | pralayaˆ [k: prālayaˆ] caiva cittasya [k gh: vittasya; kh g ‰: cityasya] cittahīnaˆ [‰: vācinna-] tad ucyate [‰: tahacyate] || acittaˆ bhavate tena [kh g: bhāvatenaiva; ‰: * nā] nairātmyoparisaˆsthitam [kh gh ‰: nairātmā-; g: nairātmyā-; k gh: -sthitaƒ] | pare śive svasaˆvittir [kh g: svasaˆcitti-; ‰: svasaˆvitti-] dhyānayuktyā gurūttamaiƒ [k gh: gurottamaiƒ] ||

Bhairava is the lord of those powers whose shouting (ravaSa) instils fear (bhī) in the souls in bondage. 86. The Sanskrit reads: kulakaulāntamadhyastham, which may also be translated '(he is) in the centre within Kulakaula'. Concerning Kula and Kaula see intro. vol. 2, p. 325 ff.. A passage is quoted there from YKh (1). This explains that Akula is the omnipresent Lord and that it is where Kula dissolves away. Kaula is the Unmanifest. The plane in the middle of Kula and Kaula is in the abode of the triple energy of Kula (i.e. the energies of will, knowledge and action). 87. It is hard to understand what purpose this verse serves here. The last question asked in chapter one about the Saˆvartāsūtra concerns Kaulīśa who is mentioned at the end of the sūtra. The following verse after the sūtra apparently summerizes the two essential points made in the sūtra. One is the nature of the maSÆala, which is said to be Bhairava. The other concerns the transmission of the teachings, which is said there to be two-fold - divine and human. The former is the Divine Current (see above 2/20-26). The latter begins with the three Siddhas (above 2/28) MI (Mitranātha), ±a (±an˜hanātha) and O (OÆÆīśanātha) who taught the three transmissions (krama) of the Child, Youth and Aged, respectively. Presumably, this verse seeks to integrate the two into four transmissions by including the Divine Current. This is identified with the Transmission of the Skyfarers (khecarakrama), which is the Śāmbhava Transmission.

The present, imperative, and optative tenses are especially preferred by the author(s) of this Tantra. Of course, this has to do with the nature of the subjects presented in Tantric texts, which generally do not require much narration. Even so, it is occasionally necessary, as in this and the following three chapters, to narrate significant mythical events. We may briefly

92 NOTES OF THE SANSKRIT TEXT OF CHAPTER THREE - उवाच note here the use of tense in these chapters. Apart from past passive participles, that are very common, we do come across verbs used in past and future tenses but when they are required they are generally replaced by the present and, occasionally the optative. The most common example is, of course, the virtually invariable use, as in most Tantric texts, of the perfect of in the standard expression 'the god or the goddess spoke' - to introduce chapters and sections of the text. The four times a verb is conjugated in a past tense in these three chapters, it is in the imperfect (see 3/84c, 5/8a, 6/44c, 6/87b and 6/119d). Although Pāṇinian Sanskrit allows for the use of the present to denote past action, if that took place in the recent past, a deviant extension of this option takes place here in the case we are examining, as in most others in this text. Thus in these three chapters, the present tense is used with a past sense at least nineteen times (see 3/72d, 75c, 79d, 82b, 88a, 161c, 5/59cd, 71d, 6/6b, 7b, 12c, 45ab (x 2), 47c, 82c, 88d, 127c, 129d, 134) and the optative is used in this way not less than five times (see 5/63b and 6/92d, 131a, 133d, 224b), perhaps six (see 3/83c). Similarly, we find that a verb in the future tense appears nine times (see 6/8d, 138b, 173a (passive), 177a, 185d, 186a, 196d, 197d, 200d), otherwise a present tense is used denote future action five times (see 4/8b, 17b, 29d, 5/61a, 6/172b, 200b) and optative once (see 6/173d). Generally, the present and optative maintain their distinctive identities but they do sometimes overlap. Thus we find one example in these three chapters of a passive optative replacing the present (see 3/143ab). The use of the present and the optative signifies, it seems, that events that occured in a mythical past or will occur in the future actually take place in a perpetual present. It is as if these events, although past, happen all the time now. All that happened to the god or the goddess, what they did or how they were are aspects of how they are. For those bound by the transitoriness of temporality this indescribable property of the semper eternum of the perpetual present is implicitely indicated by the use of the present and, occasionally by the optative, which function as a sort of 'tenseless tense'. The same effect is achieved by the absence of a marker of tense. In line 6/32cd, for example, we read that the goddess is in a place for three hundred divine years: दिव्यवर्षशतास्त्रीणि देवी तत्र व्यवस्थिता. The context tells us that, in temporal terms, she was in that place for that period of time sometime in the past but there is no direct indication of this having taken place in the past. The goddess IS there for three hundred years. 59. Irregular sandhi will henceforth be indicated as `IS'. 60. It appears, therefore, that the omission of the anusvāras is due to scribal error in the one or two MSs that were the original source of the others. The readings in MSs and are generally close and, particularly in MS, are idiosyncratic with respect to those of the other MSS

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER THREE 1. We have seen that Bhairava assumes various names when he plays the role of the first teacher (ādinātha). In the the Saˆvartāsūtra (1/2b) he was called Śrīnātha, in the previous chapter Vrknanātha (2/9ab and 2/29-31) and here Tūnnīnātha - the Silent Lord. This is also how he appears below in chapter 46, which is probably drawn from chapter 43 of the ±SS. The legends associated with him have been outlined in introduction (vol. 2, p. 474 ff.). The Cave in which TūnSīnātha sits, is the Cave of the Kadamba Tree (kadambaguhā), where the goddess received the Consecration of the Command (ājñābhineka) and enjoyed the bliss of the Śāmbhava state. This is the Cave Dwelling (guhāvāsa) to which the goddess sends the god at the end of this chapter to attain the Śāmbhava plane and receive her grace (3/162-4ab). We may surmise that TūnSīnātha is the god when he is in the Cave receiving the same empowering grace the goddess received before him. Thus the chapter turns full circle, ending where it began. These mythic motifs support and explain the symbolism of the maSÆala, which is described in the following verses, and the Yogic practice to which this verse alludes. The 'temple of Meru', on the peak of which the Cave is located, is the maSÆala. The same verse appears again below (3/30). There, instead of 'temple' (mandira) some manuscripts read maSÆala. Below in 3/48 we are told that the goddess's Triangle, which is the core and essence of her maSÆala, is the Cave Dwelling. Similarly, we have seen that according to the ±SS (2/5) a form of the SaˆvartāmaSÆala is located above the Cavity of Brahmā on the crown of the head. This has the shape of a triangle (Schoterman 1981: 50). From that, explains the ±SS (2/29), originates ‘a circle where the Mountain of the Moon (candraśilā) is located. This is called the Cave of the Moon’. The Mountain of the Moon, here called Meru, is Kailāsa, the sacred mountain in the centre of the world. Located in the End of the Twelve above the head it is, as we shall see in chapter eight, full of the phonemic energies of the letters. This inner or 'upper' maSÆala is a symbolic reproduction of the place where the first transmission of the teachings of the Kubjikā Tantras in this Age took place. Thus it is the house (veśman, grha, ghara) and place of origin of the tradition which is called the last or end one (paścimāmnāya) because, amongst other reasons, it is located here at the end of this space. It is the place where accomplished yogis attain realisation as did TūnSīnātha, the Silent Lord. In this way, the original empowerment of the outer sacred site through the descent of the goddess and her consort and TūnSīśa's enlightenment, are reproduced and made accessible to the adept. The initiate who contemplates this maSÆala and utters its mantras can draw the energy of the transmission from its original source (yoni). 2. english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER THREE 173 transmission of the tradition'. 195. Lit. ‘descent of power’. 196. We have seen (above 3/157cd-159) that the goddess immolated herself in her father’s sacrificial fire to purify herself. 197. See intro. 2, 197, 277. 198. The goddess assumes her full identity as the power of the Command once she has transmitted it to the god. She is fully enstated as the power-holder only when she has exercised her power. Her empowerment is completed by transmitting the Command and the Command is fulfilled by flowing through the lineages. The first point of exit is the god. Operating through him its flows into the whole tradition of the Kubjikā Tantras. Cf. 3/22-24, 3/66cd-67ab, 5/2-7 and notes. 199. The sequence of events is not at all as clear here as it is in the KMT. A knowledge of the original myth is presumed and so there is no need to make everything fit in a forward linear sequence. Mythical time is, anyway, not linear. Events may be `repeated’ before they take place. It is a way of expressing the peculiar circularity of self-subsistence that characterizes the spiritual world. In this case, this circularity is apparent with respect to the empowering grace, which, both cause and effect, is accomplished, as it were, right from the start and yet must be attained. The goddess who just a few lines before graced the god and so must have emerged out of the Li‰ga again becomes the Divine Li‰ga and as such re-enters it. This is the goddess’s introverted condition in which she experiences the bliss of her innate nature, the Command. In this condition it is still inside her and like the drop of vital seed in the womb fertilizes her. She who is the womb - Yoni - is in the womb of the Li‰ga of power (tejoli‰ga) and the Li‰ga which is her own nature is within her emitting the seed of the Command that sustains her (5/11cd-14). In the Li‰ga she is the Virgin practicing the vow of `ecstatic celibacy’ (see below 6/3-5). Now up to verse 5/28, the god addresses the goddess who is inside the Li‰ga. Even though she is unmanifest, she can hear and see him. She even answers him from within the Li‰ga. 200. The City of the Moon is the Triangle. The Divine Li‰ga is the Point in the centre resonant with the goddess’s seed-syllable Vidyā AI¤ or HSKHPHRE¤ that resounds in the Void of the Yoni. This is the Li‰ga in the Yoni - Sound in the Supreme Void. 201. As Śrīnātha is the speaker, it is he, it seems, who is the recipient of the Āgama. But then one would expect him to say it is his own oral tradition not Śambhu's, as if Śambhu were other than himself. This laps gives one the impression here for a moment that the mortal redactor of the KuKh is speaking, not the god.
