english: CHAPTER THIRTEEN 119 The venerable (goddess) Vakrā said: (Now) according to a different sequence, (I will expound) the teaching (nirSaya) concerning the inner sacrifice again in these, the Transmissions of the Aged and the Youth,94 that are within the Secret Place of the Siddhas (siddhaguhya), the Cave of Kula (kulakandara).95 (111) The adept, the one who recites mantra, fulfils the Transmission because he is penetrated by (AI¤) the Thunderbolt (vajra). Performing his own (ritual) gesture of union with (his) hands and making (his) mind face downwards,96 (he should) make the round MaSÆala of Gesture which is the Hermitage of the Supreme Lord.97 (112-113ab) Made of heated gold, it is pure. There is a round, light red solar disc rotating in a clockwise direction in the middle of it. In the middle of that is an unbroken circle (akhaSÆacakra), light red in colour and similar to (pure) light. In the middle of that is the supreme Island (white as) cow's milk, tranquil and watery. Recollect that there as it rotates in the midst of the teaching of the Triple Lineage (oli)98 which (constitute) the Wheel of Birth (janmacakra).99 (113cd-115) O Lord of the Universe, in the centre of that is the Circle of the Point (bindumaSÆala) which, by (its) anticlockwise motion, is like a flower (formed by whirling) a firebrand. (116) Within that is the Vidyā who is Parā, the Supreme Goddess. She is Energy in (her) terrible aspect, Mind Beyond Mind (manonmanī) (whose) form is Light.100 (117) Horrific (ghorā), she burns without smoke, (like) the flame on the wick of a lamp. Shining like countless millions of Rudras, she is Rudra's energy who is both supreme (transcendent) and inferior (immanent). (118) (This) energy is the Point, the deluge (of energy that flows) right down to the earth and contains millions of millions of Rudras. Its radiant power (tejas) is the Supreme Energy, Rudra's energy, the Great Goddess. (119) Her form is crooked because she is the Command blessed (bhāvita) by lord Śiva. She is consciousness, the goddess Śrī, Kulakubjikā and Vikāsā (Expansion). (120)

sanskrit: 120 कुमारिकाखण्ड: ४७० प्रज्वलन्ती स्वकिरणैश्चतुर्भिः रौद्रमण्डलें ' एवं तां गूढरोधेन संस्मरेत् किरणावलीम् ।। १२१ ।। ४७६ निःश्वासमेकभावेन ४ शिष्यदेह विशोधयेत् । ४७८ आकम्पो रोमहर्षश्च वर्तते दृढमुष्टिना ।। १२२ ।। ४७९ शक्तितत्त्वे च संप्राप्ते समुत्थाप्य शनैः शनैः । मध्यनाडीप्रवाहेन सुषुम्नान्ते यथा पुरा ।। १२३ ।। भुजङ्गकुटिलाकारां नाभिस्थाने प्रवेशयेत् । ४८१ । अलातचक्ररूपेण वामावर्तपरिभ्रमात् ।। १२४ ॥ नीयते ऊध्वमार्गेण८२ यावद्३ हृद्व्योमपञ्चकम् । कृत्वा चतुःप्रकारेण वामावर्तेण सा कला ।। १२५ ।। नीयते परमे धाम्नि अनामापथमण्डले । ४८७ तस्योध्वे४८ क्षीयमाणां ९ च मेरुमण्डलमध्यतः ।। १२६ ।। चतुःप्रकारक्रमान्ते” ध्वनिमात्रा” प्रवेशयेत् । शक्ति ४९२ विमलरूपेण उद्धरेत् कन्दमण्डलात् शनैः शनैरूध्वमार्गे ९५ नादरूपां लयं कुरु । ४९४ उदयं बिन्दुमध्ये तु एवमस्तमनं पुनः ।। १२८ ॥ •४९८ तत्रैव ऊध्वमार्गे तु शक्तिमाद्यां लयं कुरु । इत्याज्ञागमभेदेन अमावास्या प्रचोदिता ॥ १२९॥ ४९९ एतत् कर्मविपाक ं° तु शक्त्यावेशनधारणात्” । पुरक्षोभे तु संप्राप्ते शिष्याणां च मलक्षयम् -५०२ -५०४ ।। १२७ ।। ।। १३० ।।
english: CHAPTER THIRTEEN 121 She burns intensely with her beautiful rays in Rudra's maSÆala. Thus, by blocking the anus, one should recollect her, she who is the aggregate of the rays (of supreme consciousness) (kiraSāvalī). (121) By uniting the exhaled breath (with his own, the teacher should) purify the disciple's body. (While this happens, the disciple) shakes a little, horripilates and, when (he) reaches the Principle of Energy, (his) fist becomes firmly clenched.101 (122) Initially, once (KuSÆalinī) has been slowly raised, as before, within SunumSā by means of the flow within the Central Channel (madhyanāÆī), (the adept) should cause (her) whose form is a crooked snake to reach the navel.102 (123-124ab) By rotating in an anticlockwise direction,103 (she) is led along the Upper Path in the form of a circle (of flame like that of a whirling) firebrand, until (she reaches) the pentad of the Sky of the Heart. (124cd-125ab) Once it has been rotated four times anticlockwise,104 that energy is led up to the Supreme Abode in the Sphere of the Path of the Nameless (anāmāpathamaSÆala).105 (125cd-126ab) She is in the process of waning away above that, in the centre of the Sphere of Meru (merumaSÆala). One should make (this energy, now in the form of) pure resonance (dhvanimātrā), enter the end of the fourfold sequence.106 (126cd-127ab) One should lift up (that spiritual) energy in a pure form from the Sphere of the Root (kandamaSÆala). (Now) in the form of Sound (nāda), gradually dissolve (her) away along the Upper Path. (127cd-128ab) (This energy) arises in the centre of the Point, and in the same way, returns back (there) again. Dissolve away (that) Primary Energy there itself, along the Upper Path. In this way, the (energy of) the New Moon is variously impelled by the Command and the scriptures. (128cd-129) This is the (way) Karma matures by contemplating the penetration (āveśa) of Energy. The disciples' impurity is destroyed when (they reach the degree of Yoga) in which the body trembles (puraknobha). (130)

sanskrit: 122 कुमारिकाखण्ड: यदा प्रवर्तते देहे तदा कर्मक्षयो भवेत् । एतदाक्षेपदहन अन्तयीगे प्रतिष्ठितम् ।। १३१ ।। परानन्दस्वरूपेण भ्रमते क्रमनिर्णयम् । ५११ प्रथम” स्थूलयागस्य” सूक्ष्ममेवानुपद्धतिः ।। १३२ ।। अत ऊव १२ पूर्णभेद ३ पुनरन्यक्रमेण तु । आगमेन प्रवक्ष्यामि”“ भेदाष्टादशभेदितम् ।। १३३ ।। ऊध्वस्थानाद् बिन्दुमध्याद् रेतोरूपा समुद्धरेत् । उपक्षीणा तु या पूर्वं सा पूर्णामृतवर्षिणी ॥ १३४ ॥ ५१८ वक्रशक्तिरनन्तात्मा सौम्यरूपा विचिन्तिता । ५१९ संहारस्यागमे सृष्टिश्चिञ्चिणी परमा कला ॥। १३५ ।। आनयेच्च अनामान्ते तु क्षीरकणिकोपमाम् -५२० ५२२ । ततोऽभिषेकस्तेनैव २१ प्राक्स्वरूपेण देवता' ।। १३६ ।। हृच्चक्रे पूर्णसंस्थाने पूर्णचन्द्रसमप्रभा । एवं सञ्चिन्त्य'२३ चित्तेन' २४ स्वचक्रे तु प्रवेशयेत् ॥ १३७ ॥ ५२६ प्रहसन्ती परानन्दा द्रवते २५ साभिनन्दिता' चित्स्वरूपात्मिका—२७ शक्तिरनामानाममण्डलें तेनामृतभरा” तृप्तिः पौर्णमासी प्रवर्तते । •५३० । ५२८ ।। १३८ ॥ आगम ३० सृष्तिभेदेन एतदाज्ञाभिषेचनम् ।। १३९ ॥ गमागमेन संशोध्य पश्चात् कुर्यात् क्रमार्चनम् ।
english: CHAPTER THIRTEEN 123 Karma is destroyed when this occurs in the body. This (state of) convulsion (āknepa) and the burning away (of Karma) is well established in the inner sacrifice. (This) is the teaching concerning the Transmission (kramanirSaya). It wanders (through the body) as supreme bliss. (131-132ab) The first (division is) the gross sacrifice, the (second), according to the liturgy, is the subtle. Again, above that is the full division (pūrSabheda), which follows a different sequence. I will explain (this) division, which is (itself) divided into eighteen parts,107 according to the scripture. (132cd-133) (The adept) should elevate (the goddess) in the form of semen (retas) from the middle of the Point,108 the Upper Place. The same (Energy) that had previously waned away (now) rains down the nectar of the Full (Moon) (pūrSāmrta).109 (134) (The adept) should contemplate that crooked power (i.e. KuSÆalinī). Endless by nature, and tranquil (saumyarūpā) (she is the goddess) Ciñcinī110 who is the supreme power and the emanation (srn˜i) (that occurs when) the withdrawal (of phenomenal existence) takes place. (135) (In this state, this energy is round and white) like a drop of milk. (Contemplating it in this form, the yogi) should lead it up to end of the Nameless (anāmānte). Then the consecration takes place by that same (process).111 Once (the adept) has thus contemplated the deity in its original form, brilliant as the full (moon) in the Wheel of the Heart, the place of the Full (Moon) he should induce (her) to enter her own Wheel by means of the mind (citta). (136-137) She who is praised as supreme bliss, laughing, melts (dravate). She is the Nameless (anāmā). The energy which is consciousness (resides) in the Sphere of the Nameless (anāmamaSÆala).112 (138) (Thus, the yogi experiences) the contentment (trpti) of the night of the Full Moon that arises in this way, laden with nectar. This is the consecration of the Command, the entry (āgama) (of the breath) with the phase of emanation. (139) Once he has purified (himself) by (this process of) going and coming (gamāgama),113 (the adept) should worship the Transmission (kramārcana).114 (140ab)

sanskrit: 124 •५३२ कुमारिकाखण्ड: क्रियापादस्य ३१ प्रथमं शक्त्यावेशमिहोच्यते ' हृत्स्वरूपं खरूपं च योगभेद परापरम् । क्रमसद्भावमत्यन्तमुद्रितमाद्यपीठके ।। १४१ ।। ५३३ ।। १४० ।। इति आद्यावतार तु महाभैरवयज्ञके । मोक्षमार्गक्रम ३६ चक्रे आगमेनावतारितम् ॥ १४२ ॥ एवं देव्याक्रमं सूत्रं मानसयागसंकुलम् -५३८ ५४० । अभ्यसेत् सततं यस्तु” स योगी पाशहो भवेत् ॥ १४३ ॥ जीवन्मुक्तिधरः श्रीमान् पापं पूर्व ४२ न लिप्यते ' ५४४ ५४६ । वर्गैकेन तु अभ्यासाद्४५ द्वित्रिपञ्चभिर्वर्तते' ।। १४४ ॥ ५४७ ५४८ आत्मनः स्मरणादेव ब्रह्मघ्नः सिद्धिमाप्नुयात् । कि पुनभीवशुद्धात्मा गुर्वाज्ञाप्रतिपालकः ॥। १४५ ।। ५५० ५५२ तस्मात् सूक्ष्मशरीर तु प्राकृतं षड्विधं भवेत् । जप्त्वा लक्षाणि द्वात्रिंशद् वर्तते ३ मुद्रमण्डलें मुद्रमण्डले ४ ।। १४६ ।। भूमित्यागं पुरक्षोभं मुद्रास्फोटादिप्रत्ययम् ५५७ ५५८ ५५६ चालनावेशन “ कम्पं परसंक्रमणोऽपि वा ।। १४७ ।। प्रत्यक्षमणिमाद्यष्टौ वर्तन्ते प्रत्ययानि वै । तडित्कोटिस्वरूपेण ध्यानमात्रेण संगतिः ५६२ ५६१ ।। १४८ ।। स्तम्भनं परसैन्यानां सर्वकर्माणि कारयेत् । •५६४ अतीतानागतं किञ्चिद् वर्तमान परापरम् ।। १४९ ॥ दूरात् श्रवणविज्ञानं कौलभाषाप्रवर्तनम् ५६५ । ५५९ ५५५
english: CHAPTER THIRTEEN 125 Here it is said that the penetration of energy (śaktyāveśa) marks the beginning (part) of the ritual section part (kriyāpāda) (of the teaching). The Yoga part, superior and inferior, (corresponds to) the essential nature of the Heart and the Sky (of consciousness). It is the essence of the Transmission which is kept well sealed in the Primordial Seat. (140cd-141) This is primordial descent (of the teachings that took place) during Bhairava's great sacrifice. The sequence of the path to liberation within the Wheel has been brought down (to earth) by the scripture. (142) Such is the aphorism of the Transmission of the Goddess (devyākramasūtra). It contains (the teaching concerning) the mental sacrifice. The Yogi who practices it constantly destroys the fetters (of conditioned existence). (143) The venerable man is liberated while living and (his) prior sin does not stain (him). By practicing according to one section he abides along with two, three and five. (144) By recollecting the Self in this way, (even) a man who has killed a Brahmin gets success (siddhi). So what (to say) of one whose Self (has become) pure through these (profound states of) being and who keeps the teacher's Command? (145) Thus the subtle, natural (prākrta) body is of six kinds. Once (the adept) has repeated the mantra 3,200,000 times, he abides within the MaSÆala of Gesture. (146) And he can perform all (magical and yogic) acts, including flight (bhūmityāga), arousal of the body (puraknobha), (attainment of the) explosive power of Gesture (mudrāspho˜a) and other such signs (of accomplishment). (He attains the power of unimpeded) movement (calana), penetration (āveśa), shaking (kampa) and transference into another (body). The eight signs (of accomplishment), including the powers to become small at will (aSimā) and the rest, become directly apparent. (He can) meet (anybody at will) by means of concentration alone (that is as powerful as) a hundred million lightning bolts. (in this way he can) paralyse an opponent's armies, (know) whatever has past, is in the future and in the present as well as the supreme (transcendent) and inferior (immanent reality). (He possesses the power to) hear at a (great) distance and the (ability to speak in the secret) Kaula language (kaulabhānāpravartana). (147-150ab)

sanskrit: 126 कुमारिकाखण्ड: ·५६७ क्रमस्योध्वे५६६ क्रमाम्नाय परं सूक्ष्मं द्विधा भवेत् ॥ १५० ॥ •५६८ सूक्ष्म देहोद्भवं स्थूलं द्वाचत्वारिंशती क्रमात् । ५७० ७२ तच्छकाशाद् विनिष्क्रान्त क्रमार्थ मण्डले त्रये ।। १५१ ।। ज्ञात्वा पूर्वक्रमं योग पश्चादाज्ञाभिषेचनम् -५७४ । प्रत्ययेन यदा सिद्धिस्तदासौ क्रमपूजकः ।। १५२ ॥ इत्याद्यावतारे ७५ कादिभेदे मलक्षयाधिकारवर्णने क्रमोदयो नामानन्दः ।। १३ ॥
english: CHAPTER THIRTEEN 127 Above the Transmission (krama), the Krama tradition (kramāmnāya) is of two kinds: subtle and supreme. The subtle one is generated from the body. The gross one is the (Vidyā) of forty-two (syllables that comes) from the Krama. The teaching of the Transmission (kramārtha) has emerged from its presence into the three MaSÆalas (of the Sun, Fire and Moon). (150cd-151) The consecration of the Command occurs after one has known the Yoga that constitutes the prior Transmission. If (the adept attains) success (siddhi) along with the experience (which is the sign of attainment) (pratyaya) he is then (a true) worshiper of the Transmission. (152) This is (the thirteenth) chapter called the Description of the Authority (to bring about) the Destruction of Impurity. It belongs to the primordial descent in the division beginning with 'Ka'.

sanskrit: श्रीकौलीश उवाच' चतुर्दशानन्दः अनुज्ञातोऽभिषिक्तस्तु' वीरो वीरत्वमिच्छतः । चरेद्' विद्याव्रतं मन्त्री यथावद् विधिपूर्वतः ॥ १ ॥ तदहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि विद्याव्रतमनुत्तमम् । श्रीवक्रा उवाच' शृणु देव' प्रवक्ष्यामि विद्याया व्रतमुत्तमम् ।। २ ॥ जटी मुण्डी” शिखी वापि स्नातको ब्रह्मचारिणः । बाह्यव्रतं प्रकर्तव्यं कौलिकाचारगोपितम् ॥ ३ ॥ क्रमस्थोऽपि व्रतस्थो वा सर्वावस्थोऽपि सिद्ध्यति” । पञ्चमुद्राधरों योगी भस्मनिष्ठो” दिगम्बरः ॥ ४ ॥ चीरवल्कलधारी” वा सर्वाभरणभूषितः । २४ २६ २७ रक्तवस्त्रपटो वापि स्वेच्छावेषधरोऽपि वा ॥ ५ ॥ येन येन हि वेशेण” वर्तते साधकोत्तमः । ३२ तत् तदेव ं व्रतं प्रोक्तं इति शास्त्रस्य निश्चयः ॥ ६ ॥ ३३ ३४ यद् यदाभरणं तस्य यद् वा वदति वाचया । कर्मणा यत् कृतं तस्य क्रमाच्छादनचर्यया ।। ७ ॥ ३७ ३८ एतद् ँ बाह्यव्रतं चर्याी” अन्तव्रतमनामकम्” ।
english: CHAPTER FOURTEEN Concerning (Kaula) Conduct (caryā) The Vow of Knowledge (vidyāvrata) The Insignia, appearance, garments, ornaments and weapons of the observer of the Vow of Knowledge The venerable Kaulīśa said: 1The Hero (vīra) who has been consecrated and permitted to do so, (impelled) by the desire (to attain the highest) status of a Hero,2 should practice the Vow of Knowledge (vidyāvrata). He, the reciter of mantra, should do so properly according to the prescribed method. I want to hear of that, the most excellent Vow of Knowledge.3 (1-2ab) The venerable (goddess) Vakrā said: Listen, O god, I will explain the excellent Vow of Knowledge. (The adept may have) matted hair, a shaved head or4 a topknot, he may take baths (snātaka) or practice celibacy5 — in any condition, whether he abides in the (normal) course of practice (kramastha)6 or (the observance of this) vow, he is successful. (In any case), the external vow should be observed, that is, the concealment of Kaula practice (kaulikācāragopana). (3-4ab) (This is true also) of the yogi who bears the Five Insignias (pañcamudrā), is covered in ashes and is naked, or of who wears rags (cīra) or the bark of trees,7 or is adorned with all the ornaments, or who wears red clothes, or even one who wears whatever he pleases. (4cd-5) The teaching of the scripture is that the vow is said to be in accord with the garment the best of adepts may assume. (6) The Ornaments Whatever be his ornaments, whatever he says by way of speech8 or what is done by way of (outer) action as the conduct (caryā) (he practices), to keep the Transmission (krama) secret is the external vow and (outer) conduct (caryā). The inner vow is Nameless (anāmaka). (7-8ab)

sanskrit: 130 कुमारिकाखण्ड: जटावत् स्थापयेच्चित्तं बाह्यवृत्त्यनपेक्षणात् ” ॥ ८ ॥ मनमेकाग्रं” युञ्जीत आत्मामण्डलमभ्यसेत्” । सा जटा न जटाभार” व्रतीनां कायशोधनम् ॥। ९ ॥ आज्ञास्मरणमात्रेण ँ पतते च्छिन्नमूलवत्” । न किञ्चिदपि जानाति न शृणोति न पश्यति ॥ १० ॥ इत्याज्ञामुण्डितो मुण्डी'' न मुण्डी केशमुण्डितः । ५३ शिखा दीपोपमा यस्य विद्याहं महतारिका ॥ ११ ॥ पश्यते” याम् समाधिस्थ : सा शिखा न शिखा शिखा । भस्मीभूतः कृतः कर्म मण्डलान्तररश्मभिः ।। १२ ॥ ध्यात्वा मलक्षयं मुक्तिरेतद्” भस्मं निरामयम् । ६२ अम्बरं कथिताकाश अखण्डं शून्यमण्डलम् ॥ १३ ॥ तन्मध्ये चांकुराशक्तिस्त्रिकालभुवनालयम् । दिगम्बर ४ समाख्यातं नग्नो नैव दिगम्बरः ॥ १४ ॥ पर ब्रह्म कुलं कौल चरते ँ कुलभावितः“ । सर्वद्वन्द्वपरिक्षीणो ब्रह्मचर्यव्रती भवेत् ॥ १५ ॥
english: CHAPTER FOURTEEN 131 The Matted Hair (The adept) should establish the mind as (the ascetic keeps) matted hair, that is, out of indifference to outer activity (vrtti) (and custom), and apply the concentrated mind to the Sphere of the Self (ātmāmaSÆala)9 and to practice. This is (the real) matted hair of those observing the (true) vow; (cultivating) a load of tangled hair does not amount to the purification of the body.10 (8cd-9) The Shaved Head Merely by recollecting the Command, he falls down (onto the ground) like (a tree whose) roots have been cut. (In that state) he knows nothing at all, nor hears or sees (anything). In this way, the (true) tonsured (ascetic is one who) has been tonsured by the (goddess's) Command, not one whose hair has been shaved off.11 (10-11ab) The Topknot I, Mahātārikā, am the Vidyā of (the adept) who, established in contemplation (samādhi), sees (his) topknot (that shines brilliantly) as a lamp. That is the (true) topknot, not the topknot (made of hair at the top of the head).12 (11cd-12ab) The Ashes When Karma has been reduced to ashes by the rays (of energy) within the maSÆala and (the adept) has contemplated the destruction of impurity, this is liberation, the ash free of defect (nirāmaya).13 (12cd-13ab) The Nakedness The (true) sky (ambara) is said to be Space (ākāśa), which is the Unbroken Circle of the Void. In the centre of that is the energy which is the Sprout (a‰kurāśakti) (of the Command). (This), the abode of the world of the three times, is said to be (the truly) naked (state) (digambara). One who (simply) wears no clothes (nagna) is not (truly) naked (digambara).14 (13cd-14) The Vow of Celibacy One who observes the vow of celibacy (brahmacarya) is free of all duality. Sanctified (bhāvita) by Kula (Śiva's power) he is engaged (carate) (in the realisation of) the Supreme Brahman,15 Kula and Kaula (the transformation of Kula). (15)

sanskrit: 132 कुमारिकाखण्डः सुस्निग्ध ं यत् पर” किञ्चित् कदम्बाधारनिर्मलम् । •७४ तं पीत्वा भवते शुद्धिः स्नानमेतन्न ँ चान्यथा ।। १६ ।। चम चिञ्चिणी मध्ये पुरे पुरे” विभेदितम् । तत्रोच्चारगतिर्ज्ञेया रमणी वीरसंज्ञया ॥ १७ ॥ बाह्यक्रमविनिर्मुक्ता” धारा चामृतवर्षिणी । ८५ ॥ १८ ॥ समाधिस्थो भवेद्” योगी अम्बराम्बरमम्बर: वल्कल“ तत् समाख्यातं न चर्म वल्कल भवेत्“ । •८७ क्रमभेदेन तत्त्वानि ये स्थिता: स्थानविग्रहे ॥ १९ ॥ एतदाभरणं प्रोक्तं न हेमाभरणं भवेत् । कुलं सर्वमुखं ज्ञात्वा सर्वाभरणमुच्यते ।। २० ।। ९२ विद्या नाम परा शक्तिर्द्विभिर्भेदैव्यवस्थिता । ९६ चिच्छक्तिरिति¨ सिद्धिः स्यात् सावणी वर्णगा शुभा ।। २१ ।। ९७
english: CHAPTER FOURTEEN 133 The Bathing Supreme, ineffable (kiñcit) and very pleasant (susnigdha), its foundation the Kadamba Tree, it is pure. Having drunk this, (the yogi) is purified. This is (true) bathing (that purifies the soul) and (it is done only in this and in) no other way.16 (16) The Chowrie The chowrie (camara) is (the goddess) Ciñcinī in the centre and is distributed in each sphere of existence (pure pure or ‘in each body’). One should know that the upward movement (of KuSÆalinī) (uccāragati) (takes place) there. (This movement is the energy called) RamaSī (the Playful Lady) (who sports with the one) called the Hero. Free of outer processes, it is (the inner) stream (dhārā) (of consciousness) and rains down a shower of nectar.17 (17-18ab) The Bark Clothing The Yogi absorbed in contemplation (samādhi) (wears the) garment (ambara) that is the Emptiness of the Void (of the Absolute) (ambarāmbara). That is said to be (the ascetic's) clothing made of bark. The skin (of a tree) is not (true) bark clothing. (18cd-19ab) The Ornaments (The ascetic's true) ornament is said to be the principles (of existence) that abide within the form of (their respective) locations (in the body) (sthānavigraha) in accord with the division of the sequence (of their manifestation) (kramabheda). (Mere) gold is (not the ascetic's true) ornament. Once one knows Kula (the omnipresent power of the deity), everything is said to be an ornament. (19cd-20) The Vow of Knowledge and the Vidyā 18Vidyā is the supreme power and abides twofold. (When the adept realises that she is) the power of consciousness, (he achieves) success. Devoid of letters (avarSā), auspicious, she (the power of consciousness) is present in (every) letter.19 (21)

sanskrit: 134 कुमारिकाखण्डः १०१ १०४ विद्यामार्गे” चरेद् यस्तु” शास्त्रदृष्टेन कर्मणा ध्यान पूजा जपो होम: समयाचरणं तथा ' एतद् विद्याव्रत प्रोक्तं बाह्यव्रतमनुत्तमम् । । ।। २२ ।। विद्या ज्ञेया'' तु“ नाभिस्था चरते द्वादशान्तगा ।। २३ ।। व्रतस्थानेषु”” सर्वेषु तेन विद्याव्रत महत्४ । ११५ । ब्रह्मा विष्णुश्च रुद्रश्च ईश्वरश्च सदाशिव: ।। २४ ।। एतें स्थाना १७ व्रतस्यैव यत्र सा रमते ९ परा । ११६ १२० -१२१ तं ज्ञात्वा परमं स्थान चीर्णविद्याव्रतो २ हि सः १२५ १२३ विद्या नामाक्षरा पंक्ति: पंक्तिश्चक्रे ह्यधोमुखी । तासा’२७ रक्तव्रतस्थं तु अज्ञानपटच्छेदकम् ।। २६ ॥ अन्तरङ्गे पटं रक्तं न बाह्ये पटरक्तकम्' १३० १२९ । रक्तपटपरीधान: षट्प्रकारप्रबोधकः ।। २७ ।। कौलिकव्रतसंज्ञेय न बाह्यव्रतिनो भवेत् । १३४ ।। २८ ।। पञ्चमुद्राधरो देव:३३ पञ्चकारणकं ततः भूषितो३५ हृदि संतिष्ठेत् पञ्चमुद्राधरः शिवः' १३८ १३९ १३६ । एतैस्तु भूषितो मन्त्री पर्यटेत् क्षेत्रमाश्रितः १४१ ।। २५ ।। ।। २९ ।। श्मशाने कानने कूपे उद्याने देवकुले शुभे । शून्ये राजगृहे मन्त्री पर्वताग्रे ४५ चतुष्पथे ॥ ३० ॥ त्रिपथे ग्रामरथ्यासु महोदधितटेऽथवा ' । १४७ १४८ नदीसंगमतीरे वा एकवृक्षेऽथवानघ ।। ३१ ।। एकलिङ्गेऽथवा षण्डे क्षेत्रेष्वष्टेषु च क्रमात् । १५२ १५३
english: CHAPTER FOURTEEN 135 Meditation, worship, the repetition of mantra, the fire sacrifice and the observance of the Rule (samayācaraSa) — this is said to be the Vow of Knowledge (for one) who walks on the Path of Knowledge by means of action, in accord with scripture. (But) the external vow is not the best. (22-23ab) One should know the Vidyā located in the navel.20 It moves (and is also) present at the End of the Twelve (dvādaśāntagā). (Indeed, it is present) in all the sites (where the) vow (is observed). Thus the Vow of Knowledge is great. (23cd-24ab) Brahmā, VinSu, Rudra, Īśvara and Sadāśiva: these are the sites of the Vow where the Supreme (Goddess — Parā) sports.21 Once that supreme place is known, (the adept) has observed the Vow of Knowledge well. (24cd-25) The Red Clothing The Vidyā is the row of letters (aknara). It is the row (of letters) facing downwards within the Wheel.22 The one who is established in the vow (of wearing) red cuts through the cloth of ignorance of these (letters). The red cloth is within (antara‰ga). The (true) red cloth is not outside. The one who wears (such) red clothes awakens the sixfold (energy).23 This is called the Kaulika Vow. It is not (the vow) of one who performs external vows. (26-28ab) The god dons the Five Insignia (mudrā) and so is (himself) the fivefold cause. May Śiva, adorned and wearing the Five Insignia24 abide in the heart! (28cd-29ab) Adorned with them, the reciter of mantra, taking (the sacred) field (knetra) (of the body25 as his) refuge, should wander in a cremation ground, forest, (near a) well (or) garden. The reciter of mantra (should go) to an auspicious temple, an empty palace, the peak of a mountain, a crossing of four roads or one of three. (He should wonder) on village roads, the seashore, the bank of the confluence of rivers or, O sinless one, (in a desert where there is only) a solitary tree or (where there is just) a single Li‰ga or in a thicket (naSÆa) or in the eight sacred fields in due order.26 (29cd-32ab)

sanskrit: 136 कुमारिकाखण्डः १५७ प्रयागा४ वरुणा कोल्ला अट्टहासा जयन्तिका ।। ३२ ।। १६० चरित्रैकाम्रक५८ चैव देवीकोट्ट तथाष्टमम् । एतेषु पर्यटेन्मन्त्री योगिनीसिद्धिमिच्छतः १६२ । ॥ ३३ ॥ खट्वाङ्गधारिणो¨३ मौनी वेगात् पर्यटते सदा । ९६७ डमरु पाशखड्ग वा त्रिशूल खेटकं तथा ।। ३४ ।। १७० -१७१ ९७२ १७३ नाराच कर्तरी चक्र अंकुशं मुशल धनुः । १७४ १७५ १७६ गदा कट्टारिका शक्तिस्तथा दण्डकमण्डलुम् ।। ३५ ।। •१७७ १७८ १७९ एव ते चायुधा: श्रेष्ठाश्चर्याीकालेऽपि धारयेत् । पञ्चदैवसिक कार्य अस्त्रसंख्या व्रतोत्तमा ।। ३६ ।। द्वादशाह ४ चरेन्मन्त्री पक्षमासादितोऽपि वा ८५ । १९० षण्मासमथवाब्द८६ वा द्विरब्द त्रीणि एव वा ।। ३७ ।। द्वादशाब्द १२ चरेन्मन्त्री ब्रह्महा अपि ४ सिद्ध्यति १९७ १९५ । अन्तरङ्गे विशुद्धात्मा पारम्पर्यप्रबोधक: ।। ३८ ।। अचिरात्”“ सिद्धिभागीं”” स्यात् पारम्पर्येण मुच्यते । २०१ २०४ अब्दैकेन तु तु देवेश मण्डलीकै : २०३ प्रपूज्यते ।। ३९ ।। अन्तःपुरवरैः सार्धं राजात्मा सपरिवरः २०५ । २०६ ।। ४० ।। वशं यान्ति न संदेहो उत्तमाधममध्यमाः २०८ द्विरब्दैर्यक्षकन्याश्च कामविह्वललोचनाः । आगच्छन्ति” पुरे तस्य प्राणान् मुञ्चन्ति तत्क्षणात् ।। ४१ ।। २१३ त्रिरब्दैः”° सप्तपाताला ११ ये च१२ देवादिकन्यकाः । वशं यान्ति”४ मदोन्मत्ता १५ मदविभ्रान्तलोचनाः ।। ४२ ।।
english: CHAPTER FOURTEEN 137 The reciter of mantra, (impelled) by the desire to (attain) the accomplishment (siddhi) of the Yoginīs, should wander in these (places), namely: Prayāgā,27 VaruSā, Kollā, A˜˜ahāsā,28 Jayantikā, Caritra, Ekāmraka and Devīko˜˜a,29 the eighth. (32cd-33) Carrying an ascetic's staff (kha˜vāSga), (the adept who) observes silence (maunin), (fuelled) by (his spiritual) impetus (vega), should wander constantly. A hand-drum (Æamaru) or a noose (pāśa) and sword, trident, shield (khe˜aka), an arrow, a dagger (kartarī), discus (cakra), a goad, a pestle, a bow, a mace, a flat knife (ka˜˜ārikā), a javelin, and a stick and waterpot (kamaSÆalu) — these (O god) are your finest weapons. (The adept) should carry them also in the course of (his Kaula) practice (caryā).30 (34-36ab) The Duration of the Observance and its Fruits (The vow) should be observed (kārya) for five days. Contemplation of the weapons (astrasaˆkhyā)31 is the most excellent vow. The reciter of mantra can practice for twelve days, a lunar fortnight or a month. (Again), the reciter of mantra may practice for six months or a year, two years, three or twelve. (In this way) even (a man) who has murdered a Brahmin achieves success. (36cd-38ab) He who is inwardly a pure soul and awakens (others to the teachings transmitted through the) lineage is soon successful and is freed (by the teaching transmitted through) the lineage. O lord of the gods, in one year, (a king) gains the respect (prapūjyate) of (his) vassals.32 (38cd-39) The king with his entourage and the chosen who dwell in the inner apartments (of his palace), whether the best, middling or lowest, (all) certainly come under (the adept's) control.33 (40) With two years (practice), the damsels (kanyā) of the Yaknas, their eyes distraught with passion, come to his dwelling (pura) and give up (their) lives (prāSa) that instant (due to the intensity of their desire). (41) With three years (of practice), the young women of the gods and the others who (dwell in) the seven lower worlds, mad with passion, their eyes distraught with passion, come under (the adept's) control.34 (42)

english: CHAPTER FOURTEEN 139 (Women) endowed with eternal youth who walk (swaying with passion) like elephants in rut, (so beautiful that) they arouse (even) the best of adepts, give up (their) lives (prāSa) that instant (due to the intensity of their desire). (43) In four, five and six years, he attains the world of Brahmā and the rest.35 O fair one, in the seventh year those beings who reside in (the world of) Rudra achieve success on behalf of (him), the best of adepts. This is the certain conclusion of the scripture. (44-45ab) In the eighth year (he attains the one) called Īśvara and in the ninth (the one called) Sadāśiva. (45cd) In the tenth (year), having become the abode of the Vidyā, he is great and sports in the Void (of ultimate reality). With eleven (years of practice), O Great God, he attains Rudra's nature. (45cd-46) With twelve (years of practice), he is endowed with the qualities (of a perfect yogi) and possesses the (eight yogic powers, namely) the power to become small at will (aSimā) and the others. The reciter of mantra who practices the Kramavidyā (kramavidyādhara)36 attains the plane of the Skyfarer. (47) (This) imperishable and unconquerable yogi, omnipresent and auspicious, (engages in) play. Thus, O sinless one, the fruit of (this) vow has been told to you. (48) The Places to Observe the Vow I will now explained the path of Yoga in the form of the hermitages and the sacred places (sthāna) and, in due order, the purification of the body (that takes place by Kaula) practice (caryā). (49) The Cremation Ground The Cremation Ground is the House (grha). The House is said to be the body. (The adept), tireless, wanders (there), his mind absorbed in the Cremation Ground.37 (50)

english: CHAPTER FOURTEEN 141 The Forest Ka is said to be the body. At its extremity are the two eyes (nayana). By means of them, the Self sees (all that is made of) Speech along with the moving and immobile (universe) and so it is said to be the ‘forest’ (kānana) established within the body.38 (51-52ab) The Well It is taught that the well is the mind (manas)39 which produces many thoughts (saˆkalpa). The owner of the field (of the body) (knetrin) goes there to the foundation (of all things) and so is it known as the Well.40 (52cd-53ab) The Garden (When) the mind is located in the navel, it is active and contemplates (the higher principles) within all people. Once that plane has been reached, it leads (nayati) (upwards) and so is called the garden (udyāna). O god, that is the immortal (amrta) plane within the Void (nabhas) (of the Supreme Principle).41 (53cd-54) The Temple The yogi wonders within Kula in the fetters of Dharma and Adharma. This is why, O god, the embodied soul (dehin) is always said to be the temple (devakula).42 (55) The King and his Palace It is said that the king is the Self.43 His mind is conjoined with the principles (of phenomenal existence) and, replete with the qualities of sound and the other (sensations), is adorned with the essence (saˆdoha) of the principles (of existence). And thereby he performs action (karma) and moves along with that same (action). (56-57ab) If the mind is intent (yukta) on the Transmental state (unmanatva), it is (then) said to be the Void (śūnya). Thus, O dear one, the Void is the King's Palace, perpetually in the state Beyond Mind.44 (57cd-58ab)

english: CHAPTER FOURTEEN 143 The Mountain Peak 45The mountain is the Teacher's Mouth.46 (The votary) should catch hold of its peak. He abides there on the mountain peak and so wanders everywhere.47 (58cd-59ab) The Crossing of Four Roads Now I will explain the crossing of four roads. Vāmā, Jyen˜hā and Raudrikā along with Ambikā is the path (a˜ana) of the individual soul (pudgala), which is said to be the crossing of the four roads. This is said to be the path (patha).48 (59cd-60) The Triple Path O Mahādeva, the path is said to be the three channels (nāÆī), IÆā and the rest.49 (The vital breath) moves, coming and going constantly along the triple path. He who does (this), established in oneness on the triple path, is successful.50 (61-62ab) The Village The village (grāma) is the (maSÆala) (made of) six parts (na˜prakāra). The first village is the sphere (golaka) (in the middle of the maSÆala). It is the abode of all living beings and is (the union of opposites), pleasure and pain, supreme (transcendence) and inferior (immanence).51 (62cd-63ab) The Highway The lord of the universe who (takes as his) support the Highway (rathya), travels up and down. Thus, the highway is the channel (nāÆī) of the Self that begins with (the Cavity of) Brahmā.52 (63cd-64ab) The Shore of the Ocean The shore is said to be the bank (of the ocean). It is called Śiva's utterance (śivoccāra). The cessation of suffering, beyond (the stages of) merger, it is the shore that (by implication) denotes the sea. The one who moves (on it) is the Śiva, the pervasive God who is the supreme cause (of all things). The reciter of mantra always stands (there on the bank) and (it is there), at the conclusion (of his) practice (caryā), that (Śiva) is revealed.53 (64cd-66ab)

english: CHAPTER FOURTEEN 145 The River The supreme KuSÆalinī is the flow of Unstruck Sound (asvarā) that resounds (in all the spheres of reality). This is the river in the form of Yoga that flows constantly through the Ocean of the Sky (of the Supreme Principle).54 (66cd-67ab) The Confluence The confluence is conjoined with the supreme (power) and is revealed at the end of the Transmental. That confluence has been explained which is said to be that of a river.55 (67cd-68ab) The Bank of the River (Śiva) the foundation (ādhāra) (of existence), both supreme (transcendent) and inferior (immanent, conjoined) in every way with (his own) inherent (energy) (samavāyinī) who, pervasive, governs (the universe) by means of that (power), is said to be the bank of the river.56 (68cd-69ab) The Solitary Tree There is one tree, O god, and (only) one supreme energy, which is threefold. One (of the three aspects) is (energy) born of the senses, (another is) the channel (nāÆī) and (the third one) that has been revealed is called the Point. (69cd-70ab) She has dissolved away into the supreme abode, which is fautless and beyond mind (amanaska). So, O god, I have explained the solitary tree of those who recite mantra.57 (70cd-71ab) The Solitary Li‰ga There is only one Supreme Principle. It is the supreme nectar (of immortality) and its form a Li‰ga. He (who wears it) should wander tirelessly, night and day again and again. O god, this is the solitary Li‰ga.58 (71cd-72abc)

english: CHAPTER FOURTEEN 147 The Bunch of Flowers (naSÆa) Next comes the bunch.59 The Heart is said to be (like) a lake (saras) that has an eight-petalled (lotus). O lord of gods, the sun, by (its) dawning, causes it to blossom. (72d-73) The lotus of the Heart is attended by (the consciousness) merged in the individual soul (pudgala). The Transmental power (manonmanī), the seed of energy60 called Haˆsa (the Gander),61 sports there. In the scripture that is called the bunch. (74-75a) The Eight Sacred Fields Next (I will explain) the group of eight fields. The field is the supreme and tranquil body endowed with (all) the principles (of existence). The knower of the field moves around there established in the condition (gati) of the group of eight (sacred) sites. Thus, O lord of the gods, this is said to be the group of eight sacred fields.62 (75bcd-76) The sacred seats (pī˜ha) are indeed sacred fields and the sacred fields are sacred seats (arranged) in due order.63 (Their) names, synonyms and types are various in (differing places in) the goddess’s scripture64. (77) Prayāga is located in the navel. VaruSā is in the locus of the heart. Kollagirya65 is in the throat and A˜˜ahāsa, in the palate. The (place) called Jayantī is in the place of the Point (between the eyes) and Caritraka in that called the Sound. Those who have realised the Self should know that Ekāmra is in the Place of Power (śaktisthāna). Similarly, the eighth, Ko˜ivarna, is said to be in the Teacher's Mouth.66 (78-80ab) These places (sthāna) I have mentioned are within the inner Self (adhyātma) and are grounded in the individual soul. The eternal (Self), residing in the Wheel of the Heart, wanders constantly within them.67 (80-81ab) As long as he does not attain the sacred seat which is the inner teaching (adhyātmanirSaya)68, how can he achieve success (siddhi) even if he wanders (throughout) the triple universe? (81cd-82ab)

english: CHAPTER FOURTEEN 149 (Both) the inner and outer aspects have an inner and outer condition.69 The external sacred seats have been revealed in order to (instil) devotion in the (common) people. (82cd-83ab) Just as (the yogi) perceives the pure inner aspect with the mind, O beloved, in the same way he sees the subtle rays (of the light of the Supreme Principle) that are outside70 and they bestow union (melaka), the sacrificial pap (caru) or the liberated state (apāśavīvidhi).71 They bestow the (teachings of the) tradition and or else explain the (location of each sacred) place (sthāna).72 (83cd-85ab) O god, they do not bestow a vision (darśana) (of themselves) by means of the mind anywhere if one wanders on the earth with an impure state (of being). (85cd-86ab) Although he sees, he sees not; although (reality is) perceivable, it is not perceived. He cannot know (the rays of consciousness which are) the goddesses of various kinds.73 (86cd-87ab) It is taught that their power is the Vidyā, which is the grace they have (to give),74 whether in a town, village or forest, city or crossroad, peasant's hut, meeting ground (saˆdoha), sacred seat, field, grove, garden, small grove or in (any one of the) aforementioned (places). (Indeed), the rays of consciousness (jñāna) arise in every single place. (87cd-89) O fair-hipped one, innumerable, (they are present) in the covering of the earth, so too in water, fire, wind and space. (90) They arise in many ways in accord with the particular (nature of) the sacred seat of which they take their support. Ever devoted to eating and drinking, (the goddesses of the rays of consciousness) play even amongst those of the lowest castes. (91) And so, O god, I have talked of the sacred seats according to their external nature. The house of Veśyā (the Prostitute) is called Prayāga. Know that VaruSā75 (also spelt VaraSā) (corresponds to) ŚuSÆinī (the Barmaid)76, Kaivartī (the Fisherwoman) is in Kaullagiri,77 Kha˜˜ikī (the Butcherwoman) is in A˜˜ahāsa, KaSÆukī (the Barberwoman) is said to be in Jayantī, similarly, Rajakī (the Washerwoman) is in Caritra. The (goddess of) Ekāmra is Śilpī78 (the Sculpteress) while Kośa˜ī79 is in Deviko˜˜a.80 (92-94ab)

sanskrit: 150 कुमारिकाखण्ड: ५४४ ज्ञातव्याश्चुम्बकेनैव भुक्तिमुक्तिफलार्थिभि:' ५४८ ५४५ ॥ ९४ ॥ पर्यटेदेषु स्थानेषु पूजनीयाः सदा बुधैः । भक्षभोज्यान्नपानैस्तु” तर्पयेन्मन्त्रवित्“ सदा ॥ ९५ ॥ -५५२ -५५१ एतेषु संस्थितिस्तासां “३ योगिन्यस्त्वप्रमेयतः -५५७ ५५४ । भवन्ति च न संदेहो वरदा: साधकस्य तु ॥ ९६ ॥ तर्पिता:““ पूजिता देव्यः साधकस्य ददन्ति हि । ५६२ ५६३ ५६४ षण्मासाद्`‍ युक्तमार्गस्य समयव्रतपालनात्' ।। ९७ ।। ५६८ ५६९ ५६६ अथान्य५ संप्रवक्ष्यामि संक्षेपाच्छास्त्रवादिनाम् । आध्यात्मिक बहिश्चैव यथा जानन्ति तत्त्वतः तथा ते कथयिष्यामि शृणुष्वायतलोचन—७२ । ५७४ ५७० ।। ९८ ।। ५७५ आध्यात्म७३ कुरुते बाह्यं व्रतं चर्या च साधनाम् ।। ९९ ।। ५७७ एवं कृते भवेत् सिद्धिः सत्यमेव न संशयः ०५८२ ५७९ -५८३ । खट्वाङ्गः कथयिष्यामि अनुग्राह्यं वरानन ।। १०० ।। आपादतलमूर्धन्तं यथा भवति तच्छृणु । -५८८ -५८५ ५८६ सर्वाङ्गेषु शिराद्येषु अङ्गप्रत्यङ्गसन्धिषु ।। १०१ ।। खण्डते येन देवेश खट्वाङ्गस्तेन उच्यते । ५८९ ५९२ ५७६
english: CHAPTER FOURTEEN 151 Those who seek the fruit of worldly enjoyment (bhukti) and liberation should know these (goddesses) by means of a kiss (cumbaka).81 (94cd) One should wander in these places.82 The wise should worship (the goddesses there) constantly. The knower of mantra should always make offerings (to them) with good food, boiled rice (anna) and drink. (95) And these Yoginīs that reside in these (places) certainly bestow gifts beyond measure to the adept. By maintaining the Vow of the Rule of the aforementioned path, the goddesses, worshipped and lustrated, give the adept (their gifts) within six months. (96-97) The Inner Attributes of the Ascetic 83Now I will explain something else in brief concerning the inner and outer (reality) of the knowers of the scripture. I will tell you (this) as (the wise) know it in truth. Listen, O long-eyed one. (98-99ab) One who has thus internalized the external vow, (Kula) conduct (caryā) and (spiritual) discipline (sādhanā), (achieves) success (siddhi). O god, (this is) the truth, without a doubt. (99cd-100ab) The Ascetic’s Staff O fair-faced one, I will explain (to you) the ascetic's staff (kha˜vāSga) which should be taken up84 (that extends) from the soles of the feet up to the head. Listen to how it is. (100cd-101ab) O lord of the gods, it is called the ascetic's staff (kha˜vāSga) because it is that by means of which (the adept) pierces through (khaSÆate)85 all the limbs (of the body), beginning with the head, within the junctures between the limbs, major and minor.86 (101cd-102ab)

english: CHAPTER FOURTEEN 153 The Vow of Silence One should know that the ascetic who observes a vow of silence (maunī) is so called because, sanctified (subhāvita) by all the scriptures, he wanders constantly, by means of (his) silence, intent on the secret (and profound reality), in the Heart.87 (102cd-103ab) The Wandering Life The wandering (a˜ana) of the individual soul (pudgala) is said to be impetus (vega) because it is due to (his) impetus that he wanders, tireless, in the body again and again.88 (103cd-104ab) The Hand Drum Now, in due order, I will explain the hand drum (Æamaruka) as it truly is. The Nameless (Anāmā)89 is the supreme, subtle energy that transports (the flow) of the nectar of immortality (amrta). The Self wanders90 within91 it and (so) emits Sound within the Drop (of nectar). (104cd-105) If the Self, established in emission (visargastha), moves along the three paths, (he experiences) the hand drum there within (the reality) devoid of mind (amanaska) and perfect (nirāmaya).92 (106) The Fetter Located in the navel is the (goddess) KuSÆalī who is Māyā (by which) all the fettered souls devoid of devotion in the three worlds are fettered. This is called the fetter.93 (107-108a) The Sword Now listen to (what is meant by) the sword (khaÆga). Established in the Void (kha), Mohanī cuts the fetters to pieces with the weapon of emission (visarga). O Great God, it is that by virtue of which this imperishable energy has emerged within the sword and has attained (gatā) union with the Brahman in the middle of (Śiva) the Skyfarer (khaga) within sword. Thus, O leader of the gods, (this) weapon is called the sword.94 (108bcd-110ab)

sanskrit: 154 ६४६ कुमारिकाखण्ड: ६४७ एका एव पराशक्तिस्त्रिपथाकृतिमण्डलें ।। ११० ।। वामा ज्येष्ठा तथा रौद्री इच्छाज्ञानक्रियात्मिका ४९ । ६५१ ६५२ त्रिशूल त्रिपथं ख्यात त्रिशक्तितनुमण्डितम् ।। १११ ।। खरूपा६५३ व्योमगा६५४ शान्ता निर्मला ६५५ अटते सदा ६६० ६५६ । खेटक ६५७ तेन १५८ नाम १५९ तु द्वादशान्ते व्यवस्थितम् ।। ११२ ।। ६६३ नाराच६६१ शक्तिरुच्चार १६२ करणात्माव्यवस्थितम् ६६६ । बोधयति१६४ निरोधिन्या करणान् पञ्च एव हि ।। ११३ ।। तेन नाराचमाख्यात ६७ पर्यायेण तु सुन्दर । ६६८ ६६९ ६७१ ६७२ कर्तरी ज्ञानशक्तिस्तु येन पाशान् छिनत्त्यसौं ।। ११४ ।। सा कला परमा सूक्ष्मा मन्त्राणां बोधनी ६७३ कर्तरी कर्तृरूपेण¨५ ज्ञातव्या साधकेन तु ६७७ ६७८ परा । ।। ११५ ॥ चरते ७६ द्वादशान्ते तु क्रमात् तत्त्वानि मुञ्चति । ६७९ चक्रवद् भ्रमते नित्यं अंकुशस्था परापरा ।। ११६ ।। ६८१ अन्तरङ्गगता देव बहिरङ्गेन संस्थिता । १८४ ६८५ कुरुते८२ सतत १८३ चेष्टा आसने ५ शयने तथा ।। ११७ ।। ६८७ ६८८ धावनं वल्लन८६ रोधं अकुञ्चनप्रसारणम् ।
english: CHAPTER FOURTEEN 155 The Trident The Supreme Energy is only one in the maSÆala whose form is the triple path (tripathākrti).95 (She is equally) Vāmā, Jyen˜hā and Raudrī and (her) nature is will, knowledge and action. The Trident is called the triple path, adorned with the body of the Triple Energy (triśakti).96 (110cd-111) The Shield (This) energy whose form is the Void (kha), established in the Void (kha), tranquil and pure, wanders (a˜ate) constantly (within it). Thus (it is called) the shield (khe˜aka) established at the End of the Twelve (above the head) (dvādaśānta).97 (112) The Arrow The arrow is the upward movement of energy established in the essential nature of the (five) causes. It pierces through (vedhayati) the Five Causes by means of Nirodhinī (the Obstructress). Thus, O handsome one, it is also called the arrow (nārāca).98 (113-114ab) The Knife The knife is the power of knowledge that severs the fetters. It is the supreme and subtle energy, the supreme awakener (bodhanī) of mantras. The adept should know the knife (kartarī) to be the agent. It moves (up) to the End of the Twelve and (as it does so) progressively frees the three Transmissions.99 (114cd-116ab) The Goad The (energy) in the goad, which is both supreme (transcendent) and inferior (immanent), rotates constantly like a wheel. O god, inwardly present, she is well established externally.100 Constantly active, both on the seat and in the bed, (the energy) runs, rolls, blocks, contracts and expands.101 (116cd-118ab)

sanskrit: 156 कुमारिकाखण्ड: ६८९ मुषलत्वे स्थितो नादो ९० रेखाकारोध्वग: १९९ प्रिय ६९४ ६९२ तं भित्त्वा९३ गमनं चोवे मुषलाख्यं सदाशिवम् ।। ११८ ।। ६९५ । धनुर्लक्ष्यमनाख्य९६ तु येन ९७ वेधयते परम् ।। ११९ ।। ७०० ७०१ आपूर्य” सविसर्गेण परेण मनचक्षुषा । खर्परे करणेनैव' पर्यटेच्च अधोमुखी ऋतुद्वयविशुद्धेन कारणान्तर्गतेन तु । अनेन करणान्तेन ज्ञेया कट्टारिका परा ७०९ ॥ १२० ॥ ।। ।। १२१ ।। ७११ प्राप्नोति तत्त्वसायोज्य गदया च त्रिलोचन ७१५ ७१२ गता ह्येका ३ पर४ रन्ध्रं ददते चामृतं शुभम् गतास्ते न निवर्तन्ते ये गता गदया सह । ७१६ । ॥ १२२ ॥ ७२० शक्तिः शक्तिमतोरैक्य आत्मा चालयते सदा ।। १२३ ॥ तद् भवेद् योगसिद्धिस्तु शक्तिर्नादान्तरेऽधिप २२ । ७२४ ७२५ दण्डवदृजुरेखा तु गता सा पदमव्ययम् ।। १२४ ।। तेन २६ मार्गेण गन्तव्य २७ दण्डाकारे २८ व्यवस्थितम् २९ । ३० TM
english: CHAPTER FOURTEEN 157 The Pestle O beloved, Sound (nāda) is in the pestle’s state. The form of a straight line, it moves upwards. Once broken through that, it travels upwards. (Thus) Sadāśiva is (the reality) called 'the pestle'.102 (118cd-119ab) The Bow The (arrow shot by the) bow pierces the target, the Supreme (reality), the Inexplicable (anākhya) once filled by the supreme eye of the mind and with emission.103 (119cd-120ab) The Flat Knife104 Facing downwards, (KuSÆalinī) moves through (parya˜et) the skull as the instrument (of mantra) present within the (five) causes and purified by the two seasons. O god, one should know the supreme sacrificial knife by means of this (energy) at the end of the (five) causes.105 (121) The Mace O three-eyed one, (the adept) attains conjunction with the (Supreme) Principle by means of the mace (gadā).106 When the one supreme (energy) has reached (gatā) the Cavity (at the top of the head), it bestows auspicious nectar.107 Those who have gone with the mace do not return.108 (122-123ab) The Javelin The oneness of power (śakti — the javelin) and its possessor causes the Self to operate constantly. O lord, that is the accomplishment of Yoga (yogasiddhi), namely, the energy (śakti) within Sound.109 (123cd-124ab) The Stick (KuSÆalinī) the Straight Line, like a stick, has reached the imperishable plane. Established (in that energy whose) form is a stick, one should travel by that path.110 (124cd-125ab)

sanskrit: 158 कुमारिकाखण्डः ७३२ कं शरीरमिति” ख्यातमण्डाकारं व्यवस्थितम् ॥ १२५ ॥ ७३३ तत्राध्वा तु वरारोह शोधनीयो मनीषिभिः । ७३८ कुण्डला या परा शुद्धा सर्वशुद्धा गतात्मनि ।। १२६ ।। तेनेदं च मया प्रोक्त ९ कमण्डलु परं स्मृतम् । ७४२ ७४३ ७४० ७४१ एवं ते चायुधाः सूक्ष्माः पर्यीयैः बहुभिः पदैः ७४७ कथितं तु मया सर्व परापरं विभागशः ७४९ ७५० ७४५ ७४६ ।। १२७ ।। -७५४ बाह्यान्ते ५१ कथयिष्यामि २ दूतीना लक्षणम् परम् ं ।। १२८ ।। विचारं चैव५५ दूतीनां अपरं संप्रगीयते ७५७ - ७५८ ७५६ । माता च दुहिता भग्नी सहा अन्त्यजा तथा ५९ ।। १२९ ॥ रजकी चर्मकारी च मातङ्गी चाग्रजन्मनी M ७६० । ७६२ कौलिनी चक्रलोला ११ च मैथुनी नारसिंहकी ।। १३० ।। •७६३ ७६५ आचार मातृभिर्योनौ कथितं तु सुरार्चित । अन्त्यजानां द्विजानां च एकत्र चरुभोजनम् ।। १३१ ।। ७६६ ७६८ कर्तव्यं साधकेनैव यदीच्छेत् सिद्धिमुत्तमाम् । इत्याद्यावतारे महामन्थानभैरवयज्ञे ९ अन्वये सप्तकोटिप्रमाणे मेरुमार्गविनिर्गते लक्षपादाधिके आद्यपीठावतारिते विद्यापीठमार्गे विमलषट्कनिर्णये कादिभेदे आज्ञापारमेश्वरे स्वामिनीमते श्रीचतुर्विंशतिसहस्रसंहिताया अव्वाक्रमभाषिते चर्याधिकारो नामानन्दः ॥ १४ ॥
english: CHAPTER FOURTEEN 159 The Waterpot ‘Ka’ is said to be the body and it is established in the form of an ornament (maSÆākāra).111 O fair-hipped one, the wise should purify the Path here. (KuSÆalinī) the Coiled One (kuSÆalā) is supreme and pure. That (energy) pure in every way is present within the Self.112 Thus, I have explained this, the waterpot (kamaSÆalu) which is said to be supreme.113 (125cd-127ab) Such are your subtle attributes (āyudha) named in many ways.114 I have explained everything both supreme and inferior, part by part.115 (127) The Kaula Consorts I will (now) explain the supreme characteristic of the Consorts (dūtī) in (both) the internal and external (domain). (Now) here is another teaching (vicāra) (this time) concerning the consorts (dūtī). (128) (The consorts are the adept’s) mother (mātr), daughter (duhitr), sister (bhaginī) and twin sister (sahajā).116 (The consort may also be) a woman of the lowest (caste) (antyajā), a washerwoman (rajakī), a leather worker (carmakārī), a sweeperwoman (mātaSgī), a first-born woman (agrajanmanī), Kaulinī, Cakralolā (Swung in the Wheel), Maithunī and Nārasiˆhakī. (Thus), O adored by the gods, the Conduct in the Yoni (yoni) with the Mothers has been explained. (129-130) The adept who desires the most excellent accomplishment (siddhi) should always eat the sacrificial pap (caru) together with those who belong to the lowest caste (as well as) the twice-born.117 (131cd-2ab) This is the (fourteenth) chapter called Concerning (Kaula) Conduct (caryā). It belongs to the primordial descent into the great sacrifice of the Churning Bhairava in the tradition (anvaya) that consists of seventy million (verses) that has emerged on the Path of Meru and (extends) for more than a hundred thousand quarter (verses). It has been brought (down to earth) into the first sacred seat along the path of the Seat of Knowledge (vidyāpī˜ha). It is the ultimate purport of the Pure Six Thousand (verses vimalana˜ka) in the division beginning with `Kā' in the venerable scripture of twenty-four thousand (verses) (known as) the Svāminīmata of the Supreme Lord's command as uttered within the Tradition of the Mother (avvākrama).

sanskrit: श्रीकौलीश उवाच' पञ्चदशानन्दः कुत्सितं कथितं देवि अयुक्त शास्त्रवादिनाम् । पशूनां' यत् समाख्यातं आचारं परमेश्वरं ॥ १ ॥ एतन्मे न श्रुतं देवि प्रसादाद् वक्तुमर्हसि । श्रीवक्रा उवाच १३ साधु मे तन्महाप्राज्ञ प्रश्न चैव शुभं कृतम् ॥ २ ॥ कथयामि महाशम्भों पूर्वस्नेहेन निश्चयम् । या सा देव पराशक्तिर्जगता योनिरूपिणी ॥ ३ ॥ तत्रोत्पन्न” समस्तं हि वाङ्गमयं सचराचरम् । अव्वा तेन इमा माता: सा शक्ति: परमेश्वरी ” ॥ ४ ॥ २० २४ २६ २७ उद्भवस्था” दुहित्री” सा” दुहनाच्च जगस्य च । २८ दुहित्री सा द्वितीया तु” भगिनी च तथोच्यते ॥ ५ ॥ ३३ भगरूपा” परा” सूक्ष्मा उन्मनामात्मना सह । यथाग्निस्तेजसा नित्यं नानाभेदैव्यवस्थिता ँ ।। ६ ।। तद्वदेव हि आत्मस्था भगिनी” भगरूपिणी ।
english: CHAPTER FIFTEEN About the Section (of the Scripture) Concerning (Kaula) Conduct (caryāpāda). Kaula Consorts The venerable Kaulīśa said: 1O goddess, what you have said is reprehensible and improper for those who know the scriptures. O Supreme Goddess, the conduct (ācāra) (to which you) refer is that of the fettered. O goddess, I have not heard (anything like) that; by your grace, you should tell (me about it). (1-2ab) The venerable (goddess) Vakrā said: O greatly wise one, well done (sādhu)! that you have asked this auspicious question of me. For the sake of our previous love, O Great Śambhu, I will tell (you) the teaching (niścaya). (2cd-3ab) The Mother O god, the Supreme Energy is the womb (yoni) of the worlds.2 All that is made of Speech along with (both all that) moves and is immobile has arisen there. And so these Mothers are (all) the Mother (avvā) who is energy, the Supreme Goddess.3 (3cd-4) The Daughter Established in the outpouring (of emanation) (udbhava), she is the Daughter (duhitrī) and because (she) milks (duhana) the universe. Know her to be the Daughter.4 (Now), similarly, the Sister is going to be explained. (5) The Sister She is the womb (bhaga), supreme and subtle, the Transmental (unmanā) endowed with the (energy of the) First Digit of the Moon (amā).5 Like fire, by virtue of its radiant energy (tejas), she is always of many kinds.6 In this same way, the Sister (bhaginī), who is the Yoni (bhaga), resides in the Self. (6-7ab)

sanskrit: 162 ४० कुमारिकाखण्ड: स्वयंजाता महासूक्ष्मा गुहामध्ये विसर्पिता ॥ ७ ॥ ४४ ४५ स्वतोत्पन्ना स्वयंजाता उक्ता च सहजा कला । ४२ ४९ अन्तस्था” सर्वजन्तूनां ँ वर्तते अन्तगा परा ॥ ८ ॥ अन्ते तु” संस्थिता” ह्येका अन्त्यजा परमेश्वरी'' । ५० रजस्तमोविनिर्मुक्ता सा भवेद् रजकी इति ॥ ९ ॥ रञ्जते“ सर्वगात्रेण ँ जगत् स्थावरजङ्गमम् । ५७ ५८ ६२ ६३ चरते चर्मगा येन सुरङ्गेन' रञ्जिता ।। १० ॥ ६४ चर्मकारी तु सा ज्ञेया मातङ्गीति तथोच्यते । आत्मस्थाने च सततं गीतस्यान्तपदे स्थिता ॥ ११ ॥ ७१ मातङ्गी कथिता दूती” अग्रजन्मी तथोच्यते । ७७ ७४ ७६ सर्वेषां चैव शास्त्राणां अग्रोत्पन्ना च अग्रणी ॥ १२ ॥ नान्यत् ँ तत्र” भवेत् किञ्चिन्मनसान्ते” मनोन्मन“ । उन्मना सा” समाख्याता परा मृतवाहिनीं ॥ १३ ॥ ८३
english: CHAPTER FIFTEEN 163 The Twin Sister (sahajā) She is self-born, very subtle and has emerged from the midst of the Cave. Spontaneously generated and self-born, she is said to be the Innate (sahajā) energy.7 (7cd-8ab) The Last Born At the end (antagā) (of the hierarchy of levels) is the supreme (goddess — Parā) present within (antasthā) all living beings. The one Supreme Goddess, the Last Born (antyajā), is established within / at the end (of phenomenal existence).8 (8cd-9ab) The Washerwoman The Washerwoman (rajakī) is (the energy) that is free of the (qualities of) passion (rajas) and darkness (tamas). With all (her) body she colours (rañjate) the universe, both moving and immobile.9 (9cd-10ab) The Leatherworker She, the one (goddess), is the Leatherworker (carmakārī) because, residing in the skin (carma),10 she moves about (carate) (within the microcosm) stained with beautiful colour.11 She should be known to be the Leatherworker (carmakārī) who, established inwardly, desires intensely and so is coloured with the beautiful colour (of desire). (Now), in the same way, the Sweeper Woman (mātaSgī) is going to be explained. (10cd-11ab) The Sweeper She abides constantly in the abode of the Self on the plane at the end of Song (gīta). Thus the dūtī MātaSgī (the Sweeper) has been explained.12 (Now), in the same way, the First Born (agrajanmanī) is going to be explained. (11cd-12ab) The First-born She is the foremost (energy) (agraSī) who has come forth first (agrotpannā) (before) all the scriptures. There, at the end of the mind, there is nothing else except the (energy) Mind Beyond Mind (manonmanī).13 (And so), she is called the Transmental (unmanā),14 the supreme (energy), who transports the nectar (of immortality).15 (12cd-13)

sanskrit: 164 कुमारिकाखण्डः आनन्दं तत् समत्वं हि मदिरानन्दचेतसः“ । सिद्ध्यते नात्र“ सन्देहो गुरुवक्त्रेण निश्चयम् ॥ १४ ॥ .९० योगचर्यासमाप्ते” तु व्रतसूत्रमनन्तरम् । त्यक्त्वा संसारप्रथनं” कामरूपादिपञ्चसु ॥ १५ ॥ ततश्च” चर्याव्रतं गृह्य अन्यथा न कदाचन । महाव्रतं तु निर्वाणं तदेव सर्व - ओलिषु ॥ १६ ॥ यदा वैराग्य जन्तूनां तदा निर्वाणगं व्रतम् । 00 ९९ वक्ष्यामि कौलिकं मार्ग निर्गतं खेचर क्रमम् ।। १७ ।। १०३ कुर्याद् व्रत कुले रक्षा नग्नवासा तु पिङ्गला । । तेनैव कारयेद् घोर ं विद्यायुक्तं परापरम् ।। १८ ॥ शिर मुण्डित कृत्वादौ तस्याच्छादन वल्कलम् । अलाभात् कर्पट१२ बिल्व ३ भुवनाकृति आसनम् ॥ १९ ॥ मुखं संकुचितं तस्य संसारमलछेदकम् । ११६ ११४ प्रसादं देवि मा कृत्वा चरुकं प्रतिदेहि माम् ।। २० ।। ११७ पञ्चभिः सप्तभिर्वापि अथ चाष्टौ दश: पुन: । ११८ द्वात्रिंशदथवा भिक्षा : कर्तव्या योगचिन्तकैः ॥ २१ ॥
english: CHAPTER FIFTEEN 165 Bliss is the oneness (samatva) (with that Transmental energy) of one whose mind is blissful with wine.16 He will certainly be successful. (This) is the teaching (uttered) by the Teacher’s Mouth.17 (14) The Vratasūtra: The Observance of the Vow (vratacaryā) in the Four Lineages (Now that the teaching concerning) the Conduct of Yoga (yogacaryā)18 is complete, the Vratasūtra, follows. (15ab) Once one has abandoned the perception (prathana) of transmigratory existence in the five (sacred seats of), Kāmarūpa and the rest, one should then take the Vow of Right Conduct (caryāvrata). (It can) never (be taken) in any other way. The Great Vow (mahāvrata) is NirvāSa and (it is taught) in all the lineages (oli). If people possess dispassion (vairāgya) then (by observing this) Vow (they) attain NirvāSa. (15cd-17ab) The Vow of the Transmission of the Skyfarers (Now) I will explain the Kaula path (from which) the Transmission of the Skyfarers (khecarakrama)19 has emerged. (17cd) Observe the Vow! The naked (nagnavāsā) Pi‰galā20 protects (everybody) in the Kula. (18ab) For that reason (he should observe a) severe (ghora) (vow), both supreme (transcendent) and inferior (immanent), in association with the Vidyā. First, once he has shaved (his) head, (he dons) a garment of bark. (If) he does not have that, (he may wear) old torn clothes or (ones made of) bilva (leaves). (His) seat has the form of the world. (18cd-19) (The adept should observe the Vow strictly and repeat the Vidyā constantly); his face contracted, (he should ask) “O goddess! Be gracious to me and give me the sacrificial pap (caruka) that destroys transmigratory existence.” (20) Those who contemplate Yoga (should) beg (this way) five, seven or eight, ten or thirty-two (times). (21)

sanskrit: 166 कुमारिकाखण्ड: मद्य मांस तथा कामं लौल्यलोभविवर्जितम् । १२२ पादुका त्रिप्रकारां च इज्यार्थे विनिवेदयेत् ।। २२ ।। तदा चर्याव्रतं मन्त्री३ द्वादशाब्दैस्तु सिद्ध्यति । १२५ पीठोपपीठ सर्वेषु क्षेत्राद्यैर्भूतले ५ व्रती ।। २३ ॥ पञ्चरात्रं तु सर्वत्र भस्मगोमयमध्यतः । स्वपेदेकान्तके पुनः अटव्या निर्जने वने ।। २४ ।। १३० १३२ नाराच९ क्षुरिका खड्ग तथा कर्तरि पङ्कटी । अस्त्रपञ्चकसंयुक्तः” कौलिकास्त्रस्वलंकृतः ।। २५ ।। विचरेत् पृथिवीं सवीं प्रथमस्त्रिषु ओलिषु । १३४ १३३ १३५ अपरं संप्रवक्ष्यामि क्रमवृद्धस्य यद् व्रतम्' ।। २६ ।। तद् व्रतं नाम विद्याया: ६ ज्ञेयमाज्ञापट ७ इति । १३६ १३७ १४० कुर्यात् कार्पासिक शुद्ध” त्रिपञ्चदीर्घविस्तरम्' ं ।। २७ ।। हस्ते पटं प्रक्रतव्यं कौपीन शिरभूषणम् । मुण्डितस्य प्रकर्तव्य कामराजेन रञ्जयेत् ।। २८ ॥ १४७ ताम्रजं खर्पर पात्रं सुशुद्धं च अलातवत् । १५० पूर्ववत् कारयेच्चयीं भिक्षाश्च सप्तविंशति:' ।। २९ ।। १५२ १५३ कर्तव्या दशधा २ वापि अथवा च चतुर्वरम् । अस्त्रपञ्चकघोरास्त्रं आद्यपीठाद् विनिर्गतम् ॥ ३० ॥ अथ'५४ द्वितीयकं वक्ष्ये' व्रतं कौमारमध्यतः । तद् व्रत५६ व्रतमित्याहुः सिद्धं पूर्णाद् विनिर्गतम् ।। ३१ ।। तद् व्रतं सिद्धसंकेत“ तस्याचार यथा भवेत् । पटं च पूर्ववत् कार्यं कौपीनमथ च्छादनम् ।। ३२ ।।
english: CHAPTER FIFTEEN 167 He should (then) offer the triangular (triprakārā)21 sandal (pādukā) as an offering (to the deity), namely, wine, meat and passion (kāma) devoid of desire and greed. Then, twelve years, the reciter of mantra accomplishes the Vow of Conduct (caryāvrata). (22-23ab) (The adept who) observes this vow should sleep in a solitary place on the ground anywhere, in any of the sacred fields and seats, primary and secondary, or in a deserted forest for five nights in the midst of ashes and cow dung. (23cd-24) The foremost in the three lineages should wander over all the earth, well- adorned with Kaula weapons and possessing the five arms, namely, an arrow, a razor, a sword, a knife and an axe (pa‰ka˜ī). (25-26ab) The Vow of the Transmission of the Aged Next I will tell something else, namely, the vow of the Transmission of the Aged, the Vow of the Vidyā that should be known as the Cloth of the Command (ājñāpa˜a). (26cd-27ab) (The adept) should fashion a pure (cloth) made of cotton fifteen (fingers?) in extent. He should (hold the) cloth in (one) hand and (use his) loincloth as an ornament for the head. He should undertake (the vow) of the tonsured and colour (his consciousness) with (KRĪ¤ the seed-syllable of) the King of Passion. (27cd-28) (His) bowl (should be) a begging bowl made of copper, very pure, like a firebrand. As before, he should practice (Kaula) Conduct (caryā) and beg twenty- seven (times). (29) He should form the terrible weapon (ghorāstra) consisting of the Fivefold Weapon (astrapañcaka)22 that has emerged from the Primordial Seat (ādyapī˜ha) ten times or else four. (30) The Vow of the Transmission of the Youth Next, I will explain the second vow, which is the one in the (Transmission) of the Youth. That vow is said to be the Accomplished Vow and has emerged from the (sacred seat of) the Full One (purSa) (i.e. PūrSagiri). The convention with regard to that vow has been (established by) accomplished yogis (siddhasaˆketa), (and I will tell you) how it is observed. (31-32ab)

sanskrit: 168 रञ्जनीयञ्च`` रङ्गेन पीतेन तु महेश्वर । कुमारिकाखण्ड: तथा पात्रं च पूर्वोक्तं भिक्षाचर्यप्रतिग्रहम् ।। ३३ ॥ १६५ अस्त्रपञ्चकमेवं तु तथा पाशुपतास्त्रकम् । एतत् सिद्धव्रतं शुद्धं पालनादपि सिद्ध्यति ॥ ३४ ॥ अपरं तृतीयकं वक्ष्ये व्रतं बालक्रमस्य च । मुद्रा नाम व्रतं शुद्धं कामरूपाद् विनिर्गतम् ।। ३५ ।। १६७ । १७० पटं पूर्वक्रमेणैव यथा भवति तच्छृणु । गैरिकारञ्जित“ कृत्वा तथा खर्पर ताम्रजम् चर्याभिक्षा यथा पूर्व पञ्चास्त्रं भैरवास्त्रकम् । १७४ ॥ ३६ ॥ गृहीत्वा पर्यटेत् मन्त्री॰३ एतद् योगव्रतं शुभम् ।। ३७ ।। उलीनां क्रमसिद्धाना व्रतत्रितय दर्शितम् । ७७ एतेषामासनं श्रेष्ठं मृगचर्म सुकोमलम् ॥ ३८ ॥ आसनत्रितय' तेषां ज्येष्ठमध्ये कनीयसे । । कूर्मासन तु प्रथम तथा पद्मं द्वितीयकम् ।। ३९ ॥ तृतीयं स्वस्तिकं नाम मुद्रापूर्वक्रमव्रते । प्रयागादिगृहाणां तु स्वपेद् योगीश्वरः सदा ॥ ४० ॥ १८५ •९८६ तासां सार्धं “ तु समयं दूतीनां सह मैथुनम् । १८७ अविरुद्धं च भवति निशाचारेण कौलवित् ।। ४१ ।।
english: CHAPTER FIFTEEN 169 The cloth, loincloth and covering should be fashioned as before. O Great Lord, (the cloth) should be coloured with yellow dye and so too the aforementioned bowl used for begging alms (bhiknācaryā). (32cd-33) In the same way, (he should carry) the Fivefold Weapon and the Pāśupata Weapon. This is the pure Accomplished Vow. By observing it also, (the adept) is successful. (34) The Vow of the Transmission of the Child (Now) I will explain another vow, the third, which is that of the Transmission of the Child. It is the pure vow that has emerged from Kāmarūpa and is that of the Gesture (mudrā). (35) Listen how the cloth is according to the first Transmission. Once it has been coloured with ochre and a copper bowl (has) also (been procured), (the adept should undertake), as before, the practice of begging (bhiknācaryā). Taking hold of the Fivefold Weapon which is that of Bhairava,23 the reciter of mantra should wander (from place to place). This is the auspicious Vow of Yoga. (36-37) The three vows of the lineages (uli) and the Siddhas of the Transmissions have been explained.24 (38ab) (Now), their best seat is one of soft deerskin. (I will tell you) their three sitting postures in the (lineages of the) Oldest, Middling and Youngest. The Posture of the Tortoise (kūrmāsana) is the first and the (Posture of) the Lotus is the second. The third is that of the Svastika (and is a part of) the Vow of the Transmission (kramavrata) which is that of Gesture. (38cd-39ab) The Conduct of the Night (niśācāra) The lord of yogis should always sleep in Prayāga and the other Houses. The pledge (samaya) with them is sexual intercourse with the dūtīs. O knower of Kaula, (as a part of) the Conduct of the Night (niśācāra), it is not prohibited. (39cd-41)

sanskrit: 170 कुमारिकाखण्ड: १८९ चरुकं गृह्यतें ” गुप्तं तथा पुष्पं च अन्तजम् । १९० रसं तु वैष्णवं नाम चरुक त्रिविध स्मृतम् ।। ४२ ।। अलिफल्गुसमायुक्तं भक्षयेदविशङ्कितः । द्वादशाब्दैरतीतैस्तु” खेगतिनीत्र संशयः ।। ४३ ।। क्रमाराधनयुक्तानां विद्यानुष्ठानपारगाम् । निश्चय नात्र संदेहो इत्याज्ञा पारमेश्वरी' । ।। ४४ ।। १९९ ये योगिनीकुले जाता येषां तुष्टा ह्यहं परा । २०० २०२ । ते लभन्ति व्रत१०१ सत्यं आत्म – औल्यां? पृथक् पृथक् ।। ४५ ।। २०३ ं २०४ वीरचर्या वीरव्रतं वीरसंगमवृत्तिषु । दूतीनां सर्वगमनं सबाह्याभ्यन्तरं स्थितम् ।। ४६ ॥ निशाचारे २०५ समाचार २०६ कर्तव्यं व्रतिभिस्त्रिधा २०९ मनोरोध न कर्तव्यं यत्र यत्र व्रजेन्मनः २१० २०७ ।। ४७ ।। तत्र तत्रैव गन्तव्यं इच्छाचर्यांीं”” समाचरेत् । एतल्लिङ्ग” २ त्रिधा३ प्रोक्तं प्रकटं व्रतसंग्रहम् ॥ ४८ ॥ २१४ अष्टानां कुलदेवीनां सदा भक्ति १५ समाचरेत् । २१६ । पूजयेत् सर्वदा चाष्टौ वेश्याद्या: “ कौलिके क्रमे ॥ ४९ ॥ अथ” चर्याविनिर्मुक्तो” चरुकार्थी गृहेष्वपि । निशाचारेण कुर्वीत प्राशनात् ” ” परमा गतिः ॥ ५० ॥ २१९ व्रतिनो रुद्रवत् साक्षान्मम” तुल्यबलो” भवेत् । व्रतमव्यक्तकं येन१३ इच्छारूपधरो भवेत् ॥ ५१ ॥
english: CHAPTER FIFTEEN 171 (The adept) takes the sacrificial pap (caruka) which is secret (gupta), the Flower (punpa) that is ‘last born’ (antaja) and VainSava juice (rasa). The sacrificial pap is said to be (of these) three kinds.25 (42) Free from doubt, (the adept) should eat it along with meat and wine. He will certainly (achieve) flight after twelve years. (43) (This is) the conclusion of those intent on worshipping the Transmission and have completed the practice of the Vidyā. There is no doubt here (about this). This is the Command of the Supreme Goddess. (44) Those who are born in the Yoginīkula and with whom I, the Supreme One (Parā), am pleased, acquire the vow and truth in their own respective lineage (auli). (45) Those who undertake the vow should practice the threefold conduct (samācāra) over the course of (their) nocturnal practice (niśācāra). This is the Conduct of a Hero (vīracaryā) which is the Hero's Vow (observed) in the modalities of the Hero's union and the union Dūtīs practice with everybody (sarvagamana), which is both external and internal.26 (46-47ab) The mind should not be checked. One should go wherever the mind goes and practice the Conduct of Desire (icchācaryā).27 This is said to be the threefold sign (li‰ga) (of this practice), the sum (saˆgraha) (and substance) of the Vow, clearly evident.28 (47cd-48) One should always practice devotion to the eight goddesses of Kula. One should always worship the eight, Veśyā (Courtesan) and the others, in the Kaulika transmission. (49) Now, one who has been freed by the practice (caryā) (of spiritual discipline) and who desires (to eat) the sacrificial pap in the Houses (of these goddesses) as well, should do so by means of the Conduct of the Night (niśācāra), and (so) by eating (it) (he achieves) the supreme state. (50) Conclusion and Benefits It is directly apparent that the one who observes the vow is like Rudra and is equal to me in strength. By virtue of the vow that is hidden (lit. ‘unmanifest’ — avyaktaka) he can assume any form he desires.29 (51)

sanskrit: 172 कुमारिकाखण्ड: .२२६ तेन अव्यक्तमित्याहुः४ व्रतं १२५ कौलस्य लक्षणम् । संसारक्रमसंस्थानां अधिकारे तु संस्थितम् ।। ५२ ।। आचार्याणां समाख्यातं गुप्तं व्रतपरिग्रहम् २२७ । न तेषां कथिता चर्याी नाम संगममत् सधा ।। ५३ ॥ २२८ आत्मचर्यासमायुक्तं व्रतं गुप्ततमं चरेत् । इत्यागमविशुद्धस्य कौलिकस्य महीपतेः २३२ २३० ॥ ५४ ॥ चर्याीपादं समाख्यातं निर्णयान्ते समर्पितम् । २३४ अदत्ता३३ व्रतचर्या च अदत्तं च कुलक्रमम् ।। ५५ ।। न ग्राह्यं च परत्रार्थं३५ ग्रहनात् पतनं भवेत् । २३६ चर्याीपादेन दृष्टेन गुरूणां शास्त्रपद्धतिः ।। ५६ ।। तेनैव यद् व्रतं दत्तं चर्यासंगमकौलिकम् । तत् सर्वं सफलं शिष्ये व्रतीनां नात्र संशयः ॥ ५७ ॥ २३७ अन्यथा न व्रतं चयी न न्यासं न क्रमं क्वचित् । यावन्न“ पश्यते ज्ञानं मतार्थं शुद्धकौलिकम् ।। ५८ ।। २३९ तावद् भ्रान्तिक्षयं नास्ति तस्माच्छास्त्रं परिग्रहेत् । २४० इत्याद्यावतारे महामन्थानभैरवयज्ञे अन्वये सप्तकोटिप्रमाणे मेरुमार्गविनिर्गते लक्षपादाधिके आद्यपीठावतारिते विद्यापीठमार्गे विमलषट्कनिर्णये कादिभेदे आज्ञापारमेश्वरे स्वामिनीमते श्रीचतुर्विंशत्सहस्रसंहितायां अव्वाक्रमभाषिते चर्याीपादाधिकारो नामानन्दः ।। १५ ।।
english: CHAPTER FIFTEEN 173 Thus the (wise) say that the vow, which is the mark of (a true) Kaula, is unmanifest. Meant for those subject to transmigration (saˆsārakramasaˆstha), the secret form of the vow that teachers (ācārya) observe has been explained. Their conduct has not been explained * * * * * * (?)30 (52-53) (The adept) should practice the most secret vow that includes the Observance of the Self (ātmacaryā). Thus the section concerning the practice (caryāpāda) of a Kaulika,31 the lord of the earth, purified by the scripture, has been explained and placed at the conclusion of the teaching. (54-55ab) If the observance of the vow (vratacaryā) and the Kula transmission (krama) have not been imparted, one should not take up the transcendental teaching (paratrārtha). By adopting it (unprepared), one falls. (55cd-56ab) The path of the scriptures (taught by) the teacher (has been established) from the perspective of (Kaula) practice (caryāpāda). The Kaulika vow, which is the convergance of practice (caryā) that has been imparted with that same (perspective), all bears fruit within the disciple. Those who observe the vow have no doubt about this. Otherwise, there is no vow, no practice (caryā), no deposition (of mantras on the body) and no transmission (krama) anywhere. (56cd-58ab) As long as one does not perceive the pure Kaula knowledge, that is, the teaching of the scripture (matārtha), illusion is not destroyed. Therefore one should take up the scripture. (58-59ab) This is the (fifteenth) chapter called About the Section (of the Scripture) Concerning (Kaula) Conduct (caryāpāda). It belongs to the primordial descent into the great sacrifice of the Churning Bhairava in the tradition that consists of seventy million (verses) that has emerged on the Path of Meru that contains more than a hundred thousand quarters (of a metre) and has been brought (down to earth) into the primordial sacred seat on the path of sacred seat of knowledge (vidyāpī˜ha). It is the ultimate purport of the Pure Six Thousand (verses vimalana˜ka) in the division beginning with `Ka' in the venerable scripture of twenty-four thousand (verses) (known as) the Svāminīmata of the Supreme Lord's Command as uttered within the Tradition of the Mother (avvākrama).

sanskrit: षोडशानन्दः श्रीनाथ उवाच कुलचर्यीरतः शान्तो योगीन्द्रः सिद्धिकांक्षिणः ' । कथं भिक्षाटन ै देवि´ कथं भाषां समुच्चरेत् ॥ १ ॥ सूचिता च त्वया देवि भिक्षाची कुलाष्टके । कथयस्व प्रसादेन भाषासंकेतनिर्णयम् ।। २ ।। श्रीवक्रा उवाच o प्रयागा वरणा कोल्ला' अट्टहासा जयन्तिका । चरित्रैकाम्रक चैव देविकोट्टं तथाष्टमम् ।। ३ ॥ गृहाष्टके च देवेश भाषासंकेतकोत्तमम् । सिद्धिमुक्तिकरं देव कथ्यते चाधुना शृणु ॥ ४॥ कु ला ई आ त्रिभुवनावली दिव्याम्नाये प्रचारोपदेश : चरुकं देहि मे ई आ । अक्षरी” कथिता चर्या प्रयागाख्ये वरानन” । २३ वेश्यागृहे कुकाराख्या निशाचारे गता स्वयम् ॥ ५ ॥ २४ २० कु शा¨ ई आ सकलभुवनावली कुलाम्नाये प्रचारोपदेश: चरुकं देहि मे ई आ । २७ द्वितीया कथिता चर्या कामरूपा कुनामिका” । ३१ वरणा शुण्डिनी देवी गता समयमेलके ॥ ६ ॥ ३२ कु वे ई आ अखण्डमण्डलावली समयाम्नाये प्रचारोपदेशः चरुकं देहि मे ई आ ।
english: CHAPTER SIXTEEN The Section Concerning the Vidyā. The Secret Language of the Mantras of the Eight Mothers Śrīnātha said: O goddess, how (should) the Lord of Yogis,1 devoted to Kula practice (caryā) and desirous of success (siddhi), wander in search of alms (bhiknā˜ana)? And how should he utter (the secret) language? (1) O goddess, you have (already) referred to the practice of begging (alms) in the eight (centres of) Kula2, (now) please tell (me) the teaching concerning the convention of the (secret) language.3 (2) The Eight Mothers The venerable (goddess) Vakrā said: Prayāga, VaraSā,4 Kollā5, A˜˜ahāsa, Jayantikā, Caritra, Ekāmraka and Deviko˜˜a, the eighth — in (these) eight Houses, O lord of the gods, the convention of the (secret) language is the best. O god, it bestows success and liberation and is now being explained, (so) listen.6 (3-4) 7KU LĀ8 Ī Ā, (you who are) the series of the three worlds and the teaching preached in the Divine Tradition, give me the sacrificial pap! Ī Ā. O fair-faced one, Aknarī's9 practice (caryā) in Prayāga has been declared. Kubjikā (kukārākhyā)10 has herself gone to the House of Veśyā (the Courtesan) (in the course of her) Conduct of the Night (niśācāra).11 (5) KU ŚĀ12 Ī Ā, (you who are) the series of all the worlds and the teaching preached in the Kula Tradition, give me the sacrificial pap! Ī Ā. The second practice (caryā) has been declared. It is that of Kubjikā (kunāmikā)13 in Kāmarūpa. The goddess ŚuSÆinī (the Liquor Seller)14 in VaraSā has gone to the Assembly of the Rule (samayamelaka).15 (6) KU VE16 Ī Ā, (you who are) the unbroken series of maSÆalas and the teaching preached in the Tradition of the Rule, give me the sacrificial pap! Ī Ā.

sanskrit: 176 कुमारिकाखण्ड: ३६ कुंकुण्डी कथिता चर्या तृतीया समयगोचरे । ३९ कौल्ले कैवर्तिनी देवी कुनामाजा जगत्सुता ॥ ७ ॥ कु या ँ ई आ शिवगुरुपरमावली मुद्राम्नाये प्रचारोपदेश: चरुकं देहि मे ई आ । कौशली” कथिता” चर्या अट्टहासे गता देवी कुनामा ४४ चतुर्थी च महाबला । ४५ खट्टिकीगृहे ॥ ८ ॥ कु भुई आ आनन्दपरमावली आद्याम्नाये प्रचारोपदेश: चरुकं देहि मे आई । काञ्चीमुखा स्मृता चयी पञ्चमा भवसंज्ञका । जयन्त्यां च कृता नित्यं कुनामा कण्डुकीगृहे ॥ ९ ॥ ५३ कुक्षे ई आ मातङ्गावली षट्काम्नाये प्रचारोपदेश: चरुकं देह मे आई । वागेशी च स्मृता चर्या षष्ठी निग्रहकारिका । ५९ ६० चरित्राख्ये कृता नित्य कुनामा रजकीगृहे ॥१०॥ ६१ ६२ ६३ कु निः ई आ निशाचारभुवनावली पीठाम्नाये ? प्रचारोपदेशः ३ चरुकं देहि मे आई शाङ्करी कथिता चयी सप्तमा वरवर्णिनी । ६८ एकाम्रे शिल्पिनी देवी कुनामा समये गता ॥। ११ ॥ कुम ई आ मोक्षकुलावली पारम्पर्याम्नाये प्रचारोपदेश: चरुकं देहि मे आई ।
english: CHAPTER SIXTEEN 177 The third practice (caryā) has been declared. It is that of KuˆkuSÆī in the field of the Rule. The goddess Kaivartinī (the Fisherwoman), born of Kubjikā (kunāmājā) and the mother of the universe, is in Kaulla. (7) KU YĀ17 Ī Ā (you who are) the supreme series of Śiva and the teachers as well as the teaching preached in the Tradition of the Gesture, give me the sacrificial pap! Ī Ā. The fourth practice (caryā) has been declared. It is that of Kauśalī (the Skilful One) who is very strong. The goddess Kubjikā (kunāmā) has gone to A˜˜ahāsa, the House of Kha˜˜ikī (the Butcherwoman). (8) KU BHU18 Ī Ā, (you who are) the supreme series of bliss and the teaching preached in the Primordial Tradition, give me the sacrificial pap! Ā Ī. (This is) said to be the fifth practice, that of Kāñcīmukhā (Scissor-faced) and is called Phenomenal Existence (bhava). (She is) Kubjikā (kunāmā) who is always formed in Jayantī, the House of KaSÆukī (the Ball-making Woman). (9) KU K±E19 Ī Ā, (you who are) the series of elephants (mātaSga) and the teaching preached in the Tradition of the Six Thousand (na˜ka),20 give me the sacrificial pap! Ā Ī. (This is) said to be the sixth practice, that of Vāgeśī (the Mistress of Speech) who brings about restraint (nigraha). It is Kubjikā (kunāmā) who is always formed in (the place) called Caritra, the House of Rajakī (the Washerwoman). (10) KU NIÖ21 Ī Ā, (you who are) the series of the worlds of the Conduct of the Night and the teaching preached in the Tradition of the Sacred Seats, give me the sacrificial pap! Ā Ī. The seventh practice has been declared. It is that of Śā‰karī, the best of females (varSinī). The goddess Śilpinī (the Sculpteress),22 who is Kubjikā (kunāmā) in Ekāmra, is present in the Rule. (11) KU MA23 Ī Ā (you who are) the series of the Kulas of liberation and the teaching preached in the Tradition of the Transmission (pāramparyāmnāya), give me the sacrificial pap! Ā Ī.

sanskrit: 178 कुमारिकाखण्ड: ७२ भैरवी कथिता चर्या अष्टमा” मोक्षदायिक । ७३ देविकोट्टे तु कथिता कुनामा कौशटीगृहे ।। १२ ।। श्रीवक्रा उवाच सिद्ध्यष्टकं कुलाम्नाये मातॄणां च प्रसादतः । वेश्यारूपेण ब्रह्माणी शाङ्करी शुण्डिनी स्मृता ॥ १३ ॥ कैवर्ती नाम कौमारी खट्टिका वैष्णवी स्मृता । वाराही कण्डुकी देवी इन्द्राणी रजकी स्मृता ॥ १४ ॥ शिल्पी ज्ञेया तु चामुण्डा महालक्ष्मी तथान्त्यजा । चर्याक्षेत्रविभागेन ज्ञात्वा चयीँ समाचरेत् ॥ १५ ॥ •७८ मा मा मा य डि आ हो आव हो प्रयागभैरवि ई आ समयाचारु देहि मे चरुकम् । एषा चर्याी महाचयी वेश्यागृहे” तु कारयेत् । तस्मादवाप्य चरुकळ े तदा कौलेश्वरो भवेत् ॥ १६ ॥ अव्वे अम्बे च मे माये न च हुं हुं आ हु ँ हो पीठसमयाचारयोगानन्दे वरणाभैरवि” समयाचारु देहि मे चरुकम् । ९० वाराणस्यां तु वरणा ं समयाचारमेलके । शौण्डीगृहे महाचर्यांीं कृत्वा वागेश्वरीपदम् ॥ १७ ॥
english: CHAPTER SIXTEEN 179 The eighth practice has been declared. It is that of Bhairavī who bestows liberation. (The form of) Kubjikā (kunāmā) in Deviko˜˜a, the House of Kauśa˜ī, has been declared. (12) The venerable (goddess) Vakrā said: The Octad of Accomplishments (siddhyan˜aka)24 belongs to the Kula Tradition by the grace of the Mothers. BrahmāSī is in the form of Veśyā (the Prostitute), (while) Śā‰karī25 is said to be ŚuSÆinī (the Liquor Seller). (13) Kaivartī (the fisherwoman) is Kaumārī, (while) Kha˜˜ikā (the Chalkminer Woman) is said to be VainSavī. Vārāhī is the goddess KaSÆukī (the Ball-making Woman),26 (while) IndrāSī is said to be Rajakī (the Washerwoman). (14) One should know Śilpinī (the Sculpteress) to be CāmuSÆā, while Mahālaknmī is Antyajā (the Last Born).27 Having learned (them) according to (their) fields (knetra) and practice (caryā), (one should) engage in practice (caryā). (15) The Sūtra of the Octad of Kula (kulān˜akasūtra)28 MĀ MĀ MĀ ÕI Ā HO ĀVA HO, O Prayāgabhairavī29! Ī Ā, O (you who are) skilful in the practice of the Rule (samayācāru), 30 give me the sacrificial pap! This practice (caryā) is the great practice. (The adept) should observe it in the House of the Courtesan and, having obtained the sacrificial pap from there, he becomes the lord of Kaula. (16) AVVE AMBE CA ME MĀYE NA CA HU¤ HU¤ Ā HU¤ HO,31 O sacred seat! O bliss of the Yoga of the practice of the Rule in the sacred seat! O VaraSābhairavī! O (you who are) skilful in the practice of the Rule, give me the sacrificial pap! VaraSā is in VārāSasī in the assembly of the practice of the Rule. Once one has observed the great practice in the House of ŚauSÆī (the Liquor Seller) (one attains) Vāgeśvarī's state. (17)

sanskrit: 180 कुमारिकाखण्ड: जाग्रिणी¨ म इ दि द्वि आ घुग् घुरुमालवजन्ति आ जम्भणि जम्भणि हो कोल्लापुरभैरवि ई आ समयाचारु देहि मे चरुकम् । ९९ कोल्लापुरे महाचयी कैवर्त्ती नग्नवाससा । १०१ चरुकाज्ञाप्रसादेन ज्ञानैश्वर्यं न संशयः ॥ १८ ॥ दिद्वन द्वसयल॰३ परिवलि४ आ हो अव्वा मे कुलसिद्धि आ अट्टहासभैरवि आ समयाचारु देहि मे चरुकम् । । खट्टिकीमन्दिरे चर्या अट्टहासाकुले“ स्थिता । समयाज्ञाप्रसादेन चरुकेन तु सिद्धिदा ॥ १९ ॥ १११ १०६ सुभरि सुभरि आहो कुडि कुडि हो माये महामाये एहि एहि भो हिन: भोजय भोजय१२ भैरवी आ समयाचारु देहि मे चरुकम् । कन्दुकीमन्दिरे जाता जयन्तीकुलकन्दरे । तस्या:”५ चरुकदानेन”६ वीरेन्द्रो योगिनीकुले ।। २० ।। लम्बे लम्बे न होमालि लिलिविज्जे समर सवक् कहजन्ती सा चरित्रभैरवी आ समयाचारु देहि मे चरुकम् । जम्बुकी च परानन्दे उन्मनानन्दचेतसा । १२१ तस्याः श्रीचरुकं प्राप्य भैरवो भैरवीकुले ।। २१ ।। अव्व हो सव्व हो स ल वट्ट हो शतयोजनपरमानन्दे २ आ कन्दुकीभैरवी आ समयाचारु देहि मे चरुकम् । शिल्पीमन्दिरमध्ये तु या करोति समागमम् । १२४ योगिना१३ चरुकार्थीनां ददेत् सिद्धिमनेकधा ।। २२ ।।
english: CHAPTER SIXTEEN 181 JĀGRI¦Ī (She Who is Awake) MA I DI DVI Ā GHUG GHURUMĀLAVAJANTI Ā JAMBHA¦I JAMBHA¦I HO, O Kollāpurabhairavī! Ī Ā,32 O (you who are) skilful in the practice of the Rule, give me the sacrificial pap! The great practice in Kollāpura is the naked Kaivarttī (Fisherwoman). Having obtained the venerable sacrificial pap of Jambukī, which is within Supreme Bliss, by means of the mind (cetas) blissful with the Transmental, (the yogi becomes) Bhairava in the Bhairavī Kula.
