She who engenders union in the middle of Śilpinī's temple, bestows upon the yogis who desire the sacrificial pap accomplishments (siddhi) of many kinds.

sanskrit: 182 कुमारिकाखण्ड: मातङ्गी विमलमती” प्रकटयोगिनी समयसिद्धि ६ माये २७ समयाचारचक्रे वन्दितत्रिभुवनदिव्ययोगिनी देविकोट्टभैरवी आ समयाचारु देहि में चरुकम् । १३२ १३३ अनादिविमलमातङ्गीकुले जाता मतङ्गिनी । १३४ प्रसादबुद्ध्या चरुक संप्राप्य खेचरो भवेत् ॥ २३ ॥ १३५ इति कुलाष्टककुलचर्यासूत्राधिकारः ५ ।। || १३० १३१ श्रीनाथ उवाच १३७ समयलोपानि सर्वाणि मेरुराशिस्त्वसंख्यया' । तेषां संशोधनार्थाीय या विद्या समुपस्थिता ।। २४ ।। पीठस्तवेन सहिता यथा भवति कौलिनि'३८ । प्रमादाल्लोपमायाते३९ सिद्धे समयमण्डले ' १४० ।। २५ ।। साधकस्य भवेद् ग्लानिर्नानाविघ्नैः प्रबाध्यते ४२ । अपमृत्युभयं तस्माद् दारिद्र्य ४३ कलहं तथा ।। २६ ॥ दुःस्वप्न कार्यहानिश्च लोकद्वेष मुहुर्मुहुः । का गतिस्तस्य देवेशि४६ कथं संशुद्धिमाप्नुयात् ।। २७ ।। श्रीवक्रा उवाच साधु साधु महाशम्भो यन्मे निगदितं शृणु । विस्तरेण बहुभेदैस्तत्सर्व कथयामि ते ।। २८ ॥ पीठोपपीठसंदोह क्षेत्रोप क्षेत्रमेव च । द्वारोपद्वारस्थानानि ५२ सेवनान्निर्मलो भवेत् ।। २९ ।।
english: CHAPTER SIXTEEN 183 MātaSginī, the pure-minded and manifest Yoginī, accomplishment of the Rule! O Māyā! you who are praised in the Gathering of Conduct according to the Rule (samayācāracakra), the divine Yoginī in the three worlds, Deviko˜˜abhairavī Ā, O (you who are) skilful in the practice of the Rule, give me the sacrificial pap! Māta‰ginī has arisen in the beginingless and pure Kula of Māta‰gī. Once (the yogi) has obtained the sacrificial pap by means of the intellect graced (by this goddess), he becomes a Skyfarer.37 (23) This (completes) the section (adhikāra) of the scripture (sūtra) concerning Kula conduct with regards to the Octad of Kula. The Pī˜hastava: A Hymn to the Sixty-four Sacred Seats Śrīnātha said: Countless are all (those deeds) that break the Rule, a heap (as great as mount) Meru. O Kaulinī, the Vidyā is meant to purify them and is at hand, along with the Hymn to the Sacred Seats.38 (24-25ab) The adept suffers from lassitude (glāni)39 and is afflicted by many kinds of obstacles if, due to his negligence, (something is) omitted40 once (he has received initiation and) the MaSÆala of the Rule (samaya) has been completed (siddha). (25cd-26ab) From that (omission comes) fear of an untimely death, poverty, conflict, uneasy sleep, destruction of one's goal (kārya) and the aversion of people (towards oneself), time and again. O mistress of the gods, what happens to him and how can he attain (a state of) complete purity? (26cd-27) The venerable (goddess) said: O Great Śambhu, wisely indeed have you spoken to me. (Now) listen. I will tell you all that at length with (its) many (subtle) distinctions. (28) (The adept) becomes pure by attending to the sacred seats, the fields and the doors (dvāra), primary and secondary, along with the meeting places (saˆdoha).41 (29)

sanskrit: 184 कुमारिकाखण्ड: अथाशक्तः प्रमादी'४ वा विद्यापीठौघसेवनात् । सम्यक् संशुद्धिमाप्नोति प्रातरुत्थाय यः पठेत् ॥ ३० ॥ तदहं संप्रवक्ष्यामि समयलोपविशुद्धये“ । १५९ चतुःषष्टिस्तु चक्राणि कूटभेदेन संस्थिताः ।। ३१ ।। चतुःषष्टिस्तथा पीठान् क्रमेण कथयाम्यहम् । पश्चिमेन क्रमेणैव शाक्त प्रणवपञ्चकम् ।। ३२ ।। मातृकूटसमायोगात् पीठस्तवमुदीरयेत् । अट्टहासे६२ कदम्बस्था ३ सौम्यास्या ४ वज्रधारिणीम् ॥ ३३ ॥ महाघण्टसमोपेता प्रणमामि शिवंकरीम् । १६६ चरित्रायां करञ्जस्था कृष्णाख्या शक्तिधारिणीम् ॥ ३४ ॥ महाबलसमोपेता६९ प्रणमामि सुसिद्धिदाम् १७० अग्निकेन” समोपेतां दण्डहस्तां नगौकसाम् ।। ३५ ।। कौलगिय७३ महालक्ष्मीं नौमि लक्ष्मीविवर्धनीम्' १७४ । १७८ ज्वालामुखी जयन्त्याया निम्बस्था खड्गधारिणीम् ।। ३६ । महाप्रेतसमोपेतां नौमि सर्वार्थसिद्धिदाम् । । अश्वत्थस्था महामायामुज्जैन्या पाशधारिणीम् ॥ ३७ ॥ महाकालयुतां नौमि सर्वार्थप्रतिपादिनीम् । उडुम्बरतलावस्था वायुवेगां ध्वजायुधाम् ॥ ३८ ॥ ८७ प्रयागे पवनोपेता नौमि शत्रुविनाशनीम् । ।।
english: CHAPTER SIXTEEN 185 Now, one who is negligent (of the Vidyā) or who is helpless, by rising (early in the) morning and reading (the scripture), achieves perfect purity by attending to the Vidyā, sacred seats and the lineage (ogha). I will explain that so that (the adept can) purify the omissions of the Rule. (30-31ab) The sixty-four Wheels accord with the division of the Peak (seed- syllables) (kū˜a). Similarly, I will tell (you) the sixty-four sacred seats, in due order. sanskrit: 186 कुमारिकाखण्ड: ९० वाराणस्यां तु तालस्था ऊध्वकेशीं गदायुधाम् ।। ३९ ।। प्रणौमि शिरसा देवीं शाङ्करीं शाङ्करान्विताम् । १९३ १९७ १९४ कर्णमोटी ९५ वटस्था तु सशूला हेतुकान्विताम्” ।। ४० ।। श्रीकोटे श्रीप्रदा नौमि राज्यसंपत्प्रदायिनीम् ” । विरजायाम्बिकादेवीं२ मुद्रापट्टिशधारिणीम् ।। ४१ ॥ २०४ अनलेन २०३ समोपेतां प्रणमामि जयावहाम् । एरुडे अग्निवक्त्रां तु वज्रशक्तिधरां शुभाम् ।। ४२ ।। घण्टारवसमोपेतां नमामि रिपुनाशनीम् । २०७ मुशलायुधहस्तां तु महाजङ्घसमन्विताम् ॥ ४३ ॥ नमामि शत्रुभङ्गार्थे पिङ्गाक्षी हस्तिनापुरे । २१३ २१० २१४ २१२ २१५ एलापुरे ३ खरास्यां तु पाशहस्तां महाबलाम् ।। ४४ ।। गजकर्णसमोपेतां नौमि दुष्टप्रमर्दनीम् । •२१७ २१९ कुमारीं चैव गोकर्णे मुद्रालकुटधारिणीम् ।। ४५ ।। तडिज्जङ्घसमोपेतां नमामि रिपुमर्दनीम्” । इन्द्राणीं२२ मरुदेशे २२३ तु त्रैलोक्याकृष्टिकारिकाम् ।। ४६ ।। करालेन समोपेतां नमाम्यंकुशधारिणीम् २५ । २२८ २२९ २२६ ।। रोमजङ्घसमोपेतां नगरे तु हलायुधाम् ॥ ४७ ॥ वक्रां॰ गच्छनिवासिन्यां नमामि वरसिद्धयें । २३१ २३२ कुम्भकेन समोपेतां खट्वाङ्गकरभूषिताम् ॥ ४८ ॥ नमामि पापशुद्ध्यर्थं चामुण्डा २५ पौण्ड्रवर्धने । २३६
english: CHAPTER SIXTEEN 187 I salute, (bowing my) head to the goddess Śāˆkarī66 who is accompanied by Śaˆkara.67 Her weapon is a mace (gada)68 and, (her) hair upraised (ūrdhvakeśī), she resides in a palm (tree) in VārāSasī69 (7). sanskrit: 188 २३७ कुमारिकाखण्ड: पुरस्तीरे प्रसन्नास्यां“ वज्रशृङ्खलधारिणीम्” । ४९ ॥ नमामि त्रिजटोपेतां बन्धस्तम्भनकारिकाम् । २४१ पृष्ठापुर्यांीं४२ विद्युन्मुखीं४३ दण्डशक्त्यायुधोद्यताम् ॥ ५० ॥ नौमि घण्टारवोपेतां दैत्यस्तम्भनकारिकाम् । २४५ ।। उल्कामुखसमोपेतां ऊध्वकेशीं महाबलाम् ॥ ५१ ॥ मुद्रालकुटहस्तां तु नौमि दुष्टाङ्गभञ्जनीम् । २४७ पिशिताशसमोपेतां नौमि २५१ कट्टारिकोद्यताम् २५२ ॥ ५२ ॥ सोपारे अग्निवक्त्रां२५३ तु अशेषपशुघातनीम् । २५४ क्षीरिके लोकमातां च २५५ खड्गहस्तां नमाम्यहम् ।। ५३ ।। महासेनसमोपेतामहितौघनिकृन्तनीम् । । वज्रांकुशधरां नौमि ५८ भीमसेनसमन्विताम् ।। ५४ ॥ स्तम्भाकृष्टिकरीं देवीं मायापुयीं६२ प्रकम्पिनीम् ६३ । २६४ महाक्रोधसमोपेतां पूतनाम्रातिकेश्वरे ।। ५५ ।। गदाहलायुधां५ नौमि ताडनाकृष्टिकारिकाम् । २६७ २६६ ।। भग्ननासां राजगृहे महाकर्णसमन्विताम् ॥ ५६ ॥ वज्रशक्तिधरां“ नौमि५९ अशेषफलदायिकाम् । २७० गुह्येश्वरीं महाभोगां नित्यं पशुपतेर्युताम् ॥ ५७ ॥ नेपाले संस्थितां नौमि भवघोरान्धहारिणीम् । २७४ २७७ काश्मीरे २७६ शारदां देवीं विद्येश्वरसमन्विताम् ।। ५८ ।। विद्यापीठसमोपेतां विद्याज्ञानप्रदायिकाम्” ।

sanskrit: 190 कुमारिकाखण्ड: गद्दिहरणे१ महाशक्ति८२ नौमि दुःखक्षयंकरीम् ॥ ५९ ॥ महाशरसमोपेतां पार्वतीं५ पर्वतस्थिताम् । २८६ जयेश्वरीं८७ कुलूतायां“ चक्रेशीं२८९ नग्नवाससाम् कपालीशसमोपेता भोगमोक्षफलप्रदाम् । २९३ २९० ।। ६० ।। सिंघुहारे कुलालाख्या चित्रभोगसमन्विताम् ।। ६१ ।। भैरवेन समोपेतां नौमि किल्विषनाशनीम् २९७ २९६ ३०० भोजपुर्यांीं महाचम्पां लुलन्तीं परमां कलाम् ।। ६२ ।। कैलासेन समोपेतां नौमि दुःस्वप्ननाशनीम् । ३०३ स्त्रीराज्ये अम्बिकादेवीं दुर्गमार्गक्षयंकरीम् ॥ ६३ ॥ ३०५ नटेश्वरसमायुक्तां नौमि ज्ञानार्थसिद्धये । महेन्द्रे तु महामायां खड्गहस्तां नमाम्यहं ।। ६४ ॥ महामेरुसमोपेतां महदार्तिनिकृन्तनीम् । ३०७ अन्तर्वेद्यां महारक्तां सर्वज्ञानौघदायिनीम् ।। ६५ ॥ चण्डेश्वरसमोपेतां नित्यं नौम्यपराजिताम् । ३०८ मुशलहस्तां महामायां त्रिलोचनसमायुताम् ।। ६६ । क्रूरहस्थां” महाकालीं सर्वद्वन्द्वविनाशनीम्” । । ।। महाश्मशाने ११ घण्टाले २ घण्टाली परमायुधाम् ॥ ६७ ॥ ३१२ ३ अहिनोघसमोपेतां”४ भैरवीं प्रणमामि” ताम् । •३१८ ३१५ ३१६ ३१९ चिञ्चिणीं तु कदम्बस्था चिञ्चिनीवृक्षनायिकाम् ॥ ६८ ॥ ३२० नौमि भद्रेश्वरयुता महापापक्षयंकरीम्” । ।

sanskrit: 192 कुमारिकाखण्ड: करवीरे श्मशाने तु ऊध्वकेशीं भयंकरीम् ।। ६९ ।। नग्नवाससमोपेतां४ पानपात्रधरां शुभाम् । ३२७ -३२५ ३२६ लंगुडे च्छिन्नमुण्डाख्यां क्रोधराजसमन्विताम् कर्तरीकरहस्तां तु नौमि पापक्षयंकरीम् । ३३१ ३३२ ३३० •३३३ । ३२९ ।। ७० ।। कामशरे श्मशाने तु कामलक्ष्मीं जगत्पतिम् मन्मथेन समायुक्तां त्रिकोणाकारसंस्थिताम् ३३६ ३३५ । ३३४ ।। ७१ ।। एककोणे श्मशानाख्ये त्रिकोणां रक्तवाससाम् ।। ७२ ।। त्रिशिरेण समोपेतां नृमुण्डकरभूषिताम् । ३३९ ३४० । एकवीरे श्मशाने” तु मातङ्गीं कुलनायिकाम्” ।। ७३ ।। मातङ्गीशसमोपेतां नौमि नूपुरहस्तिकाम् २ । ३४४ डोहरे तु शिवादूतीं असुरसुरवन्दिताम् ।। ७४ ।। ३४६ हयशीर्षसमोपेतां धनुबाणधरा पराम् । श्रीपर्वते महासिद्धां सिद्धमार्गविकासिनीम् ।। ७५ ।। ज्योतिलिङ्गसमोपेतां महायुधधरां शुभाम् ३४९ ओणके तु महाशक्ति अपवर्गविकासिनीम् परानन्दसमायुक्तां पुष्पचापकरोद्यताम् ५२ । ३५१ । च्छायाच्छत्रे तु चण्डिन्यां ऊध्वकेशीं महौजसीम् ऊध्वकेशसमोपेतां मन्त्रमातृकरोद्यताम् । । ।। ७६ ।। ३५३ ।। ७७ ।।

(76cd-77ab) (I salute the goddess) CaSÆinyā140 whose hair is upraised and who is very mighty. In her upraised hand she holds the mother of mantras and (she resides) in Cchāyācchatra141 with Ūrdhvakeśa (Upraised Hair) (45). (77cd-78ab)

sanskrit: 194 कुमारिकाखण्ड: ३५६ शैलपृष्ठे ६ तु त्रिजटां शैलराजसमायुताम् ।। ७८ ।। महाडमरुकहस्तां५७ च तमान्धभयहारिणीम् । ३५८ ३६२ हक्कडोक्के रुद्रशक्ति भगाख्यां सिद्धवासनाम् श्रीकण्ठसहितां नौमि अग्निज्वालाकलान्विताम् । ३६४ देवीकोट्टे महामायां इषुपाशकरान्विताम् ॥ ८० ॥ विकरालसमोपेतां संसारभयनाशनीम्५ । महामायावने ६६ घोरे चण्डकापालिनीं शुभाम् ।। ८१ ।। प्रचण्डसंयुतां नौमि सरसृङ्गकरोद्यताम् । ३६८ श्रीमच्चन्द्रपुरे रम्ये चिञ्चिनीकुलमालिनीम् ॥ ८२ ॥ लम्बोदरसमायुक्तां तडित्कोटिकरोद्यताम् ३६९ । ॥ ७९ ॥ महामलयदेशे तु महामन्त्रमहेश्वरीम् चक्रेश्वरसमोपेतां कूष्माण्डायुधहस्तिकाम् ३७१ ।। ८३ ।। । मालवे७२ तु महाकालीं कालकङ्कालहस्तिकाम् ॥ ८४ ॥ ३७३ मेघनादसमायुक्तां ज्ञानविज्ञानदायिकाम् ३७५ । श्रीमत्केदारनिलयां संस्थितारे (?) तु मालिनीम् ।। ८५ ।। ३७६ सदाशिवसमोपेतां नौम्यहं शूलहस्तिका । ३७७ महालक्ष्मीवने घोरे महालक्ष्मीं जगत्सुखाम् नौमि तुम्बुरुसंयुक्तां वरदाभयगोचराम् ३७९ । ३७८ ।। ८६ ।।
english: CHAPTER SIXTEEN 195 (I salute the goddess) Trija˜ā (who resides) in Śailaprn˜ha142 with Śailarāja (King of the Mountains). Holding a great double-headed drum, she removes the fear of the dense darkness (of phenomenal existence) (46). (78cd-79ab) I salute Rudra's energy called Bhaga (Yoni) and whose (cosmic) idea (vāsanā) is (fully) realised. Endowed with the energy of fire's flaming power, (she resides) in HakkaÆokka143 along with ŚrīkaS˜ha (47). (79cd-80ab) (I salute the goddess) Mahāmāyā who, holding in her hands an arrow and a noose, destroys the fear of transmigratory existence. (She resides) in Deviko˜˜a144 with Vikarāla (Very Horrific) (48). (80cd-81ab) I salute the auspicious (goddess) CaSÆakāpālinī (Violent Skull Bearer) who (resides) in the terrible forest of Mahāmāyā145 along with PracaSÆa (Most Violent) and carries in her upraised hands an arrow and a horn (49). (81cd-82ab) (I salute the goddess) Ciñcinīkulamālinī146 who holds in her upraised hand countless thunderbolts and (resides) in the venerable and beautiful Candrapura along with Lambodara (Big Belly) (50). (82cd-83ab) (I salute the goddess) Mahāmantramaheśvarī (Great Goddess of the Great mantra) who holds in her hand as an attribute a watermelon and (resides) in the Land of Mahāmalaya147 along with Cakreśvara (Lord of the Wheel) (51). (83cd-84ab) (I salute the goddess) Mahākālī who holds in her hand the skeleton of death. The bestower of knowledge and wisdom, she resides in Mālava148 along with Meghanāda (Sound of the Clouds) (52). (84cd-85ab) I salute (the goddess) Mālinī whose abode is the venerable Kedāra149 and who, holding a spear, (resides) in Saˆsthitāra (?) along with Sadāśiva (53). (85cd-86ab) I salute (the goddess) Mahālaknmī, the joy of the universe who, bestowing boons and fearlessness, (resides) in the terrible forest of Mahālaknmī along with Tumburu150 (54). (86cd-87ab)

sanskrit: 196 कुमारिकाखण्ड: क्षेत्रोपक्षेत्रसंदोहा: चतुःपञ्चाश कीर्तिताः ॥ ८७ ॥ ३८३ ।। ३८४ । पीठोपपीठसंदोहान् दशान्यान् कीर्तयामि ते पूजाक्रमविधानेन कथयामि समासतः ।। ८८ ।। ३८७ ३८६ चन्द्रद्वीपे कुलालाख्या विद्याराजसमन्विताम् । टङ्कटीकरहस्ता तु पश्चिमे प्रणमामि ताम् ॥ ८९ ॥ •३९२ ३९० .३९५ रक्तां” कराला”” चण्डाक्षीं महोच्छुष्मां तु भैरवीम् ॐकारे चाग्निकां नौमि जप्यमालाकरोद्यताम् ।। ९० ।। ४०० जालन्धरस्थितां९७ देवीं ३९८ कामलक्ष्मीं जगत्प्रभाम् । फलेश्वरसमोपेतां अलक्ष्मीतमनाशनीम् ।। ९१ ।। ४०२ ४०६ । ४०३ पूर्णगिर्ये महाग्रीवां मुण्डखट्वाङ्गधारिणीम् पूर्णेश्वरसमायुक्ता वन्देऽह सर्वमङ्गलाम् ।। ९२ ।। ४११ मनोद्भवां कामरूपे काद्यखट्वाङ्गहस्तिकाम् । कामेश्वरसमोपेतां नित्यं नौम्यपराजिताम् ॥ ९३ ॥ ४१३ तिस्रपीठे त्रिभुवनां त्रिदशाधिपतीश्वरीम् । कपालदण्डहस्तां तु वरदां विश्वरूपिणीम् ।। ९४ ।।१५ •४१७ कृतिवाससमोपेतां चामुण्डा मुण्डधारिणीम् । ४२१ एकाम्रे ९ संस्थितां देवीं नमाम्यशुभहारिणीम् ।। ९५ ।। ४२३ अग्निकेन समोपेता? क्षुरधारकरार्पिताम् । कामकोट्टे ४४ मोक्षलक्ष्मीं २५ नमामि श्रीविवृद्धये ४२६ ।। ९६ ।। ।
english: CHAPTER SIXTEEN 197 The Last Ten Sites (Thus),151 fifty-four meeting grounds (saˆdoha), primary and secondary fields have been extolled. I will tell you of ten other meeting grounds, primary and secondary sacred seats. I will speak of them in brief, in accord with the prescription laid down for the liturgy (pūjākrama). (87cd-88) I salute (the goddess) called Kulālā (Potter Woman)152 who holds in her hand an axe and (who resides) in Candradvīpa153 in the west along with Vidyārāja (King of Wisdom)154 (55). (89) 155I salute (the goddess) Agnikā in (the sacred seat of) Oˆkāra.156 She is the Bhairavī Mahocchunmā who holds in her upraised hand a rosary. Her eyes wrathful (caSÆāknī), she is red (raktā) and horrific (karālā)157 (56). (90) (I salute) the goddess Kāmalaknmī (Wealth of Passion), who is the light of the universe. She destroys the darkness of misfortune (alaknmī) and resides in Jālandhara, along with Phaleśvara (the Lord of the Fruit)158 (57). (91) I salute (the goddess) Mahāgrīvā (Great Neck) who, carring a severed head and an ascetic's staff, is everything auspicious and (resides) in PūrSagirya along with PūrSeśvara (the Full Lord) (58). (92) I constantly salute (the goddess) Aparājitā (Unconquered)159 who holds a skull (kādya) and ascetic's staff and, born of the mind, (resides) in Kāmarūpa along with Kāmeśvara (59). (93) (I salute) the omniform (goddess) Tribhuvanā (Three Worlds),160 the mistress of the gods who, holding a skull and a staff, bestows boons and (resides) in Tisrapī˜ha (60).161 (94) I salute the goddess CāmuSÆā who removes all that is inauspicious.162 Holding a severed head, (she resides) in Ekāmra along with Krtivāsa163 (61). (95) In order to develop the power of sovreignty (śrī), I salute (the goddess) Moknalaknmī (Wealth of Liberation)164 in whose hand is a razor165 and who resides in Kāmako˜˜a along with Agnika (62). (96)

sanskrit: 198 कुमारिकाखण्ड: ४२९ अस्वरां ँ तु महादेवीं “ नित्यमर्बुदवासिनीम् अर्बुदेश्वरसंयुक्तां नौमि विघ्नार्तिहारिणीम् ।। ९७ ।। हिरण्यपुरसंस्था तु परां शिवसमायुताम् । । ज्ञानपुस्तकहस्तां३३ तु परमार्थफलप्रदाम् ।। ९८ । ४३८ ४४० ४३५ ।। ९९ ।। क्षेत्रोपक्षेत्रसंदोहे स्थिता भूचक्रमातरः । क्षेत्रपालसमोपेताः” कीर्तयेद् यः समाहितः प्रातरुत्थाय मन्त्रज्ञ:०२ स्वप्नकालेऽथवा ४३ सुधीः । आद्यपीठे ४ क्रमाग्रे तु योगे समयमण्डले ॥ १०० ॥ युक्तोऽपि पातकैर्घोरैर्देवीनां सम्मतो भवेत् ४४४ ४४८ ४४५ ४४७ । पितृहा मातृहन्ता च ब्रह्महा गोघ्न एव च ।। १०१ ।। ४५० ४५१ ब्रुणहा पशुहन्ता वा पापिष्टो गुरुतल्पगः । वीरद्रव्यापहारी च प्रमादात् समयच्युतः ।। १०२ ॥ मन्त्राचारविलुप्तात्मा पीठानां ४ कीर्तनादपि ४५५ । सर्वपातकनिर्मुक्तो नैव पश्यति दुर्गतिम् ॥ १०३ ॥ ४५८ । यः पुनः““ शुद्धभावात्मा त्रिकाल परिकीर्तयेत् । प्राप्नोति चिन्तितान् कामान् मातॄणां वल्लभो भवेत् ॥ १०४ ॥ कुण्डे वा मण्डले वापि प्रतिमायां पटेऽपि वा । ४६८ ४७३ लिङ्गे दक्षिणमूर्ती वा जलमध्यगतोऽपि वा ।। १०५ ।। त्रिकालमेककाल वा य: पठेत् सुसमाहितः । विषशस्त्रजलाग्निभ्यो' व्याधिभूतग्रहैरपि ।। १०६ ॥ ४७५ ४७६ अजितः सुचिरं कालं जीवते निरुपद्रवः । सबीजं साधयेत् सम्यक् सफलं नात्र संशयः ॥ १०७ ॥ निष्फलं बीजरहितं ७८ अरण्ये ४९ रोपित यथा ।
english: CHAPTER SIXTEEN 199 I salute the great goddess Asvarā166 who removes the pain of the obstacles (of life) and resides perpetually in Arbuda167 along with Arbudeśvara (63). (97) 168(I salute the goddess) Parā (the Supreme) who, carring in her hand the book of knowledge, bestows the fruit of the Supreme Reality and resides along with Śiva in HiraSyapura169 (64). (98) The Mothers of the Wheel of the Earth (bhūcakra), along with the guardians of the field,170 reside in the primary and secondary fields and meeting grounds (saˆdoha). The knower of mantra who, attentive, rising (from sleep) in the morning, praises them in the First Sacred Seat, in front of the Krama (kramāgre) within the MaSÆala of the Rule (samayamaSÆala)171 in (a state of) union (yoga), or the wise man who does so even when asleep, is honoured by the goddesses, even though he has committed terrible sins.172 (99-101ab) O beloved, by praising the sacred seats, (even) one who has fallen from the practice of mantra never sees misfortune and is freed of all sin. (This is true even for one) who has killed his father, murdered his mother, slain a Brahmin, a cow or a foetus, killed animals or who, the most sinful of men, has had sex with his teacher's wife. (He may even be one who has) stolen the sacrificial substances of the heroes, or who, through negligence, has fallen from the Rule or the practice of mantra. (101-103) Again, one who is pure by nature and praises (the sacred sites all the) three times (of the day)173 gets the things he desires and sets his mind on and is the beloved of the Mothers.174 (104) He who, well-attentive, reads (this hymn to the Mothers) in the presence of a firepit (kuSÆa), in front of a maSÆala, statue or even a cloth (with an image of the deity), a Li‰ga, or a propitious idol175 or standing in water, during the three times (of day) or (just) at one, is not overcome by poison, weapons, water, fire, disease, ghosts or (inauspicious) planets. Unconquered, he lives long, free of troubles. (105-107ab) (If the hymn is recited) with the seed-syllables, one attains (one's goal) properly and (one's efforts are) certainly fruitful. Devoid of the seed-syllables it is fruitless, like (seed) planted in a jungle. (107cd-108ab)

sanskrit: 200 ४८१ •४८२ कुमारिकाखण्ड: अट्टहासात् समारभ्य यावत् ४ २ हाटकं पुरम् ॥ १०८ ॥ त तावद् मन्त्रान्वयो ह्येष अणिमादिफलप्रदः श्रीनाथ उवाच ४८३ । अट्टहासादिपीठाणां हेमपीठान्तकावधिः ।। १०९ ।। तावत् पीठेषु सर्वेषु अशक्तोऽबीजपञ्चके । मातृकूटसमायोगात् तदुपायं वदस्व मे ।। ११० ।। श्रीवक्रा उवाच ४८५ अट्टहासादिपीठेषु कृत्वा वै दीपपञ्चकम् । तथैव मातृहृदयं हेमकूटस्य उच्चरेत् ।। १११ ॥ आद्यन्तोच्चारयोगेन सर्वे मातृकुले गताः । ४८७ आद्यन्तकरणं योग“ सबीजकरणोत्तमम् ।। ११२ ।। अशक्तानां समाख्यातं श्रीगृहे तस्य सांप्रतम् । तस्माद् भुक्तिश्च मुक्तिश्च पीठानां कीर्तनाद् भवेत्” ।। ११३ ।। ४९३ आधाराः स्तवराजस्य प्रणवाः पूर्वपश्चिमे ४ । । गुप्तोच्चारकृते सिद्धिर्यदि योगी च मन्त्रवित् ॥। ११४ ॥ ४९६ महाभये”“ समुत्पन्ने कपिलागोमयेन तु । अष्टाष्टविधानेन”“ कारयेद्”” वृत्तमण्डलम् ५०० ।। ११५ ॥ शिवरत्नं तथान्येषु एकान्ते यागमन्दिरें ५०१
english: CHAPTER SIXTEEN 201 The series of mantras (mantrānvaya), beginning with A˜˜ahāsa and ending with the town Hā˜aka (i.e. HiraSyapura),176 bestows as its fruit (the eight yogic powers) starting with the power to make oneself small at will. (108cd-109ab) Śrīnātha said: (The adept) is powerless in all the sacred seats starting with A˜˜ahāsa and ending with Hemapī˜ha (i.e. HiraSyapura) (when) the Five Syllables are not present (in their mantras) because they are not linked with the Peak syllable of the Mothers. Tell me the remedy for this. (109cd-110) The venerable (goddess) Vakrā said: Having fashioned the Five Lamps (dīpapañcaka) in the sacred seats starting from A˜˜ahāsa, one should, in the same way, utter the Heart of the Mothers (mātrhrdaya) of the Golden Peak (hemakū˜a). By the conjunction of the utterance of (the seed-syllables) at the beginning and the end all the (sites and the rest) merge into the aggregate (kula) of the Mothers. (111-112ab) The union (yoga), which is the instrument (i.e. the Five PraSavas) at the beginning and end (of mantras) and which is the most excellent manner of infusing seed-syllables (sabījakaraSa) (into them) in the Venerable House (śrīgrha) (of the Kubjikā Tantras), has now been explained for those who are powerless, by virtue of which (the adept enjoys) worldly benefits (bhoga) and (attains) liberation by praising the sacred seats. (111-113) The PraSavas at the beginning and the end (pūrvapaścima) are the foundations of (this) the King of Hymns (stavarāja). One (attains) success (siddhi) and the yogi (becomes) a knower of mantra when (mantras) have been uttered in secret.177 (114) The Ritual When great fear arises,178 one should cause to fashion a circular maSÆala in accord with the prescribed method of eight times eight (parts)179 with the dung of a brown speckled cow (kapilā). (115) (This maSÆala is called) Śiva's Jewel (śivaratna). (It should be fashioned) in a solitary place in a pavilion where a fire sacrifice is performed (yāgamandira) and in other similar (places). (116ab)

english: CHAPTER SIXTEEN 203 Supplying a seat for it (in the form of the) syllable AI¤ by which the base (kanda) is marked, a jar filled with the sacrificial substance of Heroes is placed in the middle (of the maSÆala). When this has been done, (the maSÆala should be worshipped) by attending to the King of Hymns, the adepts (sādhaka) and spiritual sons (putraka) with fragrant white flowers, well-smeared with vermilion and incenses that smell of sandalwood and the like, pleasing meat, offerings of food and drink etc. and with auspicious lamps of many kinds.180 (116cd-119ab) (The officiant) should himself deposit the letter (known as) the Great Body (mahāpiSÆa)181 on (his own) hands and body. (119) The Sacrifice of the Sacred Seats should be performed with a body that bears (this) seed-syllable (piSÆa). In the centre one should worship the golden (sacred seat i.e. HiraSyapura), which is the last one and bestows all that one desires. (120) The rest (should be worshipped) in the reverse order up to (the first which is) A˜˜ahāsaka. Sacrifice is offered to the sacred seats (by uttering their mantras) beginning with (the utterance) 'venerable site' (śrīpura) and ending with 'pādu'182. (121) All the lords of the primary and the secondary sacred seats and meeting grounds as well as those of the fields, primary and secondary, serve as doors to Śiva's sacred seat, which is in the middle. (122) Conjoined (in this way) to Śiva (Pretanātha, lit. Lord of Ghosts) they save (their devotees) by virtue of Śiva's pervasive presence (vyāpti). Established there and worshipped, mantras linked with ordered ritual action (kriyāmārgāvalambaka) bestow knowledge to all (when), auspicious, libations are offered to them with devotion. (123-124ab) Thus (one should make) every effort * * *183 HairaSya is the most excellent of sacred seats. (124cd) When the rite of adoration (pūjā) is performed there regularly (nityam), (the adept) gets everything he wants. (124-125ab) The sacred seats are located externally (on the circumference of the maSÆala) in the primary and intermediate directions. In due order, one should place the great sacred seat in this way, in the location of the womb on the seat in the centre (of the maSÆala). One should (then symbolically) transform (parivartayet) the sixty-four lamps into sacred seats.184 (125cd-126)

sanskrit: 204 ५३६ कुमारिकाखण्डः ५३७ अहोरात्रोषितो—३५ भूत्वा स्वपेकाकी सुयन्त्रितः । ब्रह्मचारीव्रतस्थश्च पिशितालिविवर्जितः ॥ १२७ ॥ -५३८ तत्र जप्यं प्रकर्तव्यं मात्रत्रिंशतिजं यतः । प्रभाते ३९ विमले ४० मन्त्री वीरभोज्यं तु कारयेत् ॥ १२८ ॥ ५४२ ततः क्षमापयेत् पीठान् निर्विघ्नस्तु ततो मन्त्री प्रणिपत्य मुहुर्मुहुः ५४३ ५४४ -५४५ । सर्वं भवति सिद्धिदम् ।। १२९ ।। ५४७ उपसर्गग्रहादीनि यक्षकूष्माण्डगुह्यकाः । शत्रोरुत्कटदेशे तु राजाभङ्गे विशेषतः ।। १३० ॥ मुच्यते ४९ स“ उपसर्गेभ्यो' धनधान्यमवाप्नुयात् । परोपघाटकृत्येषु मारणोच्चाटनादिषु ।। १३१ । ५५० पापपङ्काद् हि मुच्येत निर्मलं वास्त्र ५३ वर्तते । पीठाना ५४ क्रमयोगेन पापात्मा न पुनर्भवेत् ।। १३२ ।। ५५६ -५५७ प्राप्नुयादभीप्सितान् कामान् मृतवत् सोऽपि यों भवेत् । जीववत्सा““ भवति“” पुत्रिणी तदभिषेचनात् ।। १३३ ।। १६१ पुत्रार्थी लभते पुत्रान् सुभगत्वमवाप्नुयात् । •५६३ । ५६४ विद्यार्थी लभते विद्यां‍ धनार्थी धनवान् भवेत् ।। १३४ ॥ •५६५ दारार्थी लभते दारा६५ रूपयौवनगर्विताम् । भूम्यर्थी लभते भूमि पानार्थी पानमाप्नुयात् ।। १३५ ॥ ज्ञानार्थी लभते ज्ञानं समयार्थी समयं लभेत् । मन्त्राराधनशीलस्तु“ जायते निरुपद्रवः ।। १३६ ।। योगाभ्यासरतो नित्यं प्राप्य सिद्धि ६९ परं व्रजेत् ' ५७० ।
english: CHAPTER SIXTEEN 205 Once (the adept) has resided (there in the sacrificial enclosure) for a night and a day (ahorātronito bhūtvā), well-controlled, he should sleep alone. Observing a vow of celibacy, (his diet should be) devoid of meat and liquor. (127) The repetition of mantra (japya) generated with (the Vidyā) of thirty-two measures should be performed there. In the pure (light) of dawn, the reciter of mantra should eat a Hero's meal (vīrabhojya) (of meat and wine). (128) Then he should propitiate the sacred seats, prostrating (before them) repeatedly. Thus the reciter of mantra (is) free of obstacles and everything gives (him) success.185 (129) He is freed from troubles (including) misfortune, (malevolent) planets, tree spirits (yakna), goblins (kūnmāSÆa) and (evil) cave-dwelling spirits (guhyaka). (He is protected) in an enemy's violent land and especially when the king is deposed. He acquires wealth and is at ease (even when he is the object of) the violent magic of others such as (incantations inducing) murder (maraSa), expulsion (uccā˜ana)186 and the like. (130-131) He is freed from the mud of sin and (remains as pure as) a clean cloth. By successive union with the sacred seats, he does not become a sinner again. (132) Even one who is (as powerless) as a corpse gets the things he most desires. Consecrated with that, (one's) daughter becomes a mother (jīvantavatsā)187. (133) The man who desires a son gets (many) sons and good fortune188. The student acquires knowledge and the man who desires wealth becomes wealthy.189 (134) The man who wants a wife gets one proud of her beauty and youth. The man who desires land gets land and he who wants drink, gets drink. (135) The man who desires wisdom gets wisdom and he who desires the Rule, gets the Rule. He whose habit is to worship with (these) mantras is freed of (all) troubles. He who is constantly dedicated to the practice of (this) Yoga acquires yogic power (siddhi) and reaches the supreme (state). (136-137ab)

english: CHAPTER SIXTEEN 207 The Hymn to the Sacred Seats has been revealed in terms of sections (of mantras) and as (a series of) Vidyās (pādavidyāprasa‰gena). One obtains (everything, both) collectively and individually, by maintaining (one's practice) of reciting (this) mantra. (Thus) all that concerns the recitation of the Hymn in this tradition has been explained. (137cd-138) This is the (sixteenth) chapter called Concerning the venerable Hymn to the Sacred Seats. It belongs to the primordial descent into the great sacrifice of the Churning Bhairava in the tradition (anvaya) that consists of seventy million (verses) that has emerged on the Path of Meru and (extends) for more than a hundred thousand quarter (verses). It has been brought (down to earth) into the first sacred seat along the path of the Seat of Knowledge (vidyāpī˜ha). It is the ultimate purport of the Pure Six Thousand (verses vimalana˜ka) in the division beginning with `Kā' in the venerable scripture of twenty-four thousand (verses) (known as) the Svāminīmata of the Supreme Lord's command as uttered within the Tradition of the Mother (avvākrama).

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER EIGHT 1. The word prastāra — lit. ‘lay out’ — might simply be translated as ‘grid’. The term is used in this sense in other types of texts as well. Thus, for example, in treatises on musicology the same word denote a grid, diagram or 'graph' (as Lath calls it) on which the notes and śrutis are schematically represented. In his work on the Dattilam, Lath (1988: 74) explains that: 'The vrtti [commentary] on the Brhaddeśī speaks of three ways of representing the śruti [microtone] and svara [note] positions within a grāma [scale]. These were known as the three prastāras: (1) the daSÆaprastāra (2) the vīSāprastāra and (3) the maSÆalaprastāra '. In the case of this and other similar grids, letters of the alphabet are accomodated into its compartments. Mantras are formed by ‘extracting’ letters from these grids. Mantras are powerful configurations of phonemic energy. The letters from which they are constructed must be charged with the goddess’s energy for them to be effective. This is achieved by extracting the letters, as it were, from their original source, which is the goddess herself who is Speech. In this aspect the goddess assumes the form of various configuration of letters that are projected into grids of corresponding shapes. The Kubjikā Tantras, like all other Tantras, can be considered to be treatises on mantra — mantraśāstra. In a sense this is the subject of the Tantras. Thus the common definition the Tantras supply of what Tantra is makes good sense. A Tantra, ‘expounds many matters in conjunction with mantra and yantra.’ (tanoti vipulān arthān yantramantra- samanvitān) And as yantras are essentially geometric figures into which the mantras and parts thereof representing the sonic forms of the deities are projected and worshipped, yantras are effectively extensions or spatial applications of mantras in space. Thus the grids from which the mantras of the Kubjikā Tantras are derived are extremely important. Accordingly, Mukundarāja writes in the SamP: Now (I will) describe the conventions (found in the) Manthānabhairava- tantra. There, (amongst them) first of all, comes knowledge of the prastāras and gahvaras without which there is no understanding (saˆgati) of (the meaning of the) books of the Western Tradition. atha manthānabhairavatantrasaˆketanirūpaSam | tatra prathamataƒ prastāragahvaravijñānaˆ vinā paścimāmnāyagranthasaˆgatir nāsti || We come across several prastāras in the Kubjikā sources. Mukundarāja lists the names of fourteen prastāras and fourteen gahvaras. The latter serve the same function as the former, the difference between them appears to be solely in name. Thus we find that the Meruprastāra is also called Merugahvara (KuKh

english: NOTES OF THE SANSKRIT TEXT OF CHAPTER NINE 42 The power of lightness (laghimā) is the power to free oneself from the grossness of diversity. The power of greatness (mahimā) is the power to experience the all-pervasion of consciousness. The power to make oneself heavy at will (gharimā) [which has been omitted in the above citation] is the capacity to evolve gross forms out of one’s own consciousness. The power of attainment (prāpti) is the capacity to rest within one’s own nature. The power of wilfulness (prākāmya) is the power to grasp cosmic diversity. The power of control (vaśitvā) is the power to do whatever one wishes. The power of lordship (īśitva) is the yogi’s unbroken (akhaSÆita) freedom. (PTv (KSTS edition) p. 37 fn. 74; cf. MM pp. 126-127) Note that one of the eight yogic powers is not mentioned in these verses. This is the power to make oneself heavy at will (gharimā). Also, the power of control (vaśitā) has been replaced in our text by the power of subjugation (vaśīkaraSa). Although the two terms are similar, as are the powers they denote, the latter resonates with the added implied meaning that this is a magical power. One who recites the Five PraSavas acquires not just yogic but also magical powers. Subjugation is one of the so-called Six (magical) Acts (na˜karma), although as an analysis of a large number of texts reveals, they are basically nine. According to Goudriaan (1978: 259), these are as follows: Pacification (śānti), Subjugation (vaśīkaraSa), Immobilization (stambhana), Sowing Discord (vidvenaSa), Liquidation (māraSa), Delusion (mohana), Attraction (ākarnaSa) and Acquisition (pun˜i). Concerning the act of Subjugation, see ibid. 310 ff. Finally, the attainment of the liberated condition, which is the ‘immortal abode’ and identification with Rudra, is here represented as the eighth and highest yogic power. This conception of liberation as a yogic accomplishment (siddhi) is contrary to the view of classical, Patañjali Yoga, which maintains that yogic accomplishments are attainments (siddhi) when the yogi emerges from the state of concentration but impediments for him when he is in it and hence obstacles to liberation (te samādhāv upasargā vyutthāne siddhayaƒ — Y±ū 3/37). Kashmiri Śaivites, on the contrary, support the view generally held in most Tantric traditions, and by implication in the passage we are examining, that liberation is the supreme accomplishment (parasiddhi). Similarly, according to the Buddhist Guhyasamājatantra (chapter 18). Siddhis are of two kinds. One type is ordinary (sāmānya); the example given is the power to make oneself invisible (antardhāna). The other type of accomplishment is 'most excellent’ (uttama). This the Buddhas have declared to be the attainment of Buddhahood. 72. english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER NINE 1. The goddess is addressed as 'the Lord' repeatedly through our text. See 5/28, 5/40cd, 18/77b, 26/1d, 29/1d, 31/110b, 31/116b, 38/1, 39/20b, 40/1d, 40/110d, 40/112b, 42/49d and 67/48d, and note to Sanskrit KuKh 4/38c. 2. The following passage up to 9/19ab is also found in YKh (1) (KuKh 9/2cd, 3cd, 5cd-10cd, 11cd-19ab, = YKh (1) 49/15cd, 16ab, 17ab-22ab, 22cd- 30ab). The entire section in YKh (1) of which this is a portion is called the Dvādaśaślokasūtra — the Sūtra of Twelve Verses. No mention is made in the KuKh that this is a sūtra or part of one, suggesting that the KuKh drew them from YKh (1) or from this fragment of it, possibly when it existed only as separate parts split into independent sūtras. There, the portion of these verses end with the following verse omitted here: Omniscience arises by (this) supreme knowledge alone. These are the Twelve Verses acclaimed as being in the Śāmbhava (state). paramajñānamātreSa sarvajñatvaˆ prajāyate || ity ete dvādaśa ślokāƒ śāmbhave parikīrtitāƒ | YKh (1) 49/30cd-31ab The name of the sūtra may well have been derived from its original length, but as we have it now it is more than twelve verses long. Other fragments are incorporated in the KuKh, as 11/18 ( = YKh (1) 49/1) and 11/21-23ab ( = YKh (1) 49/2-4ab). But even if the name of the sūtra is not derived from its length it is nonetheless appropriate because, divided into twelve parts, one of the names of the syllable described in this passage is Dvādaśaśloka. For the same reason it is also called the Vidyā of Twelve Syllables (Dvādaśāknarī or Dvādaśāknarikā). This seed-syllable has already been briefly discussed in the previous chapter (8/76cd-80ab) as a part of the Samayā Vidyā. Here it is discussed again in greater detail as a seed-syllable in its own right. So, just as we have two presentations here, similarly the µīkā deals with this subject twice (both times on fl. 5b). In the first instance this seed-syllable is discussed in the context of the Samayā Vidyā of which it is a part. In the second it is discussed in the context of the Kaulikavidyā which is an expanded, 42-syllable version of the Samayā Vidyā. This seed- syllable is so important that the author of the µīkā discusses it a third time (on fl. 14b) after describing Kubjikā's main visualized form, presumably implying that the former is the mantric form of the latter. It is presented there in the context of the µīka’s commentary on this section of the Dvādaśaślokasūtra. We know that the µīkā is a commentary of the version in YKh (1) because it comments on lines of the text found there that are omitted here. english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER NINE 63 51. The New Moon is the Samayā Vidyā recited in reverse — this is the ‘division of depletion’ (krnabheda). We have seen that the encapsulation by the Five PraSavas in the manner described is the process by which the bare Vidyā is ‘transformed into nectar’ (see above 8/88 ff.). This change coincides with that of the dark lunar fortnight to the bright one. In the former the goddess is fierce and devouring. In the latter, she is peaceful and nourishing. See above note to 8/42cd. 52. See 8/92cd-100; 8/110cd-113 and note for a table of correspondences. Cf. above, 9/19cd-26ab. 53. The standard thirty-two syllable Samayā Vidyā of Kubjikā becomes the forty-two syllable Vidyā by adding the Five PraSavas in front of it in the forward order and the same PraSavas to it at the end in the reverse order. This Vidyā is given in full in two places in the µīkā (fl. 7a and 53b) where it is also called the Kaula Vidyā (fl. 7a). The form of this extended form of the Vidyā as found in the µīkā (fl. 53b) is as follows: AI¤ HRĪ¤ ŚRĪ¤ KHPHRE¤ HSPHAU¤ BHAGAVATI AMBE SKHPHRE¤ SHKHPHRĪ¤ KUBJIKE HSRĀ¤ HSRĪ¤ HSRAU¤ ¦AnA¦ANAME AGHORĀMUKHE CCHRĀ¤ CCHRĪ¤ KI¦I KI¦I VICCE HSPHAU¤ KHPHRE¤ ŚRĪ¤ HRĪ¤ AI¤ This is the form of Thirty-two syllable Vidyā with the Five PraSavas according to the µīkā. The same is to be done with the form of the Thirty-two syllable Vidyā given here. 54. Concerning the six types (jāti) and their application, see 4/10cd-11ab and note 15.

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER TEN 1. Presumably, the BhairavapiSÆa is the fifth PraSava, which is called Bhairava in 9/22 and Bhairavī Vidyā in 8/104-105ab. The version extracted in these two places of this PraSava is HSRAU-U¤. The letter R is indeed located between S and AU in this seed-syllable. 2. I read this verse in this way, supporting verse 10/5. 3. VāruSī is the energy of Amā, the sixteenth digit of the moon (see note to 9/51). As the Five PraSavas placed at the beginning of the Vidyā are uttered in the forward order, the fifth PraSava is directly in contact with the beginning of the Vidyā. It is also in direct contact with the Vidyā at the end, as the PraSavas there are in the reverse order. It appears that the form of this PraSava extracted in the previous two chapters, namely HSRAU-U¤, is functional when it is not in contact in this way with the Vidyā. In the latter case it needs to be modified to HSAU-U¤. In this form it is identified with the sixteenth digit of the moon which, freed of the heating and drying brought about by the fire of the letter Ra (but cf. 9/49ab-50ab), discharges a nectar that is not consumed within the syllable itself. Thus, free to flow, the lunar Vidyā is filled by it from both sides, as it were, and so becomes the Vidyā of the Full Moon. Mantras may be ‘locked’ (kīlana) or unlocked (utkīlana) by the adition or subtraction of syllables or words (see notes of vol. 2 of the translation, appendix 2). We observed that the changes that the ‘unlocking’ of a mantra entail in the form of a mantra may have to do, to some degree at least, with the modifications a mantra undergoes in the course of its transmission. This particular PraSava is a case in point because it is liable to considerably more variation in the texts than are the other PraSavas. And HSAUŪ¤ is indeed a common variant, more common, in fact, than HSRAUU¤. 4. The power to fly in the transcendent is the liberation to which Kaulas aspire. See PTv p. 214-215. 5. Rudra’s energy is the goddess in the form of her Vidyā — Cf. YKh (1) 37/15cd-17ab quoted above in note to 8/34ab. 6. Literally ‘one who desires knowledge’. 7. Cf. the division of this Vidyā into sixteen parts recorded above in 9/30- 35. 8. The Vidyā is: BHAGAVATI GHORE HSKHPHRE¤ ŚRĪ¤ KUBJIKE SHRĀ¤ SHRĪ¤ SHRAU¤ ¥AnA¦ANAME AGHORĀMUKHI CCHĀ¤ CCHĪ¤ KI¦I KI¦I VICCE. Cf above — the main difference appears to be the omission of the letter R from the syllables CCHĀ¤ CCHĪ¤. Although this is the form of these two syllables in the KMT, we are expressly told above (8/51) that they are ‘adorned’ with this letter, implying perhaps that this is an addition. One might compare the case of Siddhalaknmī who is samayā in the KālasaˆkarnaSīmata, more generally apotropaic (pratya‰girā) elsewhere, while being everywhere the embodiment of the Absolute. 42. The Great Journey (mahāpatha) is the last journey made, to the place of its execution, by those who have vowed to commit ritual suicide to purify themselves. They must travel towards the north-east, which is Śiva’s quarter, in a straight line without altering their course, whatever the obstacle, and eat only air and water until their body drops ‘like a dry leaf’. See Mānavadharmaśāstra, 6/1/32. 43. The teachings of the Western Transmission are meant for the Age of Strife (kaliyuga). The Vidyā is the essence of the spiritual energy transmitted through them into the world by the supreme deity from the summit of existence where all things originate.

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF THE CHAPTER ELEVEN 1. The goddess begins by listing the topics dealt with in this chapter in the order in which they are discussed. 2. Monier-Williams explains that: ‘argha (often spelt arghya-) is the ‘respectful reception of a guest by offering rice, dhūrva grass, flowers, or often only water’. Brunner says that arghya is ‘especially consecrated water that one offers to the god as one would an offering to a guest as a sign of homage’ (ŚSP vol. 1 p. 58). The way the arghya is prepared according to the prescriptions of the Siddhānta Āgamas is outlined in ŚSP vol. 1 3/37-39ab. There it is considered to be of two kinds: common (sāmānya) and special (viśena). The former is used to worship the deities and beings who accompany Śiva, the main deity. The latter is used to worship Śiva himself. The main constituent of the arghya is water, which is mixed with milk, the tips of kuśa grass, flowers, sesame, flowers and white mustard. This is technically called the arghya with eight parts (an˜ā‰ga) (ŚSP vol. 1 p. 138-39). In this case (see below 11/46cd-50) the things offered along with water are more numerous and include meat, which is excluded in Siddhānta ritual. Note also that although water is offered here to the Vidyā in the maSÆala, it is not at all clear at first sight that the offering is an argha. 3. This is the forward order moving down from the top of the body to the feet. In chapter nine (8/43-84) the thirty-two syllables of the Vidyā were extracted in the reverse order, that is, in the sequence of withdrawal. See above 8/85-6ab and note. 4. The Circle of the Fourth State (turyamaSÆala) is normally the Wheel of the Command that is located in between the eyebrows (see above 3/101). In this case, however, this place is occupied by the seventh letter. Perhaps, we should understand the head here to mean the topknot and this Circle to be the Cavity of Brahmā. 5. The Command is located in the Wheel of the Command between the eyebrows. 6. Presumably, the three mentioned here are the two eyebrows and the tip of the nose. These three places form the corners of a triangle, in the centre of which is the syllable KU, which is a common abbreviation of the goddess’s name. Note that there is no mention of the eleventh syllable. This is probably because a line is missing in the text. This syllable is KE. 7. The main topic of this chapter is the drawing of the KramamaSÆala and its use in conjunction with the Samayā Vidyā to worship the goddess in the Krama. The rite of adoration of the KramamaSÆala requires the deposition of this Vidyā on the body. Similarly, its seed form, the Khecarī Vidyā HSKHPHRE¤ is projected into the Wheels within the body and beyond. Accordingly, the deposition of the Vidyā on the body along with that of the Khecarī Vidyā is taught

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER ELEVEN 137 67. YKh (1) (18/16-24) lists the benefits of repeating the Vidyā in the same ascending order in accord with the number of times it is repeated as follows. 108: purity and the removal of obstacles. 1,000: penetration by the Gesture. 3,000: The dawning of the power of Speech and the Supreme Wheel of Energies; attainment of knowledge. 4,000: mastery of Yoga. 5,000: a great gain. 6,000: the adept becomes a king. 7,000: the City is aroused. 8,000: the adept acquires all wealth. 9,000: accomplishment of one's task. 10,000: one becomes strong. 20,000: checking of an enemy army and victory. 30,000: wealth (laknmī) of kingdom, the conquest of the eight Vetālas. 40,000: good luck in hunting and gambling. 50,000: the power to shrink (aSimā) by the Command. 60,000: the power to increase in size. 70,000: the attainment of one's desire. 80,000: the power to move trees, paralysis, cause mountains to fall and explode stones. 90,000: the planets, deities and the like that exert a negative influence are made to fall with the sound HU¤. One becomes a lion (king) (siˆhaka) and can change his form at will. 100,000: flight. 68. The text tells us that the adept should repeat this Vidyā in conjuction with niśācāra — ‘the nocturnal practice’, which involves ritual sexual intercourse (see notes to 6/5, 15/39cd-50 and 16/5). It is also called the Kaula vow and is described below in 15/39cd-50. The ŚM prescribes instead that this should be done in conjuction with the inner practice of the Yoga of Stillness (concerning which see intro. vol 1, p. 100 ff.). 69. ŚM: One should repeat the Vidyā in a cremation ground, (under) a solitary tree, on the bank of a river or a crossroad, in a deserted house, O mistress of the gods, or at the confluence of a river, O mistress of the heroes. (One should repeat it) in a sacred seat, sacred field or a meeting ground. śmaśāne ekavrkne vā nadītīre.atha catvare | śūnyāgāre ca deveśi saˆgame vīranāyike || pī˜he knetre ca saˆdohe vidyājāpyaˆ samārabhet | ŚM 9/94-95ab 70. For a commentary on this verse, and concerning the householder, see intro. vol 1, p. 513 ff.. 71. The First Seat (ādipī˜ha) is OÆÆiyāna. Also called Oˆkāra, it is the original sacred seat from which all the others originate. 72. The following chapter continues with the same topic as this one, giving the impression that the division between these two chapters is artificial. Indeed, the correspondences with sections of the same chapter nine of the ŚM continue. These will be noted as we come to them.

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER TWELVE 1. This verse is also ŚM 9/93. The reader is referred to the Sanskrit edition for variants here and in other cases where correspondences are found in other sources. It appears that our text is referring to the Samayā Vidyā here as that of the goddess Mahantārikā who is indeed a form of the goddess Kubjikā. This is perplexing because Mahantārikā is also treated separately with her own Vidyā and visualized forms. But there can be no doubt that the identification made here between the Samayā Vidyā and Mahantārikā is intentional. In the previous chapter, the goddess, with reference to her Samayā Vidyā, says that she is the Mahantārikā Vidyā (see 9/26 above). The context in both the ŚM and the KuKh is concerned with extolling the Samayā Vidyā and the right conduct one should take care to maintain while practicing it. 2. Concerning Kubjikā's alchemical and medicinal connection (rasāyana), see note to 6/135. 3. Vāgbhava, that is, the syllable AI¤, is amongst the most important seed-syllables for all schools of Śaivism. It is especially important for Kaulas as the seed-syllable of creation and representation of the triangular Yoni of the goddess. Of all the Kaula schools, the Western Tradition of the goddess Kubjikā has centred on this syllable in a particularly special way. In this sense, the teachings or school concerned with Vāgbhava is this one. 4. The Nityātantra is linked to the worship of Kālī in the KMT. Kāmeśvarī is called Nityā (KMT 10/41c). YKh (1) refers to a group of Nine Nityās (navanityā). Thus, ‘Nityā’ is a generic name for a Kaula goddess. So, presumably, the Nityā Tantras are Kaula Tantras centred on the worship of a goddess. 5. Concerning the Lākulīśa Pāśupatas, the Siddhānta, the Vāma Tantras of Tumburu Bhairava, and the GāruÆa Tantras, see Dyczkowski 1986: 19 ff. 6. Penetration by the Vidyā gives knowledge of all the systems and Tantras because they emanate, along with all the mantras and sacred sites, from the goddess's body. By projecting the Vidyā onto his own body, the adept transforms it into that of the goddess. As he rises through this body, he traverses and contains all the states and levels of being that correspond to all the schools emitted and contained in the goddess’s body, from the Buddhist at her feet to the highest — the paścimāmnāya — which, above her head, is above all the others. 7. The goddess is frequently said to be sixfold. The Vidyā is therefore also ‘sixfold’. In a general sense this is because it is has six limbs, as do all major mantras. In a special, specific sense it is sixfold because it is the essence of the Krama, which is divided into six groups of mantras. 8. The optimal progressive development through the lower teachings to this, the highest one, takes place over seven lifetimes. english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER THIRTEEN 1. The question here is that if Śiva is at all known to us and is somehow present in the world, even if he is God, is he not thereby affected by the same contingencies that affect mortal beings, indeed, any finite entity? If Śiva losses his transcendental being by his immanent presence in the world, how can he regain his power to act as God, that is, his divine agency, subject as he would be, it seems, to those factors that condition the power to act of every living being? The question poses a serious problem, because Śiva’s presence in the world is not as a disembodied, omnipresent being. His transcendental being is in contact with the world, but at its very summit as the unconditioned ‘beyond’. At the same time, this emptiness is the ‘space’, within which all existent things move and have their being and is, by the same token, the ‘space’ within them as their essential, unconditioned nature. This ‘space’ although unconditioned and hence not identifiable in phenomenal terms, is not impersonal. It is God who is called Śiva, although he is the ‘Nameless’ (anāma). If he is the Self, the most authentic and fundamental identity of every living being, the questions posed in the next verse naturally arise. 2. AvarSa literally means either ‘the letter A’ or, as is the case here, ‘devoid of letters’. The goddess is similarly decribed as ‘avarSā’ and ‘varSavāhinī’, that is, ‘she who is devoid of letters and who transports the letters’. In the former aspect the goddess is merged in the transcendent god and so both are ‘devoid of letters’. They are, in other words, at the transcendental level beyond Speech. At the next level down, at the edge, as it were, of manifestation, the goddess emerges as the energy of the will which spontaneously differentiates itself into the triangle of energies. This, the fertile womb of the goddess, contains the primal, archetypal energies of Speech. These are, on the one hand, her own energies and on the other, the fifty limbs, as it were, of the body of Śiva, the Assembly of Sounds (śabdarāśi). These energies and their possessors couple in various ways to assume the forms of the manifest world of Speech and its objects which the goddess 'transports' and hence generates, in her downward creative flow. 3. This and the following four verses describe Śiva’s supreme state, free of all phenomenal manifestation when he rests tranquil within the Voidness of his own infinite nature. This condition is represented by the letter A, which denotes Akula. Akula is the absolute which is not within the sphere of the aggregate of its energies — Kula. These energies are represented by the sixteen vowels. Identified with the sixteen digits of the moon, they increase and decrease in accord with the rhythm of phenomenal existence. In his pure, unconditioned and most essential nature, Śiva is perpetually free of this activity. This may simply be because he could not read the manuscript of his source; possibly he chose to alter the text for his own purposes. english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER FOURTEEN 1. See intro. vol 1, p. 518 ff. for a commentary on the first six verses of this chapter. This chapter is also found in the TS, KMT, KuKauM and ±SS. The details of the correspondences between these sources are found in the notes to the Sanskrit text which has been collated with them. 2. The KuKauM reads dhīra- ‘one who is firm’ for vīra- ‘hero’ and the condition he seeks is ‘dhīratva’ — (firmness). The ‘Hero’ is a man who has taken Kaula initiation and whose KuSÆalinī is therefore awake. His condition is contrasted to that of the paśu literally (tethered) beast or sacrificial victim, that is, the fettered soul. In a more specific sense, the paśu is not just the individual subject to bondage (pāśa); he is one who has not taken Kaula initiation. Jayaratha quotes a Tantra in his commentary on the TĀ (29/73cd-75ab) as saying: One should make an effort to avoid Siddhāntins, VainSavas, Bauddhas, Vedāntins and those who follow the Smārta schools (smārtadarśana) because they are said to be paśus. The verse we are examining implies that vīras need to develop further, not to attain liberation as if it were a different state, but rather to attain a full realisation of the initiated condition which, as one of identity with the goddess, is one of vīratva literally ‘hero-hood’. If this interpretation is correct, the word ‘vīra’ should also mean ‘deity’. Although the usage of this term in this sense is not common, it does occur. The Buddhist Ekālavīratantra, for example, is concerned with the worship of the god — vīra — Ekāla. The term ekavīra refers to the male deity when worshipped alone without his consort in ‘the state of a solitary hero’ (ekavīrabhāva). The YKh of the MBT prescribes a long series of rituals and mantras for the worship of the goddess Tripurabhairavī alone as Ekavīrā. The goddess of Kula (Kuleśvarī) in the early Kālī Tantras known to Abhinavagupta — such as the Devyāyāmala and the Jayadrathayāmala, — is Kālasa‰karnaSī, who can be worshipped in the centre of a maSÆala described in the TĀ (29/69-70ab) either alone (ekavīrā), in conjunction with it (cakrayuktā) or as a part of the couple within it (cakrayāmalagā). Clearly, the term denotes the deity as one of a couple when worshipped alone. The condition of the Hero in its most complete form is therefore that of the deity itself. The later Kaula Tantras developed these conceptions further and took a more positive attitude. The paśu, although not an initiate, may perform Vedic rituals or exert himself in the practice of a pious VainSava (vainSavācāra) or Śaiva (śaivācāra). However, in order to do this he must observe such a high degree of purity that some of the later texts and their commentators maintained that is not possible in the present Kali Age. english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER FOURTEEN 276 energies of the weapons are all essentially the same energy of the goddess, the same is true of the inner energies of the consorts. One view is that when celebrating Kaula rites, the adept should be assisted by a consort — dūtī. According to Jayaratha, ‘no rite can be celebrated with success according to the Kula method without a dūtī’ (commentary on TĀ 1/13). But here the view is, as with the ascetic’s weapons, the consort need not be externally present if the energy within the adept’s body which she arouses, and which is her most essential nature, is functioning. 116. The adept and his consort imitate the primordial couple, Śiva and Śakti. By uniting, they participate in their union. Thus they mend the original split which brought about their individual identities. But in order for this to happen they must share a proximity to each other in consciousness which is close enough for their union to become fusion. They must be closely related just as Śiva and Śakti are even when they are separated. The goddess originates from the god as one half of his body or as an emanation of his power. Thus she is sometimes portrayed as his daughter, as is the case with Bhadrakālī who in the MārkaSÆeyapurāSa figures as Rudra's daughter, or Mrtyukanyā, who is Yama's daughter. According to the myths of the Paścimāmnāya, she is Mālini, born of the god Śabdarāśi. At the same time, she is the Mother of all, including the god. Sometimes the goddess is the god's sister. Durgā, for example, is said to have been incarnated as the eighth issue of Devāki, KrnSa's mother, and so she is his sister. 117. The reward of those who unite with a Kaula consort is the sacrificial food they eat together. By eating it the votary attains yogic and magical powers, including the liberating power of mystical flight. But in order to do so he must set aside considerations of caste and status that prevent eating together.

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER FIFTEEN 1. The first thirteen verses of this chapter correspond to TS 15/230-243ab, KMT 25/155cd-166ab, ±SS 50/35cd-46ab and KuKauM 7/188-198. Verse 15/14 loosely corresponds to KMT 25/170 and ±SS 50/50. 2. KMT: The Mother is power, well established, the womb of the universe. ±SS and KuKauM: The Mother is power, well established; she is called supreme (parākhyā). 3. KMT et al: And so she is called the Mother and said to be the Supreme Goddess. 4. Similarly, in the HT (1/5/18ab) we read: ‘The consort (prajnā) is called 'daughter' because she extracts good qualities (duhanāt)’ (guSasya duhanāt prajñā duhitā ca nigadyate). The word ‘duhitr’ — ‘daughter’ — is correctly derived from the root duh which means ‘to milk, squeeze or extract’ in the sense of extracting or drawing out something from something else. Thus duhitr is the ‘milker’ or ‘one draws milk from her mother’ (Monier-Williams). In this case, the daughter meant here may or may not be the adept’s daughter. But whether she is or not, the dūtī is the embodiment of the energy KuSÆalinī. Like the milkmaid who milks the cow or the daughter who milks the mother, she extracts the spiritual energy of all things, which is their essence, and makes it available to the adept who is nourished by it. 5. KMT et al: She is the womb, supreme and subtle / and is not created by anything else. TS: She is born along with the Self (utpannā sātmanā saha). 6. The First Digit of the Moon is the first and foremost of all the energies (ādya- or ādi- śakti). Identified with the Transmental, it is the one universal energy that assumes the countless forms of all the energies into which it forms itself and that thus develop out of it, as do the digits of the moon from the first. 7. The Cave, as we have seen, is the Void in centre of the maSÆala, the core of reality. Here the goddess is emanated from the transcendent. But this does not mean she is created from it, rather, she arises spontaneously. As the source of all things, she also generates herself, as it were. When she has emerged out of the Void in the Centre, she unites with Śiva, who is that same Void. The universe and the teachings emanate from the emission (visarga) that comes about by their union. 8. Two types of women are considered to be particularly suitable as dūtīs. One are women to whom the adept is closely related; the other, women of low caste. Normally, union with such women is considered to be polluting. But Kaula practice is based on the insight that the observance of the norms established on the basis of the values of conventional Brahminical Dharma is not liberating. Indeed, even those who maintain their importance agree that one who observes them does not acrue any benefit by observing them, although he sins if he does not. Women

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER FIFTEEN 286 begins declares: ‘Yoga is the checking of the activity of the mind’ (yogaś cittavrttinirodhaƒ). One could cite countless texts from a wide range of schools in support of this view. The following passage from the Amrtabindūpaninad (verse 2-4) is typical: It is indeed the mind (manas) that is the cause of man's bondage and liberation. The mind that is attached to sense objects leads to bondage, while dissociated from sense objects it tends to lead to liberation. Since liberation is predicated by the mind devoid of desire for sense objects, therefore the mind should always be made free of such desire by the seeker after liberation. When the mind with its attachment for sense objects is annihilated and is fully checked within the Heart and thus realises its own essence, then that supreme state is attained. The mind should be controlled until it merges into the Heart. This is knowledge (jñāna) and this is meditation (dhyāna). All else is (mere) sophistry. The theory that is at the root of the practice of what one could call Kaula Yoga agrees with the basic principle that the activity of the mind engaged in the production of thought constructs is binding. Both approaches agree that liberation can only be achieved when this activity ceases. However, the former approach maintains that, as the activity of the mind is due to attachment to the objects of the senses, the Yogi should strive to regulate his contact with them. Here the two approaches diverge. Kaula Yoga maintains that the mind is not disturbed by the sense objects themselves but by attachment to them; therefore there is no need to check the movement of the mind amidst the senses. Indeed, it is better to let it roam freely amongst them without attachment. 29. According to 11/91cd-92ab above, the adept must constantly repeat the goddess’s Samayā Vidyā when practicing in this way. It is understandable therefore that the fruit of this practice is the same as that attained by repeating the Vidyā 100,000 times (see above 11/85cd-89ab). 30. All the MSs read nāma saˆgamamatsadhā which makes no sense. 31. The Śaivasiddhānta Āgamas are, in theory, supposed to be divided into four sections (pāda) concerned with the four major topics suggested by their name, that is, ritual (kriyāpāda), right conduct (caryā), Yoga (yogapāada) and knowledge (vidyāpāda). The prestige of this fourfold scheme was such that it was accepted as a feature of a ‘complete’ Tantra by other schools as well, including this one. Thus, the claim is made (if only by a mere reference) that this and other Kubjikā Tantras are laid out in the same pattern (see below 65/37cd-8ab). Moreover, the observance of vows is a major topic of the caryāpāda sections of those Siddhānta Āgamas that have one. See intro. vol 1, p. 510.

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER SIXTEEN 1. Concerning the Lord of Yogis and his way of life, see above, note on 5/43. 2. The practice of begging alms (bhiknācaryā) is effectively the Vow of Knowledge (vidyāvrata) explained in the previous two chapters. Concerning the interiorization of the eight centres of Kula and how these are related to inner experiences and ‘places’ see above, 14/77-81ab. The yogi goes to these ‘places’ within his Yogic body to beg from the Mothers who reside there the alms that highten his spiritual condition and give him special powers (siddhi). This has already been explained. Now the goddess wants to know about the mantras the adept should utter marking each station of his inner and outer pilgrimage. In particular, the goddess wants to know the most secret Vidyās relating to the deities, that is, the ones that contain the convention of the secret Kaula language. The Vidyās praise the metaphysical attributes of the Yoginīs who reside in these places and request their spiritual food. Each Vidyā begins with two syllables of this secret language, which indicate the identity and inner location of the Yoginī. Uttering these Vidyās, the adept shows that he is privy to these secrets and hence is an initiate who is fit to receive the grace of the spiritual nourishment the Mothers can offer. 3. This is the language of the Kula Path (see below 42/26cd ff.). It is also called the language of Yoga (42/49ab) or the language of Kula (kulabhānā). Like the knowledge of gesture and mantra, knowledge of this language is a sign of the adept’s attainment (KMT 5/19cd-20ab). The most common form of this language in the Kubjikā Tantras are mantras ‘in reverse’, that is, the practice of presenting the syllables of a mantra in the reverse order to conceal their true form. An example is found in chapter seven of the KMT where the Samayā Vidyā and its six limbs are presented in this way. There are numerous other examples throughout the Kubjikā Tantras. We have seen that the Samayā Vidyā is also presented in the reverse order above (10/11-12), although this is not said there specifically to be the form of the mantra in the Kula language. In our text this term has been reserved for a different form of this language. This consists of code words that together make up the sequence of codes (bhānākrama). Sixty-eight code words of this sort are presented below in chapter 42 where the meaning of some of them is explained. They are also found, for example, in the CMSS and other sections of the MBT. Most of these code words are effectively abbreviations formed from the first syllable of the word they denote. Abbreviations of this kind are commonly used not only as codes but also for the sake of brevity. Some of them are of common usage and their meaning is well known (see above, note to 2/28).

sanskrit: श्रीवक्रा उवाच' ।। ॐ स्वस्ति ।। श्रीनाथपादुकाभ्यां नमः। श्रीगणेशाय नमः । मन्थान भैरवतन्त्रे कुमारिकाखण्डे सप्तदशानन्दः अन्वयस्य तु यत् सारं दिव्यौघे संप्रदर्शितम् । षोडशात्मकसंकेतमधुना कथयामि ते ।। १ ।। सन्तान मेरुमार्गे च अन्वयं तत्र देवता' । निर्गमं चैव ॐकारे सिद्धान्वये प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ २ ॥ तुष्णीदेव गुहावासी वृक्ष' चैव ं कदम्बकम् । १३ सिंहसंकेतक चैव अव्वा च गुहवासिनी ॥ ३ ॥ गृह चन्द्रपुर प्रोक्तं भेदं मन्थानभैरवम् । गोत्रम् अमरिका देवी वाममार्गे प्रकल्पिता ।। ४॥ अन्वये प्रत्ययं” सारं अधिकार तु कोङ्कणे । जन्मब्रह्मशिला सिद्धस्थितिर्वै” कामरूपके २५ ॥ ५ ॥ कीर्तिश्चिञ्चिणिवृक्ष तु सिद्धिश्चैव तु सागरे । २८ तुष्टोऽहं तस्य देवेश यो जानाति कुलक्रमम् ॥ ६ ॥ अय‍ तु कौलिकं सारं कुलक्रमविनिर्गतम् । षोडशात्मकसंकेत ज्ञात्वा चान्वयिको भवेत् ॥ ७ ॥
english: CHAPTER SEVENTEEN The Venerable Sūtra of the Lineage (śrīsantānasūtra). The Sixteen Conventions1 The venerable (goddess) Vakrā said: The essence of the Lineage (anvaya) within the Divine Current (divyaugha) has been revealed. Now I will tell you the sixteenfold convention. (1) 1) The Lineage (santāna) is on the Path of Meru.2 2) There, the lineage (anvaya) is the deity.3 3) What has emerged (nirgama)4 is in (the sacred seat called) Oˆkāra and is said to be in 4) the lineage of Siddhas.5 (2) 5) The god TunSī6 resides in the cave7 and 6) in the Kadambaka tree8. 7) (The convention is) the Convention of the Lion and the Mother (avvā) is Guhavāsinī (She Who Lives in a Cave). (3) 8) The House is said to be the City of the Moon, while the 9) division (bheda) is that of Manthānabhairava (Churning Bhairava). 10) The clan (gotra) is the goddess Amarikā (Immortal) who is conceived to be (prakalpitā) on the Path of the Left (vāmamārga). (4) Within the lineage (anvaya), 11) the sign of accomplishment (pratyaya) is the essence,9 while 12) authority resides in Ko‰kaSa.10 13) (There is) the Brahmā Stone of Birth (janmabrahmaśilā), while 14) persistence is accomplished in Kāmarūpaka. (5) 15) Fame (kīrti) is the Tamarind Tree (ciñcinīvrkna), while 16) accomplishment (siddhi) is in the Ocean (sāgara). O lord of the gods, I am happy with the one who knows the Kulakrama. (6) This is the essence of the Kaula (teachings) that has emerged from the Kulakrama. One becomes a member of the lineage once one has learned the sixteenfold convention.11 (7)

sanskrit: 4 कुमारिकाखण्ड: श्रीनाथ उवाच ३१ किं मेरुमार्ग देवेशि ३३ अन्वये कात्र देवता । ३७ । ॐकारनिर्गमं ब्रूहि सिद्धौ चैव वदस्व मे ॥ ८ ॥ ४१ गुहावासान्तर किं तु कदम्बं प्रकटं कुरु । सिंहकं च न मे ज्ञातं ? चन्द्रपुर्यं विशेषतः ॥ ९ ॥ ४५ गोत्रं मन्थानभेदं च प्रकटं कुरु कौलिनि । o अन्वये प्रत्यय ँ किं तु अधिकार तथाम्बिके ॥ १० ॥ जन्मब्रह्मशिलां योनिं निगदस्व महेश्वरि । स्थिति: कि कामरूपे तु कीर्ति कथय चिञ्चिणीम् ॥ ११ ॥ ५९ सागरे तु कथं सिद्धिः” एतत् पृच्छामि कौलिनि । स्फुटं कथय एकैकं संशयं छेतुमर्हसि ।। १२ ।। श्रीवक्रा उवाच ६१ ६३ संकेतानि च देवेश कुलाम्नाये व्यवस्थिताः । चन्द्रपुर्यस्य” बिम्बस्य अन्वयं षोडशात्मकम् ।। १३ ॥ ६६ तस्य सन्तानसूत्रं तु षड्विधस्य क्रमस्य च । अधुना श्रूयतां शम्भो अमृत सारसंग्रहम् ॥ १४ ॥ पदे पदे मया ख्यातं भेदे भेदे पृथक् पृथक् । अतिगूढमिदं प्रश्न देवदेवावतारितम् ।। १५ ।।
english: CHAPTER SEVENTEEN 5 Śrīnātha said: O mistress of the gods, what is the Path of Meru? Who is the deity here in the lineage? Tell (me) about what has emerged from (the sacred seat called) Oˆkāra and the two Siddhas. (8) What is within the cave dwelling? Explain clearly (what is meant by) the Kadamba (tree). I have not learned the (Convention of the) Lion. In particular, (I want to know about) the City of the Moon. (9) O Kaulinī, explain clearly (what is meant by) the Clan and the division of the Churning (Bhairava). O mother, what is the sign of accomplishment in the lineage? And what is authority?12 (10) O Great Goddess, tell (me) about the Brahmā Stone of Birth, namely, the Yoni. What is (the condition of) persistence in Kāmarūpa? Tell (me) about Fame and the Tamarind. (11) How is it that there is accomplishment in the Ocean? This is what I am asking, O Kaulinī. Explain each one of these things clearly. You should remove (my) uncertainty (about them). (12) The venerable (goddess) Vakrā said: O Lord of the gods, (these) conventions belong to the Kula Tradition (kulāmnāya). The lineage of the original form (bimba) of the City of the Moon is sixteenfold. (13) The teaching regarding the Family Line (santānasūtra) is a part of the sixfold Transmission (krama). Now listen, O Śambhu, to the (teaching concerning) the nectar which is the collection of the essence (of the teaching). (14) I have explained it at every step and in every division (of the Tradition) individually. Brought down (into this world) by the God of the gods, this question is extremely profound. (15)

sanskrit: 6 कुमारिकाखण्डः तदहं कथयिष्यामि येन विन्दसि सर्वशः । मेरु भुवन” विख्यातं देवतालयशोभनम् ॥ १६ ॥ ७४ त्रिकूट शृङ्गरचितं त्रिभिर्देवैरधिष्ठितम् । ब्रह्मा विष्णुश्च रुद्रश्च एते सिद्धक्रमे स्थिताः ।। १७ ॥ .७५ •७६ आनन्दं विमलं चिञ्च एषां संज्ञा त्रिशुद्धिषु । आनन्दं व्यापकं देव” सर्वभूतेष्ववस्थितम् ॥ १८ ॥ सृष्टिर्विमलरूपेण” चिकाराज्ञागृहे स्थिता । एतैर्विज्ञातमात्रैस्तु मोक्षं यास्यन्ति मानवाः ।। १९ ॥ व्यापिन्या च महादेवी एकैकस्य व्यवस्थिता । तरङ्गिनी“ महाचण्डा“ काये कायेषु व्यापिनी ॥ २० ॥ त्रिरत्नभूषितैस्त्वङ्गैः“ स्वभावेन तु दीपिता” । मार्ग° चैव ऋजु” स्पष्टं सुशुद्धममृतोपमम् ।। २१ ।। अमा नाम कला सा तु आश्रमं गुह्यमण्डले । आगता सा परा देवी दाडिमीकुसुमोपमा ।। २२ ॥ .९३ द्वौ पक्षौ गुहका माया” दृश्येते ऋतुकालयोः । विचित्रा नाम विख्याता तया व्याप्तमशेषतः ।। २३ ।। एषा सा देवता देवतया ख्याता मया प्रभो । गुहाश्रमाद्“ विनिष्क्रान्ता अस्वरा स्वरवाहिनी ।। २४ ॥ शुद्धस्फटिकसंकाशा” शक्तिभि: सह संस्थिता । निष्क्रान्ता कूर्मनाड्या या इन्दुबिम्बसमायुता ।। २५ ।।
english: CHAPTER SEVENTEEN 7 The Path of Meru I will speak of that by means of which you attain (all things) in every way. Meru is said to be a world (bhuvana).13 It is the beautiful abode of the gods. (16) The summit (of Meru) is made of three Peaks presided over by three gods. These are Brahmā, VinSu and Rudra who reside in the transmission of the Siddhas.14 (17) The Tamarind (ciñcā) is pure bliss. Their designation is in the triple purification.15 O god, bliss is pervasive and is present in all beings. (18) Emanation (srn˜i), in a pure form, abides within the House of the Command of (the goddess Ciñcinī whose name begins with) the syllable CI.16 Merely by knowing these (things), men attain liberation. (19) The Deity of the Lineage The Great Goddess is pervasive (vyāpinyā) and she is present in each and every thing. (She is) Tara‰ginī (the Wave) who is very fierce and present in the body; she is (also) in (all other) bodies.17 Her limbs are adorned with the three jewels and she is energized (dīpitā) by her own nature.18 The Path is straight and clear.19 Extremely pure, it is like nectar. She is the digit of energy (kalā) of the New Moon (amā). The Hermitage (āśrama) is in the secret (guhya) maSÆala.20 The Supreme Goddess, (red) like the pomegranate flower, has come (there).21 (20-22) The two (lunar) phases (pakna), Guhakā (the Secret One) and Māyā are perceived during the two fertile seasons (rtukāla).22 She is called Vicitrā (Wonderfully Diverse) and (the maSÆala) in its entirety is pervaded by her. She, O lord, is the deity and I have spoken (of her) as the deity. She has emerged from the Cave Hermitage (guhāśrama) and, silent (asvara), she transports sound (svaravāhinī).23 (Her appearance is brilliant) like pure crystal and she, along with (her) energies, has emerged by means of the Tortoise Channel (kūrmanāÆī)24 and is linked to the lunar orb. (23-25)

sanskrit: 8 कुमारिकाखण्ड: १०३ सिद्धौ द्वाविति विख्यातौ भूषितं मेरुमण्डलम् । १०५ सृष्टिसंहारकतीरौ ं पुनश्चान्तपदे स्थित ।। २६ । १०८ ॐकारनिर्गमं देव सादाख्यं परिगीयते । अयं ब्रह्म अय विष्णुरय रुद्रो महेश्वर: सर्वदेवमयो” ह्येष ॐकार इति गीयते । ९२ ११४ ११२ ।। २७ ।। मेरोर्मध्यमतुङ्गे तु स्थिता समुद्रमालया ।। २८ ।। त्रिकोणाया”“ गुहामध्ये ॐकारस्तत्र दृश्यते । अमृतमध्ये” गुहावासी” बिन्दुना गीयते तु सा ।। २९ ।। संकेत वृक्षमूलं तु योनिमध्ये कदम्बकम् । तेन व्याप्तमिदं मेरु” आलयं सर्वयोगिनाम् ।। ३० ॥ १२४ संज्ञाभेदस्थिता' देवी' हरया४ बिन्दुसंज्ञया । भाषामुद्राणि २५ चिन्हानि संकेतेन प्रकीर्तिता: ।। ३१ ।। १२९ १२६ १३० सिंहक७ शृणु देवेश अम्बा यत्र ९ स्वयं स्थिता” । भैरवी रमते तत्र क्रीडते २ भैरवैः सह ।। ३२ ।। १३३ अधिष्ठानं महास्थानं समुद्रालयवेष्टितम् । १३६ सिंहकं तं विजानीयात् सिंहासनमुदीरितम् ॥ ३३ ॥
english: CHAPTER SEVENTEEN 9 Oˆkāra and the Two Siddhas Two Siddhas are said to adorn the Circle of Meru.25 They are the agents of creation and destruction. (Once they have performed their function), they again come to reside on the last (most elevated) plane. (26) O god, Sādākhya (the One Called Eternal) is said to be what has emerged from (the sacred seat called) Oˆkāra.26 This is Brahmā, this is VinSu, this is Rudra and Maheśvara. He is made of the gods and is called Oˆkāra. (27-28ab) The Cave Dwelling On the middle peak of Meru resides the (goddess) with the ocean (of letters) as her garland. Oˆkāra is perceived there in the middle of the Cave (guhā) within the Triangle (of energies).27 (The goddess) who lives in the cave is said to be in the middle of the nectar (in the form of a) Point.28 (28cd-29) The Kadamba Tree The Convention (which is the essential teaching) has as its root the Tree, namely, the Kadambaka in the centre of the Yoni.29 This Meru, the abode of all yogis, is pervaded by it. (30) The Convention of the Lion The goddess has diverse designations. As Harā she is called the Point. The signs consisting of Gestures and the (secret) language (bhānā) are enunciated by means of the convention. (31) O Lord of the gods, listen to (the location of the) the Lion wherein the Mother is self-established. Bhairavī sports there; she plays there with the Bhairavas. (32) The foundation (adhin˜hāna) is the Great Place, encompassed by the Abode of the Ocean. Know that to be the (the location of the) Lion, said to be the Lion Throne (siˆhāsana).30 (33)

sanskrit: 10 कुमारिकाखण्डः अम्बरस्थ३७ महाबिम्ब' षोडशस्वरभूषितम् । । तन्मध्ये तु अमा देवी गृहमेतत् प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ ३४ ॥ कूर्मयन्त्रप्रवाहेन मन्थयेच्च परस्परम् । १४१ मन्थानं सृष्टिरेवोक्त कौलिकं कलसंभवम् ॥ ३५ ॥ तस्मिन् मध्ये रमेद् धीमान् यत्र माता निरामया । अस्मिन्४३ गोत्रं प्रवक्ष्यामि अमरत्व शृणु प्रियं पञ्चरत्नस्य मध्यस्थं श्रीकण्ठादि प्रकीर्तितम् । १४६ १४७ १४८ १४५ ।। ३६ ।। एष देव्यादिगोत्रो ऽयं न गोत्रं नामसंज्ञया ॥ ३७ ॥ वामभागे स्थिता या ता वामाचारेण पूजयेत् । १५३ अमरत्वेति१५२ विज्ञेयं लम्बकं नाम विश्रुतम् ॥ ३८ ॥ १५६ सा कला भावये४ द्रव्य पिबस्व अमृतोपमम् । एषा परं महास्थानं मेरुमण्डलवेष्टितम् ॥ ३९ ॥ प्रत्ययं शृणु देवेश महाविश्वेति” दृश्यते । वर्तुलं रत्नतुङ्गाभं वणीवर्णीन्तप्रत्ययम् ॥ ४० ॥
english: CHAPTER SEVENTEEN 11 The House of the City of the Moon31 It is located in the Sky (of the Supreme Principle) and, very sacred (mahādivya), it adorned with the sixteen vowels. In the centre is the goddess New Moon (amā).32 That is said to be the House (grha). (34) The Division of the Churning Bhairava One should churn one with the other by means of the current of the Tortoise Machine (kūrmayantra).33 (The act of) churning (manthāna) is said to be emanation itself, which is the arising of the aspects of the (energy of) Kula.34 The wise man should sport there, in (SunumSā) (which is) the centre (madhya),35 where the Mother is free of blemish. (35-36ab) The Clan and Path of the Left Listen to (the nature of) the immortal state, O beloved; I will tell you of the clan (gotra) within it. (The series of letters) beginning with ŚrīkaS˜ha (A) is in the middle of the Five Jewels.36 That is the goddess's first clan (devyādigotra).37 The clan (meant here is) not (simply that indicated by the common) designation of a name. (36cd-37) One should worship (the goddess) who is on the left side (of the god) by means of the Practice of the Left (vāmācāra). One should know that this is immortality. (It is the uvula) and goes by the name of Lambaka (the Hanging One). That energy (kalā) is the sacrificial substance and it is like nectar. Drink (it to gain eternal) existence.38 That (energy) is the supreme Great Place,39 encompassed by the Circle of Meru. (38-39) The Sign of Accomplishment Listen, O Lord of the gods, to the sign of accomplishment (pratyaya).40 It is perceived as the great universe. The sign of accomplishment is at the end of (both) sound (varSa) and silence (avarSa).41 It is circular and shines as the Mountain of Jewels (ratnatu‰ga). (40)

sanskrit: 12 कुमारिकाखण्ड: १६३ तच्च पश्यन्ति योगिन्यो मत्यानां प्रकटं हर । महापर्वतबिम्बस्य पूजा कुर्वन्ति १२ योगिनः क्रमार्चनं प्रकुर्वन्ति ये स्थिता विश्वमध्यतः । १६४ ।। ४१ ।। दिव्याक्षरं तु तं पश्येत् कौलिनीपरिलेखितम् ।। ४२ ।। स एष ६६ प्रत्यय७ रुद्र प्रत्यक्ष समुदाहृतम् । १६९ १७० कृतं मयाधिकार तु पूर्णपीठे ह्यधोमुखी ॥ ४३ ॥ पुन: कोंकणावतारे कमलाव्वा प्रकीर्तिता । १७४ एतद् वै अधिकारं तु कोंकणे प्रकटीकृतम् ॥ ४४ ॥ १७५ ब्रह्मस्थाने भवेत् पद्मं सृष्ट्यर्थ ं समुपागतम् । जन्मस्थान७६ शिलामध्ये तत्र चांकुरदेवता ।। ४५ ।। १७९ तया च सा शिलाक्रान्ता जन्मब्रह्मशिला स्मृता । कन्दमूलमध: स्थाने वर्तुलं चातिशोभनम् ।। ४६ । तच्छ्रवेत् कामिनीचक्रे देवदेव महेश्वर । । कामाख्यं गुह्यसंस्थाने स्थित्वाश्रम” ममेति च ॥ ४७ ॥ १८३ करिष्यामि ह्यहं कीर्ति चिञ्चाख्ये वृक्षसंज्ञके । मयापि व्यापित मेरु २८६ रमन्ती च अहं स्थिता ।। ४८ ।
english: CHAPTER SEVENTEEN 13 O Hara, the Yoginīs see it and it is clearly manifest to mortal men. Yogis worship the form of (that) great mountain. Those (who are there), established in the centre of the universe, perform the worship of the Transmission (kramārcana). (41-42ab) One should see that divine letter written (there)42 by (the goddess) Kaulinī. O Rudra, that is the sign of attainment (pratyaya) said to be directly apparent (pratyakna). (42cd-43ab) Authority I have placed authority in the full sacred seat (pūrSapī˜ha).43 (There I) face downwards.44 Again, she is known as the Mother Kamalā (Lotus) in (her) descent (to earth) in Ko‰kaSa. That, indeed, is authority made clearly manifest in Ko‰kaSa.45 (43cd-44) Brahmā’s Stone of Birth In the Place of Brahmā (brahmasthāna) there is a lotus that has come to be placed (samupāgata) (there) for the purpose of emanation. (It is) the Place of Birth (janmasthāna) and is in the centre of the Stone (śilā). The deity of the sprout (a‰kura) (resides) there. The Stone (śīlā) is pervaded (ākrāntā) by her and (so) is said to be Brahmā’s Stone of Birth.46 (45-46ab) Stability in Kāmarūpa The Root of the Bulb (kandamūla) is in the lower place. It is round and very beautiful. O god of the gods, O Great God, it oozes into the Wheel of the Passionate Goddess (kāminīcakra). Kāmākhya is located in the Secret Place (guhyasthāna) and abiding (there), it is my Hermitage.47 (46cd-47) Fame of the Tamarind Tree I will make the (tree) called the Tamarind famous.48 I also pervade Meru and, residing (there), I play.49 (48)
