(71-72ab) O Śambhu, those who have become pure by the Command of the Western (Kula) and who expound the meaning of the verses (of the scripture) know this, the pure (scripture) of the Supreme Lord,32 once they have perceived this eightfold knowledge of the western (tradition) in this way.33 (72cd-73) The Language of the Scripture, the Oral Tradition and Admonishments The Śrīmata, which of consists of seventy million (saptako˜ika) (verses), is the knowledge of (this) eightfold (reality). It is the oral tradition of the gods that teaches the profound (hidden) reality (gūÆhārtha). (74) He who is an aspect of Rudra (rudrāˆśa) (alone) knows the Western (Tradition), which is great, extremely hard (to comprehend) and difficult to penetrate. (An ordinary) mortal does not acquire the great medicine of the tradition (saˆpradāya). (75)

sanskrit: 236 कुमारिकाखण्ड: । ३०४ क्रियाकारकसंबन्धं विभक्तिलघुप्रत्ययम् । ३०६ समासैः सप्तकैर्भेदं गुप्तं कुलवधू इव ।। ७६ ।। क्लिष्टशब्दैर्विभज्येत ँ तस्मात् क्लिष्ट त्यजेद् बुधः । अपशब्दैश्च सरलैस्तैस्तु” शैवोऽभिगम्यते” ।। ७७ ।। संकेतवर्णमेकेन”” मुखाम्नायेन शोधयेत् । न चापि लटलोटैस्तु” ” शुष्कतर्कादिभिस्तथा ।। ७८ ।। ३१५ व्याख्यायामागमे ३१४ देव दिव्या वाणी स्वतन्त्र स्था विपरीतमिदं ज्ञात्वा दिव्याम्नायः प्रवर्तते ॥ ७९ ॥ •३१६ एवं पाण्डित्यमुत्सृज्य सरल कौलिकागमम् । •३१७ । श्रोतव्यं च मुखाम्नाय कणीत् कणीन्तरागतम् ॥ ८० ॥ अक्षरार्थोपदेशश्च संप्रदायश्च कौलिकः । ३२२ निगर्भश्च षडेवैते संप्रदाया उदाहृताः ।। ८१ ।। सारं श्लोकोपदेश २३ च निर्णीत २४ तव भैरव ३२५ । कौलिकाज्ञापरं नास्ति श्रीमतात् परतरं न हि ।। ८२ ।। •३२६ मुखाम्नायात् परं नास्ति शेषं त्यज्य पलालवत् । एवं सञ्चिन्त्य यत्नेन मुखकौलं समभ्यसेत् ।। ८३ ॥ आज्ञावर्तिः शिवः पन्था वृक्षच्छाया सोमो ३२८ परं परमहंसं च कुवेर ९ पीठमावली ३३० ३२७ कुमारी कर्तरी भाषा मात्रात्मा मातरी तथा ३३४ रविः । ।। ८४ ।। । ३३२ पूर्वपश्चिममध्य च वामदक्षिणकोणकम् ॥ ८५ ॥ •३३६ योनिषट्क३५ च शृङ्गाट े आदिक्षान्तं कुलेश्वरम् । यो हि वेत्ति इदं ज्ञान स साक्षाद् भैरवः स्वयं ।। ८६ ।।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY 237 The relationship between the cases and the verb, case endings, short (and long syllables), verbal affixes and suffixes, classification into seven (types) of compounds — (all this) is kept hidden as one does a woman of good family. (76) (The sense) is lost (vibhajyeta) by using difficult words. Thus the wise man should refrain from (using) difficult (expressions). The (true) Śaivite (can) understand (the meaning of the teaching even) by means of simple and (even) ungrammatical forms (apaśabda). (77) One should purify (one's understanding of) the letter of the convention by (referring to) the one (true) oral tradition. (It should not be done) by those who speak like fools (la˜a) and blockheads (lo˜a) by means of dry logic and the like. (78) O god, there is a divine form of speech (vāSī)34 which is independent (svatantrastha) that (operates) in the scripture and (its) commentary. The Divine Tradition comes into being when this (reality), which is the reverse (of falsity), has been grasped. (79) Abandoning in this way (dry) scholarliness, one should listen to the Kaulikāgama, which is easy (Sanskrit), and to the oral tradition, which has been passed down from ear to ear. (80) These are said to be the six (kinds of) traditional teaching (saˆpradāya): the letter (aknara), the meaning (artha), the teaching (upadeśa), the tradition (saˆpradāya), the Kaulika (meaning) and the implicit sense (nigarbha).35 (81) O Bhairava, the essence (of the scripture) and the teaching concerning the Verses has been taught to you. There is nothing higher than the Kaulika Command, there is nothing superior to the Śrīmata, there is nothing higher than the oral tradition — everything else should be abandoned like rotten meat. Having reflected (on the matter) thus with effort, one should practice the (teaching of) the oral Kaula tradition. (82-83) (Consider the following): the Wick of the Command, Śiva, the Path, the Shade of the Tree, the Moon and Sun. The Supreme, the Supreme Gander, Kuvera, the sacred seat and the series (of teachers) (āvalī), Kumārī, Kartarī, Bhānā, Mātrā, and Mātarī.36a (84-85ab) (The corresponding directions are) east, west and the middle and the corners in the north and south.36b (There is also) the (hexagram consisting of the) group of six Yonis (yonina˜ka), the Triangle (śrngā˜a) and Kuleśvara (who consists of the letters) ranging from A to K±a. He who knows this knowledge36c is Bhairava himself, directly apparent. (85cd - 86)

sanskrit: 238 कुमारिकाखण्ड: •३४० ३४१ ३४४ एवं क्रमार्थतस्तत्त्वं सप्तकोट्याद् विनिर्गतम् । यो हनेत् पशुभावात्मा‍ गुरुस्तेन३ हनीकृतः परत्रं हारितं तेन मेरु४५ तेनैव लङ्घितम् । •३४७ ।। ८७ ।। इदं मतमिदं योगमिदं तत्त्व कुलार्णवम् ॥। ८८ ॥ कुलौघ क्रम - ओघ तु ज्ञानौघं च तथोत्तमम् । •३४८ ३५१ पूजनीयं प्रयत्नेन हन्यते न कदाचन ।। ८९ ॥ पञ्चस्रोतात्मके १५३ शैवे षष्ठे कुलविनिश्चये । अजवक्त्रात् परं शान्तमिदं तत् सारसंग्रहम् ३५५ ॥ ९० ॥ सिद्धसन्तानसुभग प्रत्ययाज्ञाविशारदम् । नाम्ना क्रमोदयज्ञान श्रीखगेशीमहामतम् ९ ।। ९१ ।। श्रीनाथ उवाच ३६० । सत्यमेतत् त्वया प्रोक्तं कौलिकं प्रत्ययात्मकम्' कौलज्ञानात् परं नास्ति दुर्लभं मतसंग्रहम् ।। ९२ ॥ ३६२ कोटिकोटिरसंख्याता मया शास्त्रावतारिता: । पृच्छकानुमतेनैव सर्वे‍ ते च पलालवत् ३६४ विभागं च प्रमाणं च शास्त्रमञ्जूषकं शृणु । सप्तकोटिप्रमाणेन मतं वै पारमेश्वरम् ।। ९४ । ३६५ ॥ ९३ ॥ कोटिपञ्चाशल्लक्षैक सहस्रं शतसंख्यया । शतार्धं शतपादं च सद्योजाताद् विनिर्गतम् ।। ९५ ।। नवनवतिर्लक्षाणि ३६८a लक्षकोटिस्तथैव च । तथान्याः .३६८० कोटिपञ्चाशद् वामदेवाद् विनिः श्रिताः ३६९ ।। ९६ ।।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY 239 In this way, the truth (tattva) has emerged from the teaching (artha) of the Krama, that is, from the (scripture of) seven thousand million (verses) (ko˜i). The teacher whose condition is that of (an uninitiated) fettered soul (paśubhāva) damages it and thus (by doing so) has caused (great) harm. He has stolen away the other world. He has crossed over Meru.37a (87-88ab) This is the doctrine (mata). This is Yoga. This is the truth (tattva). This is the Ocean of Kula. One should worship with effort the Current of the Kula, the Current of the Krama and the most excellent Current of Knowledge. One is (thereby) never destroyed. (88cd-89) The Descent of the Scriptures This, the synopsis of the essence (of the teaching) (sārasaˆgraha)37b that has (come) from the Mouth of the Unborn (ajavaktra), is the supreme and tranquil (reality taught) in the the sixth (current) amongst the five currents of Śaiva (scriptures).38 (90) The finest part of the Line (santāna) of Siddhas, it is proficient in the Command of Insight (pratyayājñā). It is the knowledge that comes by the arising of the transmission called the great Mata of the venerable (goddess) Khageśī (the Mistress of the Skyfarers). (91) Śrīnātha said: You have told (me) that truth which is the Kaulika (teaching), the nature of which is the direct experience (pratyaya) (of ultimate reality). There is nothing higher than Kaula knowledge. The Compendium of the Mata is (indeed) hard to acquire.39 (92) I have brought countless millions of millions of scripture down (to earth) as the one who enquired (of me) wished. (But) they are all (useless) like rotten meat. (93) Listen to the casket of scriptures, (its) division and extent. The extent of the (versions of) the Pārameśvaramata is seventy million (verses), ten million, five million, one thousand, one hundred, fifty and twenty five. It has came from (the mouth of) Sadyojāta. (94-95) Another (series of scriptures) has emerged from (the mouth of) Vāmadeva. (These consist of) nine million nine hundred thousand (verses), one hundred thousand, ten million and five hundred million (verses). (96)

sanskrit: 240 कुमारिकाखण्ड: ३७२ । कोटीन्ययुतचत्वारि लक्षाः ३७१ पञ्चाशकोटिका: सहस्रशतसंख्या च सहस्त्रैकं शतं तथा ।। ९७ ।। शतलक्षसहस्रं च अघोरात् तु विनिर्गतम् । । अर्बुदं चार्बुदं चैव खर्वश्चैव परापरम् ।। ९८ । षट्सहस्राणि कोटिश्च लक्षपादं सहस्रकम् । शतमर्ध ६ च पादाख्यं तत्पुरुषाच्च विनिर्गतम् ।। ९९ ।। ईशानस्य तु वक्त्रस्य पञ्चमस्य महात्मनः । विचार्यतोऽपि ७७ यत्नेन शास्त्रसंख्या न विद्यते ॥ १०० ॥ एवं वै शास्त्राम्नायं तु मतं ज्ञात्वा समभ्यसेत् । पञ्चश्रोतोद्भवा ह्येते ग्रन्थसंख्यासमन्विताः ।। १०१ ।। ३७९ ३८१ लोकाचारस्य हेत्वर्थे मया ते परिकीर्तिताः । षष्ठमं यन्महावक्त्रं तद् गुप्तं तु मया कृतम् ।। १०२ ।। ग्रन्थानां२ तु शतं सार्धं तस्माद् वक्त्राद् विनिर्गतम् । ३८४ स्थितं तत्८३ खेचरीचक्रे निगूढे संप्रकाशितम् ॥ १०३ ॥ शास्त्रावतारमञ्जूषं किञ्चिद् वक्ष्याम्यहं •३८६ शृणु ।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY 241 (A third series of scriptures) has emerged from (the mouth of) Aghora. (These consist of) four hundred thousand million (verses), five thousand million, one hundred thousand, one thousand, one hundred and ten thousand million. (97-98ab) (A fourth series) has emerged from (the mouth of) Tatpuruna. (These consist of) one hundred million (verses), (then again) a hundred million, ten thousand million, one hundred thousand, ten million, twenty-five thousand, one thousand and (finally) fifty. (98cd-99) The scriptures that have come from the mouth of the great-souled Īśāna, the fifth one, are innumerable. Even after much streneous thought (one could not number them). (100) Having learned the tradition of the scripture, the Mata, practice it. These are (the scriptures) that have emerged out of the five currents along with the number of (their) verses. (101) I have told you about them for the sake of the common, worldly practice (lokācāra). I have concealed the sixth great face. One hundred and fifty books have come from that face; they are within the secret Wheel of the Skyfarers (where they have been) revealed. (102-103ab) Listen: I will (now) tell (you) something of the casket of the (tradition concerning) the descent of the scriptures. (13cd-104ab)

english: CHAPTER THIRTY 243 (These scriptures are) Niƒśena, Pravara, Pracura, RatnacūÆāmaSi, Tilakamañjūnā, Niƒśvāsa, Hārīta, Somārkapralaya, Mahākālabhairava, Somārka, Tripurānta, Vaihāya, Kulamañjarī, Udadhi, Pañcarātra, Vāmanabha˜˜āraka, Bha˜˜inī, Bha˜˜akula, Ananta, Garbha, GaruÆa, Ananta, Rudra, Īśvara, Lāˆgali, Māta‰ga, Māta‰gi, Madanonmatta, Nīlāmbara, Nīnla, Kanakāvalī, NirvāSayogasiddhānta, Saˆkhyā, Mahātrailokya, Lokalokeśvara, Vajravrnda, Yogapa˜˜ā, Lokavicāra, Srn˜ivicāra, Akulaśr‰ga, Śr‰khalī, Sadya, Vāma, Tatpuruneśvara, Parabrahmabodhi, Brahmaśānti, Brahmyopākhyāna, Śabdabrahma, Sūknmabrahma, Ananta and the rest, Prthu, Skanda, Nandi, Mahākāla, Vātula, Śavara, Aghora, Kapila, Ja˜eśvara, Gaurīśvara and, finally, Mahābodhi. The Worship, Writing, Protection and Efficacy of the Śrīmata Śrīnātha said: O goddess, what is the use of the (scriptures you have just) named? (They) serve no purpose. I want to hear the Śrīmata, (otherwise known as the) Vakrikāmata of twenty-four thousand (verses). By (your) grace, tell (it to me). (104cd-105) The venerable (goddess) said: (This) Saˆhitā is composed of four sections (pāda), namely, the Kriyāpāda and the Jñāna (pāda), with the Yogapāda as the third and the Caryāpāda as the fourth.40 (106) One should make as great an effort (as possible) to protect it with care, as one would a newly-born animal. (The scripture) should be worshipped constantly with white flowers, sweet scents and the like, fragrant with incense and with liquor (ali), sacred incense, lamps and auspicious sacrificial food (caru), (all offered) with great devotion. (107-108)

sanskrit: 244 कुमारिकाखण्ड: ।। व्यावृत्ताक्षिप्तचित्तेन”“ क्रमपूजा न सिद्ध्यति । गुरुमण्डल कृत्वादौ पूजयेत् गुरुपञ्चकम् ॥ १०९ ॥ सिंहासनमिदं॰‍ पूज्य४११ त्रैलोक्यं पूजितं भवेत् । प्राणवद् रक्षणीयं तु पालनीयं गुरोर्वचम् ॥ ११० ॥ ४२४ नैव ( 2 ) ४२५ पशूनां न प्रदर्शयेत् । एकान्ते विजने रम्ये दुष्टसत्त्वविवर्जिते ।। १११ ॥ सुगन्धगन्धबहुले ँ मिष्टधूपाधिवासिते । ४२७ । चन्द्रोदयपरिच्छन्ने“ पूजासंभारसंवृते ।। ११२ ॥ दीपार्घचरुकैश्चैव क्रमिकैर्भक्तिवत्सलैः ४२९ । हेमवस्त्राद्यलंकारैर्गुरुं संपूज्य भक्तितः ।। ११३ ॥ ४३२ । कुमारी योगिनी पूज्या” हेमदानादिसुवरैः । अनुज्ञाताभिषिक्तैस्तु” अच्छिद्रं तु मतं मम ।। ११४ ।। एवं भवतु५ तैरुक्तं अर्चिता पृच्छ्यते शुभम् । अवधार्य गुरोर्वक्त्राद् दीपनं मन्दबुद्धिनाम् ॥ ११५ ॥ आगमश्रवणादाशु” महावेश: प्रवर्तते । ४४२ गृहीतव्यं महादेव सर्वस्वं योगिनीकुले ॥ ११६ ॥ श्रीमते ३ कुले दीपं दुर्लभं पारमेश्वरम् । ४४४ •४४६ ।। विधिहीने ४५ व्याख्येय न लेख्यं तु कदाचन ।। ११७ ।। ४४७ ४४८ ४४९ म्लेच्छपत्रे न लेख्यं तु न लेख्यं ताडिपत्रकें । ४५० लिखितव्यं परे भूर्जे सुशुद्धे ग्रन्थिवर्जिते ।। ११८ ।। भवेत् सिद्धिप्रदं देव अन्यथा न कदाचन । मसिं च संप्रवक्ष्यामि यादृश्या लिख्यते मतम् ।। ११९ ।। अन्यथा विघ्नदं देव ४५२ न लिखेत ४५३ कदाचन । ४५४ तच्छृणुष्व महाभाग मसीकरणमुत्तमम् ॥ १२० ॥
english: CHAPTER THIRTY 245 The worship of the Krama (kramapūjā) is not successful (if performed) by (one with a) distracted and busy mind. Having fashioned the MaSÆala of the Teachers, one should worship the Five Teachers.41 (109) When this throne has been worshipped, the Triple World has been worshipped. (The scripture) should be protected as one does one's life. The word of the teacher should be followed. ***** ***** ****.42 It should not be shown to the uninitiated. (110-111ab) The teacher should be worshipped with devotion by the votaries of the Krama who are beloved of devotion by (offering him) lamps, water, the sacrificial pap, gold, clothes and other such ornaments. (It should be done) in a solitary place where there are no people, one that is free of savage animals, which is beautiful, fragrant with fine scent, purified with sweet incense, covered (with the light of) the rising moon and equiped with the requisites of worship (pūjāsaˆbhāra). (111cd-113) A virgin Yoginī should be worshipped (there) with beautiful gifts of gold and the like by those who have received permission to do so and have been consecrated. Having said: 'my teaching (mata) is without fault. So be it; (let it be copied)!' and having worshipped (her), (they) ask (her) what is auspicious (or otherwise). (114-115) Having heard attentively from the teacher's mouth (the teaching), which is illumination (dīpana)43 for those of slow intellect, the Great Penetration (mahāveśa) quickly takes place by listening to the scripture.44 O Great God, one should (thus) lay hold of the essence of the Yoginīkula.45 (116) This, the Śrīmata of the Supreme Lord, is the lamp of Kula which is hard to acquire. It should not be explained to one who is devoid of the enjoined method, nor should it ever be written (by one such as him). (117) It should not be written on paper (mlecchapatra) or palmleaf, but on the best, purest birch-bark free of knots. (O god, in this way the Śrīmata) gives success and never in any other.46 (118-9ab) Now I will tell you about the ink with which the Mata should be written. O god, it should never be written in any other way, otherwise it gives rise to (many) obstacles. Listen, O most handsome one, to the best way in which the ink is made. (119cd-120)

sanskrit: 246 कुमारिकाखण्ड: सिन्दूरं लाक्षया तोयं दूतीकुंकुममिश्रितम् । स्त्रीपुष्पमलिनाथं तु तथा वै वैष्णवं रसम् ।। १२१ ।। उपदेशवशेनैव ५५ अङ्कयेल्लोहकरे । अर्धशेषं तु संगृह्य अघोरास्त्रेण मन्त्रवित् ।। १२२ ।। तच्च ते संप्रवक्ष्यामि विघ्ननिनीशनं परम् । ४५८ ऐं ह्रीँ ह्रीँ हूँ प्रस्फुर प्रस्फुर घोर ५९ घोरतर तनुरूप ४६० चट चट प्रचट प्रचट कह कह वम वम घाटय घाटय हूँ हूँ हूँ फट् फट् फट्। अघोरास्त्रमिदं देव मम क्रोधाद् विनिर्गतम् ।। १२३ ।। सप्तोच्चारणमात्रेण षोढान्यासफलं लभेत्‍ । षट्प्रकारा मसी प्रोक्ता तया लेख्य मतं त्विदं ॥ १२४ ॥ अन्यथा न लिखेद्४ देव लिखितं विघ्नदायकम् । यथा व्याख्याविधिः ख्याता तथा लेखनकर्म ४६५ च ॥ १२५ ॥ •४६६ •४६७ ४६८ लेखकं भक्त शुद्ध च पारम्पर्यविशारदम् । •४६९ गुरुभक्तिरतं शान्तं कुलागमप्रपूजकम् ।। १२६ ।। कुमारीयोगिनीभक्तं ब्रह्मचर्यपरायणम् । कुलशास्त्ररतं दक्षं दम्भमायाविवर्जितम् ।। १२७ ।। •४७१ सुस्नातं मन्त्रपूतं च यक्षकर्दमचर्चितम् । । ४७३ •४७४ वस्त्रयुग्मं परीधाय ं पुष्पमालाविभूषितम् ।। १२८ ॥ सुधूपधूपितं कृत्वा अनामा हेममुद्रिकाम् । कटकङ्कणहारैश्च हेमगोदानदक्षिणैः ॥ १२९ ॥ तोषयित्वा तु स्वगुरुं यथाविभवविस्तरम् । ४७९ ४७७ ।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY 247 (The ink should contain) vermillion (sindūra) with lac and water mixed with the consort’s red cosmetic powder (dūtīkuˆkuma), menstrual blood, liquor (alinātha) and VainSava juice. (121) (Then) the knower of mantra should enscribe it in accord with the teaching once he has laid hold of the remaining half (contained) in an iron bowl with the Weapon of Aghora. I will tell you that, the supreme destruction of obstacles. (122-123ab) AI¤ HRĀ¤ HRĪ¤ HRŪ¤ PRASPHURA PRASPHURA GHORA GHORATARA TANURŪPA CAµA CAµA PRACAµA PRACAµA KAHA KAHA VAMA VAMA GHĀµAYA GHĀµAYA HŪ¤ HŪ¤ HŪ¤ PHAµ PHAµ PHAµ AI¤ HRĀ¤ HRĪ¤ HŪ¤ Explode with light! Explode with light! O terrible one! Most terrible one! Subtle One! Crackle like fire! Crackle intensely! KAHA! KAHA! Vomit! Vomit! Beat! Beat! HŪ¤ HŪ¤ HŪ¤ PHAµ PHAµ PHAµ O god, this is the Weapon of Aghora that has emerged from my anger. Merely by reciting it seven times, one gains the fruit of (the full) sixfold deposition. (123cd-124ab) The ink (masī) with six ingredients (na˜prakārā) has been explained. This Mata should be written with that. Otherwise (without this ink), O god, it should not be written, (for if it is) written (with the wrong ink), it gives rise to (many) troubles. (Thus) just as the method concerning the commentary has been explained, so has the procedure for writing (the Śrīmata). (124cd-125) The writer (should be a) pure devotee, versed in the tradition, intent on devotion to (his) teacher, tranquil, a worshipper of the Kula scripture. (126) (He should be) devoted to the virgin Yoginī and practice celibacy. (He should be) intent on the Kula scripture, skilful, free of deceit and magic (māyā), well bathed, purified by mantra and smeared with perfumed paste (yaknakardama).47 (127-128ab) He should don a pair of pieces of cloth. Then, having adorned (his teacher) with garlands of flowers, having well fumigated (him) with incense and having placed a gold ring on (his) ring finger, (he should) satisfy his teacher according to his means with gold bracelets, necklaces and gifts of cows and gold as the sacrificial fee. (128cd-130ab)

sanskrit: 248 कुमारिकाखण्ड: आरात्रीं कारयेत् पश्चात् कुलकुम्भं प्रपूरयेत् ।। १३० ।। •४८२ -४८३ तत्रस्थमागमं पूज्यं पूज्यं दिव्यवस्त्रविभूषितम् । क्रमं च पूजयित्वा तु गुरुमण्डलपूर्वकम् ।। १३१ ॥ ४८४ ४८५ ४८६ ४८७ दातव्या दीपमाला तु मतराजस्य सुन्दर । वीरभोज्यं प्रकर्तव्यं यथा ख्यातं पुरा मया ।। १३२ ।। परशिष्ये न दातव्यं ददेदादेशपूर्वकम् । अन्यथा ददते यस्तु स विघ्नैश्चाभिभूयते ।। १३३ ॥ सुपरीक्ष्य प्रदातव्यं दूतीनां क्रमभाषितम् । ४९० कर्मणा मनसा वाचा त्रिशुद्धिर्भक्तिवत्सले ।। १३४ ।। तस्येदं” श्रीमतं दद्याद् अथवा स्वगुरोज्ञया । ४९२ अन्यथा न प्रदातव्यं गुरुशुद्धिविवर्जिते ।। १३५ ।। अर्थलोभाद् भयात् प्रीत्या न” दद्याच्च कदाचन । •४९५ ४९४ एतत् समय” देवेश प्रयत्नाद् धारितो मया ॥ १३६ ॥ भक्तिहीने शठे क्रूरे निःसत्ये कलहप्रिये । ४९७ ४९८ तान्त्रिके द्वेषदुष्टे च गर्विते च अहंकृते ।। १३७ ॥ पारम्पर्यविनिर्मुक्ते नैव लोभात् प्रदापयेत् । ४९९ ५०३ ५०४ ।। ओलिशुद्धिविनिर्मुक्ते क्रमशुद्धिविवर्जिते ॥ १३८ ॥ समय भ्रष्टे ५०२ च पापिष्टे वञ्चके गुरुदूषके । ईश्वरे चित्तलोभिष्टे तथा पापरते जने ।। १३९ ॥ ज्ञानोपजीवकासक्ते कायस्थे हेतुवादिने । .५०६ लक्षरागचले शिष्ये कार्यार्थी भक्तिवत्सल' -५१२ । ५०८ अभक्ते चैव कृपणे” चपले पानलम्पटे” । देवार्चनविनिर्मुक्ते शौचाचारविवर्जितें ।। १४१ ।। कपटव्रतचारिणे१३ मतराजं न दापयेत् । । ।। १४० ।।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY 249 Then he should wave lamps (before the Śrīmata). After that he should fill the Kula jar (with liquor). (After that) the scripture that is placed there and adorned with divine clothes should be worshipped. (Then) having worshipped the Krama after the MaSÆala of the Teachers, O handsome one, a garland of lamps should be offered to the King of Matas. (130cd-132ab) One should take a Hero's Meal as I have previously explained. It should not be given to another (teacher's) disciple, but should (only) be given with prior permission. (132cd-133ab) He who gives it in any other way is overcome with troubles. The Krama taught by the Dūtīs should be given (only) after (the disciple) has been well tested. (133cd-134ab) O beloved child of devotion, the triple purification (takes place) by means of action, speech and mind. This Śrīmata should be given to (such a) one (who is thus purified) or else (who is) in accord with the teacher's command. (134cd-135ab) Otherwise, one should not give it to one who has not been purified by the teacher. It should never be given out of greed for money, fear or (mere) affection. (135cd-136ab) O Lord of the gods, this is the Rule I have kept with effort. One should not give it out of greed to one who has no of devotion or to one who is deceitful, cruel, false, enjoys quarelling, a Tāntrika, a person who hates, (utters) malicious (words) or to one who is proud, egoistic or without a lineage. (136cd-138ab) (It should not be given) to one who (has not undergone) the purification of the lineages (oli) and the Krama, to one who has fallen from the Rule, a great sinner, a cheat, one who denigrates the teacher, a (rich selfish) lord, one who is mentally greedy, a person devoted to sin, one who makes a living from knowledge, one who is attached, a clerk (kāyastha) or to a logician. (138cd-140ab) O beloved child of devotion, one should not give (this), the king of Matas, to one who is deceitful because of (his) attachment to (some selfish) goal, a disciple who has (some ulterior) purpose, to one who is not devoted, mean, fickle, dedicated to drink, who does not worship the gods, who does not observe cleanliness or who practices deceit. (140cd-142ab)

sanskrit: 250 कुमारिकाखण्ड: स्थिरचित्ताङ्गभावे च सर्वस्वविनिवेदके ।। १४२ ॥ ५१४ ५१५ कर्मणा मनसा वाचा विशुद्धे भक्तिवत्सलें । भिन्नदेहाङ्गभावे १६ च १७ गुवाम्नायविशारदे ॥ १४३ ॥ च१७ मतराजं प्रदातव्य” द्वादशाब्दपरीक्षिते ५२० । ।। ।। नार्थलोभाद् भयात् प्रीत्या नोपरोधेन विद्यया ।। १४४ ।। न दातव्यमिद५२२ रत्नं ज्ञानकोष २३ कुलागमम् । ५२४ पुत्रस्यापि न दातव्यं किं पुनरितरे जने ।। १४५ ।। विशेषेण २५ न दातव्यं कार्यार्थी भक्तिवत्सल५७ । । ५२८ कलौ युगे महाघोरे स्वल्पचित्तैस्त्वचेतनैः ।। १४६ ।। आचार्यै: ५२९ शक्तिहीनैश्च ज्ञानहीनैश्च निश्चयै: ५३० ५३१ ५३२ ते तु ये दीक्षिता देव शिष्याश्चैवापरीक्षिताः' ।। १४७ ।। प्रमादेन कथञ्चित् स्यात् दुःखान्यनुभविष्यति । ५३५ भक्तिहीन क्रियाहीनं भावहीनं तु चुम्बकम् ।। १४८ ।। न ज्ञानं निर्मल५३७ तस्य नैव दद्यात् कुलागमम् । ५३८ आज्ञापहारः कर्तव्यः परिहार्यः प्रयत्नतः ॥ १४९ ॥ ५४० तदा सिद्धि“३९ लभेन्मन्त्री अन्यथा पापकृन्मतः ।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY 251 The king of Matas should be given to one whose mind and limbs are firm, who offers (freely his whole) wealth, who is pure by way of (his) action, speech and mind, to one who is a beloved child of devotion, one who is detached from the body, who is an expert in the Tradition of the Masters (gurvāmnāya)48 and who has been tested for twelve years. (142cd-144ab) This jewel, a treasury of knowledge, the Kula scripture, should not be given out of greed for money, fear, (mere) affection, constraint or for (mere intellectual) knowledge. (144cd-145ab) It should not be given even to (one's) son (if he is not qualified to receive it), what (to say) of other people. Especially, O beloved child of devotion, it should not be given to one who has (some ulterior) purpose. (145cd-146ab) O god, in this very terrible Age of Strife, untested disciples, initiated by mistake by thoughtless teachers with little intellect who are devoid of power and (whose) doctrines are devoid of knowledge, will experience (many kinds of) sufferings. (146cd-148ab) The knowledge of one who has no devotion, who does not practice the rites, who is devoid of deep sentiment and who is a rogue (cumbaka) is not pure. One should not give (him) the Kulāgama. (148cd-149ab) The Command should be taken away (from him) and (he) should be streneously avoided. Then the reciter of mantra attains success (siddhi), otherwise he is considered to be a sinner.49 (149cd-150ab)

sanskrit: 252 कुमारिकाखण्डः ५४१ निर्वाणोत्तरयोगे च तथा कालोत्तरे परे ॥ १५० ॥ ऊध्वस्रोते च करणे ५४२ तथा स्वच्छन्दभैरवे ' ५४४ ५४३ । नित्यातन्त्रे यामले च तथा च त्रिपुरार्णवे ।। १५१ ॥ यामले रुरुभेदे च तथा च ब्रह्मयामले । ओडामरे १४५ डामरे वा तथा वै चर्चिकाक्रमे ॥ १५२ ॥ -५४७ पिच्वाख्ये तु महादेव अथवा कालिकाक्रमें । तन्त्रे च भैरवे वापि४८ सोमसिद्धान्तलाकुले ।। १५३ ॥ ५५१ तुम्बुरे चैकवीरे वा जयातन्त्रे तु वासुकें । मातङ्गे ब्रह्मतन्त्रे च प्रतिष्ठापारमेश्वरें ।। १५४ ।। ५५२ ।। आणवे“३ पिङ्गले“४ चैव रसस्वच्छन्दके तथा । वाचस्पते ५५ च आद्ये वा लक्षपादेऽथ सुन्दर ६ ।। १५५ ।। वाममार्गे च गौर्यायाः सिद्धयोगेश्वरीमते । -५५७ -५५६ मते पिचुमते चैव तथा देव्यामते तु च ।। १५६ ।। शिवादूतीमते देव खेचर्याश्च ५८ मतोत्तरे ५९ । । मते डामरदूती च तथा वै सुन्दरीमते ।। १५७ ।। मङ्गलाया मते चैव व्योमसन्तानसन्ततौ५६१ । व्योमगर्भे ६२ हृषीकेशे तथा चैव‍ तु गह्वरे ॥। १५८ ।। ५६४ दीक्षिता ये कलौ देव शिष्यास्तन्त्रागमेषु च । ५६५ ५६६ कलौ युगस्य संसिद्धिं न ते प्राप्यन्ति पुत्रकाः ५६७ ।। १५९ ।।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY 253 (The Tantras are): NirvāSayogottara and the Kālottara. (There is) Para, the Ūrdhvasrota and KaraSa as well as the Svacchandabhairava. (There is the) Nityātantra, a Yāmala and the TripurārSava. (150cd-151) (There is another) Yāmala, the Rurubheda, and the Brahmayāmala, OÆāmara, Õāmara, as well as the Carcikākrama. (Another is) the one called, Picu and so too, O Mahādeva, the Kālikākrama as well as the Bhairavatantra, Somasiddhānta, and Lākula. (152-153) (Others are) the Tumbura, Ekavīra, Jayātantra and Vāsuka. (There is the) Māta‰ga (Āgama), the Brahmatantra, Pratin˜hā, and Pārameśvara. (154) (Others are the) ĀSava (Tantra), Pi‰gala, Rasasvacchandaka and, O beautiful one, the Vācaspati, Ādya, and Laknapāda. (155) (Others are) the Vāmamārga of (the goddess) Gauryā, the Siddhayogeśvarīmata, the Mata, the Picumata, as well as the Devyāmata. (156) (There are the) Śivādūtīmata, Khecarī, Matottara, Õāmaradūtīmata, Sundarīmata, Ma‰galāmata, the lineage of the Vyomasantāna,Vyomagarbha, Hrnīkeśa and Gahvara. (157-158) O god, those disciples and spiritual sons (putraka) who have been initiated in the Age of Strife into the Tantras and Āgamas (such as these) will not attain success in the Age of Strife. (159)

sanskrit: 254 ५६९ कुमारिकाखण्ड: यावन्न कुलसिंहस्य क्रमोदय महीपते । पश्चिमस्य गृहस्यैव पुत्रकानां प्रवेशनम् तावत् तेषां कुतो भोग्यं कुतः प्रत्यय ५७० ॥ १६० ॥ कौलिकम् । कुतो मोक्ष दरिद्राणां कुलक्रमविवर्जिताम् ॥ १६१ ॥ पुनर्दीक्षारिहाः सर्वे मेरुमार्गविवर्जिता: ४ । ५७३ भविष्यन्ति कलौ देव पश्चिमे सिंहदर्शने -५७७ ५७६ ५७५ ।। १६२ ॥ कृत्वा त्यागं गुरोः पूर्वं त्यक्त्वा पूर्वाश्रमक्रमम् । ततश्चानुग्रहं कुर्यात् सविशेष तु पश्चिमे ।। १६३ ॥ अन्यथा पशव: ९ सर्वे भ्रामितास्ते मया कलौ । ५८२ युगानुरूपतो मोक्ष दर्शनं दर्शनं प्रति ।। १६४ ॥ कृतयुगे ऊध्वस्रोत वै त्रेतायां दक्षिणं तथा । द्वापरे ८४ वामस्रोत तु पश्चिम कलिरुच्यते ।। १६५ ।। कलौ तु पश्चिमं स्रोत सद्योजातं कुलक्रमम् । उदय चतुधी प्रोक्तं युगानां शैवदर्शने ॥ १६६ ।। यस्य यस्य युगस्यैव अन्तर्धानं तस्य तस्य भवेत् सिद्धिरन्यथा न गतस्य च । कदाचन ।। १६७ ।। •५९२ युगोऽन्य दर्शनं चान्यं तथा चान्य गुरुस्तथा । सर्वं तं निष्फलं तस्य यथाज्यं भस्ममध्यतः ५९४ ।। १६८ ।। गृहम् ५९८ एवं ज्ञात्वा तु प्रथम कलिस्या पश्चिम गुरुश्चाह च पूर्वेषां श्रीमतार्थे महेश्वर ।। १६९ ।। ६०२ मम ॐकारपीठे व अवतारं ०० ६०३ महेश्वर । तु । तथाधिकार॰॰ सिंहस्य आख्यातं दक्षिणापथे तत्रैव प्रत्यय शुद्धं चतुष्पादेषु संस्थितम् । ६०६ । ।। १७० ।। क्षेत्रमाहात्म्य शिष्याणां वर्तते च गृहे गृहे ।। १७१ ॥ मुद्रास्फोटादि वेधञ्च कोङ्कणे दक्षिणापथे ।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY 255 O Lord of the Earth, unless the Transmission of the Lion Kula (siˆhakulakrama) arises and the spiritual sons (putraka) enter the Western House, how can they possess the object of pleasure (bhogya) (or achieve) Kaula realisation (pratyaya)? (160-161ab) How is liberation possible for those poor people who do not have the Kulakrama? O god, in the Age of Strife they will become the destroyers and enemies of initiation and will not possess the Path of Meru in the Western Teaching of the Lion (siˆhadarśana).50 (161cd-162) Once one has given up the tradition of one's previous stage of life (āśrama)51 and abandoned (all things) before the teacher, (the latter) should then grace him in a special way in the Western (Tradition). All those (who act) otherwise are fettered souls, deluded by me in the Age of Strife. (163-164ab) Liberation and the doctrine (darśana) accord with the Age (of their revelation). In the Krta Age (the revealed doctrine is that of) the Upper Current, in the Tretā Age, the Right (Current), in the Dvāpara Age, the Left Current while the Western Current, which is the Kulakrama of Sadyojāta, is (the one revealed) in the Age of Strife. The fourfold arising (udaya) of the Ages has (thus) been stated according to Śaiva doctrine (śaivadarśana).52 (164cd-166) One has success (siddhi) if the Age in which (the teaching) has been hidden accords to the one that one is in, and never otherwise. (If) the Age is one and the teaching (darśana) and the teacher are another, then all that will be fruitless for him, like (offering) clarified butter into ashes. (167-168) Once one has understood (the matter) thus, (one knows that) the Western House is the first (and best) in the Age of Strife. And, O Great Lord, I am the teacher of the meaning of the Śrīmata of the ones that (came) before. (169) O Great Lord, I have descended into the sacred seat of O¤ and the authority of the tradition (siˆha) has been explained in the Deccan (dakniSāpatha). There insight (pratyaya) is pure and established on (all) four legs. (170-171ab) (A eulogy of) the glory of (that) sacred area (knetra) is in the home of every disciple. Explosions at a mere gesture (mudrāspho˜a) and the piercing (of the inner centres by KuSÆalinī) take place (everywhere) in Ko‰kaSa, in the Deccan (dakniSāpatha). (171cd-172ab)

sanskrit: 256 कुमारिकाखण्ड: तत्राज्ञा ख्यापिता पूर्वं मया पूर्णाख्यसंज्ञके ॥। १७२ ।। नाख्यातं मानवे गुह्यं गुरुणा दक्षिणापथे । ६११ तवाख्यातं तु सिद्धस्य रहस्यं मेरुमार्गगम् ।। १७३ ।। पीठोद्याणे १२ त्रिमुद्रायां मण्डलं च कुलागमम् । चतुर्विंशतिसाहस्रं उद्धृतं लक्षपादकात् ।। १७४ ।। मयापि खेचरात् प्राप्तं हिमवन्तान्मुखागमम् । प्राप्ते कलियुगे शंभो १५ म्लेच्छराज्ये तथोत्तरे ।। १७५ ।। मधुमन्थनावतारे ६१६, ६१६७रावणस्य समागमे । a तस्मिन् चैवाद्यपीठस्य श्मशाने करवीरके ।। १७६ ।। रुद्रांशकस्य सिद्ध्यस्य विद्धचित्तस्य १८ भैरव । ६१९ अधिकार१२° प्रदातव्यं एतत् सिद्धकुलागमम् ।। १७७ ।। उपदेश” यथावस्थ” निशाचारेण १२३ कौलिकम् १२४ । संहितार्थं महत्यर्थं कथनीयमदृष्टवत् ।। १७८ ।। ६२५ •६२६ दद्याद् ज्ञानं क्रमाम्नायं कीत्यर्थं दक्षिणापथे । सविशेषं च हृदय—२७ चातुर्विंशत्सहस्रकम् ।। १७९ ।। दातव्यं धीपुरे शक्त्या रूपमाश्रित्य मानवम् । मानवस्य तु शिष्यस्य भावशुद्धस्य सुन्दर ।। १८० ।। तस्य दद्यान्न दोषोऽस्ति‘१९ अन्यथा दोषभाग् भवेत् । तेनैवाराधिता पूर्वं अहं त्रिदशमण्डले ।। १८१ ॥ तस्य तुष्टा ह्यहं शम्भो १३१ निर्मितो ३२ मत्यलोकत: ६३४ ६३५ ६३३ । मानवेन तु रूपेण सिद्धोऽसौ नात्र संशयः ।। १८२ ।। जन्मजन्मान्तराभ्यासात् अहमाराधिता हर ।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY 257 There, I imparted the Command in (the seat) called PūrSa. The secret that was not told amongst men was (imparted) by the teacher in the Deccan (dakniSāpatha).53 (172cd-3ab) I have told you who are the Siddha, the secret on the Path of Meru, the maSÆala and Kula scripture within (the Triangle called) the Triple Gesture which is in the garden of the sacred seats. (173cd-174ab) The (Śrīmata) of twenty-four thousand (verses) has been taken from (that of) one hundred and twenty-five thousand. I too have obtained the oral scripture (mukhāgama) from Himavat, the Skyfarer. (174cd-175ab) O Śambhu, when the Age of Strife comes and the rule of the barbarians (mleccharājya) (is established) in the north with RāvaSa's arrival54 and the descent (of the teachings takes place by) the churning of the honey (of the ocean of the Yoni),55 one should give authority, O Bhairava, to the Siddha whose mind has been pierced (with divine power) and who is a part of Rudra (rudrāˆśa). (This should be done) in the cremation ground (called) Karavīra belonging to the First Sacred Seat.56 (175cd-177abc) This is the scripture of the Siddhakula. This is the Kaulika teaching established by the practice that takes place at night (niśācāra). (177d-178ab) The meaning of the scripture, its great meaning, should be told as if (the scripture) had not been seen. One should impart the knowledge, which is the Krama tradition, in the Deccan in order to (spread) the fame (of the deity). (178cd-9ab) In particular, assuming a human form, one should impart the heart (of the scripture, namely) that of twenty-four thousand verses, within the citadel of the intellect (dhī) by means of the power (of grace). (179cd-180ab) O handsome one, it should be given to a human disciple whose sentiment is pure. (Thus) there is no defect; otherwise, one shall have no share of it. (180cd-181ab) O Śambhu, I was worshipped by him in the past in the midst of the Circle of the Gods (tridaśamaSÆala). I was pleased with him (and so I) fashioned (him) in the world of mortals. (181cd-182ab) He is, without a doubt, a Siddha in human form. O Hara, I was worshipped by (his) practice from one birth to another. (182cd-183ab)

sanskrit: 258 कुमारिकाखण्ड: पूर्व ३६ रुद्रांशको यस्तु स लभेद्धि कुलागमम् ॥ १८३ ॥ सिद्धो मानुष्यरूपेण निर्मितो मत्यलोकत: ६३८ ६३९ ।। । उपकाराय जन्तूनां स लभेत्परमं मतम् ॥ १८४ ॥ वेत्त्यसौ संहितार्थं तु दुर्बोध्यं देवदुर्लभम् । ६४१ सूत्रसंकेतभाषार्थं पारम्पर्यक्रमागतम् ।। १८५ ।। तत्राह४२ मन्त्रमूर्तिस्था४३ त्व४४ तत्र परमो गुरुः । ६४५ । तत्र पूजा त्रिकालं तु कर्तव्य मण्डलं पुनः ।। १८६॥ यथाहं च तथा त्वं च ४६ तथा वै खेचरं क्रमम् । यथागममहाज्ञानं तथासौ मतबोधकः ।। १८७ ॥ पश्यते ज्ञानचक्षुभ्यां न द्वैतं गुरुणा सह ६५३ ६५० तस्यापमान ? द्रोह १२ च वचनलङ्घनं तथा ।। १८८ ॥ न कर्तव्यं कदाचिद् वा ६५४ ६५५ विद्वेषं न समाचरेत् । अन्धकारे ५६ यथा दीपो निशायां तु निशाकरः ।। १८९ । १६५८ तथासौ दीपको मन्त्री ओलीनां गोत्रसन्ततौ । ६६० तस्यैव५९ यत् कृतं किञ्चित् परार्थ चैव पुत्रकैः ॥ १९० ॥ तत् सर्वं मे प्रमाणं तु तस्य तिष्ठाम्यहं पुरे । मन्त्रसिंहासनं तस्य अधिकारं त्रयोलिषु ॥। १९१ ॥ ६६४ मतबोधकसिद्धस्य आख्यात दक्षिणापथें । योजनशतदूरस्थ पश्यते ज्ञानचक्षुषा ।। १९२ ।। रिक्तहस्तैर्न६७ सिद्धि:१६८ स्यात् पूर्णहस्तेन सिद्धिभाक् । ।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY 259 The one who is a part of Rudra should, first of all, obtain the Kula scripture. (He is) the Siddha who has been fashioned in the form of a man in the world of mortals. (183cd-184ab) In order to help people, he should obtain the supreme Mata. He (is the one who) knows the meaning of (this) scripture which is hard to understand and obtain (even) by the gods. (184cd-185ab) (It is) the meaning of the language of the convention of the sūtra that has come down through the sequence of the line of teachers (pāramparyakrama). There I am established in the form of mantra and you are the supreme teacher. (185cd-186ab) There the rite of adoration takes place at (all) three times, and (so) one should fashion the maSÆala (there). Just as I am so are you — and such, indeed, is the Transmission of the Skyfarers (khecarakrama). (186cd-7ab) Just as is the great knowledge of scripture, so is he the one who awakens to (the meaning of) the Mata. He (who) sees with the eyes of knowledge (realises) that there is no duality (between himself) and the teacher. (187cd-188ab) One should never disrespect him, do violence (to him), disobey (his) words or despise (him). (188cd-189ab) This reciter of mantra is the illuminater of the lineages of the family of the clan (gotrasantati), just as a lamp is in the darkness and the moon at night. (189cd-190ab) Whatever he does is for the sake of others, and along with (his) spiritual sons (putraka), he is the means of my knowledge (pramāSa) and I abide in the city of his (body). (190cd-191ab) The lion throne of mantra, which is the authority in the three lineages of this accomplished one who awakens to (the teaching) of the Mata, has been explained in the Deccan. (191cd-192ab) He (can) see with the eye of knowledge (an object even) at a hundred leagues distance. (192cd) Those whose hands are empty (and do not bear offerings to their teacher and the deity do) not (achieve) success. (But, on the contrary), one whose hands are full is successful. (193ab)

sanskrit: 260 पश्यत्यसौ महामन्त्री गुरुं प्रत्यक्षभैरवम् ६७१ कुमारिकाखण्ड: ।। १९३ ।। । अन्यगोत्रस्य शिष्येन चर्चा ७२ नैव ६७३ तु कारयेत् । ६७५ कन्यसोऽपि गुरोरोघे ५ स ज्येष्ठ इति मन्यते ।। १९४ ।। •६७७ •६७८ • स्व-ओल्या च क्रम तस्य शोध्य॰॰९ वक्राकुलागमे ततः सिद्धिर्भवेच्छिष्ये अन्यथा न कदाचन ।। १९५ ।। ६८२ ६८३ यस्येदं“ ” श्रीमतं देव गृहे तिष्ठति पूजितम् । ·६८४ । तस्य लक्ष्मी सदाकाल अह८५ तिष्ठामि८६ तत्पुरे ।। १९६ ।। ६८७ ·६८८ यत्र यत्र शुभ“ किञ्चित् तत्राहं चाधिकारिणी ८९ । ६९० पठते यस्तु तत्त्वज्ञः सकलं वा तदर्धकम् ॥ १९७ ।। अधीर्धमथ पादं ९९ वा१९२ श्लोकमेक तदर्धकम् । ६९१ ६९४ तस्य ज्ञानफलावाप्ति इहलोके च भुक्तिभाक्' ६९६ ६९८ स पुनर्विन्दते सर्वं चतुःपादं क्रमेण तु । ६९५ । ।। १९८ ।। प्रत्यक्षं चिञ्चिणीनाथ९९९ मायारूपेण मानवः ॥ १९९ ॥ यो योऽवलोक्यते जन्तुः सोऽपि याति परे पदे । 006 ७०१ ७०३ दर्शनात् स्पर्शनादेव” आलापात् सह संगमात् ।। २०० ।। पापीना जायते सिद्धिज्ञानदीक्षा प्रवर्तते । •७०७ पठितं शृणुते यस्तु श्रीमते कुलागमम् ॥ २०१ ।। मन्त्रोद्धारं तु यः पश्येत् प्रमादादविभावितः । तत्क्षणाद्“ दीक्षितोऽसौ वै गतोऽसौ पश्चिमे गृहे ।। २०२ ।। गुरुमण्डलकं कार्यं आगमस्य गुरोग्रतः । साष्टाङ्गप्रणिपातैस्तु त्रिप्रदक्षिणपूर्वकैः ।। २०३ ।। ७१२ नमस्कारेन्महाभक्त्या अभिवन्द्य पुनः पुनः । ७१४ तस्य वेत्ता पुर्नर्मन्त्री॰३ पूर्णसिद्धि: प्रवर्तते ।। २०४ ।। ते शिष्याः क्रमिका:५ शुद्धाः यैर्दृष्टं श्रीमतं त्विदम् । ७१७ ते मुक्ता जीवमान्तोऽपि अन्ये जीवन्तका मृताः ।। २०५ ।।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY 261 That great reciter of mantra sees his teacher as Bhairava directly visible. (193cd) One should not discuss (matters of doctrine) with disciples of other spiritual clans (gotra). (194ab) Even the youngest member of the teacher’s spiritual current (gurvogha) is considered to be the oldest (amongst those who are not). (194cd) The Krama in his own lineage is to be purified (in the manner taught) in the scripture of the Vakrākula. Thus the disciple will have yogic power (siddhi) within himself. Otherwise never. (195) O god, I, the goddess of wealth (Laknmī) am always present in the home of one in which this Śrīmata is present and is worshipped. I am the authority wherever there is anything auspicious. (196-197ab) The knower of reality who reads it all, or half or a quarter (of it), or (even just) one verse, or a half or a quarter (of one), gets the fruit (of it) in this world and he enjoys worldly benefits. He then gradually gets the entire (scripture) and (all) four parts (pāda) (of it). (197cd-199ab) CiñciSīnātha is directly visible in (his) Māyā form as a man.57 Whoever he gazes at, that person also reaches the supreme plane (of existence). (199cd-200ab) Sinners gain yogic power (siddhi) (just) by seeing (him) (darśana), touching (him), speaking or meeting (with him), and the Initiation of Knowledge takes place.58 (200cd-201ab) He who hears this Kula scripture, the Śrīmata being read, or who, due to negligence, is unnoticed and sees the extraction of the mantras, is initiated that very moment and enters the Western House.59 (201cd-202) One should fashion the MaSÆala of the Teachers of the scripture in front of the teacher.60 It (should be) worshipped repeatedly with great devotion by performing full-length prostrations preceded by triple circumambulations. Then the reciter of mantra (comes to) know it and (he achieves) complete success. (203-204) Those disciples are pure and belong to the tradition (kramika) who have seen this Śrīmata. They are liberated although still alive, while the others, (although) alive, are (as if) dead.61 (205)

sanskrit: 262 कुमारिकाखण्ड: इह जन्म” समासाद्य येनाभ्यस्तं न श्रीमतम् । तथा नाकर्णितं भक्त्या वृथा तस्य तु जीवितम् ।। २०६ ।। येनावधारितं नैव महारत्नं कुलागमम् । ७२० पुनस्तद्” दुर्लभं तस्य अन्यजन्मनि जन्मनि ।। २०७ ।। प्राप्तो मणिर्यथा शुद्ध : १ चन्द्रकान्ति॑ि॰?” त्यजेन्नरः । ७२१ ७२३ भूयोस्त दुर्लभं तस्य तथा श्रीश्रीमतं नृणाम् ।। २०८ ।। यो द्विषेत् श्रीमत? देव आचार्यं मतबोधकम् । ७२७ ७२८ यात्यसौ७२६ नरकं घोरं यावद् भूतसंप्लवम् ।। २०९ ।। श्रीनाथं भैरवं चैव पादुकामिति उच्चरेत् । ७३० ७३१ अग्रतः पार्शवतो” वापि क्रमत: स्वगुरोग्रतः ।। २१० ।। यत्र यत्र॰’२ गतो मन्त्री त्रितयं तु समुच्चरेत् । ३३ शिवायेति॰३४ न वक्तव्यं मन्त्रमेतत् षडक्षरम् ।। २११ ।। नोच्चार्य३६ कौलिके३७ मार्गे पादुकामिति उच्चरेत्” । मण्डलं च क्रमोद्धारं कारयेन्मतसन्निधौ ॥। २१२ ।। अथवा भव्यते” भक्त्या गुरुमण्डलपूजनम् ७४१ ७४० । कृत्वादौ क्रमपूजां च पुष्पधूपादिभिः क्रमात् ।। २१३ ।। चन्दन कुंकुम चैव कस्तूर्याी च विलेपयेत् । अलिपिशितसंयुक्तं दीपं प्रज्वाल्य शोभनम् ।। २१४ ।। पुष्पप्रकरं कर्तव्य॰॰५ सुगन्धं गन्धमोदितम् । कुमारी पूजयेदेका तथा आचार्यपुत्रकम् ।। २१५ ।। ७४९ आदौ मन्त्राश्च मुद्राश्च गुरुपञ्चकमण्डलम् । ७५० । मम विद्यामूलसूत्र नत्वा ध्यायेत् कुलागमम् ।। २१६ ।। एकान्ते विजने रम्ये दुष्टजन्तुविवर्जिते । ७५३ आचार्यं स्वगुरुं वाथ गुरोमीतामथापि वा ।। २१७ ।। एषामाज्ञा¨¨४ प्रर्थयित्वा ददादेशमिति ब्रूयात् । -७५७ मतार्थ”“८ भवत्वस्माकं तथा सिद्धिस्तु कौलिकी ।। २१८ ।। ईदृशेन विधानेन ततो वाच्यं महेश्वर M ७६० ।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY 263 The life of one who, born here (in this world), has not practiced the Śrīmata or listened to it with devotion, is useless. (206) He who has not paid attention to the Kula scripture, the great jewel, (will find it) hard to acquire it again in subsequent lifetimes. (207) Just as upon finding a flawless gem, a man should give up a moonstone (and keep the gem) which is hard to acquire again, such is the case with the venerable Śrīmata for men.62 (208) O god, he who hates the Śrīmata and the teacher who awakens (to the meaning of the) Mata goes to a horrible hell until all things are destroyed. (209) One should utter (the words) 'Bhairava', 'Śrīnātha' and 'pādukā' in due order, in front and to the sides, before his teacher. (210) Wherever the reciter of mantra may be, he should recite (‘pādukā’ which is) the third one. He should not say 'śivāya'. This six-syllabled mantra63 should not be uttered on the Kaulika path. One should say 'pādukā' (instead). (211-212ab) One should cause the maSÆala to be fashioned and the Krama extracted close to the Mata. Otherwise, one can contemplate the worship of the MaSÆala of the Teachers with devotion. (212cd-213ab) Having first worshipped the Krama with flowers and incense in due order, one must smear (it with) sandal paste and vermillion along with musk and (make offerings) of meat and wine. Having lit a beautiful lamp, one should make a sweet-smelling heap of flowers daubed with scent. (213cd-215ab) One should worship a virgin along with the teacher and (his) apprentice (putraka). (And then, having) first (uttered) the mantras, (made) the gestures, (worshipped) the maSÆala of the five teachers and bowed to the Root Sūtra of my Vidyā,64 one should study the Kula scripture in a beautiful, solitary place where there are no people or ferocious animals. (215cd-217ab) (The disciple) should request either the officiant (ācārya), his teacher or the teacher's mother65 for the Command. (Then) he should say: "Give (us your) permission (ādeśa). May we have the meaning of the Mata and the Kaulikī accomplishment (siddhi).” Then, O Maheśvara, it should be uttered (by the teacher) according to this prescription. (217cd-219ab)

sanskrit: 264 कुमारिकाखण्ड: अन्तरङ्गीसुभाषादिशुद्ध” चातिमनोहरम् ।। २१९ ॥ किञ्चित्काकलिशब्देन‍ सिद्धान्तं तत्र कारयेत् । ७६७ ७६४ सद्यातिललिता‍ भाषा गान्धर्वादेरनेकशः ।। २२० ।। तया॰॰५ समयमेवोक्त॰६६ श्रद्धया ँ तत्८ पठेन्नरः । अन्यथा सिद्धिहानिः स्यात् साधकस्य भवेत् तत ७७२ निशाचारेण व्याख्यात? कुलाचारेण कारयेत् । व्याख्याने या विधिः पूर्वं तवाख्याता वरानन ७७४ -७७५ ७७३ कृत्वा चाकर्णयेदेव नान्यथा तु कदाचन । ७७७ ७७० ।। २२१ ।। ।। २२२ ।। दिव्ये ६ मनोरमे स्थाने पशुदृष्टिविवर्जिते ।। २२३ ।। पुष्पप्रकरसंकीर्णे सुगुप्ते चाधिवासिते । महाधूपसुगन्धाढ्ये' आचार्य: पूर्वसंमुखः ।। २२४ ।। पश्चिमाभिमुखैः शिष्यैः श्रोतव्यं च कुलागमम् । ७७९ गुप्ते प्रकाशयेच्छिष्य दातव्यं च मुखागमम् ।। २२५ ।। तथा गूढार्थचित्तं स्यादचिर८३ वा भविष्यति । तन्मूलक्रमविद्या च षोढान्यासं यदुद्धृतम् ।। २२६ ॥ अलिना कुंकुमेनैव लिख्य “पूज्य प्रदापयेत् । ७८९ गृहीत्वा क्षाम्यते“ शिष्य : अलिना शोधितं पिबेत् ।। २२७ ।। तत्पश्चात् समया श्राव्या संक्षेपेणाष्टक च यत् ९२ । न निन्द्याद्¨” योगियोगिन्यो” नेक्षेन्नग्नां परस्त्रियम् ।। २२८ ॥ न जातु कुत्सितं ब्रूयात् अनिच्छन्तीं न कामयेत् । ७९८ गुरुपत्नीँ वीरभार्या वक्रिका वामनीं तथा ।। २२९ ।। कुमारीं व्रजिकां” चैव च्छिन्ननासां न कामयेत् । ८०० ८०२ ८०३ एवं वै समयाः श्राव्याः संक्षेपेण वरानन ।। २३०॥ ८०४ पूरत: कथयिष्यामि चतुःषष्टिसमयान् यथा । ७९९
english: CHAPTER THIRTY 265 The teaching (siddhaanta), which is very beautiful and pure with fine esoteric dictums, should be expounded there briefly in sweet tone of voice. (219cd-220ab) The Rule has been uttered many times by that speech (bhānā) which is (charming) like that of the celestial musicians, and which is artistically expressive (atilalitā) and easy to grasp. Man should study it with faith. Otherwise, the adept's accomplishments are annulled. (220cd-221) (The teaching) has been explained (essentially) as (being) the Conduct at Night (niśācāra).66 (The teacher) should have (his disciple) apply (it) by the Conduct of Kula (kulācāra). (222ab) O handsome one, the way (of listening to) the explanation (vyākhyāna) was told to you before. Once it has been applied, one should listen (to the scripture) in the same (way). It (should) never (be done) in any other way. (222cd-223ab) One should listen to the Kula scripture in a sacred and pleasing place out of sight of the uninitiated. (It should be) strewn with heaps of flowers, well hidden, purified and rich with the fragrance of fine incense. The teacher sits facing east with the disciples facing west. (223cd-225ab) The Kula scripture should be given and explained to the disciple in secret. In this way the mind should be (centred) on the deep (hidden) meaning (of the scripture), or it will be so in a short time. (225cd-226ab) Once it has been written with vermillion and liquor67 and worshipped, (the teacher) should give the Vidyā of the main Krama (mūlakrama) and the sixfold deposition (to his disciple). (226cd-7ab) Taking (the sacrificial drink),68 the disciple is graced and, once it has been purified, he should drink it with liquor. After that he should be made to hear the Samayā (Vidyā) in brief along with the group of eight (mantras of the Mothers). (227cd-228ab) One should not criticise yogis or Yoginīs and one should not (look) at a naked woman of another (man). One should never use vulgar language or desire a woman who does not want (to be desired). (228cd-229ab) One should not desire the wife of the teacher, the wife of a Kaula yogi (vīra), a hunchbacked woman, a female dwarf, a virgin, a nun or (an adulteress) whose nose has been cut off. (229cd-230ab) In this way, O handsome one, (the teacher) should cause (the disciple) to hear the Rules in brief. Later on I will tell (you all) the sixty-four Rules69 (completely). (230cd-231ab)

sanskrit: 266 कुमारिकाखण्डः गुरोराज्ञा न लङ्केत लङ्घनान्नरकं भवेत् ।। २३१ ।। पालनाद् भवते सिद्धिः पदं प्राप्नोति शाश्वतम् । कुगृहे कुजने देव स्थाने चैव तु कुत्सिते ।। २३२ ।। पशुमध्ये न चाख्येय आगमार्थं“ मुखागमम् । नैव दद्यात्” तु सहसा पशूना न प्रदर्शयेत् ॥ २३३ ।। संवृत्य तूष्णीमास्थाय”” तदा मौनं समाचरेत् । ९८१४ गुर्वोघं यस्तु जानाति तथा सांवत्सरं क्रमम् ।। २३४ ।। मण्डलं मूलसूत्रं तु तस्य देयं मुखागमम् -८१५ । अन्यथा निर्गुणं शिष्यं ज्ञात्वा भक्तिसमन्वितम् ।। २३५ ।। स्वशिष्य”६ च तत:“ ँ कृत्वा तदा देयं मुखागमम् । अन्यथाभावुक”” शिष्यं नैव दद्यान्मुखागमम् अवस्थां उन्मनीभावं आज्ञाप्रत्ययपूर्वकम् । ८२३ ८१९ ।। २३६ ।। जानाति २१ देहजं चिन्हं सोऽस्ति २२ शिष्यः कुलागमे ।। २३७ ।। । स्फुरते प्रत्ययावस्था २५ यस्य तिष्ठति भावना २६ । सहजमेलकट २७ शम्भो स भवेन्मतभाजनः ॥ २३८ ॥ क्रमभक्तिरता ये च पीठाराधनतत्पराः । २९ ८२८ तेष्वग्रे दर्शयेत्” देव भक्तिहीनान् विवर्जयेत् ।। २३९ ।। ८३१
english: CHAPTER THIRTY 267 There, with sweet-sounding words, (the teacher) should impart the doctrine (siddhānta), which by virtue of its esoteric, fine language and the rest is pure and very beautiful. (219cd-220ab) One should not disobey the teacher's Command. By transgressing (his commands, the disciple goes to) hell. Success (siddhi) (is achieved) by observing it and he (who does so) attains the eternal plane (of existence). (231cd-232ab) O god, the meaning of the scripture, the oral scripture, should not be explained in a bad household, amongst bad people, in a place of ill repute or amongst the uninitiated (paśu). (232cd-233ab) It should not be given out hastily (sahasā). It should not be shown to the uninitiated (paśu). (But), covering (the scripture) quietly, one should practice (it in) silence. (233cd-234ab) The oral scripture, the maSÆala and the Root Sūtra should be given (only) to one who knows the Current of the Teachers (gurvogha) and the liturgical year (saˆvatsarakrama). 70 (234cd-235ab) Or else, when (a teacher) comes to know of a disciple (of another teacher) who does not have the yogic power (guSa) (imparted by initiation but) who possesses devotion, he should adopt him as his own disciple and then the oral scripture should be given to him. (235cd-236ab) One should never, in any other circumstance, impart the oral scripture to a disciple who is otherwise disposed. He who knows the Transmental state heralded by the signs of attainment of the Command is (a true) disciple of the Kula scripture. (236cd-237) He for whom the state of realisation (pratyayāvasthā) manifests, whose contemplative absorption (bhāvanā) abides (without change) and who (experiences) the spontaneous union (sahajamelaka) (of Śiva and Śakti), possesses the Mata. (238) O god, the (scripture) should be shown (only) to those who are devoted to the Transmission (krama) and who are intent on worshiping the sacred seats. One should avoid those who are devoid of devotion. (239)

sanskrit: 268 कुमारिकाखण्ड: गुरोरुपजीवका ये च कपटव्रतधारिणः । न तेषां सह संभाषं ३३ श्रीमतं न ४ प्रकाशयेत् ।। २४० ।। मतमेकमिदं सारं देव्यादेशात् प्रकाशयेत् । •८३६ ये बुध्यन्ति नरा देव ते मुक्ता नात्र संशयः ।। २४१ ।। .८३८ .८४० ८४१ इत्याद्यावतारे महामन्थानभैरवयज्ञे अन्वये सप्तकोटिप्रमाणे ३९ मेरुमार्गविनिर्गते लक्षपादाधिके विद्यापीठमार्गे विमलषट्कनिर्णये कादिभेदे आज्ञापारमेश्वरें स्वामिनीमते श्रीचतुर्विंशत्सहस्रसंहितायां अव्वाक्रमभाषिते श्रीकुलागम- माहात्म्यवर्णने ४२ लिखनव्याख्यानविधिर्नामानन्दः ३ ।। ३० ।। ८४३
english: CHAPTER THIRTY 269 One should not converse with those who live off the teacher and who are intent on practicing deceit. The Śrīmata should not be shown (to them). This essence (sāra) (of the scripture), the one Mata, should be revealed (only) at the goddess’s command. O god, those who understand (it) are, without a doubt, liberated beings. (240-241) This is the (thirtieth) chapter called the Prescribed Way of Writing and Explaining (the Scripture), which comes in the course of describing the greatness of the scripture of the Śrīkula. It belongs to the primordial descent into the great sacrifice of the Churning Bhairava in the tradition (anvaya) that consists of seventy million (verses) that has emerged on the Path of Meru and (extends) for more than a hundred thousand quarter (verses). It is on the path of the Seat of Knowledge (vidyāpī˜ha) and is the ultimate purport of the Pure Six Thousand (verses) (vimalana˜ka) in the division beginning with `KĀ' in the venerable scripture of twenty-four thousand (verses) (known as) the Svāminīmata of the Supreme Lord's command as uttered within the Tradition of the Mother (avvākrama).

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER SEVENTEEN 1. The first part of this chapter, from verses two to seven, is the Santānasūtra. The rest of the chapter is dedicated to an explanation; it is set in the technical and symbolic language of the Kubjikā Tantras. The Santānasūtra is a list of sixteen ‘conventions’ (saˆketa), that is, topics, points of doctrine or brief teachings (numbered one to sixteen in the translation) concerning the lineage of the transmission, its nature, founder and the maSÆala from which it originates. The latter is the triangular core of the SaˆvartāmaSÆala, which is described in the Root Sūtra (see chapters 26, 38 and 42). Recited in the course of the ritual, the adept would memorize this and other similar sūtras to enable him to recall each point along with the explanation he received from his teacher. Presumably, in the course of time the explanation was set to writing and came to form the second half of this chapter. The Saˆvartārthaprakāśa (fl. 6a-6b) reproduces most of this chapter and comments on it in its usual brief manner. Chapter 53 below consists of another, shorter, Santānasūtra, which is also called the Jñānasūtra. A few of the ‘conventions’ we find in this Santānasūtra are also found in that one. They are compared in the notes. There is a more substantial correspondence with chapter 22 of the Ambāmatasaˆhitā. The first fifteen odd verses that introduce the Santānasūtra are essentially the same in the KuKh and AS. KuKh 17/2-6 = AS 22/2cd-7ab and AS 22/12-16ab essentially (but not literally) in large part correspond to KuKh 17/8-12ab. These have been compared in the critical apparatus of the edition. These verses are a list of sixteen 'conventions' and a series of questions concerning them. The rest of the chapter is a response to these questions. Thus the sixteen 'conventions' are the same in both texts; however, the explanations, although compatible, differ. According to the AS, the sixteen ‘conventions’ are taught in the Transmission of the Child (bālakrama). They are as many mantras or seed-syllables that should be deposited on the body to purify it as a preliminary to the worship of the Śrīkrama. The teacher projects them onto the body of the disciple as a part of his consecration (abhineka). As usual, if this is done correctly and successfully, the disciple shakes and exhibits the other signs of attainment (pratyaya) that accompany the penetration of the energy of the deity into his body. Our text prefers to focus on aspects and parts of the maSÆala and their formation as symbols of phases or states of emanation and levels of sonic consciousness. In order to understand the answers to the questions we must know this language of symbols. By now the reader who has read attentively will have absorbed much of this language and have a sense of its meaning. Even so, he will be assisted in the more obscure cases with brief ‘translations’. 2. The SamP says:

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER SEVENTEEN 21 Meru. This Tree is the goddess's seed-syllable. She pervades it and from there radiates out into the rest of the Triangle. The 'fame' of the tamarind is due to the presence of the goddess within it. It is, in other words, the energy of the goddess in her seed-syllable. The tamarind is in the City of the Moon. The first Siddha is said to have bent it with his power and so acquired fame. 50. The SamP explains that: The Ocean (in this case) is the Ocean of Words. There (one will find) accomplishment. (One attains) success by the study of the śāstra. sāgaraƒ śabdasāgaraƒ | tatra siddhir [siddho] bhavet | śāstrādhyayanena siddhir [siddho] bhavati | The Ocean is the Point, the Great Place, the Unbroken MaSÆala of the Point encompassed by Meru (17/39) which, in the centre of the Triangle — here called the Heart — is at its apex and hence beyond it (24/41). See 14/64cd-66ab and notes; also 2/34cd-5ab and 65/10ff. 51. The Body of Kula is made of the energies of the letters. See note to 2/32 above. 52. The maSÆala of Nityaklinnā is the Yoni.

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER EIGHTEEN 1. See intro. vol. 2, p. 254 ff.. 2. See below 19/17. 3. After discussing the Samayā Vidyā in previous chapters, the text has moved on to discuss other basic mantras and depositions of the Kubjikā Tantras. According to the ±SS 12/87, Mālinī, Śabdarāśi, Trividyā and Aghorān˜aka, along with the deposition of twelve and six limbs, constitute the body of Kula. The first four of these six are treated in the same order in this and the following chapters. 4. It is standard practice to perform a series of six depositions of mantras and syllables onto the body. This identifies it with the body made of the mantras of the deity. This chapter of our text opens with the god addressing the goddess as ‘you who are my body!’ Possessing this body, the adept is identified with the god and, thereby purified, he is ready to worship the deity he has become. Indeed, he is the teacher himself: O Mother of the Śrīkula, the teacher (ācārya) is accompanied by the guardians of the idols (mūrtipāla). He possesses supreme bliss and, self- controlled, he has performed the sixfold deposition. ācāryo [kh, g: ācārya] mūrtipālaiś [kh: -pālaś] ca sametaƒ śrīkulāmbike | paramānandasampannaƒ [g: -nnāƒ; other MSs: -panno] noÆhānyāsakrto yamī || KRU 14/145 Externally, the adept’s body made of mantras is the ‘outer’ differentiated, immanent form of the deity. Inwardly, he is one with the deity’s essential, formless and transcendental nature. This condition he renews daily, each time he performs the sixfold deposition in order to worship: O mistress of the gods, having risen in the morning, having performed the morning rite and then having again offered bali to the ghosts (bhūta), he should purify the body. Once he has performed the great sixfold deposition and is conjoined to the presiding deity of the Wheel, he offers sacrifice. He should then make the offering to the fire (homa) along with (the deities) who possess a (divine) form (mūrti). The best of teachers is himself as pervasive as am I (the god). O beloved, his form is the Void (vyomarūpa) and, endless, he has no master (but is himself the Lord) and is not present (in this world of bondage) (anāśrita). These are said to be those who possess a divine form who have taken up their abode on the plane of Stillness (nirācāra). Their bodies are girt (sannaddha) with mantras and they are skilled in ritual.

The body, made of the five elements, is the domain of Nature. By depositing Mālinī’s sonic energies on the body it is immersed in the sacrificial pit, that is, the Triangle pervaded by Mālinī’s energy, which absorbs and transforms it; and so, the individual soul is liberated from the tyranny of Nature and the five elements. 61. The Person is pervaded by the sixteen energies of the Full Moon (AS 5/156cd-157ab).

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER NINETEEN 1. This is the Wheel of the Command where the Fourth state is experienced (see above 3/133). The Point there is identified with the Divine Will (icchā). It is in the centre of the triangle in which the letters of the alphabet that constitute the Assembly of Sounds are written. Placed above each letter in the form of anusvāra, it transforms it into a seed-syllable mantra. These seed- syllables are the waves of nectar of this, the Ocean of the Point (bindvarSava). 2. VarSa (lit ‘letter’), śabda (lit. ‘word’) and rava (lit. ‘sound’) all denote the same ultimate reality, namely the Sound Absolute embodied in the figure of Bhairava, the Assembly of Sounds (śabdarāśi) who is the subject of this chapter. In these verses we are told that it is represented by the Point in the centre of the Triangle which, in the form of anusvāra, is conjoined with each letter making up the fifty aspects of the Assembly of Sounds. The Point, as we have had occasion to observe on several occasions, is the goddess as the Transmental (unmanā) which is the Command. Indirectly, therefore, we are told here that the divine energy of the Command is also the energy of mantra which, pervading the letters, transforms them into mantras. This is the Sound of Kubjikā, the Yoginī who is the energy of Speech (vācchakti). 3. These four Yogic states are discussed in the KMT chapter 17-19. There they constitute the last group of four of the Sequence of Twenty-eight. See also beginning of chapter 11 of the KMT where they are equated with the four seats, and below at 44/6cd-8ab for the same equation. This identification implies that the four states are included in the Triangle. Beyond Form is the Command, the Transmental in the center, from which the other three originate and which thus contains them. Here this is called the Stainless (nirañjana). 4. KuSÆalinī is also said to be the Body of fifty letters. As such she is Tara‰ginī. See above note to 2/34cd-35ab. 5. Concerning the Tree of Speech see intro. vol. 2 p. 118 ff.. 6. The expression ‘kārikākramasantati’ also means ‘the lineage of the transmission of the (goddess) who acts’. 7. The transmission begins with the Rudra called Bhargas or Bhargojāta — the sun. See above, note to 2/7cd-8ab. Above (see 8/26cd) the alphabet, each letter of which is governed by a Siddha, is called the ‘sequence (krama) of mātrkās’. Śabdarāśi is the assembly of the fifty ‘male’ letters. When these are understood to be energies it is called the Sequence of Mātrkās who are their fifty female counterparts. One could say, in general terms, that they are the partners of the Bhairavas but in more elaborate expositions and practical applications, they are the Yoginīs (who could also be called mātrkās) who govern the letters of the Mālinī alphabet. english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER NINETEEN 50 41. In this context Śiva is Śabdarāśi and Śakti is Mālinī. Deposited from the top of the head to the tips of the nails of the toes and back, they generate energy which expands out in the Teacher’s Mouth, the Triangle in the centre. This is NirvāSa and the Abode of the Thirty-two syllable Vidyā (see below 22/19). This is where they unite. Thus the yogi experiences the Fourth realised state of consciousness of Śabdarāśi Śiva and the Transmental energy of the Command of Mālinī, the Yoni, in a union with him that leads to the liberated state Beyond the Fourth (turīyātīta). 42. The Five Jewels in this case are the Five PraSavas (see below 24/103cd-115). Thus the ŚM enjoins that: ‘one should deposit Navātman encapsulated with the Five PraSavas (praSavādyantasaˆpu˜ena navātmānaˆ ca vinyaset | ŚM 22/119cd). A variant of this deposition of the letters of Navātman is found in some manuscripts of the ŚM (after ibid. 22/117). Each of the nine units there consists of 1) The Five PraSavas 2) a letter of Navātman 3) the place of depostion on the body in the locative 3) the salutation ‘NAMAÖ’ 4) the Five PraSavas. Thus, for example, the first unit is: AI¤ 5 HA ŚIKHĀSTHĀNE NAMAÖ AI¤ 5. The variables are: 1) Ha — the location of the topknot 2) Sa — the head 3) K±a — the forehead 4) Ma — the mouth 5) La — the heart 6) Va — navel 7) Ra —genitals 8) Ya — knees 9) Ū¤ — the two feet. ‘The location of the topknot’ may be taken to be the Cavity of Brahmā on the crown of the head. The second place — the head — is missing here, and instead of the knees there are the thighs and the shanks. 43. The text reads āraktaˆ śuddhadhavalaˆ but there is no substantive qualified by these adjectives. The armour is the next limb that follows in serial order, so presumably that is meant. 44. See above notes to 4/10-11ab.

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER TWENTY 1. Line 20/2ab is too corrupt in the MSs to reconstruct. 2. Chapter 11 of the ±SS deals with the Aghoryan˜aka, Trividyā and Tadgraha which are presented in chapters 21, this one and 23, respectively. The Triple Vidyā is presented in chapter 18 of the KMT (which corresponds to chapter 27 and 30 of the ±SS). The Parāparā Vidyā is presented in KMT 18/4-24, the Aparā Vidyā in KMT 18/25-29 and the Parā Vidyā in KMT 18/30-31. The variants of the Vidyās in these sources will be compared with the ones here. The passage there concludes by stressing the intimate relationship between the Triple Vidyā with Mālinī and Śabdarāśi and its essentially unitary nature, related to the Trika triad of goddesses Parā, Parāparā and Aparā: Conjoined with the utterance of the PraSava, the (triple) Vidyā consists of the three principles (Śiva, Vidyā and the Self) and she is established in the form (mūrti) of Śabdarāśi and Mālinī. She burns with the qualities of a body made of the Vidyās. KMT 18/32. 3. The text of this chapter is corrupt in places in the MSs., It appears that the Parāparā Vidyā, reconstructed by comparing with its version embedded in the Tadgraha mantra presented in chapter twenty-three, is: AGHORE HRĪ¤ PARAMAGHORE HRAU¤ GHORARŪPE HAÖ GH(O)RĀ- MUKHI BHĪMABHĪ±A¦I VAMA VAMA PIVA PIVA HA HE RU K±A RU K±A RAÖ RAÖ VICCE AI¤ HRĪ¤ HAU¤ The whole Vidyā embedded in Tadgraha below in chapter 23 is: AGHORE HRĪ¤ PARAMAGHORE HRAU¤ GHORARŪPE HAÖ GHORA- MUKHI BHĪMABHĪ±A¦I VAMA VAMA PIVA PIVA HA HE RU RU RA RA VICCE AI¤ HRĪ¤ HŪ¤ HRĪ¤ AI¤ HRĪ¤ AI¤ K±A¤ HRĪ¤ HSRAU¤ The first forty-five syllables of the Triple Vidyā inserted into the mantra Tadgraha presented below in chapter twenty-three are as follows: AGHORE HRĪ¤ PARAMAGHORE HRAU¤ GHORARŪPE HAÖ GHORA- MUKHI BHĪMABHĪ±A¦I VAMA VAMA PIVA PIVA HA HE RU RU RA RA VICCE AI¤ HRĪ¤ HŪ¤ HRĪ¤ AI¤ The remaining five syllables of the two other Vidyās combined embedded in Tadgraha are: HRĪ¤ AI¤ K±A¤ HRĪ¤ HSAU¤. The MSs link ई disjunctively in this way to words in this mantra in as many as four other instances ie परमघोयी + ई, घोररूपा + ई, घोरमुखा + ई and फेत्कार्याी + ई. These are not, of course, regular Sanskrit forms. It would be easy to emend to the intended dative - घोयी + ई > घोर्यायै – a reading supported by the KMT and SKh. english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER TWENTY 56 three deities are Brahmā, VinSu and Maheśvara. The three trees are the Kadamba, Ciñca and the Bilva. Concerning these three trees and their relation to the Wheels in the body and to states of consciousness, see below 46/20-26. According to the KRP fl.15b as reported by Schoterman (1981: 51): Kulācāra holds three caves in high esteem: the Candrākhyā, the YakniSī and the Śa‰khinī. According to the ±SS (1/30), Candraguhā (the Cave of the Moon) is located where emission takes place (visargasthāna), that is, in the Cavity of Brahmā or the End of the Twelve. The three energies are will, knowledge and action. The three Vidyās are Parā, Parāparā and Aparā. The three three channels are IÆā, Pi‰galā and SunumSā. There are thus eight triads mentioned here, making twenty-four entities altogether. Four triads are listed in 39/60cd-62 where they are related to the three lineages, to conclude that the Tradition (anvaya) consists of triads that relate to the triple division of reality into gross, subtle and supreme. The following is a table that integrates these two references. I presume that the three deities mentioned here are the three goddesses listed in 39/60cd-62. 4. Variously called the Aghorān˜aka (KuKh 21/1), Aghoryan˜aka (ibid. 21/9cd), Aghoryādyan˜aka (ibid. 21/10d) Aghoryān˜aka and Ghoryān˜aka in the ±SS (11/38ab and 11/105ab, respectively), this is a deposition in eight parts called Aghorās or Ghorikās. It is found in variant forms in several Kubjikā texts. In order to edit the text, I refer to three of these sources, the KMT, ±SS and the SKh. The KMT and our text relate the Aghoryān˜aka to the subtle body called the City of Eight (puryan˜aka) (see below 21/27-28), which the KMT (18/33) explains is ‘located in Aghorī’. It goes on to give eight mantras that are formed from eight parts of the Aghorī Vidyā that make up Aghoryān˜aka to which the City of Eight is conjoined. The adept, says the KMT, should deposit the eightfold body (a‰ga) in eight vessels (18/35), which are, presumably, the eight constituents of the City of Eight listed below (21/28; see above, 13/4cd-6, note 4). The eight mantras are presented directly in eight lines of prose marked ‘verse' 34 of chapter 18 of the edition of the KMT. Each section is deposited on a separate part of the body and on the eight petals of a lotus. The core of each unit is one of the words of the Aghorī Vidyā. This is first given in the vocative and then repeated in the dative; to these, two seed-syllables are added. The ±SS (11/38-102) basically follows the KMT expanding it by adding syllables and altering some. In both texts the Vidyā is, essentially, as follows: AGHORE PARAMAGHORE GHORARŪPE GHORAMUKHI BHĪMANĀME BHĪ±A¦E VAMA PIBA The complete set of eight in the KMT is as follows. english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER TWENTY-TWO 1. See 22/11, cf. 21/1 and note. 2. Cf. 39/147. 3. The word ‘noÆhā’ is an indeclinable that means ‘in six ways’. Indeed, above (18/19cd-20) we have come across a set of six depositions collectively called ‘±oÆhānyāsa’. But this is not the only meaning of the word. Chapter 23 of the ŚM is dedicated to ±oÆhānyāsa. There it consists of a series of sixteen depositions. Thus in that case ‘noÆhā’ is equivalent to ‘noÆaśa’ — sixteen. In this line we are told that ±odhā has sixteen divisions; however, the exposition that follows is of a twelvefold deposition (22/11). An EkāknaranoÆhānyāsa is presented in the SKh (MS G fl. 13a) which is projected into twelve parts of the body. Another more extensive ±oÆhānyāsa is recorded in the SKh (MS G fl. 12b) in twenty-four units, however neither of these two appear to be the deposition described here. Kubjikā is commonly said to be sixfold (na˜prakāra), for reasons we have examined (see intro. vol. 1, p. 698). Possibly for this reason the Supreme Goddess is identified as an energy called ±oÆhā (lit. ‘the Sixfold One’). According to the KMT, in her transcendental aspect she is ‘devoid of the six letters’ i.e. forms. In her immanent aspect, she assumes the form of six energies described in the following passage: ±oÆhā is said to be power. She is supreme, the auspicious letter (aknarā). She is KuSÆalī located in the navel. She is supreme and her form the Void. She is one, supreme, subtle, imperishable and consists of radiant energy (tejas). She should be known to be the Supreme Goddess (Parā Devī), the energy devoid of the six letters. The ‘natural' (svābhāvika) (deposition) is said to (takes place when) 1) the energy Sūknmā is in Brahmā's place. 2) (This energy) is called Calā in VinSu's place. 3) She who is considered to be Dīptā is in Rudra's place. 4) She is called Stable (sthirā) within Īśvara. 5) Within Sadākhya (she is called) Born of the Melting (dravasaˆbhavā). 6) Those who know reality should know that, established in Śakti, she is the Void. She of Six Qualities (naÆguSā) is the foundation of the six yogic powers and awakens them; (she is) the Pervasive One, She Whose Form is the Void, the Endless One, She who is Without Lord (Anāthanā) and Entered In (Āśritā), She Who Connects and She Who Disconnects. Thus the one supreme energy, established in the attributes of Being (is various) according to her various functions. Her (various) types (bheda) are due to the variety of (her) functions. In reality there is no diversity (bheda). O goddess, once one performs the deposition in this way, it operates internally. Externally, she is in the form of letters. She is one and (operates) in many ways.

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER TWENTY-TWO 67 This deposition is the sixfold one with twelve divisions. It is said to take place within the ‘coming and going'. KMT 5/138cd-146ab. 4. The Moon is Sa. The letter above it is Bha. The Sun is Ha; above it is Ma. Perhaps the syllable is µHBHMĪ¤. Possibly the head of the Sun and Moon is simply the Half Moon, in which case the syllable is µHĪ¤. Either way, the Twelve Gaurīs mentioned below are probably this syllable repeated twelve times. 5. Gauryākā, I suppose, is the collective aggregate of the Twelve Gaurīs. These are the uttered in the 'going' phase marking the rise of KuSÆalinī that burns impurity (dahana) as it ascends. The 'coming' phase which is that of nourishment (apyāyana) is marked by the repetition of the second series of syllables that begins with the seed of emanation, that is, AI¤ which is also called the Lion Throne (see above 17/33 note 30) and the letter of the Lion (61/95cd-96). 6. ‘Coming and going’ is, amongst other things, the forward and reverse recitation of a mantra. See note to 3/122cd-123ab. 7. Mālinī is also said to be in the teacher’s mouth (above 18/90). 8. From what follows, it appears that in this case Parā Vidyā is AI¤ which is the goddess who is the Transmental that ‘faces downwards’ and is the female Neuter that flows with lunar nectar. The EkāknaranoÆhānyāsa presented in the SKh (MS G fl. 13a) consists simply of AI¤ SHA¤ AI¤ deposited in twelve places in the body from the head down to the genitals. Clearly that deposition differs from this one. Nonetheless, the dominant presence of AI¤ appear to be common. Indeed, it is likely that the energy ±oÆhā is this syllable. This is deposited in the twelve places in the body listed above (22/12), it seems, with twelve syllables formed from the consonants — Rudras — indicated above in code (22/4cd-8) to each of which is added a Gaurī i.e. the letter Ī is added at the end with the usual nasalization and, if I have understood correctly, with Ū at the beginning. 9. See intro. vol. 1, p. 309 ff. concerning the ‘Neuter’ and the goddess's condition as such. 10. See 24/96.

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER TWENTY-THREE 1. The goddess’s body is made of mantras and is adorned by them. Accordingly, in chapter 18 the KMT presents its exposition of the main Vidyās and mantras in this frame work. First comes the Triple Vidyā who ‘burns with the qualities of a body made of Vidyā’ (KMT 18/32). This is followed by the Aghorān˜aka, which corresponds to the goddess’s subtle body (puryan˜aka) (ibid. 18/33-35). Then comes the deposition of the Twelve Limbs (dvādaśā‰ga), which is the means through which the goddess’s ‘outer’ body is generated (dehaninpattikaraSa) (KMT 18/36-37). This is followed by the deposition of the standard six limbs by which the individual soul, firmly established (sthirīkrta) in the body of the goddess by the previous deposition, is made manifest (vyaktatvaˆ bhajate) (KMT 1/348d). In this way the ‘supreme body and supreme path’ is generated (ibid. 18/40ab). Next comes the goddess’s belt (mekhalā). This is the mantra called Twelve Verses (Dvādaśaśloka) (see below 24/13-17 and notes). Then comes Tadgraha which is the Thread of Brahmā, the Brahminical cord that, shining brilliantly and fiercely powerful, ‘should be hung with the Yoga of Tadgraha from the head to the feet’ to adorn the goddess (KMT 18/41ab, 55) . Tadgraha is said to emerge from A because it begins with this letter. It is given in full in KMT 18/56 and ±SS 11/102ff. It consists of fifty parts (pada) each of which is in three sections. First comes a letter from the Assembly of Sounds. This is followed by the equivalent letter drawn from the Mālinī alphabet and a syllable of the Triple Vidyā, which consists of the Vidyās Parāparā, Parā and Aparā, in that order. Located ‘on the plane of bliss', this triad of the Assembly of Sounds and the rest is said to be the triple form of Kubjikā as Rudraśakti. (KMT 18/57; ±SS 11/109cd). Thus the three sections of each the fifty parts of Tadgraha are called Raudras who encompass one another in concentric circles (valaya) (KMT 18/54cd-8). The ±SS (11/109 ff) explains them as follows: 1) The left Raudra: This is Mālinī and is Śākta (i.e. it pertains to Śakti). It is on the right. 2) The right Raudra: This is the Assemby of Sounds and is Śāmbhava (i.e. it pertains to Śiva). It is on the left. 3) Raudrāraudra: This is the triple Vidyā and is ĀSava (i.e. it pertains to the individual soul). The left is usually feminine and the right masculine. In this case, however, these positions are reversed. Thus the male letter of the Assembly of Sounds comes first and so is on the left, while Mālinī is on the right (KMT 18/58). A permutation of this basic form is described in the ±SS. This involves the encapsulation of each unit, placed first in the forward and then the reverse

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER TWENTY-THREE 78 should be) the colour of lotuses, orpiment (gorocana), pearls, water or crystal. (It should be) auspicious with one, two, three, four or five beautiful holes and fourteen lines (vidyārekhā). A bad (skull) is one that is uneven, distorted, incomplete, (too) long, with depressions or dots. All the various deities should be carved on its surface with a hard, thin scalpel and, beautiful, should be worshipped along with their limbs. TĀ 27/22-23ab, 25-8ab. According to common Indian belief, the soul finally exits from the body after death only when the skull is broken open or destroyed. Thus, an unbroken skull still contains the presence of the person. Although this is not commonly explicitely stated, this presence keeps the skull alive, as it were, and so renders it particularly fit to be an object into which the deity can be invoked, no less than the living body. The sacrificial function of the skull is very ancient. The following passage from the BrhadaraSyakopaninad (Br. Up. 2/2/3) is perhaps derived from an earlier passage in the Atharvaveda (AV 10/8/9). It teaches the interiorization of the outer sacrificial vessel into the skull. It also implies the use of skulls in non-Vedic rituals of the time: There is a cup with its mouth below and its bottom up. In it is placed every form of glory. On its rim sit seven seers. Voice as the eighth is united with prayer (brahman). The Upaninad goes on to explain that this cup is the head. The glory it contains are the vital breaths as are the seven seers on its rim. 12. The rules (samaya) the initiate should observe are listed in detail in chapter 37. 13. Kaulinī, that is, the energy Kauleśī, is in the centre of the KramamaSÆala, which is thus her residence and city. See above 11/31-32ab and note to 3/13-14ab. 14. Referring to the teachers, the µīkā explains that: ‘one should request them for the remains of the offerings (ucchin˜a). One should eat this at all times. There is purity in the body by eating.
