english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER TWENTY-FOUR 1. ‘KumārikākhaSÆa’ is both the name of this section of the MBT and the land of Bhārata, which is shaped like the trangular — ‘part of the Virgin Goddess’ that embodies her. Cf. KMT 2/118 and above 6/220cd-221ab. 2. We find several cosmogonies in the Kubjikā Tantras. Although they vary in detail, sometimes to a large extent, they all agree that prior to creation there is a primordial Darkness from which emerges, at the initial moment of creation, the Divine Will embodied in the goddess from whom creation proceeds. Variations in the understanding of the nature of the goddess account for the nature of the universe generated from her and its equivalent in the Kubjikā Tantra’s system of representation. Thus, for example, further ahead (cf. below 28/143cd- 145), the goddess’s triadic nature is emphasized when she emerges out of the pre- cosmic Void as the Transmental as the source of the three Transmissions (krama). Similarly, the following cosmogony at the beginning of chapter fifteen of YKh (2) serves to explain the progressive generation of the Siddhas. The part quoted extends up to the creation of the first three Siddhas. It goes on to talk about the generation of the Five (see below notes to 25/41-46ab) and Nine Siddhas (see above 7/60ff.) and then of the others (See also Yoga (2) 11/10cd-20): O Great God (mahādeva), when the universe, mobile and immobile, was a formless Void there was neither you nor I, neither Brahmā nor Keśava (VinSu), neither gods nor the worlds, neither Gandharvas nor Kinnaras, neither Nāgas nor the netherworlds (where they reside). I had burnt (them all) with the Fire of Time (kālāgni). Nothing came into being and all things were darkness wrapped in inertia (tamas). The divine Command arose there in (that) formless ocean. Once again I emanated that (Command), beautiful with the Earth and (the other principles of existence). The God of the gods, the Supreme Lord without beginning, the agent of the emanation of the radiant energy (tejas) (to which belongs all that) extends from Brahmā up to the end of the worlds, slept. O Hara, the unmanifest god generated the Cosmic Egg (aSÆa). O fair- faced one, there in the middle, you and I abided for a cosmic age (kalpa). O Bhairava, by the Yoga of the Sequence of Withdrawal (saˆhārakrama), I came to be (saˆbhūtā). O beautiful one, listen to what I, who had just come forth, did. Taking that Egg into (my) hand, I then churned it. Then when the Egg had been churned, Brahmā and VinSu came into being. Thus, the Egg of Brahmā was adorned and (there arose) the great state (pada) of the three and, O god, the Supreme Lord without beginning abided self-established (svayameva). Brahmā, VinSu and Rudra: these are the first Śāmbhava Siddhas. Brahmā resides in the Egg of Brahmā, Keśava in the location of the Yoni (bhagasthāna) and Rudra in that of the Li‰ga. I who (thus) possess three natures am threefold, and I generated the

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER TWENTY-FOUR 97 whereas here the seed-syllable is GSPMNCHŪ¤, in the KMT it is GSPMNLŪ¤. 46. It appears that a part of text referring to the second and third Jewel are missing. Presumably these are projected into the navel and the heart. 47. The ‘field’, as we have seen, is the Yoni which is denoted by the syllable AI¤. Thus, presumably what is meant here is that the syllables of the Five Jewels are encapsulated by the syllable AI¤ and so ‘dissolve away’ into it when it is uttered at the end of each one. 48. According to KMT 18/74, quoted above in the note to 24/105: ‘the body (piSÆa) has sixteen limbs (avayava) and is well regulated (yantrita) by the sixfold deposition.’

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER TWENTY-FIVE 1. The Six Wheels are described in verses 5 to 28 of this chapter, the Sixteen Supports in verses 29 to 30ab, the Three Signs in verses 36cd to 37 and the Five Voids in verses 38 to 49ab. After this come a few verses concerning the Nine Kulas collectively referred to as ‘the Ocean of the Kula division’ (49cd- 56ab). But these verses may be an interpolation. The name of this chapter suggests that it is only fifty verses long. And indeed, the previous topics are covered in this number of verses. Moreover, although the first four groupings are not found together in the KMT, they appear as a standard set in the later Kubjikā Tantras. A hymn in the SKh eulogizes them together as an integral part both of the goddess’s maSÆala and the body: I praise the Self present in the Point and the Triangle and (Hexagon) marked with the six energies by means of the path of the Sixteen Supports and the energy of the Three Signs within the lotus of the water of the Five Voids within the channels (of the vital breath) (nāÆī) in the abode of the Heart within the abode (of the body and the maSÆala) that wanders within the form of Energy by checking the ten vital breaths. I praise the authority of the Command in the maSÆala of the support and the sustained that abides constantly in (the Wheel of the) Self-supported in the abode Full of Gems. (I praise its) twofold state in (the Wheel of) Unstruck Sound and in the Pure (Wheel) in (the throat which is) the stick of the head that dissolves away in the Supreme Void by the power of the (Wheel of the) Command. I praise the radiant energy of the nature of Sound that is (constantly) replenished by Bhairava. Endowed with the three Kulas (of the Triangle, he is) the venerable teacher, clothed in nakedness who (abides) within the SaˆvartāmaSÆala adorned with the fivefold Command (of the Five Siddhas) in the form of the tradition of the Siddhas as it is in reality, in accord with the modality of emanation. vande bindugatātmānaˆ trinkoSaˆ na˜kalā‰kitam [g: -kalānvitaˆ] | noÆaśādhāramārgeSa laknatritayaśaktinā || pañcavyomāmbukamale nāÆyante hrtpure [g: rhyahrt] pure [g: missing] | daśavāyunirodhena [g: dasa-] bhramate śaktivigrahe [g: sakti-] || vande ājñādhikāraˆ [k kh g: -re] tu ādhārādheyamaSÆale [k: ādhārāceya-] | svādhin˜hāne sthitaˆ nityaˆ maSipūrSapure tathā [k kh: tridhā] || anāhate dvidhāvasthaˆ viśuddhe daSÆamūrdhani | ājñābodhabalenāpi pare vyomni layaˆ vrajet || vande [g: caˆdre] nādātmakaˆ tejo [k, kh, g: tejaˆ] bhairaveSānupūritam [k, kh: bhairavenānu-; g: bhairavenānatupūritaˆ] |

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER TWENTY-FIVE 123 there also. Matsyendranātha, the founder of Kula Tantrism in this Age, is said to have twelve disciples called ‘princes’ (rājaputra). Six of these did not have disciples, whereas the other six established six lineages (see Dyczkowski 1988: 70 for a chart). These are known to Abhinavagupta — who refers to them in chapter twenty-nine of his Tantrāloka (29/29cd-41) — and to the KMT (1/43) and the Kubjikā Tantras in general, just as they are known to the Kālīkrama Tantras. The KMT presents them as the preceding lineages (pūrvasantāna). These six are 1) Ānanda 2) Āvali 3) Prabhu 4) Yogī 5) Atīta and 6) Pāda. All the MSs read ‘atītam’ in the place of ‘pādam’. But as the former is repeated twice and this set of six is well known, I have emended accordingly. 20. KuKh 39/141b reads Ghorākhya as the name of this Tantra. 21. This group of nine is mentioned again below in 39/140cd-141 where they are described as the ninefold root of the Kaula teachings. The Siddhakaula appears to be the name of a Kaula school whereas the rest, it seems, are Tantras. A text called Candrakaula is mentioned in the KJN (21/4). A Tantra called Candragarbhā appears in the list of sixty-four Tantras in the JY. One called Candrā and another called Candralekhā are mentioned in the ŚrīkaS˜hīyasaˆhitā quoted in the commentary on the Tantrāloka (Dyczkowski 1988: 121, 123). Raurava and Vīra are two Siddhāntāgama. GaSa appears in a list of Tantras in the KRU (1/16) as does the BhūtaÆāmara, which is also mentioned in the list of sixty- four Tantras in the NityānoÆaśikārSava. The CMSS refers to the Khecarīmata (see above note to 16/5) as does Abhinavagupta, but does not quote it (TĀ 29/165). 22. Kula in this context means the body in the Void of the deity that the adept attains with realisation.

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER TWENTY-SIX 1. The Root Sūtra embodies in verbal form the essential nature of the place of origin of emanation and so is said to be equal to the Skyfarer, that is, the deity who resides in the transcendental Void. It describes in brief the essential nature, contents and dynamics of the triangle that lies at the centre of the SaˆvartāmaSÆala, which represents the interface between the transcendent and its immanent emanation of which it is the source. A cardinal theme of the teachings of the Kubjikā Tantras, we have had occasion to examine this more than once in various contexts, both internally as part of the Yogic body, and externally as the site for the worship of the Krama. There are two other versions of the Root Sūtra in chapters 38 and 42. A variant of the version in chapter 42 is found in the beginning of the CMSS (1/4-6). The Root Sūtra is also reproduced at the beginning of the Kramasūtrādhikāra where it functions as the initial invocatory verse (ma‰galacaraSa). Apart from one minor variant, the first verse is the same as the one here (see notes to 42/5). Of the three versions in our text, the most elaborate and longest is the one in chapter 38, which we will analyse in due course. Mukundarāja, the author of the Saˆvartārthaprakāśa, quotes the version of the sūtra found here and paraphrases the following verses that explain it with a few additions of his own (SaˆP fl. 4b ff.). He informs the reader that the form of the goddess as power (śakti) is described in the Manthānabhairavatantra (tatra manthāne yādrśatvenākhyātā) which is the source of all the sūtras he presents in his Saˆvartārthaprakāśa. Here (26/2) we are told that this is the first Root Sūtra, which may simply mean that it is the first of the three versions of the Root Sūtras in the KuKh, it may also be the earliest version. The six quarters of the following verse and a half correspond to 42/5cd, 42/4cd and 42/6b in that order. The second and last quarter are missing in the version of chapter 38. The remaining quarters correspond to 38/9d and 38/7d-8a, respectively. The first two and the last quarters are missing in the version here. The next three quarters correspond to 26/5b and 26/4cd, in that order. The first four quarters agree with CMSS 1/4. KuKh 38/2-3a agrees with KuKh 42/3-4a. The latter variant is one quarter longer than the former. It is hard to say which of the two versions is the original. This version fits exactly the four quarters of a verse. However, in this version the last of the four sacred seats is not qualified by an attributive compound (bahuvrīhi) as are the other three. The other version is complete in this respect but is one quarter too long (see translation below and the critical apparatus of the Sanskrit of 26/3d). Further ahead (38/34) we are told that this is the first (ādi) sūtra of the tradition and that the maSÆala is to be drawn 'as explained in the Root Sūtra in accord with the previous tradition (krama)’ (33/62). Perhaps this reference to a ‘previous tradition’ may be evidence that the Root Sūtra belongs to an early strata

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER TWENTY-SEVEN 1. The µīkā (fl. 83a) also says that there are three forms of the maSÆala. One is gross. This is the external maSÆala ‘with form’ (sākāra) onto which the mantras of the Krama are projected. The second form of the maSÆala is subtle. This is within the body. The third is supreme. This is the maSÆala which is reality itself (tattvabhūta). The MaSÆala of the Teachers is described twice in our text. Once in this chapter and again in the first part of chapter forty-eight. The two are similar but not the same. The existence of two maSÆalas appears to be recognised below (27/9) where we are told that the one described in this chapter is ‘the second of the two maSÆalas that have authority’. The syllable Navātman, as the sonic form of Bhairava who is Kubjikā’s consort and the first teacher, is important in both maSÆalas as are the Five Siddhas who embody the Five PraSavas. However, the latter are the main object of worship in this one. Instead, the primary object of worship in the MaSÆala of the Teachers in chapter forty-eight is linked to Navātman. A few verses there, probably drawn from the Śrīmatottara (KuKh 48/12-14ab = ŚM 23/38-40ab), outline how it is projected into that maSÆala. The procedure is described at great length in chapter twenty-three of the Śrīmatottara and the µīkā, which is based on it. See appendix 2 of intro. vol. 2, where the relevent sections in the µīkā and the ŚM are presented in full. The projection of the Five Siddhas, who are the core of the maSÆala described here, into the Wheels of the body (27/17cd-19) may perhaps be an indication that this, ‘the second maSÆala’, is the internal one, whereas the one in chapter forty-eight is the outer one. 2. These lines briefly describe the composite form of Bhairava who is the First Teacher worshipped in the centre of the GurumaSÆala from whom the other teachers emanate. The ‘five forms’ of Bhairava are the Five Siddhas also called the Five Nāthas. These should not be confused with the five Siddhas who preside over the five sacred seats (see above 8/112-114ab). The ‘five forms’ of Bhairava in this case are the Five Siddhas who preside over the five gross elements as the agents of emanation in these five Kulas (see above 25/41-45ab and KMT 3/94ab- 110). The disciples of the Five Siddhas are listed below in chapter 43 (43/4-30). These five are worshipped in the centre of the maSÆala (see note to 48/14cd-16ab) and, as we shall see (27/17cd-19), in the five Wheels in the body of the worshipper. The sixteen limbs of Bhairava are the descendents of the Sixteen Nāthas (see above 7/77 ff. and below chapter 56). The ninefold form consists of the Nine Nāthas who embody the letters of Navātman. Cf. above 27/42cd-43ab and note. 27. The standard set of three gestures (mudrātraya) are those of the Lotus (padmamudrā), the Three Flames (triśikhāmudrā) and the Yoni. These gestures are linked with a complex series of transformations and motions of the vital breath and, with it, consciousness. They are discussed extensively in these perspectives in chapter six (49 ff.) of the KMT which is drawn from the TS. Despite their importance in the KMT and its expansions, the ŚM and ±SS, they are not prominent in the rites of the MBT. It is possible therefore that these are not the three gestures meant here. According to a parallel description of the formation of the maSÆala in chapter forty-eight below, the three gestures are made with the little finger, thumb and middle finger, respectively. english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER TWENTY-EIGHT 1. All three Kramas described in this chapter consist of twenty-seven ‘divisions’ (bheda) — i.e. mantras — in six units (prakāra) configured 4-5-6-4-5-3. This appears to be the basic setup in the KuKh, which was probably inspired by the YKh (cf. chapter 17 of YKh (2) where a Krama of Twenty-seven mantras is described). Note that the Krama in chapter twenty-six consists of twenty-eight ‘divisions’ configured 4-5-6-4-5-4, as we find in the KMT. However, it seems in order to reconcile these two formats. The last unit is said to originally consist of three mantras, to which a fourth will be added which relates to the seat of the future — Tisra (26/25). Thus, the Krama of twenty-seven mantras is the present one, although in actual fact the one of twenty-eight is older. 2. The sacred seat of O¤ is OÆÆiyāna. 3. Air is missing. Below in 44/15-17ab, the order is reversed. OÆÆiyāna (O¤) corresponds to the Earth element and so forth. Māta‰ga is the fifth seat that corresponds to Space. Cf. chart in chapter 21. 4. 11. english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER TWENTY-EIGHT 171 Śiva and Śakti which emerges in between. See above 28/138cd-139ab. 22. Concerning the deviant ambā > avvā, see intro. vol. 3, p. 277 ff., cf. below 28/162cd-164. 23. Concerning the goddess's six faces and limbs see above 10/28-41. 24. The Octad of Kula, i.e. the Eight Mothers, is described above in 14/93- 94, especially 16/3 ff. and notes. 25. In this setup, the Wheel in the navel is an eight-petalled lotus. There is an eight-petalled lotus on each petal and a ninth in the centre. Forms of Navātman mantra are projected onto these lotuses, each of which is presided over by a Bhairava. In this arrangement the Mothers are, presumably, the consorts of the Bhairavas of these lotuses and they are thus all related to Navātman. This is perhaps why CāmuSÆā has been inserted in the scheme outlined in this passage as an extra Mother to make nine, rather than the usual eight. 26. I suppose that the three seed-syllables are the first three PraSavas AI¤ HRĪ¤ ŚRĪ¤, which are sometimes found together as a triad. 27. See 25/5-7ab. 28. In other words, the form of each mantra is as follows: Five PraSavas > name of the goddess > AVVĀ > -PĀDUKĀ¤ VICCE. Often the Five PraSavas are also added, in the reverse order (cf. above 7/34-35ab), at the end of a mantra, but this does not appear to be the case here. Thus, for example, the first mantra of the series of Mothers is: AI¤ HRĪ¤ ŚRĪ¤ KHPHRE¤ HSRŪAU¤ AÖ BRĀHMA¦Ī AVVĀ- PĀDUKĀ¤ VICCE

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER TWENTY-NINE 1. The god says that he is the goddess’s disciple by his very nature. Their relationship is not just a possible one, as between husband and wife; it is an inherent one. The goddess is not just the god’s consort; she is also his mother and, as such, his teacher. Cf. 5/8-14. 2. The Root is above, grounded in the transcendent. The Cave is the Void of the Li‰ga (58/7cd-8ab). The Root is the Point and its foundation, the transcendent. 3. The goddess is praised in these two verses as KuSÆalinī. As such she has two aspects. Borrowing the terminology of the Kashmiri Śaiva texts, we may call them the upper (ūrdhva) KuSÆalinī and the other the lower (adhaƒ) one. These two correspond to her two movements of ‘going and coming’ (see 3/124 n. 161). In both aspects she resides in a triangle. The upper one faces downwards and is in the End of the Twelve. The lower one faces upwards and is in the Cave of the Root. The Root (kanda), which is said to be the location of the triangle (trikoSasthāna) is located ‘below the navel’ (nābhyadhaƒ) (see Schoterman 1981: 81). We have already had occasion to observe that, according to the Kubjikā Tantras, the ‘root of the navel’ is the location of KuSÆalinī when she sleeps in the body in the form of a coiled snake (see above 3/120-121 and below 58/93cd-94ab and 59/75cd-76). 4. This is the seat of the Age of Strife. It replicates the entire Triangle. 5. Cf. 3/46. 6. The Great Jewel is the Circle of the Navel where KuSÆalinī resides and so, by extension, is a name of KuSÆalinī to whom this hymn is addressed. 7. Brahmā, VinSu and Śambhu are the lords of the three energies, Vāmā, Jyen˜hā and Raudrī. The three couples emerge from the unmanifest energy of the goddess to form the triangle that surrounds her and contains her 50 energies that constitute Speech. The form and nature of this Triangle has been discussed above (see 7/12-15ab). Here this Triangle is called the Heart of the Yoginī. There it is called the House of the Yoginī. 8. This is the syllable HSKHPHRE¤; see above 9/1 ff. and notes. 9. This is the triangle in the centre of the maSÆala. It is called this because it is formed by the energy of the three gestures corresponding to the three sacred seats (see notes 2/14 and 3/48, 8/87). In the KMT and its expansions, the ŚM and the ±SS, the three Gestures are described in great detail each in three aspects, namely, gross, subtle and supreme. They are: Yonimudrā, Padmamudrā and Triśikhāmudrā. There they are are not specifically associated with sacred seats as is the standard practice in later Kubjikā sources. Note that here the model is triadic; there are only three sacred seats. In this case, I suppose that this is simply to accommodate the standard set of three Gestures. As usual in the triadic model,

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER TWENTY-NINE 200 notes to 1/1 and 7/60 ff.). The goddess resides in the End of the Twelve, the Heart and the abode of KuSÆalinī as these three lineages. (µīkā fl. 13b-14a). Note that, according to the Svacchanda and other Tantras, the hells are triangular (ete 'tighorā narakās trikoSāƒ parikīrtitāƒ | SvT 10/53ab). The goddess who resides in the triangle thus resides here as well. 52. The visualization of the goddess taught here should be coupled with that of Navātmānātha whom she embraces. Thus the goddess who is Vāgbhava (AI¤) is coupled with Navātman (HSK±MLVRYŪ¤). Rūpaśiva promises that he who regularly practices this visualization soon gets all he desires. He attains all the pleasures of the world (including sexual) (kāmopabhoga) as well as liberation while still alive (jīvanmukti). He attains all this no doubt because once he has learnt the Dhyānasūtra, he can go on to worship the Krama (kramārcana) (µīkā fl. 14a). Indeed, this is the usual sequence in most rites of adoration (pūjā). After the preliminary purifications and the rest comes the visualization (dhyāna) of the deity, which is followed by the rite.

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER THIRTY 1. After the disciple has received initiation, the teacher dictates the Tantra to him, explaining it as he goes along. This twofold process is called ‘vyākhyālekhana’ (see below 30/27 and note). 2. KuKh 30/2-33ab roughly corresponds to ±SS 3/3-28cd. The texts do not coincide completely, although verses, lines and quarter-verses are the same here and there. In some cases, one line of text in the ±SS is expanded into two in the KuKh. There are extra lines in both texts not found in the other as well as reworking of common lines. The reader is referred to the notes of the edition of the Sanskrit text for details. According to the ±SS, the Śrīmata is the KMT as well as its expanded version, the ±SS. Here the Śrīmata is the Manthānabhairavatantra ‘consisting of twenty-four thousand verses’. 3. This passage, which continues up to 30/47, describes how the scripture should be copied and transmitted from the teacher to his disciple and how it should be worshipped on that occasion. ±SS 3/19-29 deals with the same subject. Here it is resumed from 30/111cd and continues up to the end of the chapter concluding with admonishments to worship and preserve the scripture and conceal it from the unworthy. 4. Sch oterman translates the version of this line in the ±SS as follows: ‘On the tithi [called] PūrSā there should be neither sun nor moon.’ This occurs when there is a lunar eclipse. 5. The text reads: ‘sūryeSa tu samanvitām’ which literally means ‘along with the sun’ that is, I suppose, on a Sunday or possibly, when the sun is in a favourable asterism. 6. The ±SS 3/19 says that this should be done in a temple (mandira). As this is a secret ritual meant only for initiates, this is surprising. Thus, presumably, an isolated, deserted temple is meant. Apparently, in order to circumvent this problem, Schoterman has translated this word as ‘spot’ i.e. place. 7. This is the scripture of twenty-four thousand verses, that is, the Manthānabhairavatantra. See above 30/2cd-3ab. It is named again this way below in 68/48. The three sections (khaSÆa) are listed below in 69/28cd-29ab. The first section is said be this one, namely, the KumārikākhaSÆa. The second is the SiddhkhaSÆa and the third is the ĀdyakhaSÆa. See intro. vol. 3, p. 99 ff.. 8. Concerning the worship of the scripture see appendix X. 9. The MSs read ‘mātrmaSÆalam’ which makes no sense. I have emended to ‘mātrkhaSÆakam’ which may be the KumārikākhaSÆa. The MantrakhaSÆa may be the SiddhakhaSda. 10. Schoterman translates the equivalent passage in the ±SS (3/19-23a) as follows:

sanskrit: ।। ॐ स्वस्ति ।। श्रीनाथपादुकाभ्यां नमः। श्रीगणेशाय नमः । मन्थान भैरवतन्त्रे कुमारिकाखण्डे एकत्रिंशानन्दः श्रीनाथ उवाच कुलागमविधान' तु मया ज्ञातं महेश्वरि । अधुना श्रोतुमिच्छामि दीक्षाविधिं यथाक्रमम् ॥ १ ॥ तदह ै श्रोतुमिच्छामि यत् सारं पश्चिमान्वये । दीक्षायानन्तर ै सर्वं पूजा – आगममण्डलम् ॥ २ ॥ दीक्षाशब्द किमित्युक्तं प्रसादाद् वक्तुमर्हसि । श्रीवक्रा उवाच शृणु नाथ प्रवक्ष्यामि दीक्षां तें प्रवदाम्यहम् ।। ३ ॥ दीयते ज्ञानसद्भावं क्षीयते पाशपञ्जरम् । दानक्षपणधर्मित्वाद् ं दीक्षा तेनेह कीर्तिता ॥ ४॥ श्रीनाथ उवाच कतिविधं भवेद् वेध कस्मिन् स्थाने प्रयोजयेत् । कथमाज्ञाप्रभाव” तु पशूनां मलशोधनम् ॥ ५ ॥ समयी पुत्रकश्चैव ं साधकस्तु कथं भवेत् । आचार्यत्वं समासेन चतुराश्रमनिर्णयम् ।। ६ ।। सर्वं कथय देवेशि यदि तुष्टासि वक्रिके ।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-ONE The Initiation by Piercing (vedhadīknā) Initiation and Initiates Śrīnātha said: O Great Goddess, I have understood the method enjoined (for the copying and explanation of) the Kula scripture. Now, in due order, I want to hear the prescription concerning initiation. I wish to know this, the essence of the Western Tradition. Everything (comes) after initiation — the rite of adoration (pūjā), the scripture and the maSÆala. (1-2) Why is the word ‘dīknā' used (to mean initiation). By (your grace) please explain this (to me). (3ab) The venerable (goddess) Vakrā said: O Lord, listen, I am speaking. I will explain (the true nature of) initiation to you. It is called ‘dīknā' here (in this world) because it has the power to `give' and `destroy'. It gives (dīyate) the essence of knowledge (jñānasadbhāva) and destroys (knīyate) the cage of the fetters.1 (3cd-4) Śrīnātha said: How many kinds of piercing (vedha) are there?2 Where should it be applied? What is the power of the Command and the purification of the impurities of the fettered? (5) How is the follower of the Rule (samayin), the spiritual son (putraka) and the adept (sādhaka)? (What is) the state of the teacher (ācārya)? In brief, (what is) the teaching concerning the four stages of life (āśrama)?3 O mistress of the gods, tell me all (this) if you are pleased (with me), O Crooked One. (6-7ab)

sanskrit: 4 श्रीवक्रा उवाच कुमारिकाखण्डः अथार्घपात्रसंशेकात् क्रमपूजावलोकनात् ।। ७ ।। समयानां श्रवणाद् ँ वाथ समयित्वं लभेन्नरः । दन्तकाष्टेन संजल्पात् पुत्रकत्वं प्रपद्यते ।। ८॥ वेधितश्चाभिषिक्तश्च साधकः सिद्धशासने । २२ संक्रान्तज्ञानविज्ञानः” क्रमौघसुविशारदः ॥ ९ ॥ अभिषिक्तः प्रमुक्तिज्ञो देशिकः प्रविधीयते । अथायत् परमं गुह्यं वेधविज्ञानमुत्तमम् ।। १० ।। अध ऊध्वविभागेन वेधक्रममिहोच्यते । मन्त्रवेध तु नादाख्यं बिन्दुवेधमतः परम् ॥। ११ ॥ शाक्तं भुजंगङ्गवेधं तु परं वेधमुदाहृतम् । मन्त्रवेधं तु मन्त्रेण चक्रादिपरिभावनात् ॥ १२ ॥ •२७ ज्वालामालाकुलं ध्यायेत् षडा चक्रमुत्तमम् । द्वादशारेऽथवा” व्याप्तिः श्वासकुम्भकयोगतः ।। १३ ॥ परं चित्तं” प्रबोधव्य” मन्त्रवेधमुदाहृतम्” ।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-ONE 5 The Four Types of Initiate The venerable (goddess) said: Now, a man attains the status of a follower of the Rule by the (purifying) consecration (saˆśeka) of the sacrificial vessel, by seeing the worship of the Krama (kramapūjā) or hearing the rules. (7cd-8ab) He attains the status of a spiritual son through the rite of the stick for brushing the teeth.4 An adept in the Teaching (śāśana) of the Siddhas is one who has been consecrated and pierced (by the power of grace). (8cd-9ab) The teacher (deśika) should be a man to whom (a correct) understanding of the knowledge (of the tradition) has been transmitted. (He should be) well versed in the Current of the Krama, consecrated and know the state of total liberation.5 (9cd-10ab) Types of Initiation by Piercing6 Now, (I will tell you) something else, namely, the supreme secret which is the most excellent knowledge of (the various types of) piercing (vedha). (10cd) Here it is said that the piercing process (vedhakrama) is divided into (two phases, namely, the piercing that takes place) below (in the lower centres) and (the one that takes place) above (in the upper centres).7 (11ab) Varieties of the Lower Piercing The Piercing with Mantra, the one called (the Piercing with) Sound after which comes the Piercing with the Drop and (the Piercing with) Energy, the Piercing with the Snake and the one said to be supreme. (This) is said to be ‘piercing’ (vedha).8 (11cd-12ab) The Piercing with Mantra The Piercing with Mantra (takes place) by contemplating (paribhāvana) the Wheels and the rest (in conjunction) with mantra.9 (12cd) One should visualize (dhyāyet) the excellent Wheel of Six Spokes surrounded by a garland of flames. Or else, (one experiences) pervasion (vyāpti) within the Twelve-spoked (Wheel) in conjunction with the retention of the breath. (The teacher) should awaken the mind of the other (i.e. his disciple). (This) is said to be the Piercing with Mantra.10 (12cd-14ab)

sanskrit: 6 कुमारिकाखण्ड: ३२ हृच्चक्रे च महेशान बिन्दुज्वालाकुलप्रभा ॥ १४ ॥ तेन संबोधयेच्छिश्य ं बिन्दुवेधमुदाहृतम् । ३८ शाक्त शक्ति समुच्चार्य ऊध्वचारेण सुन्दर ॥ १५ ॥ शृङ्गाटकासनस्था” तु कुब्जिका कुटिलाकृतिः । आधारादिसमुच्चार्या दीपाकारा शिखोपमा ।। १६ ॥ स्थिरचित्ताङ्गभावेन वेधयेदखिलं जगत् । भ्रमदण्डमहावेगः” शाक्तवेधमुदाहृतम् ।। १७ ।। ४३ एषा सा परमा शक्ति: परानन्दविकासिनी । ४४ जन्मस्थानात् परं याति पञ्चपञ्चकभूषिता ॥ १८ ॥ तान्येव परतत्त्वाच्च कलापञ्चक६ दक्षिणे । ४८ व्योमा शान्ता च विद्या च प्रतिष्ठा च निवृत्तिका ं ॥१९ ।। नन्दा भद्रा जया रिक्ता पूर्ण सूक्ष्मा परामृता । कुलपञ्चकसंयुक्ता व्योमपञ्चकभूषिता ।। २० ।। ब्रह्मपञ्चकसंयुक्ता पञ्चकारणसंयुता । एवं पञ्चप्रकारा” तु ब्रह्मस्थानाद् विनिर्गता ।। २१ ।। 10 ब्रह्मस्थाने तु विश्रान्ता तडिद्रूपा विराजते । ५२ प्रतिष्ठा वेधयेत् कायं परात्मानं च बोधयेत् ।। २२ ।। एवं भुजङ्गवेध तु कथितं कुलशासने ।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-ONE 7 The Piercing with the Drop O Great Lord, there is a light in the Wheel of the Heart which is full of the flames of the Drop. One should awaken the disciple with that. This is said to be the Piercing with the Drop.11 (14cd-15ab) The Piercing with Energy O handsome one, the Empowered (Piercing takes place) once one has projected forth (samuccārya) Energy by the upward movement. Kubjikā, whose form is crooked, sits on the seat of the Water Chestnut. Her form is that of a lamp, like a flame (śikhā). She should be led upwards from the Foundation onwards. (15cd-16) With the mind and limbs firm, pierce the entire universe. The Empowered Piercing is said to be the mighty force that wanders in the (Cosmic) Egg (bhramadaSÆamahāvega).12 (17) The Piercing with the Snake She is this Supreme Energy who brings about the expansion of Supreme Bliss. Adorned with the five groups of five,13 she travels from the Abode of Birth to the Supreme (Place).14 (18) O skillful one, these (pentads ranging) from the Supreme Principle are (firstly) the Pentad of Energies (kalāpañcaka). (These five are) Vyomā (Sky), Śāntā (Tranquil), Vidyā (Knowledge), Pratin˜hā (the Established One) and Nivrttikā (Cessation).15 (Again), the subtle (goddess who is) supreme nectar (is) Nandā,16 Bhadrā (Auspicious), Jayā (Victory), Riktā (Empty) and PūrSā (Full). She is endowed with the Pentad of Kula, adorned with the Pentad of Space and, conjoined with the Pentad of Brahmā, is endowed with the Five Causes.17 (19-21ab) In this way, (the goddess) with five aspects, has emerged from the Abode of Brahmā. Reposing in the Abode of Brahmā she appears in the form of a lightning flash. She who is well-established (pratin˜hā) should pierce the body and awake the Supreme Self. This is the way the Piercing by the Snake is explained in the Kula Teaching.18 (21cd-23ab)

sanskrit: 8 कुमारिकाखण्ड: संस्फुरकादिवेध” तु कलापादाध्वोदाहृतम् ।। २३ ॥ नाख्येयं कस्यचिद् देव गोपनीयं प्रयत्नतः ५७ । गुह्याद् गुह्यतरं गुह्यं रक्षणीयं शरीरवत् ॥ २४ ॥ ६३ क्षीणे चित्ते सुरेशान परानन्दमुदाहृतम्” । नेन्द्रियाणि न च प्राण ै नान्तःकरणगोचरम् ।। २५ ।। न मनो नापि मन्तव्यो मन्तान्यो नैव विद्यते । सर्वभावपरिक्षीणे परं वेधमुदाहृतम् ।। २६ ।। एतत् ते कथितं सर्वं भक्त्या परमया मया । गोपितव्य प्रयत्नेन चौरेभ्यो द्रविणं यथा ।। २७ ।। मध्यमेनैव चारेण मध्यमान्ते प्रवेशनम् । मध्यमा रुद्रशक्तिस्तु अधश्चोव प्रपीडयेत् ।। २८ ॥ बिन्दुरूपी तदा प्राणं शक्त्यग्रे विनियोजयेत् । तद्रूपं लक्ष्येदात्मा सूक्ष्मं खद्योतसन्निभम् ।। २९ । पादांगुष्ठात् समारभ्य विशतेऽलक्ष्यलक्षितम् । यावन्नाभिप्रादेशे” तु रुद्रशक्ति” नियोजयेत् ॥ ३० ॥ पुरे शृङ्गाटकाकारे कुण्डलाकृतिविग्रहाम् । सुसूक्ष्म भ्रममाणां च ज्वालामालासमप्रभाम् ॥ ३१ ॥ ज्वलन्ती सर्वरन्ध्रेषु मध्यदेशे विचिन्तयेत् । ७७ मुहूर्तं यावद्” देहे तु शक्तिस्तिष्ठति रन्ध्रगा ।। ३२ ।। तदा चोत्पद्यते मूर्छा सर्वव्याप्तिस्वरूपिणी । ८२ ८० । एजते नात्र संदेहो च्छिन्नमूलं द्रुमं यथा ।। ३३ ॥ निःशंको विह्वलश्चैव काष्ठवत् पतते भुवि । अमृताख्या तु या शक्ति: पूर्णचन्द्रस्वरूपिणी ॥ ३४ ॥ तया ं व्यापितमात्रस्तु“ ससंज्ञो भवते ततः ।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-ONE 9 The Piercing (with its different types) such as the Illuminating (Piercing) (saˆsphuraka) is said to be the Path of Energy and of the Parts (pāda). O god, it should not be told to anybody but should be kept secret with great effort. (This) secret is more secret than secret and should be protected as one does (one's own) body. (23cd-24) The Supreme Piercing O Lord of the gods, when the mind ceases, (that) is said to be Supreme Bliss. (In that state) there are no senses, vital breath or field of the inner (mental) senses. There is no mind, no object of the mind nor cogitating subject (mantr). When all phenomenal existence (bhāva) ceases, that is said to be the Supreme Piercing.19 (25-26) I have told you all this out of supreme devotion (for you). It should be kept concealed with effort, as one does wealth from thieves. (27) Entry into the Centre takes place by the movement in the Centre. The (Goddess of the) Centre (madhyamā) is Rudra's energy. One should squeeze (it) above and below.20 (28) Then the vital breath (prāSa), in the form of a Drop, should be applied to the Tip of Energy (śaktyagre). The Self should mark that Form which is subtle like (the light of a) firefly.21 Commencing from the big toe of the foot (it moves upwards until it) enters the Undefinable (alaknyalaknita). Rudra's energy should be applied up to the location of the navel.22 (29-30) She is in the citadel whose form is (triangular like) a water chestnut.23 Her shape is (round like) an earring (kuSÆala). She is subtle and rotates (on herself constantly). (Her) light is like a garland of flames. One should visualize her within the centre of all the cavities (of the body) as burning fiercely. (31-32ab) If Energy abides (even) for a short time in the body within the cavities,24 a state of swoon (mūrchā) arises which is (the initial experience of) universal pervasion. (When that happens the adept) invariably shakes as does a tree cut (down from the) root.25 Fearless (of pain) (niƒśa‰ka) and distraught, he falls (senseless) to the ground, like a stone. Then, pervaded by the energy called Amrtā (Nectar), the Full Moon, he regains consciousness. (32cd-35ab)

sanskrit: 10 कुमारिकाखण्ड: ८६ अधो वेधः समाख्यातः ऊध्ववेधमतः शृणु ।। ३५ ।। उन्मनान्ते ँ मनं” कृत्वा परा सामनरूपिणी । पूरयन्ती जगत् सर्वं आसप्तभुवनान्तिकम् ॥ ३६ ।। तस्यान्ते व्यापिनी शक्तिर्मेरो: शृङ्गाटशेखरे । सा एव ब्रह्मरन्ध्रस्था हिमकुन्देन्दुनिर्मला ।। ३७ । ९४ संघट्टे” शशिसूर्यान्ते भूतासननभाकृतिः । ९५ ९६ नाभिपद्मस्य मध्ये तु भित्त्वाहता विनिर्गता ।। ३८ ।। सुसूक्ष्मां भावयेद् देव कण्ठनालान्तरे परा । भुजङ्गकुटिलाकारा यावद् ब्रह्मबिलं गता ॥ ३९ ॥ १०२ तत्र लयं कृत्वात्मना ं” ब्रह्मद्वारं विभेदयेत् । पूर्णिमा कामरूपेण अमावास्या प्रवर्तते ।। ४० ।। धरातत्त्वाच्छिवान्तं च विद्युज्जिह्वा महाज्वला' । निर्गच्छेदूध्वरन्ध्रेण यावत् साध्यस्य मूर्धनि ।। ४१ ॥ द्वादशार्कसमाकारा प्रलयाग्निसमप्रभा । मध्यमाकर्षण प्रोक्तं सर्वज्ञानप्रदर्शकम् ॥ ४२ ॥ षट्चक्रे षोडशाधारे उल्लसन्ती परा कला । काकचञ्चपुटस्था सा अक्षपक्षक्षयंकरी ॥ ४३ ॥ तालुमध्ये तु नादान्ते बिन्दु” वेधयते परा ।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-ONE 11 Varieties of the Upper Piercing Entry Through the Cavity of Brahmā The lower piercing has been explained; now listen to the upper piercing. (35cd) Once one has fixed the mind within the Transmental, then the Supreme (Energy), in the form of the Equal One (sāmana), fills the entire universe, up to the end of the seven worlds. (36) The Pervasive (vyāpinī) Energy is at the end of that, on the peak of the triangle (śr‰gā˜a)26 of Meru. She resides in the Aperture of Brahmā and is as pure (white) as snow, the jasmine (flower) and the moon.27 (37) Within the conjunction between the Sun (Ha) and the Moon (Sa), (her) form Space, (she is) the seat of the Elements. Penetrating into the middle of the lotus of the navel, she has emerged as Unstruck (Sound).28 (38) O god, contemplate the subtle Supreme (Energy) within the channel of the throat in the form of a snake until she enters the Aperture of Brahmā. (39) Once merger has been brought about there, the Self should perforate the Door of Brahmā. (Then) the Full Moon in the form of (the divine) will (kāmarūpeSa) becomes the New Moon. (40) She is a great flame of fire and her tongue is a lightning flash. She emerges out of the Principle of the Foundation and (moves upward) by means of the Upper Cavity until she reaches the deity's (sādhya) head. Her form is like that of (all the) twelve suns (of the year). Her light like that of the Doomsday Fire (pralayāgni).29 (Thus the process) that reveals all knowledge (whereby) the Centre is draw towards oneself (ākarnaSa), has been explained. 30 (41-42) Entry through the Beak of the Crow The Supreme Energy moves up joyfully (ullasantī) through the Six Wheels and the Sixteen Supports. Located in the encapsulated Cavity of the Beak of the Crow,31 she destroys the aspect (which relates to the manifest, differentiated) letters (aknapakna). She, the Supreme (Energy), pierces the Drop in the centre of the palate at the End of Sound. (43-44ab)

sanskrit: 12 कुमारिकाखण्डः काकिनी काकरूपेण हंसिनी हंसविग्रहा ॥ ४४ ॥ विश्वेशी” विश्वसंहारी” संसारसरसारसी । एषा सा उन्मना सूक्ष्मा सर्वद्वन्द्वनिकृन्तनी ३ ।। ४५ ।। । अतीतानागता”४ चैव वर्तमाना १५ तु योगिनी१६ । खेचरीचक्रसामान्या स्वेच्छया भवते ततः' ।। ४६ ।। ११८ १२० तस्योध्वे खेचरीसिद्धिजीयते वीरवन्दित' । खगमा २१ खगतिश्चैव २२ खगतिखगमध्यगा१२३ ॥ ४७ ॥ १२४ ।। खस्वरूपा ४ खगेशी च कुब्जिका खगमा परा । १२६ षट्प्रकारा' २५ खगेशी सा सुषुम्णा व्योमरूपिणीं २८ ॥ ४८ ॥ तत्र संपश्यते” योगी सिद्धांश्चैव अनेकधा । १३३ तदूध्वे” मोक्षमालय” भेदयित्वा च सुस्फुटम् ॥ ४९ ॥ प्रयत्नाद् दिव्ययोगीन्द्र: पूरयेच्छक्तिमुत्तमाम् । विशेन्निरामये७ तत्त्वे व्यापके निर्गुणे परे ।। ५० ।। सर्वज्ञता सुतृप्तिश्च अनादिबोधमालयम्” । ९४२ १४३ स्वतन्त्र”॰ नित्यमलुप्तमनन्तं शाश्वतं ध्रुवम् ॥ ५१ ॥ व्यापिन व्योमरूपान्त अनन्तनाथेनाश्रितम् । सुसूक्ष्मं च परं शान्तं गमागमनवर्जितम् ॥ ५२ ॥ तं ध्यायेद् नित्ययुक्तात्मा घनमाकाशसन्निभम् १४८ निरञ्जनं परं शान्तं निर्वाण निर्विकारकम् ॥ ५३ ॥ कुलोद्भवं कुलं कौल अकुलं तु परापरम् । १५० सा च रौद्री मयाख्याता राहुमुक्तो रविर्यथा ॥ ५४ ॥ सूर्यकोटिप्रतीकाशा कालानलसमप्रभा । ध्यायेत् तां नित्ययुक्तात्मा यावच्छक्त्या लयंगतः ।। ५५ ।।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-ONE 13 KuSÆalinī In the form of a crow (she is called) Kākinī (the Female Crow). In the form of a gander, she is Haˆsinī (the Female Gander).32 (44cd) Mistress of the universe, who destroys the universe, she is the female swan (who swims) in the lake of transmigratory existence. She is that subtle Transmental (Energy) who uproots all duality. (45) She is the Yoginī who was in the past, is in the present and will be in the future. Then by her own (free) will, she is the universal (Energy) of the Wheel of Khecarī. (46) O you who are praised by the Heroes (vīra), above that is the Accomplishment (of the energy) of the Skyfarer (khecarīsiddhi). She moves in the Sky and is (herself) the movement in the Sky. She is in the middle between the one who moves in the Sky and the movement. (47) She is Khageśī (the Skyfaring Goddess) who is (both) the Void (kharūpā) and Kubjikā, the Supreme (Energy) who moves in the Void. She, Khageśī, is sixfold and (as) SunumSā, she is the Void (vyomarūpiSī). (48) Again and again the yogi sees many kinds of Siddhas there.33 Above that is the clearly evident abode of liberation. Having penetrated (into it), the divine yogi should fill (that) most excellent energy with effort and enter the Pure Principle, which is pervasive, free of the qualities (nirguSa) and supreme. (Therein) is omniscience, perfect satisfaction and the abode of beginningless consciousness (bodha). (49-51ab) The (yogi) who is ever intent (yukta) should contemplate (therein the Principle) which is free, eternal, never destroyed, endless, perennial, stable, pervasive, within the Void (vyomarūpānta)34 occupied by the endless Lord (anantanātha), extremely subtle, supreme, tranquil, free of going and coming,35 dense (and uninterrupted) like the sky. It is stainless (nirañjana), supreme, tranquil, unchanging, NirvāSa, generated out of Kula, Kula (itself), Kaula, Akula, both supreme (transcendent) and inferior (immanent). (51cd-54ab) And she is the (goddess) Raudrī I have told (you about who is brilliant) like the sun freed from Rāhu (who obscures it). The constantly attentive soul should contemplate her, whose light is like that of the Doomsday Fire, brilliant as a hundred million suns, until by means of (that)36 energy he dissolves away. (54cd-55)

sanskrit: 14 कुमारिकाखण्ड: सन्निरीक्षत्यसौ'५२ तत्र रुद्राणां चरण ३ सदा । एवमभ्यस्यमानस्तु योगी तत्रैव लक्षयेत् ॥ ५६ ॥ १५४ नाभिमध्याद् विनिष्क्रान्ता शिखा दीपशिखोपमा ५५ । १५७ । पश्यते तत्र मध्ये तु हुताशकणिकाकृतिः ।। ५७ ।। बिन्दोर्विसर्पते सा तु स्फुरमाणा स्वतेजसा । १५९ प्रवेशे हृदयान्तस्था कृत्वा तस्यैव कल्पनाम् ॥ ५८ ॥ ऊध्वे‍ तु सर्पते तस्मात् स्निग्धदीपशिखोपमा । स्फुरल्लिङ्गनिभां तन्तु सूक्ष्मरूपां तु भेदयेत् ।। ५९ ।। सा च देवी ह्यहं तत्र कुब्जिकाकाररूपिणी । कण्ठरन्ध्रमनुप्राप्य विरमेत् सूक्ष्मरूपिणी ।। ६० ॥ १६७ ऊध्वं सा च विनिष्क्रम्य तालुरन्द्रान्तगोचरें । घण्टिकाद्वारमार्गेण क्रमाख्ये बिन्दुगोचरे ।। ६१ ।। लक्षयेद् बिन्दुमध्ये तु शब्दस्तत्र“ नानाकृतिः १६९ बिन्दोरूध्वं विनिष्क्रान्ता कला सा कालकर्षणी ।। ६२ । ज्योतिरूपस्वरूपा७२ सा निर्धूमाङ्गारवर्चसा । १७३ १७७ १७६ निर्वाणा¨¨ शान्तरूपाख्या प्रसुप्ता अहिरूपिणीं निराभासा सुप्रकाशा द्वादशान्ते समाश्रिता' । शब्दाम्बरधराकारा श्वासनिःश्वासवर्जिता ।। ६४ ।। १७८ ॥ ६३ ॥
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-ONE 15 There he views the plane (caraSa)37 of the Rudras constantly. The yogi who always practices in this way should mark (her) there. (56) Another Ascent The Navel The Flame (śikhā) (is KuSÆalinī) who, similar to the flame of a lamp, has emerged from the centre of the navel. She is seen there in the centre, her form (like) a spark from a fire.38 (57) The Heart She emerges out of the Drop and scintillates with her own radiant energy (tejas). In (the phase of) entry, once (the yogi) has conceived (her through meditation) she resides in the heart. (58) The Throat From there, like the flame of a (well) oiled lamp, she crawls upwards. She should split apart the subtle thread (of SunumSā) which is like a radiating Li‰ga.39 (59) I am the goddess who resides there in the form of a hunched-back woman.40 (Her) form subtle, she rests when she reaches the throat’s cavity. (60) The End of the Twelve and Ultimate Realisation She exits upwards through the field of the cavity of the palate by the path of the door of the uvula into the sphere of the Drop called the Krama.41 Then one should perceive (laknayet) (her) in the centre of the Drop. There is a Sound there of many forms. (61-62ab) That Energy (kalā) that exits upwards above the Drop is Kālakarninī (the Attractrix of Time). Her nature and form is light that shines like a smokeless burning coal.42 (62cd-63ab) She is NirvāSā (Cessation) and is called the Form of Peace (śāntarūpā). In the form of a snake, she sleeps.43 The unmanifest (nirābhāsā), she is the beautiful light within the End of the Twelve. Devoid of inhalation and exhalation, her form is the flow (dharā) of the Void of Sound (śabdāmbara). (63cd-64)

sanskrit: 16 कुमारिकाखण्ड: निःशब्दं परमं तत्त्वं अव्यक्तस्थानमुच्यते । ९ वै स्थानं तु संप्राप्य योगी दिव्यगुणान्वितः ।। ६५ ।। १८२ दिव्यज्ञानं दिव्यचक्षुर्दिव्यतेजो नभाकृतिः' । दिव्यदेहे प्रविष्टोऽसौ संसारत्यक्तचेतसः ।। ६६ ।। कालत्रयस्य वेत्तासौ अदृष्टज्ञानविग्रहः । स्वयं कती स्वयं हत इच्छारूपधरो भवेत् ।। ६७ ।। ८७ दिव्य च कुरुते कर्म व्रतिनो योगवित् सदा । रन्द्रत्रयेण“ निर्गत्य पश्यते सूर्यबिम्बवत् ॥ ६८ ॥ कदम्बगोलकाकारं स्फुरन्तं तेजवर्चसम्” । लक्षयेत्” शिखा सूक्ष्मा द्वारत्रयविनिर्गता ।। ६९ ।। लीयते मण्डले तस्मिन् कदम्बाकारगोलके ९२ । । भित्त्वा सूर्यं च सोमं च तृतीयं वह्निमण्डलम् ।। ७० ।। इच्छाज्ञानीक्रिया”” तत्र ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेश्वराः । १९५ तत्र देवगणाः सर्वे सशैलवनकाननाः ।। ७१ ।। रेखात्रयं ततः पश्येन्महानासाग्रसंगमे । भस्मे वा सलिले वापि ज्ञानशूलं च विन्यसेत् ।। ७२ ।। तेन विन्दितमात्रेण प्रत्यक्षं देविदर्शनम् । १९७ तत्क्षणात् कुरुते वेध जगत्स्थावरजङ्गमे ।। ७३ । प्रत्यक्षे वा परोक्षे वा शङ्खे पुष्पाञ्जलीघटे । २०० चालनावेशन कम्प तडित्तरलगोचरम् ॥ ७४ ॥ कुरुते तानि कर्माणि अस्य योगप्रभावतः । ।।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-ONE 17 The Supreme Principle is devoid of Sound (niƒśabda). It is said to be the Place of the Unmanifest. Once the yogi reaches that place, he is endowed with divine qualities. (65) His mind has abandoned the world of transmigratory existence and his form is (the transcendental) Void. 44 He has entered the divine body (of the deity) and possesses divine power (tejas), sight and knowledge. (66) He knows the three times and his form is that of unseen knowledge. He is himself the agent and the destroyer and assumes (whatever) form he desires. (67) He observes (the Kaula’s) vow (vratin), he performs divine works and knows (the supreme state of) Yoga at all times. Once he has left (the body) by means of the Three Cavities, (the Drop) becomes perceptible. (Its) form is (round like) the bud (golaka) of a Kadamba (tree) and is luminous with radiant energy (tejas) like the solar orb. (68-69) He should mark it attentively (laknayet). The subtle Flame, which has come forth through the Three Doors, penetrates through the Sun, the Moon and the Circle of Fire, which is the third. It then merges into that Circle shaped (like) the bud of a Kadamba (tree).45 (70) (The energies of) will, knowledge and action (are located) there (along with) Brahmā, VinSu and Maheśvara. The hosts of gods are all there and there are (many) mountains, forests and groves.46 (71) Then he should see the three lines at the great junction at the end of the Great Nose (mahānāsa). He should deposit the Trident of Knowledge onto water or ashes.47 (72) The Fruits of Attainment A direct vision of the Goddess through the senses is only (possible) by attaining this. In that very moment (she) pierces through (all) that is moving and immobile in the universe.48 (73) The power of his Yoga evokes the modalities of motion, penetration (āveśa), trembling and the pulsing field of lightning, whether the conch and the jar (to which one offers) the handful of flowers are directly apparent to the senses or not. (74-75ab)

sanskrit: 18 कुमारिकाखण्ड: २०३ तदासौ मानवो‍ सिद्धः सिद्धिं प्राप्नोत्यखण्डिताम् ।। ७५ ।। दिव्या४ च जायते कान्ति अणिमादिगुणाष्टकम् । भूतवेतालयोगिन्यो गुह्यका मातृकास्तथा २०७ २०६ एतेभ्यः सिद्धिमाप्नोति वेधसिद्धो वरानन ।। ७६ ।। । २०८ पद्मपत्रे फले” तोये” स्थावरे जङ्गमेषु च ।। ७७ ।। काष्ठे लोष्टे च पाषाणे योगी सर्वत्र वेधकः । नातः परतरं किञ्चित्”” त्रिषु लोकेषु विद्यते ॥ ७८ ॥ ज्ञात्वा वेधक्रमं देव त्रिषु लोकेषु दुर्लभम् । वेधयेन्मन्त्रतन्त्राणि परतत्त्वावलोकनात् ।। ७९ ।। अमृताख्या तु या शक्तिश्चन्द्रगभीद् विनिर्गता । ब्रह्मरन्ध्रं तु संप्राप्ता वेधयेद् भुवनान्तरम् २१३ २१२ भुवने भुवने वेधं विग्रहे विग्रहे स्मरेत् । २१४ ।। ८० ।। आकारे तु महावेधं विग्रहे तरलकारकम् ॥ ८१ ॥ निर्धूमे धूमजं वेधं अर्केण १६ चार्कज १७ विदुः । अनाख्ये तीव्रवेधं तु कथितं ते महेश्वर ।। ८२ ॥ खद्योतेन १८ महावेधं ज्योतिरूपं तथैव च । बिन्दोर्वेधं तथा नादे कलायां च तृतीयकम् ॥ ८३ ॥ घटवेधं महादेश खवेधस्तथैव च । शक्तिवेध” तथा चोग्रं नानाश्चर्यप्रवर्तकम् २२२ शक्तिगर्भस्तथा २३ हक्को २४ व्योमचक्रे प्रवर्तते । ।। ८४ ।। वर्णजाल १२५ च शब्दस्थं व्यापकं तमनुस्मरेत् ॥ ८५ ॥
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-ONE 19 Then that man (becomes) a Siddha and he achieves unconditioned success. (He acquires) a divine beauty and the eight (yogic) qualities including the power to make himself small at will (aSimā) and the rest.49 (75cd-76ab) O handsome one, the (yogi) who has managed to pierce (through the inner centres) acquires yogic power (siddhi) from ghosts, Vetālas, Yoginīs, Guhyakās and the Mothers (mātrkā). (76cd-77ab) The yogi pierces through everything, a lotus leaf, a fruit, water, the immobile, the moving things, wood, iron and stone. There is nothing higher than this in the three worlds. (77cd-78) O god, once one has known the process of piercing (the inner Wheels) (vedhakrama), which is hard to acquire in the Three Worlds, one should pierce the mantras and Tantras by gazing at the Supreme Principle. (79) The Energy called Amrtā (Nectar) has come forth out of the womb of the Moon. Once it reaches the Aperture of Brahmā, it should (go on to) pierce through the inside of the worlds. (80) The piercing (motion passes) through every single world. One should recall it in each corporeal form (vigraha). The Great Piercing takes place in (all that has) shape; within (one's own bodily) form it causes trembling. (81) The piercing born of smoke takes place within the smokeless.50 (The wise) know that (the piercing that takes place) by means of the Sun is born of the Sun. O Great Lord, it is said that your Intense Piercing (takes place) in the Nameless (anākhya). (82) In the same way, the Great Piercing which is Light (takes place) by means of the Firefly.51 The piercing of the Drop (takes place) within Sound and the third one within Energy (kalā). (83) There is the Piercing of the Jar (that is the body), the Great Command (mahādeśa) and the Piercing of the Sky. Again, there is the fierce Piercing of Energy which brings about many wonders. (84) A Sound (hakka) full of Energy arises within the Wheel of the Void. One should (then) recollect the net of letters (varSajāla), that pervading (all things), is established in the Word. (85)

sanskrit: 20 कुमारिकाखण्ड: २२६ मनोबुद्धिरहंकारं यत्नतः सर्वरन्ध्रतः । २२८ ।। प्रथयेत्७ परमे धाम्नि हृत्कण्ठे तालुमध्यतः ॥ ८६ ॥ नासिकान्ते यथा” प्राप्तं कुरु कर्म यथेच्छया । वेधयेत् काष्ठपाषाणान् वृक्षाणि च वरानन २३० काष्ठेन काष्ठवेधं तु तच्च३ ज्ञानविवर्जितम् । २३४ २३५ २३२ ।। ८७ ।। एवयोगविधौ देव लब्धलक्षस्तु ५ योगवित् ॥ ८८ ॥ २३६ प्रत्यक्षं कुरुते सर्वं यत्र यत्रैव योजिता । योगसिद्धो महादेव जायते भैरवः स्वयम् ।। ८९ ॥ मदीयाज्ञाप्रभावेन कुलक्रमरतः सदा । अभिषेक २३७ तस्य संजात २३८ श्रीमच्चन्द्रपुरे गृहे ॥ ९० ॥ कुचन्द्रशेखरो नाम आज्ञाधरो” महाबलः । २४१ श्रीनाथ ४० मित्रसंज्ञोऽयं श्रीकण्ठः ४९ तूष्णिसंज्ञया ·२४४ २४२ षष्ठमोडीशाचार्योऽयं २४३ सदाख्यं पिङ्गलं महत् । नवनामकृतं५ नाथं चिञ्चिवृक्षावलोकनात् ।। ९२ ॥ नवधा तत्त्वमाख्यातं भूगृह६ देवतालयम् । ॥ ९१ ॥ योऽसौ आज्ञापयेद् देवान् ९ नाम्ना करणसंज्ञया ।। ९३ ।। २५० भविष्यन्ति भवे ह्येते भविष्यन्ति हि दक्षिणे । एकधात्रिस्वरूपेण पञ्चसप्तनवार्णकम् ।। ९४ ॥ षोडशान्तं क्रमान्तं २५२ च २५३ आयातं क्रमपद्धतौ । युग्ममष्टादशैर्भेदैः२५४ कथिता क्रमपद्धतिः ।। ९५ ॥ ।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-ONE 21 (The yogi) should make an effort to perceive the mind, the intellect and the ego through all the cavities in the Supreme Abode, (namely) the heart, the throat and the centre of the palate. (86) When (the Plane) at the extremity of the Nose (nāsikānta)52 has been attained, then do what you like. O handsome one, he should pierce through trees, stones and wood. (87) The Wooden Piercing (kān˜havedha) takes place with difficulty (kān˜hena) and that is devoid of knowledge (jñāna).53 (88ab) O god, the knower of Yoga who has attained the goal in this kind of yogic practice, makes all things visible to the senses wherever (that energy) is applied.54 O Maheśvara, one who has accomplished Yoga becomes Bhairava himself. (88cd-89) By the power of my Command he is always devoted to the Kulakrama and his consecration has taken place in the House of the venerable City of the Moon. (90) The Nine forms of the First Teacher and the Lineages of Teachers 55The one called Kucandraśekhara who, very powerful, is the bearer of the Command is Śrīnātha, the one called Mitranātha, ŚrīkaS˜ha with the name TūnSī(nātha), ±an˜ha(nātha), OÆīśācārya, the one called Sadā(śiva) (Sadākhya) and the great Pi‰gala. The Lord (nātha) assumed nine names by gazing on the Tamarind Tree.56 (Thus) the ninefold Principle, which is the house of the world and the abode of the gods, has been explained. (91-93ab) The gods he commands by name and by their causal terms (karaSasaˆjñā) will come into existence in the world of bondage (bhava). They will come into being in the South of India (dakniSa). (93cd-94ab) Of one kind with three natures, five, seven and nine letters and the End of the Sixteen which is the culmination of the transmission (krama) has come into the Krama liturgy. The Krama liturgy is said to be the Couple, along with the eighteen divisions (of the Divine Current).57 (94cd-95)

sanskrit: 22 कुमारिकाखण्ड: एवं यो विन्दते देव वेधमार्ग कुलागमे । २५७ अग्निना २५६ दह्यते नैव शस्त्रैश्चापि न भिद्यते ।। ९६ ।। २६० २६२ नोदके २५८ मृयते ५९ देव न च दुष्यति ११ जन्तुभिः । भुञ्जते विविधान् भोगान् सदेवासुरमानुषान् ।। ९७ ॥ दिव्यरूपो ४ महाकान्तिः त्रिष्कालज्ञो भवत्यसौ । २६८ । विद्धोऽयं६६ तत्त्वतः प्रोक्तो यावद् देव निरामयम् ।। ९८ ।। दर्शयेत् सर्वलोकस्य मायां च रचनाकुलाम् २७१ २६९ । शक्ति ० तु कमलाकारां सूर्यकोटिसमप्रभाम् ।। ९९ ।। चन्द्रकोटिसहस्राणि विद्युत्कोटिशतानि च । हुताशनान्यनेकानि वायुवेगान् बहून्यपि ॥ १०० ॥ ईदृशं चिन्तयित्वा तु शक्तिरूपं विशेत् क्षणात् । वेधयेच्च३ जगत् सर्वं दिव्यशक्तिप्रभावतः ।। १०१ ॥ सर्वध्यानमशेषस्य २७४ शाक्तं ध्यानं विशिष्यते । एवं यो जानते ५ देव स च कौलीशमीश्वर: २७६ स चात्मा सर्वलोकानां स एव शाश्वतं पदम् । २७७ २७८ ।। १०२ ।। सवै ब्रह्मा स शक्रश्च चन्द्रादित्यौ स वै वह्निः २७९ ।। १०३ ॥ यमश्च° स च धर्मो वै स च वै मरुतो भवेत् । सर्वगः स विमुक्तात्मा तिष्ठते हंसवत् स्वयम् ॥ १०४ ॥ २८४ २८३ भवितस्तारणार्थाीय अवतीर्ण:५ कलौ युगे । यथाहं च यथा त्वं च तथासौ साधकोत्तमः ॥ १०५ ॥ २८७ संसाराच्चैव८६ सारस्य सारमुत्तारणक्षमः । २८८ २८९ यो जानाति इदं शम्भो अग्रजन्म: स उच्यते ।। १०६ ॥ वेधक्रमं च देवेश यो जानाति स देशिकः । पशुग्रहणवेधं तु सद्यः प्रत्ययकारकम् ।। १०७ ।। करोत्याज्ञाप्रसादेन कुलभेदेन भैरव ।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-ONE 23 The Fruits of Attainment (continued) O god, he who attains the Piercing Path (vedhamārga) in the Kula scripture is not burnt by fire and is not cut by weapons. O god, he does not die (of drowning) in water and is not harmed by anybody. He constantly enjoys many kinds of enjoyments, including those of men, gods and demons. He possesses a divine form, great beauty and knows the three times. (96-98ab) In truth he is said to be pierced to the extent the stainless god shows (him) the Māyā of all the world, full of (its own) creation. (98cd-99ab) The Contemplation of Energy Having contemplated Energy (śakti) in the form of a lotus whose light is like a hundred million suns and (contemplated) tens of billions of moons, billions of lightning bolts, countless fires and multitudes of violent winds, he should enter (that) Energy in a moment. He should pierce the entire universe by the power of divine Energy. (99cd-101) Of all (types of) contemplation (dhyāna), that of Energy is the most important. O god, he who knows (reality) in this way is the Lord, the Lord of Kaula. (102) He is the Self of all the worlds. He himself is the eternal plane. He indeed is Brahmā, Śakra, the Sun and the Moon. He is Fire, Yama, Dharma and the Wind. Omnipresent, the liberated soul is like the Gander (the Supreme Soul) himself. (104) He is venerated (by the fettered) for (their) salvation and so descends (into the world) during the Age of Strife. This most excellent of adepts is as you are and I am. (105) He is able to understand completely the essence of the essence of transmigratory existence. O Śambhu, he who knows this is said to be in his last life. (106) He who knows the piercing procees (vedhakrama), O Lord of the gods, is a (true) teacher. O Bhairava, by the grace of (his) Command and the splitting apart of Energy (kulabheda), he instigates the piercing which lays hold of the fettered soul and immediately brings about realisation (pratyaya). (107-108ab)

sanskrit: 24 २९१ कुमारिकाखण्डः एका शक्तिः परा सूक्ष्मा विज्ञानानेककारिका गोपनीया प्रयत्नेन यदीच्छेद्”” दीर्घजीवितम् । २९२ ॥ १०८ ॥ श्रीनाथ उवाच २९४ ईदृशं वेधविज्ञानं महदाश्चर्यकारकम् ।। १०९ ॥ कीदृशं करणं चैव पशुवेधं वद प्रभो ९५ । श्रीवक्रा उवाच २९६ २९७ । शृणु नाथ प्रवक्ष्यामि सारात् सारतरं परम् ।। ११० ।। षट्त्रिंशदंगुलाधारात्” हृत् कण्ठं द्वादशांगुलम् । •२९९ पशुं सन्मुखमास्थाय शक्तेरुच्चारसंवृतम् लोलीभूतं ततो गृह्य” आनयेच्च स्वकं पुरम् । ३०१ ॥ १११ ।। रेचकेन तु विश्राम्य कुम्भकेन विदारयेत् ।। ११२ ।। संस्कार पूरकेणैव प्रशान्तेन तु शोधनम् । निष्कले निर्मले शान्ते निष्प्रपञ्चे निरामये ।। ११३ ।। रेचकेन तु उद्धृत्य पूरकेन तु निक्षिपेत् । कुम्भके कुम्भवत् तिष्ठेदुद्भव े गोलकामृतम् ।। ११४ ।। तत्त्वे तत्त्वे तु संयोज्या विद्रुमाकाररूपिणी । शक्तिः कुटिलरूपेण“ सर्वसिद्ध्यर्थदायिका ।। ११५ ।।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-ONE 25 If one wishes to live a long life, one should keep the one subtle and supreme Energy who brings about countless forms of consciousness, concealed with great effort. (108cd-109ab) The Initiation by Piercing Devoid of Outer Means Śrīnātha said: Such knowledge of the act of piercing inspires great wonder. O Lord, tell (me) about the instrument (of realisation) (karaSa), namely, the piercing of the fettered. (109cd-110ab) The venerable (goddess) Vakrā said: Listen, O Lord, I will tell (you) the supreme (teaching), more essential than the (very) essence. (110cd) The heart is (at a distance of) thirty-six fingers from the Foundation. The throat is twelve fingers (from the heart).58 (111ab) Having placed the fettered soul, who is enveloped in the utterance of Energy and in dynamic union (with it) (lolībhūta), in front of himself and, having laid hold (of him), (the teacher) should lead him to his own abode (pura). (111cd-112ab) Having brought him to rest by means of exhalation (recaka), he should (then) be penetrated by suspending the breath (kumbhaka). Latent traces of past action (saˆskāra) are purified within the pure, undifferentiated (ninkala), tranquil and flawless transcendent (reality) by means of tranquil inhalation (pūraka). (112cd-113) Having first extracted it by means of exhalation, he should throw it into the jar (of breath retention) (kumbhaka) and abide (therein immobile and vacuous) like a jar (while) the ball of nectar (amrtagolaka) is generated (within it). (114) The Energy whose form is the Tree (vidruma) (of the Transmental), who bestows all the goals of accomplishment (siddhi), should be conjoined within every single principle in her ‘crooked’ aspect (as KuSÆalinī).59 (115)

sanskrit: 26 कुमारिकाखण्ड: श्रीनाथ उवाच सूचिता वेधदीक्षेयं उपायरहिता प्रभो ३०७ । शाम्भवं ब्रूहि देवेशि न च योन्या पुनर्भवः ।। ११६ ।। ३१० श्रीवक्रा उवाच ३१२ सरहस्यं कृतं चोद्यं संस्फुटं शृणु भैरव । श्रूयतां परमं ज्ञानं प्रत्यक्षं सर्वतोमुखम् ।। ११७ ।। योगिनीनां यथा बीजं त्वया गोप्यं तु सर्वदा । काकचञ्चुमयं”४ स्थानं१५ अध- ऊध्वविवर्जितम् ।। ११८ ।। तालुमण्डलमध्यस्थं षोडशारं महाद्युतिः । ३१६ तत्र सा रमते काचित् सर्वकामिकसंज्ञिका ।। ११९ ।। तस्मिन् स्थाने यदा स्पर्शस्तदा” वेधयते पशून् । विन्दते च परं स्थानं शिवं सर्वगतं स्मरेत् ॥। १२० ।। एतत् ते कथितं वेध” श्रीमताख्ये मतोत्तमे । यो विजानाति तत्त्वेन तस्य तुष्यन्ति देवताः ।। १२१ ।। चतुःषष्टिमहाचक्रे”” खेचरीचक्रनायके । ३२३ ३२० खेभूपातालवासिन्यो गुह्यकाश्चान्त्यजाश्च ये ।। १२२ ।। सहजाः” कुलजाश्चैव” तुष्यन्ति च पदे पदे । स्निग्धपद्मदलाकारैस्तारैस्तरलतारकैः ।। १२३ ।। आकर्णजातै: २४ सरसैर्ललितैर्लोचनै: ३२५ प्रिय । वीक्षन्ति२७ योगिनीजस्य साधकस्य न संशयः ।। १२४ ।। ३२९ ३३० ३२६ यत्रस्थः स॰ लभेदेव” विधिना सुसमाहितः । निग्रहानुग्रहं वाथ सिद्ध्यते ह्यविचारतः ।। १२५ ।।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-ONE 27 The Śāmbhava Piercing Śrīnātha said: O Lord, the Initiation by Piercing devoid of (outer) means has been explained. O mistress of the gods, tell (me about) the Śāmbhava one by means of which there is no further rebirth. (116) The venerable (goddess) Vakrā said: The question (you) have asked (concerns a) secret. O Bhairava, listen to the clear (reply). Listen to the supreme knowledge that is visible to the senses and is present everywhere. You should always keep it hidden as one does the seed of the Yoginīs. (117-118ab) (There is a) place made of the Beak of the Crow,60 which is devoid of upper and lower. It is a (Wheel of) sixteen spokes that possesses great lustre and is located in the middle of the Circle of the Palate. There that certain (subtle Energy) called `she who desires everything', sports. (118cd-119) If a (subtle) tactile sensation (sparśa) occurs within that place, (the teacher) then pierces (all) fettered souls and (each one) attains the supreme abode. (Thus) he should recall the omnipresent Śiva. (120) This, the (act of) Piercing, has been explained to you in the Śrīmata, the best of Matas. The deities residing in the leader (of all the Wheels), namely, the Khecarīcakra (the Wheel of the Skyfarers),61 which is the great Wheel of the Sixty-four (Yoginīs), are pleased with one who knows it correctly. (121-122ab) The Guhakas who live in the sky, on the earth and the lower regions, (the Yoginīs called) Antyajā (Last Born), Sahajā (Innately Born) and Kulajā (Born of Kula) are pleased (with him) at every step. Certainly, O beloved, they view (this) adept, the son of a Yoginī, (lovingly) with their long, playful, swan-like eyes that shine like twinkling stars and whose form is like charming lotus leaves. (122cd-124) Well attentive, wherever he may be, he gets (whatever he wants) by (this) practice. Without (needing) to reflect, he accomplishes (both) chastisment (nigraha) and grace (anugraha). (125)

sanskrit: 28 कुमारिकाखण्ड: चलचक्रविभागेन षट्चक्रे लक्ष” योजयेत् । ३३३ ३३४ पुनश्चाल्य पुनावेश्य पुनश्चाल्य प्रसन्नधीः ।। १२६ ।। चालनावेशनाच्चैव३५ तदा वेधयते पशून् । योगेन वेधयेत् पिण्डं पिण्डोदरपुटीकृतम् ।। १२७ ।। पिण्डेन वेधयेत् पिण्डं पिण्डं पिण्डेन साधयेत् । स्वमात्मा३६ बहिरात्मा च एकत्र विनिवेशितौ ॥ १२८ ॥ ३३७ ३३८ आत्मनात्मा पुरा शोध्यः ८ शक्तिपातेन तत्त्ववित् । एतन्मे कथितं देव तव भक्त्या तु भैरव ।। १२९ ।। ३४० अकुलास्ते विभाषन्ते सर्ववर्णाद् विजातयः । ३४१ । भविष्यन्ति युगस्यान्ते म्लेच्छराज्यसमुद्भवे ।। १३० ॥ अल्पायुषोऽल्पचैतन्या४२ नराः नरा: ३४३ पलितयौवनाः । अगम्यगमनाश्चैव३४४ सदाचारविवर्जिताः ।। १३१ ।। ३४६ अतिलौल्या: ४५ प्रसक्ताश्च विप्लवन्ति यतस्ततः । •३४७ ३४८ ३५० । ।। गुरुसुश्रुषणं नास्ति न४९ मातापितृसुश्रुषाः ।। १३२ ।। भविष्यन्ति कलिस्यान्ते साधकाः कौलसंस्थिताः । ३५२ चातुर्वणी भविष्यन्ति ब्राह्मणाश्च विशेषतः ।। १३३ ॥ उत्तमा वेदविद्वांसा अन्त्यजाश्च तथापरे । अन्त्यजानां द्विजानां च एकत्र चरुभोजनम् ।। १३४ ॥
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-ONE 29 The Practice of the Moving Wheel (calacakra) One should fix one's mark in the Six Wheels in accord with the division of the Moving Wheel (calacakra).62 The (adept) of contented intellect should again set (them) in motion and then having again penetrated (into them) set (them) in motion once more. (126) By setting (them) in motion and penetrating (them thus), he then pierces (all) fettered souls. By means of Yoga, he should pierce the body (of the letters) (piSÆa)63 that has been encapsulated in the belly of the body. (127) By means of the body (of the letters) he should pierce the body (of the universe). He should conquer the body (of the universe) by means of the body (of the letters). (Thus) one's own (inner) Self and the external Self are brought together in one place. (128) O knower of reality, the Self should be purified by the Self through the power of grace (śaktipāta). O Bhairava, because of your devotion (for me) I have told you this, O god. (129) Conclusion — The Evils at the End of the Age of Strife At the end of the Age, when barbarian rule is established, there will be those who belong to none of the castes, speak incorrectly and have no lineage (kula).64 (130) Men (will be) young and pale. (They will be) short lived and have little consciousness. Devoid of right conduct, (they) go to places where one should not go. (131) Extremely greedy and attached (to material things), they lay waste (the world). There will be no desire to listen to a teacher nor will they want to listen (to even their own) mother and father. (132) (But at the same time), at the end of the Age of Strife, there will be adepts who belong to Kaula (lineages). They will be members of (all) the four castes and, in particular, Brahmins. (133) The best (will be), well versed in the Veda (but) there will also be others who belong to the lowest caste. Those of the lowest caste and the twice born eat the sacrificial pap together in one place. (134)

sanskrit: 30 कुमारिकाखण्ड: भविष्यति३५३ कलिस्यान्ते३५४ तवाख्यातमशेषतः । ३५६ तेन मन्दतरा १५५ आज्ञा भविष्यति न संशयः ।। १३५ ।। ३५७ इत्याद्यावतारे महामन्थान भैरवयज्ञे अन्वये सप्तकोटिप्रमाणे मेरुमार्गविनिर्गते' लक्षपादाधिके विद्यापीठमार्गे विमलभेदोत्तरषट्कनिर्णये कादिभेदे आज्ञा- पारमेश्वरे स्वामिनीमते श्रीचतुर्विंशत्सहस्रसंहितायां अव्वाक्रमभाषिते वेधदीक्षाधिकारवर्णने क्रमोदयो नामानन्दः ।। ३१ ।।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-ONE 31 I have told you everything (that) will take place at the end of the Age of Strife. And so the Command will certainly be extremely weak. (135) This is the (thirty-first) chapter which is the emergence of the transmission (kramodaya) with regards to the description of the Initiation by Piercing. It belongs to the primordial descent into the great sacrifice of the Churning Bhairava in the tradition (anvaya) that consists of seventy million (verses) that has emerged on the Path of Meru and (extends) for more than a hundred thousand quarter (verses). It is on the path of the Seat of Knowledge (vidyāpī˜ha) and is the ultimate purport of the Subsequent Six Thousand (verses) of the Pure Division (vimalabhedottarana˜ka) in the division beginning with `Kā' in the venerable scripture of twenty-four thousand (verses) (known as) the Svāminīmata of the Supreme Lord's command as uttered within the Tradition of the Mother (avvākrama).
