english: CHAPTER THIRTY-TWO The Characteristic Signs of Teachers and Disciples. The Arising of the Years (abdodaya) The venerable (goddess) Vakrā said: O Lord, I will now explain the great arising from the centre of Meru by knowing which alone, the descent (of deity into the world) takes place. (1) Sumanta, Pramukha, Bhūti, Sumukha, Balavat, Nidhi, Pratāpin, Pramādhin, Praharna, Vijaya, Anurakta, Sudhanya, Dhanavat, Dhārin, Kāla, ŚravaSa, Yama, Marīci, Viraja, Vāgmin, Vipula, Kulin, Pati, Indrajit, Himavat, Maulin, Kāmada, Śa‰kha, Bodhaka, Viśvā‰gin, Śubhada, Krūra, Acintya, Vijayin, Pati, Sumālin, Śarvara, Kānta, Śuci, Vādin, Śucivrata, Kulajihva, Sama, Śakra, Sumantrin, Vanavān, Madhu, Gāndhārin, µaˆkavrt, Śārva, Śūra, Bha˜˜a, Vikrama, Udghona, Bhrgu, Śrīvatsa, Kaustubha, Malaya, Rathin, Vika˜a, Śaˆkara, Garva, Sunanda, Hanumantaka, ViśvāSga, Viśvajit, Vāgmin, Kaśmala, Amala, Bhīmasena, Subhīma, Bhīmarūpa, Mahābala, Vasu, Vasubhrta, Dhātr, Vasava, Āsava, Guru, Tejasvin, Sarvadarśin, Sarvātman, Priyavādin, Pretavāsa, Priya, Svātin, Viśāla, Abhaya, Śaśi, Śr‰gārin, Sundara, Ratna, Vicitra, Bhoga, Õambhaka, Mahāharna, Mahājihva, Krakaca, ŚūladaSÆin, Śatakratu and Dakna. This year is one of a hundred sacrifices. (2-10ab)

sanskrit: 34 कुमारिकाखण्ड: ५१ ५२ महाहर्षो” महाजिह्वः क्रकचः शूलदण्डिनः ॥ १० ॥ ५३ शतक्रतुश्च दक्षश्च वर्षमेतच्छतक्रतुः । अब्दोदयमिदं प्रोक्तं सुमन्तादौ दक्षान्तिकम् ॥ ११ ॥ चक्रवत् परिवर्तन्ते सुमन्ताद्युदयो ं भवेत् । ५७ दक्षान्ते तु क्षये प्राप्ते सुमन्ते च प्रवर्तते ।। १२ ॥ उदयास्तमने चैव ज्ञातव्यास्तु कृतादिषु । ५८ दक्षः शतशतातीते शताब्दशतकेन तु ॥ १३ ॥ ५९ ततो दक्षांशके शेषे शिवमासे शिवाष्टमी । पश्चिमे उदय° जातं सिद्धनाथाभिषेचितम् ॥ १४॥ ६३ एवमब्दोदय' नाम दैविकं समुदाहृतम् । वेत्ति यो देशिकेन्द्रस्तु¨ सोऽधिकारी कुलान्वये ।। १५ । श्रीनाथ उवाच ऐहिकामौष्मिक चैव पशूनां पापमोचनम् । ·६८ कथं गुरु परीक्ष्येत वेधविज्ञानपारगम् ॥ १६ ॥ ७२ बहवो विचरन्त्यस्मिन्” गुरवः पृथिवीतले । सद्गुरोर्लक्षणं ब्रूहि श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः ॥ १७ ॥ शिष्याणामपि देवेशि लक्षणं तु यथार्थतः । ब्रूहि दीक्षाविधानेन स्फुटार्थं पुनरेव हि ॥ १८ ॥ समयाचरण चैव निर्वाण च वदस्व मे । श्रीवक्रा उवाच ७७ •७८ साधु साधु महाशम्भो पृच्छसे माँ सुविस्तरम् ॥ १९ ॥ सर्व” यथाक्रमेणैव वक्ष्यामि शृणु साम्प्रतम् । येन सर्वत्र योगीनां महाव्याप्तिः: प्रवर्तते ।। २० ।।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-TWO 35 This is said to be the Arising of the Years (abdodaya) which begins with Sumanta and ends with Dakna. (They) change (one after another) like a (rotating) wheel. The arising (of the years) commences with Sumanta. When it ends with Dakna, it (again) starts in (the year) Sumanta. (10cd-12) (All the members of the series) should be known in the course of (their) arising and falling away (in this way) within (the four Ages) beginning with Krta and the rest. Dakna (lasts for) for a hundred centuries after the passing of ten thousand (years). (13) Thus the arising (of the tradition) when (only) Dakna’s part remains, that is, the eighth (lunar day) of Śiva in Śiva's month consecrated by Siddhanātha, occurs in the West. (14) The arising of the years (abdodaya) in this way is said to be that of the gods (daivika). The best of teachers who knows this possesses authority in the Kula tradition.1 (15) True and False Teachers and Disciples Śrīnātha said: (The true teacher) frees the fettered from sins in this and the next world. How, (then), should one test the teacher (to see if) he is one who has completely understood (pāraga) the science of piercing (the psychic centres)? (16) There are many teachers who wander on this, the surface of the earth. Tell (me) the characteristic of a true teacher. I wish to hear (it) as it truly is. (17) O mistress of the gods, tell (me) correctly the characteristic of (true) disciples also. Tell me clearly about the practice of the Rule and NirvāSa in accord with the prescribed method of initiation. (18-19ab)

sanskrit: 36 कुमारिकाखण्डः मायारूपधरा” देव आचार्याः पृथिवीतले । देशिकाचारमाश्रित्य जीविकां कल्पयन्ति ये ।। २१ ।। ८४ कुलभ्रष्टाः” कृपाहीना: कुत्सिते सर्वदा रताः । ८७ मद्यमांससमासक्ताः चपलाश्च सडम्बकाः ।। २२ ।। पैशुन्यनिरताश्चैव“ क्षूद्रकर्मरताः “ सदा । ९२ अहंकृताः शठाः क्रूरा: मिथ्याज्ञाज्ञानभाषकाः ॥ २३ ॥ कलिकती मदोन्मत्ताः सततं परनिन्दका: ९५ । लोभासक्ताश्च मोहाढ्या वञ्चने सततोद्यताः ।। २४ ।। परोपदेशं चिन्वन्ते” कृत्रिमव्यवहारकाः” । १०२ एतैरेव गुणैर्युक्ता आचार्यनामधारकाः ।। २५ ।। भक्षाद्वैतरता नित्यं न ते पूज्या महीतले । गुरुद्रव्याभिलाषिन्यो योगिनीद्रव्यभक्षकाः ।। २६ ।। १०३ १०४ चण्डाश्च हिंसकाश्चैव कापालिका विशेषतः । १०७ वीरद्रव्याभिलाषिन:°५ च पूजासंस्कारवर्जिताः ।। २७ ।। प्रायाश्चित्तीचलाचार्या अभक्षभक्षणे रताः । १११ अपेयपाननिरताः” परिहार्या: प्रयत्नतः ।। २८ ।। गुर्वाज्ञा लङ्घयेद् यो हि नरकान्न निवर्तते । ११४ तैस्तु ये दीक्षिता: शिष्या न ते कल्याणभाजनाः ११५ ।। २९ ।।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-TWO 37 The False Teacher The venerable (goddess) Vakrā said: O great Śambhu, wisely indeed have you asked me about (this) most extensive (matter). Now listen, I will explain everything in due order by virtue of which the Great Pervasion yogis (experience) occurs everywhere. (19cd-20) O god, those teachers who earn a living by being teachers on the surface of the earth wear Māyā's (deluding) form. (21) They have fallen from (their) Kula, they have no mercy and are always intent on what is despicable. They are attached to meat and wine and are fickle and deceitful. (22) They are ever devoted to slander and vile actions. They are proud, dishonest and cruel. They impart ignorance (born of) false empowerment (mithyājñājñana). They are quarellsome, garrulous and always speak badly of others. They are attached to (their) greed, full of delusion and are always ready to deceive (others). (23-24) They collect the teachings of others (but do not practice anything) and their behaviour is false. Those who have these (defective) qualities are teachers (only) in name. (25) (Caring nothing about purity and pollution, they profess to be) always intent on oneness in the food they eat. These (teachers) should not be venerated in the world. They desire the substances (offered) to a teacher and (deceitfully) eat the (sacrificial) substances (offered) to the Yoginīs. (26) They are fierce and violent, particularly (those who call themselves) Kāpālikas and they crave for (the wine and meat that are) the (sacrificial) substances of Heroes. (27) They are false teachers who (profess to be engaged) in penance (although) devoted to eating what should not be eaten and drinking what should not be drunk. (Such teachers) should be streneously avoided. (28) He who disobeys the teacher's Command never leaves the hell (he is condemed to enter). The disciples they initiate will not possess auspicious good fortune (kalyāSa). (29)

sanskrit: 38 दीक्षयन्ति च लोभेन मोहविषयकंक्षया ११६ वेधदीक्षाविहीनाश्च चुम्बकाः क्रमतल्पगाः कुमारिकाखण्ड: ११७ ते”“ पूजारहिता”” देव पतन्ति नरकार्णवे । १२० ' । ।। ३० ।। तरुस्तारयते नद्यां न शिलां तारयते शिला ।। ३१ ।। तथैव निर्गुणाचार्यस्तारयेन्न” भवार्णवात् । वर्जनीयः १२२ प्रयत्नेन मतबाह्य विधीयते ।। ३२ ।। १२४ चातुर्वर्णेषु आचार्यीन् श्रूयतां कमलानन । ब्राह्मणः क्षत्रियो वाथ वेश्य : २५ शूद्रोऽपि मद्यपः ॥ ३३ ॥ १२७ चातुर्वर्ण २६ मया चोक्त आचार्यीणा लक्षणं यथा । तीव्राज्ञाबोधसंपन्नाः श्रीमतार्थावबोधकाः ।। ३४ ॥ ज्ञानविज्ञानसंपन्ना गुर्वाज्ञाप्रतिपालकाः । निर्मला निष्प्रपञ्चाश्च निर्ममा निष्परिग्रहाः ।। ३५ ।। अनुद्विग्नाः सदानन्दा निर्लेपा २ निर्विकल्पगाः' १३५ १३३ । क्षमान्विता दयायुक्ता सत्यवादी जितेन्द्रियाः ।। ३६ ।। अहिंसातत्परा'३६ सर्वे ३७ सर्वजीवदयापराः । १३८ शान्तचित्ता: सदाचाराः सदाचारा:”” द्वन्द्वत्यागी दृढव्रताः ।। ३७ ।। न स्त्रीलोल्या न च क्रूराः क्षुद्रकर्मपरान्मुखाः । दिव्यज्ञानेन संतृप्ताः उदाराश्च प्रसन्नधीः ।। ३८ ॥ गोत्रवात्सल्यसद्भक्ताः” राजद्रव्यमुपेक्षकाः । १४३ गुरुपर्वाधिकारिनो आज्ञापरा महाबलाः ।। ३९ ॥
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-TWO 39 They give initiation out of greed and crave for the objects of delusion. Devoid of the initiation by piercing (vedhadīknā), they are lustful and have sex with the wives of (those who taught them) the Krama. (30) O god, devoid of the rite of adoration (pūjā), they fall into the ocean of hell. Wood gets one across a river; a stone does not get one across stone. Similarly, a teacher devoid of (good) qualities does not save one from the ocean of phenomenal existence. He should be strenously avoided and excluded from the Teaching (mata). (31-32) The True Teacher O lotus faced one, listen to (the qualities of true) teachers belonging to the four castes. (The teacher can be a) Brahmin, Knatriya, Veśya or Śudra who drinks wine. (33) I have explained the (true) sign of the teachers belonging to the four castes. They possess the awakened consciousness of an intensely powerful Command and enlighten as to the meaning of the Śrīmata. (34) They are endowed with both knowledge and understanding and carry out the teacher's Command. They are pure and thought-free, selfless and detached. (35) They are not troubled, but are always blissful, without stain and without (obscuring) ideation, they are merciful, compassionate, truthful and have conquered the senses. (36) They are all intent on non-violence and have compassion towards all living beings. Their mind is tranquil, their behaviour correct, they have abandoned duality and firmly maintain their vows. (37) They are not greedy for women or cruel and are averse to vile actions. They are satisfied with divine knowledge, dignified and (their) intellect is tranquil. (38) They are always devoted to the loving affection of (their spiritual) clan and are indifferent to kingly riches. They are fit (to be worshipped) on the teacher's day and intent on (his) Command. They are very powerful. (39)

sanskrit: 40 कुमारिकाखण्ड: योगिनः१४४ प्रियवादिनो ४५ दाता ४६ भोक्ता अयाचका: १४७ । वेदान्तं वाथ सिद्धान्तं तथान्य” वामदक्षिणम् वामदक्षिणम् ं ।। ४० ।। न दूषयन्ति' शास्त्राणां सद्भक्ताश्च कुमारीनाम् ५३ । १५६ योगियोगिनिवीराणा४ देशद्रष्टा न क्षुद्रक : त्रिष्कालज्ञानिनो धीरः शापानुग्रहकारकः' । १५८ १६० ।। ४१ ।। प्रत्यक्षे च परोक्षे वा वेधदीक्षाविशारदः ।। ४२ ।। १६१ १६३ अनुष्ठानरतः शान्तो‍ लघ्वाशी च सुयन्त्रित: । १६४ दिव्यानन्दरतो नित्यं नित्यं शुचिः पवित्रकः ।। ४३ ।। कुलकौलाप्तविभवः पश्चिमान्वयपारगः । अजुगुप्सी सर्ववेत्ता धातुर्वरमुपेक्षकः १५ ।। ४४ ।। समयाचारपालज्ञ: पारम्पर्यविशारदः । १६७ संकेतज्ञानी विद्वांसः सतताव्यक्तलिङ्गिनः ।। ४५ ॥ साधुमार्गप्रपन्नस्तु¨८ असन्मार्गमुपेक्षकः । लोकधर्मप्रपन्नश्च वेलाशी निष्परिग्रहः ।। ४६ । १७० क्रियाकाण्डरतः शान्तः ९ एकान्तः पुरवासिनः सुभट्टी मानधारी च ७३ सर्वशास्त्रार्थपारगः १७४ १७१ । ।। ४७ ।। सर्वदा हृष्टमानस:१७५ त्यागी सर्वजनप्रियः । दीक्षाप्रतिष्ठाकुशल:७६ तत्तदर्थपरिग्रही ।। ४८ ।। १७८ १७७ १८० स त्यागी धर्मपालज्ञ: कालसेवी न हिंसक : वीरमार्गप्रपन्नात्मा मद्यगोष्टिमुपेक्षक : २ ।। ४९ ॥ १८३ १८२ भट्टभार्यो विशुद्धस्तु पशुमार्गमुपेक्षकः । १८४ उन्मनो मदनावस्थ: तन्त्राचारविवर्जितः ।। ५० ।। ।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-TWO 41 They are yogis and speak in a pleasing way. They are benefactors, enjoyers (of the best things of life) and ask nothing of others. They do not find fault with the Vedānta, (Śaiva) Siddhānta or other (schools of the Tantras whether) of the Left (vāma) or the Right (dakniSa). They are true devotees of the scriptures and the virgins (kumārī). (40-41ab) (The true teacher is one who) sees the land of yogis, Yoginīs and Heroes. Not vulgar, he is compassionate and knows the three times. Steadfast, he both blesses and curses. He is well versed in the initiation by piercing, both when (the disciple is present) visible (before him) and when (he is) out of reach of the senses. He is devoted to the practice of austerity, tranquil, desires little, is disciplined, always intent on divine bliss, he is always pure and saintly. (41cd-43) His greatness is in conformity with Kula and Kaula and he has mastered the Western Tradition. He does not feel disgust, knows everything and is indifferent to the gift of a benefactor. (44) He knows how to maintain the practice of the Rule (samayācāra) and is well versed in the (teaching handed down through) the lineage. He knows the conventions and is learned (but) never sports any (external) sign (of his attainments). (45) He is given to the path of the wise and rejects the false one. He is dedicated to (his) worldly duty, eats at the correct time and is detached. He is devoted to ritual and, tranquil, is solitary (although) he lives in a town. He is a learned versed and respected man who has mastered all the scriptures. (46-47) He is always joyful, a renounciate and liked by all. He is an expert in the rites of initiation and installation (of idols) (pratin˜hā) and grasps every single meaning (of the scripture). (48) He is a renounciate and knows how to follow Dharma. He attends to (the auspicious and inauspicious) times and is not violent. He is set on the Heroes’ Path (but) avoids drinking parties. (49) His wife is learned (bha˜˜abhārya), he is pure and rejects the path of the fettered. (He) is beyond mind and his state is one of (spiritual) inebriation. He is free of (lower) Tantric practice (tantrācāra). (50)

sanskrit: 42 कुमारिकाखण्डः १८५ प्रतिष्ठादिविनिर्मुक्तः सत्यशौचरतः सदा' । १८७ शिष्यवर्गविचारज्ञ: निर्मुक्त: शुद्धचेतसः ।। ५१ । श्वेतवस्त्रपरीधान: “ मुक्तकेशी दिगम्बरः । सुभगो दर्शनी वाग्मी नानाव्रतमुपेक्षकः ।। ५२ ॥ स्वेच्छावेशधरो वाथ सुधौतो मतिलम्पक : ' १९१ । रागद्वेषसमासक्तो दुराचारोऽथ वा भवेत् ॥ ५३ ॥ प्रत्यन्तवासी आचार्य:” दूरतः परिवर्जयेत् । १९३ साधुदेशसमुद्भूतों निग्रहानुग्रहक्षमः ।। ५४ ।। १९४ आचार्येदृक् समाख्यातः अन्वयेऽस्मिन् शुभप्रदः । ईदृश तु गुरुं प्राप्य को न मुच्यति बन्धनात् ।। ५५ ।। आचार्यलक्षणं प्रोक्तं शिष्याणामधुना शृणु । नापरीक्षितशिष्याणां योग्यता पश्चिमान्वये सुभक्तश्च” विनीतश्च पितृमातृप्रपूजकः । २०२ २०३ ॥ ५६ ॥ सदा धर्मरतः १ शान्त: त्यागी आचारवान् सदा ।। ५७ ।। २०४ गुरुपादार्चनरतः देवाग्निगुरुपूजकः । संसारभयभीतात्मा मुक्तिमार्गभिलाषिणः २०६ ॥ ५८ ॥ २०८ अधूर्तो मतिमान् शान्तस्तर्कशास्त्रमुपेक्षकः । २१० योगिनीना” सदा भक्त: कुमारीणां प्रपूजकः ।। ५९ ।। अक्रोधिनो अपिशुनः २ यत्नेन सुपरीक्षितः । २११ २१४ २१३ २१५ उदारार्थपरिच्छेदी अशठः सत्यवाक् सदा ॥ ६० ॥ शरीरं प्राणसर्वस्वं गुरवे विनिवेदक: २१६ । २१८ ।। ६१ ।। कर्मणा मनसा वाचा त्रिशुद्धो” भक्तिवत्सलः
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-TWO 43 He is free of (concern for) the rites of installation and the like and is always intent on truth and purity. He knows his disciples views; he is free and his mind is pure. (51) He wears a white cloth (or) is naked and has dishevelled hair. Handsome, he wears (the yogi’s) earrings (darśanin), speaks well and is unconcerned with (the ostentatious performance) of many vows. He dresses as he likes,2 is very clean and desires sound understanding (matilampaka). (52-53ab) One should avoid (and maintain) a great distance from the teacher who is attached to attachment and aversion or who behaves badly and lives far away (in inauspicious places) (pratyantavāsin). (53cd-54ab) One who is born in a country of wise people and can both grace (good disciples) and chastise (the wicked) — such is the teacher in this tradition who bestows (all that) is auspicious. Once attained a teacher like this, who is not liberated from bondage? (54cd-55) The True Disciple The mark of a (true) teacher has been explained. Now listen to that of the disciples. Disciples who have not been tested are not fit for the Western Tradition. (56) (The true disciple is one who is) a good devotee, well behaved, reveres (his) mother and father, is always intent on virtue, tranquil, a renounciate and practices (spiritual disciplines) constantly. (57) He is intent on worshipping the teacher's feet, the gods, fire and the teacher (himself). He is frightened of the fear (inherent in) transmigratory existence and desires the path of liberation. (58) He is not malicious. (He is) wise, tranquil and has no interest in (dry) logic. He is always devoted to the Yoginīs and venerates virgins. He does not get angry, does not backbite and has been well and streneously tested. He distinguishes profound matters (from the trivial). He is not a cheat, (but) always speaks the truth. (59-60) He offers (his) body and the very essence of (his) life to the teacher. Triply pure by (his) action, speech and mind, he is a dear child of devotion. (61)

sanskrit: 44 कुमारिकाखण्ड: २१९ २२० शाठ्यमात्सर्यनिर्मुक्तः परदारमुपेक्षकः । मुक्तिज्ञानाभिकांक्षी च शिष्योऽयं कुलदीपकः ।। ६२ ।। अविवादी न२२१ विद्वेष्टो २२२ नतो ज्येष्ठजने २२३ सदा । २२४ समयाचारपालज्ञः” निमित्तक्रमपूजकः ।। ६३ । देवार्चनरतो नित्यं गोत्रवात्सल्यतत्परः । २२६ २३० २२७ एवंभूतगुणी शिष्यः नानात्वेन परीक्षितः ।। ६४ ।। दीक्षार्हो २८ हि२९ भवेत् सो वै तीव्राज्ञयावलोकनात् । अन्यथा विपरीतार्थयुक्तो दीक्षयते शिशुः ।। ६५ ।। स आचार्यः स शिष्यस्तु रौरवं नरकं व्रजेत् । २३३ २३५ ब्राह्मणा क्षत्रभृच्छूद्रा४ अन्ये वा अन्त्यजातयः ॥ ६६ ॥ सर्वे शिष्याः प्रकर्तव्या नात्र कार्या विचारणा । भावभक्तिविशुद्धा ये विरक्ताः पृथिवीतले ।। ६७ ।। जातिं तेषां न गृह्णीयाद् भक्तिमेषा परीक्षयेत् । २४० २३७ । ब्राह्मणस्तु अभक्तश्च चण्डालः स विधीयते ॥ ६८ ॥ भक्तिमान् यदि चण्डालो ब्राह्मणः स४२ विधीयते । जातिभेदेन २४३ किं तेन भक्तिरेवात्र कारणम् ।। ६९ ।। २४४ पण्डितोऽप्यविवेकी तु मूर्खतुल्यो महीतले । मूर्खोऽपि हि विविक्तश्चेत् विशुद्धो भक्तितत्परः ।। ७० ।। विबुधस्तु स विज्ञेयः स योग्यः कुलसन्ततौ । २४९ २५० २५२ कुपात्रे कुत्सिते मूर्खे भक्तिहीने कुसंगते ।। ७१ ।। २५३ शठे च दूषके चैव कौलत्वं न २५४ समाचरेत् ५५ ।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-TWO 45 He is free of deceit and envy and is indifferent to the wives of others. He craves for the knowledge of liberation. This disciple is the very light of Kula. (62) He does not quarrel, is not disliked and is always respectful towards elders. He knows how to keep the practice of the Rule and worships by means of the occasional (rites of the) Krama (as well as by the regular ones). He is always intent on worshipping the gods and is intent on the loving affection of (his spiritual) clan. (63-64ab) The disciple who has such qualities and has been variously tested, deserves initiation by means of the most intense Command (transmitted through the teacher's) gaze. Otherwise, if (the teacher) initiates a neophant who has opposite aims (to the correct ones), (then both) that teacher and student will go to the Raurava hell. (64cd-66ab) Brahmins, Knatrīyas, Śūdras or members of other low castes should all be made disciples. One should not hesitate to do so. One should not take into consideration the caste of those who, in this world, are detached and whose feelings (bhāva) and devotion (bhāvabhakti) are pure. (Instead of inquiring into their caste) one should test their devotion. (66cd-68ab) A Brahmin who is not a devotee is considered to be an outcaste (caSÆāla). If an outcaste possesses devotion, he is considered to be a Brahmin. What is the use of caste distinctions? Here, (in this case), devotion alone is the prime factor. (68cd-69) Even a scholar who lacks discrimination in the world is no better than a fool. And even a fool who has discrimination and is intent on devotion, is perfectly pure. He should be known to be well awake. He is fit (to belong to) a Kaula Family. (70-71ab) Do not confer Kaula status to one who is a bad recipient of it, is vile, a fool, devoid of devotion, keeps bad company, is a cheat and is hard to bear. (71cd-72ab)

sanskrit: 46 कुमारिकाखण्ड: अथवाप्याचरेद् यो वै द्रव्यलोभेन मोहितः ।। ७२ ।। योगिन्यस्तस्य कुप्यन्ति भक्षयन्ति वसामिषम् । २५७ तस्मात् ५६ सर्वप्रयत्नेन दीक्षां लोभान्न कारयेत् ।। ७३ ।। इत्याद्यावतारे महामन्थान भैरवयज्ञे अन्वये सप्तकोटिप्रमाणे मेरुमार्गविनिर्गते लक्षपादाधिकारे आद्यपीठावतारिते २५९ विद्यापीठमार्गे ६० विमलषट्क— निर्णये २६१ कादिभेदे२६२ आज्ञापारमेश्वरे स्वामिनीमते गुरुशिष्य - लक्षणाधिकारवर्णने २६३ क्रमोदयो नामानन्दः ।। ३२ ।।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-TWO 47 Otherwise, if (a teacher), deluded by greed for wealth, does confer (it on one such as this), the Yoginīs will be angry with him and eat the fat and the meat (of his body). And so one must make every effort not to confer initiation (motivated) by greed. (72cd-73) This is the (thirty-second) chapter which is the emergence of the transmission (kramodaya) with regards to the description concerning the Characteristics of Teachers and Disciples. It belongs to the primordial descent into the great sacrifice of the Churning Bhairava in the tradition (anvaya) that consists of seventy million (verses) that has emerged on the Path of Meru and (extends) for more than a hundred thousand quarter (verses). It has been brought (down to earth) into the first sacred seat along the path of the Seat of Knowledge (vidyāpī˜ha). It is the ultimate purport of the Pure Six Thousand (verses vimalana˜ka) in the division beginning with `Kā' in the venerable scripture of twenty-four thousand (verses) (known as) the Svāminīmata of the Supreme Lord's command as uttered within the Tradition of the Mother (avvākrama).

sanskrit: श्रीवक्रा उवाच' त्रयस्त्रिंशानन्दः सुपरीक्षितशिष्यस्य कुलदीक्षां ब्रवीम्यहम् । योगदा भोगदा चैव दीक्षा च द्विविधा स्मृता ॥ १ ॥ परोक्षे योगदा प्रोक्ता प्रत्यक्षं भोगदा भवेत् । द्वावेतौ' संप्रवक्ष्यामि तव भक्त्या च भैरव ॥ २ ॥ हृदयं चलते ँ वेगादग्निज्वालामिवात्मनि । तालुरन्ध्रं व्रजत्याशुः स्फोटशब्द तदा भवेत् ॥ ३ ॥ तन्मनश्चञ्चलं विद्ध” मनो निश्चलतां व्रजेत् । दीपवत् दृश्यते” रौद्री हंसस्य गतिपूरणात् ।। ४ ॥ पश्यते तेन शक्ति६ उच्छालत्व प्रपद्यते । तत्त्वदृष्टि:“ समायाति त्रितीयं नयनं भवेत् ।। ५॥ •१९ निर्वाणस्य तदा प्राप्तिर्बिन्दुरूपं प्रपश्यति । अद्वैतपदसंप्राप्तिर्यदा निश्चलतां गतः ।। ६ ॥ २३ २४ द्वन्द्वत्याग” कालग्रन्थ्या” लोलीभूतं परे पदे । दृढलक्षाजडत्व च मातृचक्रपरिग्रही ।। ७ ।। भूतं चैव भविष्यं च वर्तमानं हितायते ।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-THREE Concerning the Initiation with Seed The venerable (goddess) Vakrā said: (Now) I will explain the Kula initiation of a well-tested disciple.1 Initiation is said to be of two kinds according to whether it bestows worldly benefits (bhogadā) or Yoga (yogadā). The one that bestows Yoga2 does so invisibly, while the one which bestows worldly benefits, does so visibly. O Bhairava, I will explain both of these out of devotion (to you). (1-2) The Initiation that bestows the Yoga of the Command The Heart moves within the Self due to the force (vega of Energy) as does a flame of a fire. (KuSÆalinī) moves quickly (up) to the cavity of the palate and then the sound of a powerful explosion (spho˜aśabda) occurs. (3) When that fickle (cañcala) mind is pierced, it becomes immobile (and) Raudrī is perceived (like the motionless flame of a) lamp by completing the movement of the Gander. (4) Thus one perceives Energy, which (thereby) moves upwards; a vision of reality arises and one (obtains) the third eye (of inner vision). (5) Then one attains NirvāSa and clearly sees the form of the (Supreme) Drop and (so) if (the mind) becomes motionless, one attains the plane of nonduality. (6) (Then one) abandons the duality of the Knot of Time and (everything) is merged together on the supreme plane (of existence). (One's) aim becomes firm and, (freed of) insentience, one lays hold of the Wheel of the Mothers. Past, present and future each do good (to such a one). (7-8ab)

sanskrit: 50 कुमारिकाखण्ड: जलधारा पतत्याशुनीडीसंकोचन तथा ।। ८ ।। अग्निप्रवेशमपरं समाधौ च प्रपश्यति । वेतालै: सह संवादमाशीवाद च श्रूयते ॥ ९ ॥ दिव्यज्ञानं प्रपश्येत” दिव्यकान्तिश्च जायते । ३६ ३७ एवं ते चतुराशीतिः अवस्थाः परिपाठतः ॥ १० ॥ ३९ यथा ह्येका तथा सर्वाः” चिन्हमेतत् कुलक्रमे । निर्दिष्ट शिष्यपुत्राणां तेषां ये मुक्तिभाजनाः ॥ ११ ॥ अवस्थाहीना” ये शिष्याः क्रमिक लङ्घयन्ति च । न ते मुक्तिमवाप्यन्ते कल्पकोटिशतैरपि ।। १२ ॥ बीजहीनान् विजानीयात्” तेषां नैवोद्भव क्वचित् । पुनर्दीक्षाहीनाः सर्वे मलक्षयविवर्जिताः ।। १३ ॥ २ ५३ तीव्राज्ञा शक्तिपातेन वेधाज्ञाया महेश्वर । अवस्थाज्ञा विना देव प्रत्यय नैव जायते ॥ १४ ॥ प्रत्ययेन विहीना ये पशवस्ते प्रकीर्तिताः । ५९ परोक्षवेध' देवेश अवस्था: संप्रवक्ष्यते ।। १५ ।। षडध्वकृतसंस्कारा अवस्थापरिवर्जिताः” । ६४ दीक्षितास्तेऽपि‍ पशवः कीर्तिताः ४ सिद्धशासने ।। १६ ।। ६७ परोक्षवेधविद्धाना अवस्थाः प्रभवन्ति हि । मलक्षय“ तदा जातं इत्याज्ञा पारमेश्वरी ॥ १७ ॥ योगदा कथिता दीक्षा आज्ञाया योजनाशतैः ।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-THREE 51 In deep contemplation (samādhi) he sees a fast falling waterfall, the contraction of the psychic channels and entry into fire. (8cd-9ab) (He) converses with ghosts (vetāla) and he hears (them) blessing him. He perceives sacred knowledge and divine beauty manifests (everywhere). Such are your eighty-four states enumerated completely.3 (9cd-10) Just as one is, so are they all. This is the sign taught in the Kulakrama of disciples who are (as close to the teacher as are his) sons and are (veritable) vessels of liberation. (11) Those disciples who possess none (of these) states and disobey (the teachings of) the transmission (kramika) do not achieve liberation even in countless millions of aeons. (12) Know that they have no seed (that can give rise to the liberated state) and they do not develop anywhere. None of them are initiated and their impurity (mala) has not been destroyed. (13) O Great Lord, an intensely powerful Command (is transmitted) by the grace (śaktipāta) of the Command that brings about the piercing (of the inner centres). O god, without the Command (that gives rise to) the states, no sign of attainment (pratyaya) arises. Those who are devoid (of any) sign of attainment are said to be fettered souls (paśu). (14-15ab) O lord of the gods, (now I) will explain the invisible (parokna) piercing4 and (its corresponding) states. Even those who have been initiated and purified the Six Paths (naÆadhvakrtasaˆskāra),5 but are devoid of the state (of attainment) are said to be fettered souls according to the teaching of the Siddhas (siddhaśāsana). (15cd-16) The states (of attainment) of those who have been pierced by the invisible piercing (paroknavedha) develop in strength.6 Then the destruction of impurity (malaknaya) takes place. This is the Supreme Goddess's Command. (Thus) the initiation of the Command that bestows Yoga (that can be performed) even at a great distance (yojanāśata)7 has been explained. (17-18ab)

sanskrit: 52 कुमारिकाखण्ड: तत्त्वदीक्षा षडध्वनि” तत्त्वमन्त्रपदात्मिका ॥ १८ ॥ वर्णभुवनसंयुक्ता रजकुण्डसमण्डला । अस्मिन् श्रीकुलसन्ताने” दीक्षा च द्विविधोदिता ॥ १९ ॥ तन्त्रकौलिकभेदेन होत्री वेधवतीति च । मन्त्रजापप्रसक्तानां होत्री सर्वत्र दर्शिता ।। २० ।। आज्ञापूर्वी” योगदा च° वेधदीक्षा सुदुर्लभा । स्वगुरोः पादुकाध्यानात् कम्पते देहपञ्जरम् ।। २१ ।। विधानं वेधदीक्षायां साम्प्रतं कथयाम्यहम् । ८३८४ वेधान् च' मानवे शिष्ये दीक्षाकाले प्रयोजयेत् ।। २२ ।। पुष्प शङ्खाभिषेक च तुलाप्रत्ययमेव ँ च । स्तोभनं पालन चैव दीक्षा पञ्चविधा स्मृता ॥ २३ ॥ o पुष्पैरञ्जलिमापूर्य स्वयमारुह्य मस्तके । मन्त्रशक्तिप्रभावेन” तदा पुष्पाभिषेचनम् ।। २४ । करस्थं” शङ्खपात्रं यत्” पुष्पाक्षतसमन्वितम्¨ । आरुहेत् क्रमशो मूर्ध्नि तदा शङ्खाभिषेचनम् ।। २५ । ९६ तुलया शोधितः शिष्यो दीक्षयेत् तदनन्तरम् । कर्मच्छेदात् ” लघुत्वं हि तुलाप्रत्ययः स्मृतः ।। २६ ।।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-THREE 53 Varieties of the Initiation by Piercing The Initiation by means of the Principles (tattvadīknā) (that takes place) on the Six Paths, consists of the Principles, mantra and the parts (of mantra) along with the letters and worlds and (involves the use of) coloured powders (rajas), a fire pit and maSÆala. (18cd-19ab) The initiation that takes place in this, the family (santāna) of the Śrīkula, is of two kinds, according to whether it is Tāntrika or Kaulika. (The former involves) sacrificial offerings to the fire (hotrī) and (the latter) is one that takes place by piercing (vedhavatī). The one requiring offerings to the fire is everywhere said to be for those who are engaged in the repetition of mantra. (The second type is) the initiation by piercing which bestows Yoga. It is heralded by the Command and is very hard to acquire. (In the course of this type of initiation) the cage of the body shakes by meditating on the teacher's sandals. (19cd-21) Now I will explain the method enjoined for the initiation by piercing. One should make use of the (various forms of) piercing in the course of initiation in the case of a disciple who is at the human (mānava) (level).8 The Flower and the Consecration of the Conch, the Sign of the Balance (tulāpratyaya), Paralysis (stobhana) and Protection (pālana) — initiation is said to be of five kinds. (22-23) The Consecration of the Flower The Consecration of the Flower takes place by the power of the energy of mantra when, having filled the folded hands with flowers, (the neophant) lifts them up by himself to (his own) head. (24) The Consecration of the Conch The Consecration of the Conch takes place when (the neophant) gradually lifts a conch bowl held in (his) hand, along with flowers and unbroken rice, to the head. (25) The Sign of the Balance The disciple who has been purified by the Scale should be initiated after that. The decrease in (his) weight that results from the elimination of Karma is said to be the Sign of the Balance (tulāpratyaya).9 (26)

sanskrit: 54 कुमारिकाखण्ड: लिखित्वा षड्दलं पद्मं बाह्यतो वज्रमण्डलम् । तन्मध्ये स्थापयेच्छिष्यं योगिनीद्रव्यसंयुतम् ।। २७ ।। संपूज्य योगिनीवृन्दं गन्धधूपस्रगादिभिः । अवलोकनात् तदा व्याप्तिः सर्वाङ्गेषु प्रकम्पनम् ॥ २८ ॥ १०८ विद्धः पतति निःसंज्ञो नात्र कार्या विचारणा । एवं दीक्षाविधिर्भाव्या पारम्पर्यक्रमागता ।। २९ ।। दीक्षा च त्रिविधा प्रोक्ता आणवा शाक्तशाम्भवा । प्रत्यक्षे आणवा प्रोक्ता शाक्ता या सा च पञ्चधा ।। ३० । षडध्वकृतसंस्कारा दीक्षा सा शाम्भवा स्मृता । ११५ येन केनापि मन्त्रेण पाशस्तोभोऽभिजायते ॥ ३१ ॥ कालान्तरगतातीता” आणवा संप्रकाशिता । ।। दर्शनात् स्पर्शनाच्चैव” वाचिका मानसी तथा ।। ३२ ।। एवं चतुःप्रकारा च आणवा सा विधीयते । १२० दण्डं कन्था पटं पात्रं इत्यादिस्पर्शनेन तु ॥ ३३ ॥ अङ्गस्य स्पर्शनाद् वापि स्पर्शवेधस्तदुच्यते । योजनानां शतैर्वापि पञ्चभिवी वरानन” ॥ ३४ ॥ दूरादपि क्रमेदाज्ञा त्रिशुद्धिर्भक्तिवत्सल१३ । तस्य शक्तिर्गुरोराज्ञा कारुण्याद् देवता भवेत् ।। ३५ ।। तदेव गुणसंप्राप्तिमनसीवेध उच्यते । ११३
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-THREE 55 (The teacher) should first draw a six petal lotus with a circle of thunderbolts (vajramaSÆala) outside (around) it. He should place the disciple in the middle of it along with the sacrificial substances (offered) to the Yoginīs. (27) Having worshipped the host of Yoginīs with scent, incense, garlands and the rest, then, by (the power of the teacher's) gaze (the disciple experiences) pervasion (vyāpti) and shaking in all the limbs of (his) body. (28) Pierced (by that divine power) he falls down unconscious. (This is certain), one need not reflect here (about this). One should understand this, the prescribed method of initiation transmitted through the succession (of teachers), in this way. (29) Three kinds of Initiation by Piercing Again, initiation is said to be of three kinds, namely, Individual (āSava), Empowered (śākta) and Śāmbhava.10 The one that takes place in a visible way is called Individual. The Empowered one is of five kinds. The initiation in which the Six Paths have been purified is said to be Śāmbhava. (30-31ab) The Individual (āSava) Initiation The Individual (initiation) is manifest when the fetters are paralysed by means of a mantra, whatever it may be. It is (both) within time and beyond it. The Individual (initiation) is of four kinds, namely, by seeing, by touching, verbal and mental.11 (31cd-33ab) Piercing by Touch (The initiation a teacher imparts) by touching (his disciple) with (his) staff (daSÆa), quilt (kanthā), cloth (pa˜a), (drinking) vessel or the like or else by touching a limb (of his body directly) is said to be piercing by touch. (33cd-34ab) Mental Piercing O handsome one! O beloved child of devotion! The triple purification (takes place) even if the Command traverses a distance of five hundred leagues. The power of one (initiated this way) is (his) teacher's Command that, out of compassion (for the disciple), is deity. This same attainment of (spiritual) qualities is called Mental Piercing.12 (34cd-36ab)

sanskrit: 56 56 १२८ कुमारिकाखण्ड: १३० मानसं वेधन “ शम्भो स्पर्शवेध” द्वितीयकम् ॥ ३६ ॥ दृष्टिवेध” तृतीयं तु दुर्गवेध” चतुर्थकम् । १३३ एवं चतुष्प्रकारा तु ज्ञानदीक्षा प्रतिष्ठिता ।। ३७ ।। अन्तजं दीक्षयेच्छिष्यं दृष्टिवेधः स उच्यते । एवमुक्ता महादीक्षा सद्यः प्रत्ययकारिका ॥ ३८ ॥ १३६ ज्ञानदीक्षाविधानेन शिष्यो लब्धगुवाज्ञो यः दीक्षोपकरण१७ सर्वमानयेद् गुरुसन्निधौ ।। ३९ । १३८ सुगन्धमक्षतं पुष्पं धूप दीपं चरुं तथा । १४० तथा । भक्ष भोज्यं तथा पानं वस्त्रादिसहिरण्यकम् ।। ४० ।। गजाश्ववाहनादीनि द्रव्योपकरणानि४३ च । कृत्वा संपूर्णत: सर्वं विनिवेद्य गुरोग्रतः ॥ ४१ ॥ पूजयेद् योगिनीवृन्दं कुमार्याश्चैव भक्तितः । कटकंकणवस्त्राद्यैर्दिव्यैराभरणैस्तथा ।। ४२ । गुरुपूर्वाणि सर्वाणि परिधाय¨¨ स्वशक्तितः । ततः पश्चाच्छरीर स्व४९ श्रीगुरुभ्यो निवेदयेत् ।। ४३ ।। अथवा वित्तहीनोऽसौ गुरो: ५५ क्लेशपरायण: ५२ । १५१ कृत्वा दण्डनमस्कार ५३ सर्वस्वं विनिवेदयेत् ॥ ४४ ॥ धनाढ्य“४ धनहीन वा त्रिशुद्धिर्भक्तिवत्सल““ । ज्ञात्वा परीक्ष्य आचार्य: ५७ कारुण्यादवलोकयेत् ॥ ४५ ॥ भवते दृष्टिविश्रामात् स विद्धः पतति क्षणात् । अकथ्यं ज्ञानसद्भाव स शीघ्रं समुदीरयेत् ॥ ४६ ॥
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-THREE 57 O Śambhu, Mental Piercing (is the first). The Piercing by Touch is the second. The Piercing by Sight is the third, while the Arduous (durga) Piercing is the fourth.13 In this way, the fourfold Initiation of Knowledge is well established. (36cd-37) Initiation by Sight If one initiates a disciple of the lowest caste, this is called Piercing by Sight. Such is said to be the great initiation that gives immediate realisation. (38) The Empowered (śākta) Initiation In accord with the prescribed method for the Initiation of Knowledge, the disciple who has received the teacher's Command should bring all the offerings for initiation close to the teacher. (These include) fragrant unbroken rice, flowers, incense, a lamp, the sacrificial pap, food and drink, clothes and the like along with gold, elephants, horses and other vehicles as well as offerings of the sacrificial substances. (39-41ab) Having done that and offered everything completely before the teacher, (the neophant) should worship devoutly the troupe of Yoginīs and virgin girls14 with divine ornaments, bangles, gold, clothes and the rest. (41cd-42) Dressing (them with these things), as far as he can, on all the days sacred to the teacher, he should then offer his own body to the venerable teacher. (43) Or else, (the neophant) who seeks refuge from (his) aflictions (kleśaparāyaSa) (but) has no (great) wealth, should, after he has made a full prostration before the teacher, offer (him) all he possesses. (44) The Arduous Initiation by the Gaze O beloved child of devotion, once the teacher has known and tested (the disciple, irrespective of whether) he is rich or poor, (the teacher) should gaze upon him out of compassion. And so, by resting (his) gaze (upon him, the disciple receives) the triple purification and, pierced, he falls (to the ground) in a moment.15 Rapidly, (the teacher) should utter the essence of knowledge which should (otherwise) not be spoken. (45-46)

sanskrit: 58 कुमारिकाखण्ड: आनन्दमुद्भवः॰ कम्पो‍ निद्रा घूर्मिस्तु ६२ पञ्चमी' ६३ । तत्त्वविद्धस्य शिष्यस्य पञ्चावस्था प्रपद्यते ॥ ४७ ॥ भूमित्याग पुरक्षोभ मुद्रावेधास्त्वनेकधा । दूराच्छ्रवणविज्ञान कौलभाषाप्रवर्तनम् ।। ४८ ॥ सर्वमन्त्रमनोन्मादो गीतं च हसितं तथा । •१७० । नृत्यं च वलन चाद्यं स्वेच्छया संप्रवर्तते ॥ ४९ ॥ पूर्वोक्ता हि गुणा: सर्वे उत्पद्यन्ते न संशयः । १७७ तद्विश्रामात् सहस्रं तु तल्लीने लक्षमेव च ॥ ५० ॥ १७९ तस्मिनेव लयातीते तीव्राज्ञायाः प्रभावतः । प्राप्नोति परमं स्थानं जरामरणवर्जितम् ।। ५१ ।। एवं दीक्षाविधानं तु त्रिविधं योगनायक । मानवः स्मरणाच्चैव तृतीयश्चावलोकनात् ॥ ५२ ॥ एवं सा विविधा दीक्षा पञ्चावस्थाप्रपादिका । १८१ श्रीभैरव उवाच १८२ १८५ अद्य मे सफलं जन्म येन ८३ त्व१४ वरदा मम ॥ ५३ ॥ १८६ १८७ योगदीक्षा मया ज्ञाता सद्यः प्रत्ययकारिका' । षडध्ववर्जिता या सा ज्ञाता मे त्वत्प्रसादतः ।। ५४ ।। १८९ किन्तु पृच्छाम्यहं देवि तत्त्वाम्नायकमागतम् । षडध्वदीक्षाभेदं च ब्रूहि मे परमार्थतः ।। ५५ ।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-THREE 59 The Five Signs of Attainment of the Empowered Initiation The disciple who has been pierced by the (Supreme) Principle (experiences) the fivefold state. This is joy (ānanda), an upward movement (udbhava), a tremor (kampa), sleep (nidrā) and vibration (ghūrSi) as the fifth.16 (47) (The initiate acquires the power to) quit the ground (bhumityāga), agitate (and sexually arose) the citadel (of any woman's body) (puraknobha). (He has the power to) pierce by making a gesture,17 which is of many kinds, and (possesses) the knowledge of how to hear from a great distance. (He) starts (to speak spontaneously in) Kaula language (kaulabhānāpravartana).18 (Divine) madness (is induced) by every mantra. Song, laughter, dance, rolling around and the like come about spontaneously.19 (48-49) The Śāmbhava Initiation All the aforementioned yogic powers (guSa) certainly come about (within the disciple). By his resting a thousand and when merged in that, one hundred thousand times. In that very (condition) beyond merger (layātīta),20 he attains the supreme place, free of old age and death, by the power of the intense (form of the) Command. (50-51) O master of Yoga, such is the threefold method of initiation, namely, the human one, (the initiation) by recollection and the third by the gaze (of the teacher). Such is the initiation which is of many kinds and gives rise to the five states.21 (52-53ab) Initiation by Means of the Six Paths The venerable (god) Bhairava said: Today my birth has born fruit for you have given me a (great) gift. I have understood the initiation by Yoga that gives immediate realisation. By your grace I have come to know the (form of initiation) devoid of the Six Paths. (53cd-54) Even so, O goddess, (the question) I am (now) asking (you concerns) the form of initiation by means of the Six Paths which is a part of the tradition concerning (the ultimate) Principle that has come down (through the line of teachers). Tell me (this) as it truly is.22 (55)

sanskrit: 60 श्रीवक्रा उवाच कुमारिकाखण्ड: शृणु नाथ प्रवक्ष्यामि यत् त्वया परिपृच्छितम् १९३ १९० तत् सर्व” निपुन? देव तथ्येन मुनिनायक ॥। ५६ ।। षडध्वसंस्कृता दीक्षा योगदा तत्त्वविस्तरात् । विद्यमाना कुलाम्नाये तत्र तेऽद्य ब्रवीम्यहम् ॥ ५७ ॥ आदौ परीक्षयेद् भूमि वास्तुविद्याविशारदः । खानयेत् सप्तहस्तानि“ पुनः खातं प्रपूरयेत् ॥ ५८ ॥ पांसुरभ्यधिका यत्र सा भूमिः सर्वकामदा । २०० २०४ शोधयेत् तां प्रयत्नेन तुषशल्यविवर्जिताम् ।। ५९ ।। कण्टकाङ्गारकेशाद्यैः २०६ कारयेत् तां ँ प्रयत्नतः २०९ २०८ मध्याज्य ९ च तथा क्षीरं तक्रं पञ्चद्रुमत्वचा त्रिफला बीजवृक्षस्य”३ सारं ४ चैव एतैस्तु उदक१५ कृत्वा सिञ्चयेत् तां २१२ तु खादिरम् । पुनः पुनः ईशान्यां तु प्रकर्तव्य मण्डलं सर्वकामदम् तच्च पूर्वक्रमेणैव मूलसूत्रेण कथ्यते ।। ६२ ।। २२१ २२० । ।। ६० ।। २१७ ।। ६१ ।। । अष्टम्यां वाथ भूताख्या पौर्णमास्याथ सप्तमी । दशमी नवमी वाथ तृतीया द्वादशी भवेत् ॥ ६३ ॥ २२४ कृष्णपक्षेऽथ शुक्ले वा कारयेन्मण्डलं शुभम् । ग्रीष्मे वाथ वसन्ते वा शिशिरे शरदेऽपि वा २२५ ॥ ६४ ॥ २२७ २२८ उपसन्ना५ महावीरा भक्तिवन्त: शुचिव्रताः । २२९ २३० २३१ परीक्षा यै: समुत्तीणी यथा शास्त्रे निदर्शिता ।। ६५ ।। शूद्रो द्वादशभिर्वर्षैर्वेश्यो ४ नवभिरेव च । २३६ २३९ क्षत्रियः ३५ षड्भिरब्दैश्च ब्राह्मणस्तु तदर्धतः ।। ६६ ।। परीक्षेद्३७ विपरीतेन कर्मणा कथयाम्यहम् । अधमश्चोत्तमे २४० कर्मे २४१ उत्तमोऽधमकर्मणि २४२ ।। ६७ ।।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-THREE 61 The venerable (goddess) Vakrā said: Listen, O lord, I will tell (you) truly and well all that you have asked about, O god, leader of the sages. The initiation that has been purified through the Six Paths bestows Yoga by virtue of the extension of the Principles (of existence). It is a part of the Kula tradition. Today I will tell you about it. (56-57) The Construction of the Pavilion for the Śrīyāga First of all (the teacher) who is well versed in architecture (vāstuvidyā) should examine the ground. He should dig (to a depth of) seven hand spans and then fill (the hole he has) dug. The ground which gives all that one desires is one where the soil is greater (than the hole). (58-59ab) It should be cleaned with effort and made free of thorns and chaff, embers, hair and the like. It should (then) be sprinkled repeatedly with water (mixed) with wine, clarified butter, milk, buttermilk, the skins of five trees, the three myrobalans, the sap of a citron tree, and khadira wood. (59cd-61) (Then), in the north-east quarter, one should fashion a maSÆala that fulfils all desires as explained in the Root Sūtra in accord with the previous procedure (krama).23 (62) One should cause the auspicious maSÆala to be fashioned on the eighth (lunar) day, on the fourteenth (bhūtākhyā),24 the full moon, the seventh, the tenth, the ninth, the third or the twelth (day) in either the dark or the bright (lunar) fortnight. (It may be done) in the summer, spring, winter or autumn. Great heroes (should be present) who possess devotion and whose vows are pure along with those who have passed the test as prescribed in the scripture. (63-65) The Selection of the Disciples A śūdra should be tested for twelve years, a veśya for nine, a knatriya for six and a brahmin for half that (time). (The teacher) should test (them) by (engaging them in) work that is contrary (to the one appropriate to their caste status in the manner) I am (about to) explain. The lowest (should do) the highest work and a (member of) the highest (caste should be made to do) the lowest work. (66-67)

sanskrit: 62 २४४ कुमारिकाखण्ड: २४५ एवं नानाप्रकारैस्तु सुपरीक्ष्याः प्रयत्नतः । २४६ २४७ परीक्षायाः समुत्तीणी: समुत्तीणीः सुयोग्याश्च सुयोग्याश्च सुशासिताः तेषामनुग्रहः५° कार्यो यथायोग्य “ फलस्य तु । २४९ २५४ ।। ६८ ।। विलोमान्५२ वर्जयेद् यत्नान्न'३ ते चान्वयभाजनाः ॥ ६९ ॥ नायोगिनीकुले जाता दीक्षां२५५ विन्दन्ति २५६ शासने २६० २५७ । कुशिष्यान् २५८ यदि५९ लोभेन मोहाद् वा यदि दीक्षयेत् ।। ७० ।। उभयोरचिराद्११ विघ्नं जायते नात्र संशयः । एवं ज्ञात्वा महामन्त्री उपसन्नो ३ महाधीमान् ४ ।। ७१ ।। आज्ञापयेत् तदाचार्यो द्रव्यसंभारसंभृतिम् । २६५ २६६ क्रियतामविकल्पेन ततः पूज्या कुमारिका ।। ७२ ।। २६७ पूजयेत् तत्र देवेशं महाश्रीयागमण्डपे । लोकपालैः समायुक्तं द्वारपालैः समन्वितम् ।। ७३ ।। २६८ चूतपल्लवसंच्छन्नं स्रगमालावलम्बितम्९ । कलशाष्टक२७० दिग्विदिक्ष्वीशान्यां कुलकुम्भकः •२७३ अस्त्रवर्धनिसंयुक्तं पुष्पमालासुपूजितम् । पूजयेत् तत्र देवेशं नवात्मानन्दभैरवम् ।। ७५ ।। २७५ २७२ । कुण्ड४ तु कारयेद् देव विधिविस्तरशोधितम् ५ । हस्तमात्रमधः खातं त्र्यश्रं चैव त्रिमेखलम् ।। ७६ ।। २७६ एवं कृत्वा तु देवेश पश्चाद् यजनमारभेत् । आदौ तु मण्डले पूजां कारयेत् सुसमाहितः २७८ २७९ २७७ पूजयेद् देवदेवेश नवात्मानं महाद्युतिम् । ।। ७४ ।। ।। ७७ ।। तस्योत्संगगता देवी परा चैकाक्षरा भवेत् ।। ७८ ।।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-THREE 63 They should be streneously tested in many such ways. Those who have passed the test and are well fit and instructed should be given, as is appropriate, the grace of the fruit (of their efforts). (68-69ab) One should carefully avoid those who (behave in a manner) contrary (to their caste norms) (viloma). They do not possess the tradition. Those who are not born into the Yoginīkula do not get initiation into the teaching. If one initiates bad disciples out of greed or delusion, both (the teacher and the taught) are certainly very soon afflicted with troubles. (69cd-71ab) The Śrīyāga Then, once the very wise teacher and great reciter of mantra, has know (his disciples) in this way and is present (there), he should order that the sacrificial substances and (other) requisites for the rite (be brought). He should do this without a thought. Then a virgin girl25 should be worshipped. The lord of the gods, along with the guardians of the quarters and the doors, should be worshipped there in the pavilion of the great Śrīyāga (the Venerable Sacrifice). (71cd-73) A group of eight jars, covered with mangoe leaves and bedecked with garlands (should be placed and worshipped) in the primary and secondry directions with the Kula jar in the north-east.26 (74) There, one should worship the lord of the gods, that is, Navātman Ānandabhairava.27 He is associated with the jar of the weapon (astravardhani)28 and is properly worshipped with garlands of flowers. (75) O god, one should cause the construction of a fire pit purified in accord with the prescribed procedure. (It should be) dug only (to a depth of) a single handspan. (Its shape should be) triangular and (it should have) three (round encompassing) girdles (mekhala). (76) O lord of the gods, once one has done this, one should commence the sacrifice. The well attentive (priest) should first cause the rite of adoration (pūjā) to be performed within the maSÆala. (77) He should worship the Lord who is the God of the gods, Navātman of great lustre and the goddess Parā, the One-syllable (Vidyā), should be next to him.29 (78)

sanskrit: 64 २८३ कुमारिकाखण्ड: २८४ पद्महस्ता महाकाया शान्तरूपा वरप्रदा । पिबन्तीं मदिरां दिव्यां५ विहसन्तीं मदोत्कटाम् ।। ७९ ।। तथा मातृगतां बाह्ये यथोक्तं संप्रपूजयेत् । २८८ २८९ नैवेद्यं द्विविधं दद्यात् सुरासवसमन्वितम् ॥ ८० ॥ ९० ॥ एवं पूजा प्रकर्तव्या क्रम संपूज्य भक्तित: ९२ । पूर्व यत् सूचितं तुभ्यं दिव्यसंभारसंभृतम् ।। ८१ ।। तथा संपूज्य देवेशं विज्ञायेत्” परमेश्वरम् । अच्छिद्रं कुरुते नाथ अस्मिन् श्रीयागमण्डपे १९७ २९८ तथा संसिद्धिदं देव” भवते त्वत्प्रसादतः ३०० । ॥ ८२ ॥ गत्वा चाग्निसमीपे तु यथानुक्रमयोगतः ।। ८३ ॥ गर्भीधानादिकं कर्म शिवान्तं यावदेव हि ४ । कर्तव्यमविचारेण आहुतिं पञ्चपञ्चभिः ३०७ ३०८ ।। ८४ ।। । हुत्वा चैव ततः पश्चात् पूजनं पूर्ववत् कुरु तर्पयेन्मण्डलान्तःस्थं द्वात्रिंशाक्षरविद्यया ।। ८५ ।। ३११ स्थण्डिलस्थं वरारोह आत्मस्थं च विशेषत: ३१३ । कर्तव्या विधिवत् पूजा सदा एकान्तसत्क्रिया ।। ८६ ।। बलिं च वटुकं देव क्षेत्रपालादि योगिनीम् ३१८ ३१७ । दत्वा निवेद्य संकल्प्य विद्यापीठे क्रमस्य च ।। ८७ ।। ततः प्रवेशयेच्छिष्यं”” पुष्पहस्तं सुयन्त्रितम् । । देवस्य पश्चिमे भागे पुष्पं मुञ्चापयेत्” ततः ।। ८८ ।। प्रणिपत्य महादेव २ गच्छेत्” कुण्डसमीपतः षडध्वं • ३२५ ३२४ । मनसा ध्यात्वा शरीरे विनिवेशयेत् ।। ८९ ।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-THREE 65 Her body is large and she holds a lotus. Her form is tranquil and she bestows boons. She drinks divine wine and, inebriated, she laughs.30 (79) She should be worshipped, in the manner explained (previously) outside (the maSÆala) in the midst of the Mothers.31 Two kinds of food offering should be made (to them, one) with wine (surā) and (the other) with liquor (āsava).32 (80) Having worshipped the Krama with devotion, one should perform the rite of adoration in this way.33 (One should offer), in the manner previously indicated to you, the divine requisites of worship. (81) Once worshipped the Lord of the gods in this way, one should address the Supreme Lord (thus): “O Lord, in this pavilion of the Venerable Sacrifice (śrīyāga), (the Lord) makes one free of defects (acchidra). O god, in the same way by your grace, (may the sacrifice) bestow complete success (saˆsiddhi).”34 (82-83ab) Having approached close to the fire, one should perform, without (unnecessary) reflection, (all the) rites (of the life cycle) beginning with impregnation and ending with (the funerary rite that conjoins with) Śiva, in due order. (83cd-84c) Then after having made twenty-five offerings to the fire perform the rite of adoration as before. One should offer libation to (the deity) residing in the maSÆala with the Thirty-two syllable Vidyā.35 (84d-85) O fair hipped one, (one should also offer libation to the deity) in the sacrificial area (sthaSÆila) and, in particular, to the one in the Self. One should always perform the rite of adoration according to the prescribed method, in a solitary place and correctly.36 (86) Entry into the Pavilion Having offered animal sacrifice37 to the god Va˜uka, the guardians of the field and the rest and the Yoginī and made food offerings to the Krama in the Sacred Seat of Knowledge (vidyāpī˜ha)38 and determined (in his mind his purpose),39 (the teacher) should cause the well disciplined disciple to enter with flowers in his hand. Then he should cause him to release the flowers (from his hands) to the west of the god. Having prostrated before the Great God, he should go near the the fire pit and, having mentally meditated on the Six Paths, he should introduce them into the body. (87-89)

sanskrit: 66 कुमारिकाखण्ड: तर्पणं २७ सन्निधानार्थं २८ आदिक्षान्तस्य सुव्रत । ३३२ ३३३ चरुक” प्राशयेन्मन्त्री क्षीरेणामृतवत् सदा ॥ ९० ॥ ३३६ श्यामाकन्दलैर्देव शालिना वा ५ प्रियंगुभिः । मसुराश्च यवा देव तथा गोधूमव्रीहिभिः ।। ९१ ॥ सौवर्णे३३७ रौप्यताम्रे ३८ वा अथवा मृन्मयेऽपि वा ३४० ३३९ । पात्रे च निर्व्रणे स्निग्धे बालबालुकवर्जिते ।। ९२ ।।३ ३४४ अस्त्रेण शोधयित्वा तु ज्वालयेन्मूलविद्यया । ३४८ ३५० शिवाग्नौ४६ चोल्मुकं ३४७ गृह्य बहिरन्ते ४९ तु दीपयेत् ॥ ९३ ॥ ५२ ३५७ स्थापयेत्३५३ तत्र५४ चाग्नौ५५ तु कृतरक्ष: ३५६ प्रसन्नधी: । घृतादिना ५८ ततः स्थालीं कृत्वा क्षीरपरिप्लुताम् ।। ९४ ।। ३६० स्थापयेद् वह्निमध्ये तु यथा सा निश्चला भवेत् । •३६२ ३६३ चालन मूलमन्त्रेण द्वात्रिंशाक्षरविद्यया ॥ ९५ ॥ सितासितपिधान तु कर्तव्यं मूलविद्यया । ३६७ प्रोक्षणं चालन ५ चैव कर्तव्यं सततं बुधैः ।। ९६ ।। ३६९ सिद्धपात्रं५८ स्थितं कृत्वा दशभागानि कारयेत् । ३७३ प्रथमं स्थण्डिले देयं द्वितीयमुत्तरे दिशि ॥ ९७ ॥ तृतीयं चैव७४ आग्नेयं चतुर्थमात्मनस्य तु । ३७७ ३७८ ३७५ •३७९ ३८० नैवेद्यं तु त्रिभि: स्थानैः बलि दत्वा तु बाह्यतः ।। ९८ ।। पालानां तु मातराणां८२ तु क्षेत्रभूतप्रपालकान् ३ । ३८४ एवं संतर्पयित्वा तु पश्चादाचमनं कुरु ।। ९९ ॥ ३८६ प्रणिपत्य८५ ३८५ ततो देवं स्तुत्वा चैव समासतः ३८९ ३८७ । दन्तकाष्ठं ततो दद्यात् सक्षीरं ग्रन्थिवर्जितम् ॥ १०० ॥
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-THREE 67 O (observer of) good vows, libation (is offered to the deity of the letters) from A to K±a in order to invoke the presence (of the deity) (sannidhānārtha). The reciter of mantra should always eat the sacrificial pap with milk (as he would) nectar. (90) O god, (he should offer) red lentils and barley, along with dark blue Kandala flowers, the Priya‰gu creeper, wheat and rice, both cultivated and wild, in an unbroken and beautiful vessel without hair or dust, made of gold, silver or earth. (91-92) Once purified with the Weapon, it should be set alight with the Root Vidyā. Laying hold of a firebrand in Śiva's fire, one should light up (everything) inside and outside. (93) Libations and Food Offerings The man of contented intellect who has performed (the rites) of protection should place it there in the fire once the caldron has been flooded with milk, clarified butter and the like. (The vessel) should be placed in the middle of the fire in such a way that it does not move. It is stirred (cālana) (inwardly) with the Root mantra, namely, the Vidyā of Thirty-two Syllables.40 One should fashion a white and black cover with the Root Vidyā. The wise should constantly sprinkle (proknaSa) and stir it (cālana) (it). (94-96) Once the Vessel of the Siddhas has been prepared, (the contents) should be divided into ten parts. The first (part) should be given to the sacrificial area. The second (is offered) in the northern quarter,41 the third is (for the south-east which is) fire’s (quarter) and the fourth belongs to the Self. (97-98ab) A food offering is made to the three places and then (the remaining parts are) offered outside as bali to the protectors, the Mothers and the protectors of the fields and ghosts (bhūta).42 After having offered the libations, (the officiant) should rinse (his) mouth. (99) The Stick for the Teeth Then, having prostrated before the god and praised him briefly, one should offer, along with milk, a stick to brush the teeth without knots. (100)

sanskrit: 68 कुमारिकाखण्ड: तालमेकायत” कार्य ऋजुः ९२ स्निग्धं सुशोभनम् । चूतमर्जुनवृक्षोत्थमश्वत्थमथापि वा ॥ १०१ ॥ ३९६ अथाश्वत्थादिकं देव उक्तं पुष्पादिसंहितम् । दद्यान्मन्त्राणि९७ मन्त्रित्वा सर्वकामफलप्रदः ।। १०२ ।। •३९९ ४०० ४०३ पात तस्य ं विलक्ष्येत” शोभनं वाप्यशोभनम् ' वारुण्यां४ भवते श्रेष्ठं सन्मुखश्चोत्तम ४०७ ४०८ उत्तरा सा ँ शुभा“ विद्याद्” ईशान्यां ४१२ भवेत् ॥ १०३ ॥ च तथोत्तमम् । अन्येषु तु महादेव दिशेषु च विलोमतः ॥ १०४ ॥ लक्षयेत” प्रयत्नेन आचार्यः सुसमाहितः । शुभे सिद्धिमवाप्नोति अशुभ होममाचरेत् ।। १०५ ॥ ४१५ संस्वयेन्द्र४ जनीं तौ” तु सखायैः सहितः स्थितः । स्वप्नमानवकं६ तेषां शिष्याणां प्रतिपादयेत् ।। १०६ ॥ प्रत्युषे विमले गत्वा सन्ध्योपासनपूर्वकम् । ४२० •४२४ ४२१ ४२५ देवान् पितॄन्”” नमस्कृत्वा आगत्य गुरुसन्निधौ ॥ १०७ ॥ स्वप्नं४२२ प्रकाशयेच्छिष्य: ४२३ शुभ ४ वा यदि वाशुभम् । शुभे२६ सिद्धिमवाप्नोति अशुभे होममाचरेत् ॥ १०८ ॥ एवं कृते”” भवेत्” सिद्धिर्विघ्नोपशमनं भवेत् । ४२९ ४३३ ।। पिष्ठगोवलकान्”” कृत्वा श्रीवराश्रयने प्रिय ॥ १०९ ॥ उन्मत्तपत्रबिल्वाद्यैराहवेत्” तत्” प्रयत्नतः । ४३७ ४३८ करणीं४३६ गृह्य कपीसीकसमुद्भवम् ।। ११० ।। खटिकां” ग्राहयेत्” शुद्धां शुक्लां चैव समाहरेत् ।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-THREE 69 It should be made the length of the palm (of the hand) and be pleasing and beautiful. (It may be) made of mango, Arjuna or Aśvattha wood. O god, the Aśvattha and all else that has been mentioned along with flowers and the rest should be offered once the mantras have been intoned. (In this way the rite) gives the fruits of all (one's) desire. (101-102) (The disciple throws the stick. The teacher) should observe (where) it falls (to see) whether (the direction in which it falls) is auspicious or otherwise. The most excellent is in (the west), VaruSa's direction. In front of one's self it is (also) excellent. The north should be known to be auspicious and it is also excellent (if it falls) in the north-east. O Great God, in the other directions it is otherwise. (103-104) The well attentive teacher should careful observe (all this). If (the direction is) auspicious, he attains success; if inauspicious, he should make a fire offering. (105) ******* (?) along with his companions ****** he should give (an effigy of) the ‘little man of sleep’ (svapnamānavaka) to those disciples.43 (106) Prognostication of the Disciple’s Dreams Having first performed the morning rite (sandhyopasana) and gone (to the sacrificial area) at dawn when the sky is clear, saluted the gods and ancestors, and come close to the teacher, the disciple should tell (him his) dream, whether it is auspicious or not. If auspicious, he attains success, if inauspicious, he should make a fire offering. When this has been done there is success and the impediments are stilled. O dear one, once one has fashioned crushed govalakas (?) in the abode of the most excellent splendour (śrīvara) (?) one should, with effort, make a fire offering with thron-apple leaves, bilva and the rest. (107-110ab) The Drawing of the MaSÆala Having first taken a barbed arrow, knife and (a thread) made of cotton, one should take a piece of pure, white chalk and draw it towards oneself. (110cd-111ab)

sanskrit: 70 •४४३ कुमारिकाखण्ड: ब्रह्मस्थानगतं? सूत्र३ स्थापयेत् पूर्वतो दिशि दक्षिणाच्च तथा देव सूत्रपातं विशिष्यते । ४४९ ४४७ । ४४५ उत्तरांशे तु योगेन साधयेत्” तत् प्रयत्नतः ४५३ ४५१ ।। १११ ।। ।। ११२ ।। -४५५ चतुर्भीगान् ततः कल्प्य ४ पूर्वसूत्रे समाश्रितान् । •४५६ चतुर्थं यद् भवेद् भागं तेन मत्स्यद्वय ५६ भवेत् ॥। ११३ ।। ४६० साधयेद् दिग्दिशाष्टौ च५९ पूर्वपश्चिमपातनात् । दक्षिणोत्तरमेव४६१ स्यात् पश्चात् कोणान् तु साधयेत् ।। ११४ ।। •४६६ आग्नेयां नैर्ऋतिं४ तावद्५ वायव्यान्तां यथाक्रमम् । एवं तु साधिते क्षेत्रे साधयेच्चतुरश्रकम् ।। ११५ ।। •४६९ चतुरश्रीकृते क्षेत्रे पश्चात् पद्मं“” प्रकल्पयेत् । चतुर्विंशांगुलायातमालिखेत् पद्ममुत्तमम् ।। ११६ ॥ ४७१ अष्टपत्र७२ सम४३ कार्यं कर्णिकाकेसरोज्ज्वलम् ४७६ ४७४ ।। । प्रथमे कर्णिकाभाग: ४७५ केसराणि द्वितीयके ।। ११७ ।। ४७७ त्रितीये दलसन्धीनि दलाग्राणि चतुर्थ । प्रतिवारणरेखां तु दद्यात् पद्मस्य बाह्यतः ।। ११८ ॥ पत्रक बाह्यतो देयं चतुरंगुलमानतः ४८० । तेषां तु बाह्यतो वीथीं हस्तमात्रप्रमाणतः पद्ममानं स्मृतं द्वारं तदर्धेन अथापि वा ४८७ ४८४ ।। ११९ ॥ । एवं वै सूत्रयित्वा तु रजांसि विनिपातयेत् ।। १२० ॥ ४८९ ४९३ रक्ताः पीतास्तथा” तथा शुक्ला: ४९ कृष्णास्ते समुदाहृताः समा रेखा ९४ प्रकर्तव्या अव्युच्छिन्ना सुशोभना ।। १२१ ।। •४९८ रेखानामन्तरं योग“ यवमात्रं प्रकल्पयेत्” । कर्णिका पीतिका कार्या पुष्कर रक्तवर्णकम् ॥ १२२ ॥ ।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-THREE 71 The thread is in Brahmā's abode One should place it in the eastern direction. O god, the placing of the thread from the southern direction is especially important. Accomplish that in the northern part with effort by the conjunction (of the threads).44 (111cd-112) Then having made four parts in the thread in the east, two fish are formed from the fourth part. (113) One should form the eight quarters by (first) measuring out the (direction) from east to west. It should be the same in the south and north. After that one should form the corners. (114) (Finally), (one should form the intermediate quarters) in due order (beginning with) the south-east and south-west up to the north-west in the end. Once the field has been formed in this way, one should make a square (around it). (115) The Drawing of the Lotus Then, when the square field has been made, one should fashion a lotus. One should draw an excellent lotus twenty-four fingers in breadth. (116) (The lotus has) eight petals that should (all be) made the same (size). It is brilliant with (its) calyx and stamens. The calyx is the part (of the lotus) in the first (section), the stamens in the second, the conjunctions of the petals in the third, and the tips of the petals in the fourth. A line that wards off (evil influences) should be placed outside (around) the lotus. (117-118) A leaf should be made outside (the lotus), measuring four fingers. Outside (all of) these, one should fashion an enclosure (vīthī) measuring just one handspan. (119) The door (on each side of the square) is said to be the same size as the lotus or it may be half (the size). Having first marked it out with the thread in this way, one should then spread (coloured) powders (along the lines). (120) (The lines) are said to be red, yellow, white and black. (Each) line should be straight, unbroken and beautiful. (121) The junction between the lines should be made the size of a grain of wheat. The calyx should be yellow and the lake,45 red. (122)

sanskrit: 72 कुमारिकाखण्ड: ५०४ केसरा०३ रक्तपीताढ्याः ४ शुक्लाञ्चैव तु कारयेत् । ५०६ ५०७ ५०८ ५०९ ५१० दला: शुक्ला: प्रकर्तव्याः सर्वतः समलंकृताः ॥ १२३ ॥ ५१२ संक्षेपेण वरारोह ? विधियुक्तस्तु साधकः । ५१३ -५१४ अस्मिन् युक्तो महादेव न भूयो जन्ममाप्नुयात् ।। १२४ ।। •५१६ तावद् भ्रमति संसारे यावत् तत्त्व न विन्दति । एकीभावगते चित्ते न बद्धो न च मुच्यते ॥। १२५ ।। ५१९ वणीध्वान समासेन कथयामि शृणुष्व तत् । ५२१ सर्वसंहारकर्तीर° स्वखपादतले बुधः ।। १२६ ।। ५२२ अर्चयेद् भैरवं देवं व्योमचक्रे यथास्थितम् । ५२३ गन्धैः पुष्पैश्च नैवेदैः सुधूपैश्चापरैः शुभैः ।। १२७ ॥ पूजयित्वा प्रयत्नेन पश्चाच्छिष्यमाषेचयेत् । अङ्गन्यासविधानेन स्तोभयेत् तावत् तत्त्ववित् ।। १२८ ॥ क्षकारादि—अकारान्त“ ” शब्दराशि २८ प्रयोक्तव्यम् ५२९ । क्षकार ३० विग्रह ३१ ज्ञेयं तत्त्वन्यासस्य अध्वनि' ५३२ ।। १२९ ।। ५३३ उक्तोऽयं मातृकान्यासः संहारतत्त्वसंपुट: । ५३६ ५३७ तत्त्वध्याते ३५ च विन्यस्ते ततो दीक्षा शुभप्रदा ।। १३० ।। यथात्मनि तथा शिष्ये योजयेत् तत्त्वमातृकाम् । पाशस्तोभं ततः कृत्वा कलायोगेन योगवित् ।। १३१ ।। सन्मुखं योजयित्वा तु ततः शिष्यं तु वेधयेत् ।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-THREE 73 One should make the stamens red, yellow and white. The petals (should be) white and adorned in every way. (123) In brief, O handsome one, the adept intent on (following) the prescribed method (should do all this). O Great God, he who is engaged in this (work) is not reborn gain. (124) He wanders in the world of transmigratory existence until he attains the (Supreme) Principle (of existence). When the mind is solely intent on God, he is neither bound nor (needs to be) freed. (125) Initiation by Means of the Letters I will now briefly tell (you about) the Path of the Letters.46 Listen to that. (126ab) The wise man should worship the god Bhairava, who brings about universal destruction, as he is in the Wheel of Space (vyomacakra) on the plane of his own Emptiness (svakhapādatala).47 (126cd-127ab) After he has worshipped him with effort with perfumes, flowers, food offerings, fine (varieties of) incense and other auspicious things, he should consecrate the disciple. The knower of reality should thus paralyse (the disciple’s fetters) by depositing (the letters) on (his) limbs. (127cd-128) One should apply the Assembly of Sounds (śabdarāśi) (in the reverse order) beginning with the letter K±a and ending with the letter A. One should know that the letter K±a is the one that separates (vigraha) (the series of letters)48 on the path of the deposition of the Principles. (129) The deposition of the letters (mātrkā), encapsulated by the principle of withdrawal (K±a), has been explained. Once the Principles have been visualized and deposited (in the body), then initiation bestows auspicious (results). (130) (The teacher) should conjoin the sonic energy of the principles (tattvamātrkā) within the disciple as he does within himself. Then, once the knower of Yoga has paralysed the fetters (of the disciple) by conjoining the energies (kalāyoga) (to his body) and caused the disciple to face him, he should pierce him (with the energy of the Command). (131-132ab)

english: CHAPTER THIRTY-THREE 75 Initiation by Means of the Thirty-six Principles Śrīnātha said: (This), the Initiation by the Letters (varSadīknā), is the supreme essence (of the teachings) that can free from transmigratory existence. Now I want to hear about the Initiation by the Principles (tattvadīknā) as it truly is. (132cd-133ab) The venerable (goddess) Vakrā said: Listen, O long eyed one, I will tell (you) about the Initiation by the Principles (tattvadīknā).49 (133cd) Earth, water, fire (tejas), air and space - O handsome one, one should purify the (reality) consisting of six parts (na˜prakāra)50 with these purified (Elements). 51 (134) Thus, there are said to be (five) organs of action and five organs of knowledge. One should know that there are (also) five subtle elements (tanmātra). Now follows the characterization (of these principles). (135) Sound, touch, taste, form and smell. (This) is the pentad of the subtle elements. The group of five senses (consists of) the ear, skin, eyes, tongue and nose. (136) The (names of the) sense organs of knowledge have been stated. Listen to (the next) group of five. Speech, hands and feet, the genitals and the anus as the fifth. O three eyed one, you have been told this, the pentad of action. (137-138ab) The mind, intellect and ego up to Nature (prakrti), in due order; sattva, rajas and tamas that arise as the qualities of Fundamental (Nature) (pradhāna) and the Unmanifest (avyakta), said to be the twenty-fifth. (138cd-139) The twenty-sixth should be known to be the Person (puruna) who experiences pleasure and pain. He is the Knower of the Field (kntrajña) bound by the Karma he has accumulated due to Nature.52 (140) It is said that (the result of) all action and the latent traces (it leaves behind) must be experienced (bhogya). All the seeds of conditioned existence are purified by this knowledge. (141)

sanskrit: 76 कुमारिकाखण्ड: ५९२ ५९४ शेषा”” ये क्रमशः सर्वे अध्वाने तु यथा स्थिता: ५९६ ५९८ तदूवे नियतिः ख्याता नियमिकाध्वनि स्थिता' कालसंख्यौ प्रकर्तीरौ ६०० ६०२ यत् कृतं तस्य शोभने । •६०४ ६०६ ५९५ ५९९ ' ।। १४२ ।। कलया व्यापितं॰३ तत्त्व कलित तु यथा कलित तु यथा स्थितम् ।। १४३ ।। ६०८ ६०९ तेनैषा च कला प्रोक्ता रागाद् दलितचेतसः । रागेन रञ्जितो ह्यात्मा मायया वलितों मायया वलितो”२ भवेत् ३ ॥ १४४ ॥ विद्या१४ वेदनिका ज्ञेया विद्या वेत्ति शुभाशुभम् । पराविद्यार्थवेत्तार:१५ शुद्धमार्गमवाप्नुयात् ।। १४५ ॥ ६१९ अदृष्टाधिष्ठितो भूयो जन्ममृत्युमवाप्नुयात् । मोक्ष वा यदि वा भोगमीश्वरेण प्रचोदितम् ॥ १४६ ॥ ।। सदाशिवस्तु वेत्ता``३ वै पशूनां २४ मोचको २५ भवेत् २६ । ६२७ ६२९ मायाबीजपदं त्यक्त्वा भोगान् भुक्त्वा अशेषतः ।। १४७ ।। शक्तिस्तु व्यापिनी सूक्ष्मा शिवधर्मानुवर्तिनी ३१ । •६३२ ६३५ शिव३२ तु सर्वगं‍ प्रोक्त शान्तरूपं व्यवस्थितम् ।। १४८ ॥ एवं शोध्यतमं देव३७ अध्वानं१३८ तत्त्वसंख्यया९ । षटत्रिंशतिपदा ह्येते शोधनीया मनीषिभि:' ॥ १४९ ॥ ६४० ६४३ नवतत्त्वस्वरूपेण प्रकृत्यादिक्रमेण तु । ६४६ ६४२ शोधनीया वरारोह५ अणूनां चित्तभोगिका ४४ ६४७ ।। १५० ।। ६४९ । आत्मविद्याशिवाख्य' तु तत्त्वत्रयमुदाहृतम् । मुख्यास्त्वेते समाख्याता: १५१ शोधनीयास्तु २ देशिकै: ६५४ ·६५५ ६५६ एतैः शुद्धेर्विशुद्धयेत ४ षडध्वान त्रिलोचन । ६५७ ६५८ । ६५३ तद्वत्तैर्भाविता: सर्वे द्रष्टव्याश्च मरीचिभि:' ।। १५२ ।। ।। १५१ ।।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-THREE 77 (Now I will ennumerate), in due order, all the remaining ones on the Path. (The Principle of) constraint (niyati) is said to be above (the previous Principles). Established on the Path, (its function is) to constrain and regulate (the lower principles) (niyamikā). (142) O fair one! Time and number (kālasaˆkhyā) are the two (that measure) what (the Person) has done. Reality (tattva) is pervaded by energy (kalā) and is differentiated (kalita) according to (its phenomenal) condition. For that reason (this Principle) is called `kalā’. The mind (of the individual) Self is broken apart by passion and is coloured (rañjita) by it. (Due to it) he is encompassed by Māyā. (143-144) (The Principle of limited) Knowledge (vidyā) should be know to be that which knows. It knows what is auspicious and inauspicious. He who knows the object of supreme knowledge, attains the pure path. (145) The one who is governed by fate (adrn˜a) is subject repeatedly to birth and death. Whether it be (the experience of) liberation or worldly experience (bhoga), it is impelled by the Lord. (146) Sadāśiva is the knower. He liberates fettered beings once (they have) abandoned the plane of the seeds of Māyā and have experienced all (their) worldly experiences. (147) The Pervasive (vyāpinī) energy is subtle and is in accord with Śiva’s nature (śivadharma). Śiva is said to be omnipresent and abides in a tranquil form.53 (148) O god, such is the Path that is to be purified in terms of the number of Principles. These thirty-six planes should be purified by the wise. (149) O handsome one, (the energy) that experiences the mind of the individual souls is to be purified by means of the nine principles that constitute the sequence of (the Principles) beginning with Prakrti. (150) Ātman, Vidyā and Śiva are said to be the Triad of Principles. These are said to be the main ones the teachers should purify.54 (151) O three - eyed one, one should purify the Six Paths with these pure (principles). Everything is sanctified by those who possess this (Triad). They should be perceived by means of the rays (of the deity). (152)

english: CHAPTER THIRTY-THREE 79 The Path of the Forces (kalādhvan) O virtuous one! Now I will tell you about the Path of the Forces (kalā). (153ab) The (one) Principle is pervaded by the forces (kalā). The (one) Principle is indeed force. Force is the form of the Great God, the omniscient, Supreme Lord. (153cd-154ab) The (five) forces (kalā) corresponding to Earth and the other (principles) are said to be Nivrtti (Contentment), Pratin˜hā (Establishment), Vidyā (Knowledge), Śānti (Tranquillity) and Śāntyātītā (Beyond Tranquillity) which one should know to be supreme. (154cd-155ab) The pervasive energy (vyāpinī) of the Lord of the gods is subtle, very subtle. Pervasive, its form is the Void and endless; it is present (āśritā) in the Lord (nātha). (And so), O sinless one, you have been told about the Path of the Energies in brief. (155cd-156) In this way, one out of these (Paths) should be purified by the high-minded teacher. The Path of Mantra, supreme and inferior, should be purified by means of the Vidyā. (157) O Great Lord, the Path of the Worlds should be awakened by the one who contemplates (the Supreme) Principle.55 Starting with the first force (kalā)56 up to Śiva, this procedure is in six parts (na˜prakāravidhi). O Great God, it should be applied, in due order, within the letters and the entities (of the Paths) by means of (ritual) action seen in the scripture. (158-159) The Nature of Impurity, Karma and Māyā Thus, O god, one out of these (Paths) should be purified with effort. Once the teacher who knows the Path has done this up to the extreme end of transmigratory existence, he should grace fettered souls as he pleases. (This can be done) once he has know (the Path) in its (phases of) emanation and withdrawal in accord with (the disciple's past) action (karmānurūpataƒ).57 (160-161) He who is subject to transmigratory existence and is governed by virtue (dharma) and vice (adharma) is said to be a fettered soul.58 He resides in the cage of the fetters that constitute the bondage of (his) previous (Karma and) Māyā. (162)

sanskrit: 80 कुमारिकाखण्ड: यस्त्वनादिमलो ह्येको” बीजभूतो व्यवस्थितः । प्ररोहत्वमिति” धर्मक्षेत्रमाश्रित्य क्षेत्रमाश्रित्य सुव्रत ७२४ च२५ ७२२ ७२० ।। १६३ ।। क्षेत्र माया भवेत् तस्य सहजस्य पशोर्मल: । यथाश्वत्थस्य ३ बीजं तु पतितं च प्ररोहति ।। १६४ ।। शाखास्कन्धसहस्रैस्तु¨¨ क्षेत्रस्याश्रययोगतः ७३० ७२८ । एवं मायाश्रितो” ह्यात्मा नित्यं मायात्मको” मतः ७३३ माया या'' सन्निमित्तत्वात् प्रवर्तते अणोर्हि सा अनिमित्तस्य देवेश ७ नैव माया प्रवर्तते ॥ १६६ ॥ ७३८ कदाचिद् भाविनोऽप्येव शुद्धाध्वं न न शिवो? विद्यते देव४२ माया ह्येका ७४४ ७५० ७३९ सा तु बन्ध:४५ स्वभावेन ४६ न मोक्षो विद्याशक्ति:४९ स्मृता सा तु मोक्ष योगे न तेषां भवते मोक्षो‍ अनिमित्तो ७५६ ७४० ७३२ ।। १६५ ॥ ७३६ । प्रवर्तते । भवेत् तदा ।। १६७ ।। ७५१ यदा ७४८ । विद्यते क्वचित् स्मृता भवेत् ।। १६८ ।। भवेत् । ७५५ यथा राजा¨¨६ स्वदोषे“ तु बद्धो बन्धे प्रवर्तते ।। १६९ ।। न मोक्षो बन्धनं तस्य तत्त्वात्मा यत् प्रसह्यते M । ७६० ७६१ ७६२ आश्रयः सहजः॰६३ पुंसां मलो ह्येकः प्रबन्धकः ।। १७० ।। तदा तस्य प्रवर्तेत माया सन्तानबोधिता M । ७६६ ७७० ७६८ बोधितो मायया तत्त्वे विश्लेष? चाधिगच्छति ७७३ कलावलितचैतन्य ँ ँ३ विद्यादर्शितगोचरम् M ७७४ । रागेन५ रञ्जितश्चासौ बुद्ध्यादिकरणैर्युतः ।। १७२ ॥ ७७२ ।। १७१ ।।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-THREE 81 O virtuous one, the one beginningless impurity abides in the form of a seed (bījabhūta). It grows when it enters the field of Dharma (and Adharma).(163) The field of Māyā is the impurity (of the fettered soul) that is born along with it (sahaja).59 Just as the seed of an Aśvattha (tree) that has fallen (on the ground) grows with thousands of branches and parts by virtue of its association with the field (in which it grows), in the same way the (individual) soul who resides in Māyā is always considered to be of the (same) nature as Māyā. (164-165) The Māyā that operates due to some (specific) cause is that of the individual soul (aSu). O Lord of the gods, Māyā does not function in the absence of an instigating cause (animittā). (166) Thus the Pure Path never operates for the worldly man (bhāvin). O god, then there is no Śiva. There is only Māyā. (167) By its very nature (Māyā) is bondage (and when the soul is under its influence) there is no liberation (for him) anywhere.60 (But) in the Yoga of Liberation (moknayoga) that (same Māyā) is said to be the power of knowledge (vidyāśakti). (Otherwise) if liberation were devoid of (any) means (of attainment) those (fettered souls) could not (be liberated). (168-169ab) Like a king who, bound in his own defects, (finds himself) in prison (but nonetheless remains a king), he who is the (Supreme) Principle, is not (really) subject to bondage or liberation. (169cd-170ab) The only support individual souls (puˆs) have is the binding impurity that is born (sahaja) (along with them). Then (when the time comes) Māyā begins to function, awakened by the chain (of the soul's previous births) (santāna). (When the soul) is awakened by Māyā, he is is released into (a particular) Principle (in accord with his Karma). (171) The field (of his) consciousness, which is associated with the power of limited action (kalā), is displayed by (limited) knowledge (vidyā) and, coloured by passion, he is linked to the organs (of perception), the intellect and the rest. (172)

sanskrit: 82 कुमारिकाखण्ड: ७७९ ७७६ •७७७ ७७८ ७८० एवं मायात्मक बन्ध प्रसज्जते शुभाशुभम् । तदाश्रयगुणोऽधर्मस्तद्धमीच्च समासतः ।। १७३ ।। ७८३ ७८४ ७८५ तदात्मकौ स्मृतौ पाशौ पाशितस्तैस्तु तिष्ठति । ७८७ ७८८ ७८९ तेषां ज्ञात्वा तु विश्लेषं आत्ममायाशिवस्य तु ।। १७४ ।। पाशशैथिल्यतः”° पश्चात् यथा भवति तच्छृणु ७९१ ७९५ ७९२ अचेतन:৺९३ प्रमादेन४ अहिदष्टोऽगतायुषः ।। १७५ ।। स्पन्दते चैव तीर्थे वै प्रार्थयति”“ च । चलते ७९६ ८०२ दृश्यते”” मन्त्रसामथ्य किमत्र प्रविचार्यते ' ।। १७६ ।। शिलानां कम्पनं ३ स्तोभं स्तम्भनं ४ गतिरागति: । ८०८ तेषां तु प्रवरा: श्रेष्ठाः प्रत्ययास्तु “ वरानन ८०५ ८०९ ।। १७७ ।। धर्माधर्मात्मको बन्धः आत्मनस्य न चान्यथा १२ । ८१३ तस्यैव ९४ क्षपण १५ कार्य दीक्षया परमेश्वर १७ ।। १७८ ।। ८२० कृतानि यानि कर्माणि इदानीं यान् करोति च । ८२२ ८२३ क्षीयन्ते” दीक्षया?” तस्य पिण्डपाते शिवं व्रजेत् ॥ १७९ ॥ क्षीणे धर्मात्मके पाशे८२५ अधर्मे ये व्यवस्थिताः ८२७ । अपरो८२८ नास्ति देवेश २९ येनासौ३० तिष्ठतेऽध्वनि ।। १८० ।। पाशैर्मुक्तो यदा ह्यात्मा निराधारश्च तिष्ठति ३३ । ८३७ ८३५ पतते ३४ कम्पते चैव च्छिन्नमूलो यथा द्रुमः ५ ।। १८१ ।। ६ यथा वृक्षो बहिर्घातैच्छिन्नः कम्पति” भूतले पतते च न संदेहो तथा ह्यात्मा मलच्युतः वियोगश्चैव पाशानां कर्तव्यो दीक्षया बुधैः' ८४७ ८४५ ८४३ । । ।। १८२ ।। वियोगस्तु यदा जातस्तदा स्तोभो न संशयः ।। १८३ ।।
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-THREE 83 Thus, bondage, which is Māyā, auspicious and inauspicious, follows as a consequence. In brief, vice (adharma) as an attribute (of the fettered condition) takes its support from that, while (Adharma is derived) from Dharma.61 (173) The two fetters are said to be those two (Dharma and Adharma); (the fettered soul) is bound by (all of) them. Once one has known (their true nature), the (individual) Self, Māyā and Śiva are disassociated (from each other). (Now) listen to what happens after the fetters have become loose. (174-175ab) The Disjunction and Paralysis of the Fetters A distracted person (acetana) who, because of he is careless, has been bitten by a snake, (but has) survived, moves about, trembling in the sacred bathing site (tīrtha) (to which his well wishers) send (him to be cured). (175cd-176ab) The power of mantra is visible. There is nothing to reason about here. (By the power of mantras) rocks shake, (the body is) paralysed, (armies are) checked (in their course), (KuSÆalinī) comes and goes (ascending and descending). O handsome one, (these) are their best and most excellent signs of attainment (pratyaya). (176cd-177) Bondage is nothing but the Dharma and Adharma of the (individual) Self. O Supreme Lord, this must be destroyed by (the rite of) initiation. (178) Whatever deeds (the fettered soul) has done, or is doing at present, they are all destroyed by initiation and when the body drops (at death) he attains Śiva.62 (179) When the fetter of Dharma has been destroyed, those (fetters that are) grounded in Adharma (are also destroyed). O Lord of the gods, nothing else keeps him on the Path. (180) If the Self is freed of (its) fetters, it is left without support. (And so the body) shakes and falls, like a tree whose roots have been cut. Just as a tree that is cut by external blows shakes (and then ultimately) certainly falls to the ground. Such is the case with the Self from which impurity has fallen away.63 (181-182) The wise should bring about the disjunction of the fetters (from the fettered soul) by means of initiation. If (this) disjunction has taken place, (the fetters) are certainly paralysed. (183)

sanskrit: 84 कुमारिकाखण्ड: ८५० स्तोभो” नाम““ समुद्दिष्ट: ९ कम्पनं पतनं “ २ तथा५३ । । कस्यापि तत्र ८५४ संस्थस्य ८५६ संस्थस्य -८५५ योगश्चैव निरामयः ॥ १८४ ॥ ८५८ ८५९ ।। पाशस्तोभो“ भवत्येवं मुक्तो धर्मादिबन्धनै: 148 मोक्षं तु भवते तस्य इत्यागमप्रचोदनम् ॥ १८५ ॥ पाशस्तोभाद्६२ भवेत् ३ सिद्धिः संसिद्ध: ४ सोऽपि संवरे ६५ । संवरो नाम चित्तस्तु यथा मुक्तिरसंशयात् ॥ १८६ ॥ ८६७ तस्मात् मुक्ति:““ स्फुटा ह्येषा योगदा भोगदा शुभा । यो जानाति महेशान स मुक्तो मोचयेत् पशून् ॥ १८७ ॥ । इत्याद्यावतारे महामन्थान भैरवयज्ञे अन्वये सप्तकोटिप्रमाणे मेरुमार्गविनिर्गते लक्षपादाधिके” विद्यापीठमार्गे विमलषट्कनिर्णये कादिभेदे आज्ञापारमेश्वरे स्वामिनीमते श्रीचतुर्विंशत्सहस्रसंहितायां ८७४ ८७५ अव्वाक्रमभाषिते सबीजदीक्षाधिकारो नामानन्दः ।। ३३ ॥ •८७३
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-THREE 85 It is taught (in the scripture) that whoever is established there (and experiences) the paralysis (of the fetters), (his body) shakes (kampana) and falls (patana) (to the ground). And (ultimately, he attains) flawless Yoga. (184) The paralysis of the fetters takes place in this way and one is freed of the bonds of Dharma and the rest. The scripture prescribes that such a one is liberated. (185) Yogic accomplishment (siddhi) is attained by the paralysis of the fetters. (The soul who attains this) is accomplished in religious observance (saˆvara). Religious observance is the mind (citta); without a doubt it is like liberation (itself). (186) Therefore, this auspicious liberation clearly bestows both Yoga and worldly enjoyment. O Great Lord, he who knows this is liberated and he frees the fettered. (187) This is the (thirty-third) chapter called Concerning the Initiation with Seed. It belongs to the primordial descent into the great sacrifice of the Churning Bhairava in the tradition (anvaya) that consists of seventy million (verses) that has emerged on the Path of Meru and (extends) for more than a hundred thousand quarter (verses). It is on the path of the Seat of Knowledge (vidyāpī˜ha) and is the ultimate purport of the Pure Six Thousand (verses vimalana˜ka) in the division beginning with `Kā' in the venerable scripture of twenty-four thousand (verses) (known as) the Svāminīmata of the Supreme Lord's command as uttered within the Tradition of the Mother (avvākrama).

sanskrit: श्रीनाथ उवाच चतुस्त्रिंशानन्दः दीक्षितस्य' च शिष्यस्य कथं होमो विधीयते । नित्यकर्मणि युक्तस्य' सिद्धिर्नैमित्तिक कथम् ॥। १॥ श्रीवक्रा उवाच परोपजीवकाना' तु रागोपहतचेतसाम् । न तेषां हुतिकर्माणि विद्याजापं न शस्यते ॥ २ ॥ o गार्हस्थ्यनिरतानां तु देवाग्निगुरुपूजकाम् । व्यवस्थेय गृहस्थाना विद्याहोमः प्रशस्यते ॥ ३ ॥ ३ एकान्ते विजने रम्ये भूमि संशोधयेत् ततः । वास्तुयागादिकं कृत्वा कारयेद् यागमण्डपम् ॥ ४॥ १४ चक्रे दक्षिणभूमूर्ती च त्रिरत्र च त्रिरस्रकम् । कुण्डं सलक्षणं प्रोक्तं खातं कुर्याच्च तत्समम् ।। ५ ॥
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-FOUR the Teaching Concerning the Offering to the Fire. Preamble — The Sacrifice to the Fire for Regular (nitya) and Occasional (naimittika) Rites Śrīnātha said: How is the offering to the fire (homa) of the initiated disciple to be performed? How is the accomplishment of the occasional rites of one who is engaged in the regular ones (nityakarman)? (1) The venerable (goddess) Vakrā said: Neither the ritual offering to the fire nor the the repetition of the Vidyā is meant for those who live off others and whose minds are smitten with attachment.1 (2) The fire offering along with the (repetition of the) Vidyā (vidyāhoma) is enjoined for those who are devoted to the householder's life2 and those who worship the gods, the teacher and the fire. This is the condition of householders. (3) The Construction and Purification of the Fire Altar, Sacrificial Area and the Introduction of the Fire Thus, one must purify a piece of ground in a isolated, beautiful place where there are no people. Once performed the sacrifice of the site (vāstuyāga) and the rest, one should have the pavilion erected. (4) (One should draw) a triangle in the Wheel which is within the icon on the right.3 The fire pit is (also) said to be triangular and is dug equal (in size and shape) to that (Wheel) with (all the neccesary) characteristics. (5)

sanskrit: 88 कुमारिकाखण्ड: वेदी कुर्वीत षट्भागे वर्तुला भुवनाकृतिम् । ऊर्ध्व” पीठत्रयं कुर्यात् कापूजा तु क्रमेण तु ।। ६ ॥ २२ शतपञ्चैक” सन्त्यादौ” अङ्गुलानि समासतः । अज्ञत्वे” विपुलत्वे च” प्रजानां न विधीयते ॥ ७ ॥ २७ त्रिकोण समुदायेन साधार” सर्वसिद्धिदम् । मुमुक्षूणां” विमुक्त्यर्थमन्वये” होमकर्मणि ॥ ८ ॥ ३१ आज्ञास्त्रैः प्रोक्षणं कुर्यात् कवचेनावगुण्ठनम्” । ३४ उन्मूलनं तु नेत्रेण महन्तायी” अनन्तरम् ॥। ९ ॥ पूरणं खेचरीचक्रे समीकरनं वाग्भवैः •४० ३७ । सिञ्चन” चन्द्रगर्भेन” कुट्टन भैरवेच्छया ॥ १० ॥ मार्जनं परमानन्दैर्विद्याबीजैस्तु” लेपनम् । प्रोक्षणामन्त्रणं कुर्यात् शोषणं पीठपञ्चकैः ॥ ११ ॥ प्रोक्षणागुण्ठनं चैव उन्मूलनं ँ प्रपूरणम् । समीकरणं सिञ्चनं च कुट्टन संमार्जनम् ॥ १२ ॥ लेपन प्रोक्षणं चैव शोषण नाम उच्यते । ५२ इत्येकादशसंस्काराः करणेनाभयप्रदाः ।। १३ ॥ सम्यग्मूर्तिचतुष्क तु कुण्डस्यात्र प्रवर्तते । असंस्कृत कृतं यस्मात् तदा कुण्डमसिद्धिदम् ॥ १४ ॥ तत्रासनमघोरास्त्रं बिम्बमध्ये च कारयेत् । त्रिःकोण कूटभुवनं शलाकास्त्रेण उद्धरेत् ।। १५ ॥
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-FOUR 89 The altar should be made in six parts, round and the shape of the world (bhuvana). Above (it), one should fashion the three sacred seats, namely, KĀ (Kāmarūpa), PŪ (PūrSagiri) and JĀ (Jālandhara), in due order.4 (6) In brief there are 106 fingers (in length) in the beginning (?).5 This is not enjoined on (common) initiates (praja) because (the form of this type of altar) is very large (and complex). Moreover, (they would) not know (how to construct) it. (7) The triangle which, as an aggregate (of parts), has a (solid) base bestows all the accomplishments. It is (used) in the rite of the fire offering and is (taught) in the tradition so that those who desire liberation may achieve it.
