english: CHAPTER FORTY-SIX 363 (The Siddha gave) this as his command: “Get up! He is the lord of the universe. He is the venerable Mūlanātha himself (sāknāt) who has descended into the moving and immobile (universe) to grace all living beings. Take refuge in him. He is the Lord who is eternal bliss and resides in the centre of the radiance of the Moon.49 Worshipped, he bestows (that) eternal accomplishment (of all) desire.” (And so she worshipped him) with garlands that exude divine fragrance and pastes perfumed with incense, with food of many different flavours and many divine sweet meats and snacks along with alcoholic drinks of (all) six flavours and the best kinds of wine and meat and, having praised (that) god whose form was (then) invisible with many kinds of divine hymns and eulogies, she passed the night.50 (73cd-78ab) She got up (next morning) and, her heart full of bliss, having adorned (herself), wearing all (her) ornaments and accompanied by (her) maids and attendants, the young woman went there to the hermitage where the Lord of Siddhas resided.51 (78cd-79) She approached him with humility, in the proper way, along with her surrounding entourage and then she worshipped the omniscient Nātha, the lord who is the cause (of all things), well. Pleased, he taught them the Transmission of the Skyfarer (khecarīkrama). (80-81ab) Viewed (avalokita) by Śrīnātha's Command, they all attained the state of flight (khagati). Then all the host of gods, their eyes wide with wonder, looked at each other and discussed with one another. Rudra, Indra, Viriñca and the other (gods) where full of great wonder. (81cd-83ab) They attained the supreme state by the grace of Siddhinātha (the Lord of Accomplishment), that is, with ease (līlayā) by the (power of his) Command alone and not by (many) repetitions of mantra, austerities, fire sacrifices or many kinds of spiritual disciplines (sādhana) or much ritual action whatever it may be.52 Thus they were all awakened in the festival of the joy of the Kula's Command and possessed supreme devotion. (83cd-85abc)

sanskrit: 364 कुमारिकाखण्ड: ३१० भक्त्या परमया युक्ता वसवो मारुतश्च ये ।। ८५ ।। ससुताश्च”” सदम्पत्यो” मुनयः संश्रितव्रताः ३१४ । अत्र्यङ्गिरौ” पुलस्त्यश्च मरीचिर्नारदस्तथा ।। ८६ । विश्वामित्रो याज्ञवल्क्यो १६ मानवोऽन्ये तदात्मजाः । ३१९ ३१७ ३१८ दानवेन्द्रा ग्रहाश्चान्ये गन्धवी: खगनायकाः ।। ८७ ।। तथान्ये॰ षोडश: ३२१ कोट्यो २ रुद्रमुख्यामरोत्तमाः । जमदग्निर्भृगुर्दक्षो भरद्वाजोऽथ कश्यपः ।। ८८ ।। किन्नराप्सरसो नागाः लोकेशान्ये तदंशजाः । ३२६ ३३० ३२७ ३२५ ३२८ सप्तकोट्य: २९ सपत्नीकाः सपत्नीका: देवा विष्णुपुरोगमाः ।। ८९ ।। क्रतुर्वसिष्ठः” पुलहो” गौतमश्च प्रचेतसः । ३३६ ३३४ ब्रह्माद्या३५ दशसंख्याश्च ६ कोटयः सुरनायकाः ३३९ ३४२ ३३७ ॥ ९० ॥ ।। ९१ ॥ एवमेते यथोद्दिष्टा आदिमध्यान्तसंस्थिताः । क्रमेण सिद्धनाथस्य चरणान्ते समागताः ततः सुरवरास्तस्य३ समभ्यर्चयाङ्घ्रिपङ्कजौ । आनीतं परमानन्दजनन पानमुत्तमम् ।। ९२ ।। विविधं तालजं पत्रवृक्षजं पुष्पजं तथा । • ३४५ •३४७ ३४८ ३४६ द्राक्षमिक्षुरसोद्भूत” माध्वी गौडी च पिष्टजा ३५१ । ३५० ३५३ ।। ९३ ।। । खर्जूरी पिष्टजा लोध्री ५२ तथा वै शालिकादयः ३५६ असंख्याता५४ ह्यनेकाश्च कस्तान् वर्णयितुं क्षमः ।। ९४ ।। विविधानि च“७ नामानि स्वादवर्णान्यनेकधा । ३५७ ३६० आनीतं विविधैर्भक्त्या’““ पिशितानि बहून्यपि ।। ९५ ।। सुस्वादूनि च दिव्यानि भक्ष्यभोज्यानि सुव्रत ६२ । ३६४ ३६५ लेह्यपेयानि३६३ चोष्याणि गन्धधूपस्रगानि १४ च १५ ।। ९६ ।। निवेदितानि विधिवत् प्रणम्य शिरसा क्षितौ ।
english: CHAPTER FORTY-SIX 365 (They were, amongst others) the Vasus, the Māruts, husbands and wives with their offspring, sages who observed vows, Atri, A‰giras, Pulastya, Marīci, Nārada, Viśvāmitra, Yājñavalkya and other human beings along with their offspring, the gods and demons, the planets, heavenly musicians, the leaders of (the beings) who move in the Void so too other most excellent immortals lead by Rudra, numbering one hundred and sixty million. (85d-86ab) (Again, amongst them were) Jamadagni, Bhrgu, Dakna, Bharadvāja, Kaśyapa, Kinnaras, Apsaras, Nāgas and other lords of the worlds and those born from their limbs. (There were the) gods led by VinSu who, along with their wives, numbered seventy millions, Kratu, Vasin˜ha, Pulaha, Gautama, Pracetasa and the lords of the gods beginning with Brahmā and the rest numbering a hundred million. (88cd-90) In this way, (all) these came (to worship) at the feet of the Lord of the Siddhas in due order, according to whether they were told to be at the beginning, the middle or the end. Then after the most excellent gods had worshipped his two lotus feet, the best drink, which generates the highest bliss, was brought (there for them to drink). (The drink was spiritous liquor) of many kinds, made from fan- palms (tāla), leaves, trees and fruit. (91-93ab) (There was wine produced from) grapes (drāknā), sugarcane juice, honey, brown sugar, flour (pin˜aja), dates, lodhrī,53 rice and more that has not been mentioned. (Their) names, tastes and colours were very varied. Indeed (they were so many and of so many kinds that) who is able to describe them (all)? (93cd-95ab) Out of devotion, the many kinds (of beings) brought many (kinds of) meat. O one of good vows, the food preparations were very delicious and divine. (They brought snacks) to lick, drink and suck along with scent, incense and garlands. They were offered to (the Lord of the Siddhas) in the prescribed manner, bowing (their) head to the ground. (95cd-97ab)

sanskrit: 366 ३६७ कुमारिकाखण्ड: ततो गीतमहावाद्यस्तुतिस्तोत्रवरोत्तमैः ॥ ९७ ॥ आराधित:३८ सुरैः३६९ सम्यक् श्रद्धाविनयशालिभिः ततः सिद्धवरैर्दिव्यपात्राणां पानमुत्तमम् ।। ९८ ॥ उद्धृत्वाधेय” मार्गस्थः पाणिभिः प्रथमं ततः । •३७४ ३७३ ३७५ ३७० । स्वयं पीत्वा तदुच्छिष्ठ पानं त्रिदशनायक ॥ ९९ ॥ दत्तं तुष्टेषु नाथेषु योगावस्थेषु सुन्दर । ३७९ ३७७ ३८० ३७८ स्वभावस्वच्छरूपेषु ँ” घूर्णमाणैस्तु लोचनैः ॥ १०० ॥ ३८१ ३८२ संगृहीत्वा सुरश्रेष्ठैर्लोकपालैस्तपोधनैः २ । ३८३ ३८४ । मूर्धनाभिनन्द्य विनतैः पीतं तदमृताधिकम् ॥ १०१ ॥ श्रीनाथाज्ञाप्रभावेण सर्वे ते विकलेन्द्रिया: । ३८५ ३८८ ३८६ सर्वे ते परमानन्दनन्दिता ३८७ चरलोचनाः ।। १०२ ।। ३८९ ९३ ३९४ •३९१ तेन पानस्य संज्ञा वै सुरापान प्रकीर्तितम् । यैर्न तत्९२ प्राशितं देव असुरास्ते च राक्षसाः तामसो यातुधानाश्च स्वरूपविभवोज्झिताः' । ३९७ ४०० ३९५ ॥ १०३ ॥ च पार्वती ॥ १०४ ॥ संतुष्टेनाथ तेष्विदं श्रीनाथेन ९ च पार्वती •४०१ वर? श्रीवीरपानस्य दत्तं दृष्ट्वा महत्सुखम् अक्षयेदं परानन्दस्थापन भवते सुरा •४०३ ४०४ ४०६ मन्त्राराधनयागेषु॰ योगिभिस्तु समन्ततः । ।। १०५ ।। यज्ञे श्राद्धे विवाहे च प्रतिष्ठामङ्गलेषु च ।। १०६ ।। योगिनी—ऋषिभि:“ सिद्धैर्देवाग्निगुरुतर्पणैः । ४११ ४०९ ज्ञानविज्ञानसंक्रामे काले सैन्यमहाहवे ।। १०७ ॥ न हि तत्र भवेत् सिद्धिः सुरा यत्र न विद्यते ।
english: CHAPTER FORTY-SIX 367 Then he was fitingly worshipped by the gods, who were full of faith and humble virtue, with songs, great instruments and the best hymns and eulogies. (97cd-98ab) The Boon of the Heroes Drink — the Sacrificial Wine and its Glory Then (these) excellent Siddhas took up the best of drinks (contained in) divine vessels with their hands. (Siddhanātha), established on the path to be attained, first drank (it) himself and, O leader of the gods, what drink remained (ucchin˜a) was given to the Nāthas who content, were in yogic states, their eyes rolling in inebriation and their inner being, pure. (98cd-100) It was taken by the best of the gods and the guardians of the directions, rich in penance and humble and, making a gesture of salutation with (their) head, they drank that (liquor) which was more than nectar. They were (all) completely drunk (vikalendriya) by the power of Śrīnātha's Command and their eyes, moving (around with inebriation), were all joyful with supreme bliss. (101-102) This is why drink (pāna) is called the drink of the gods (surapāna). O god, those who do not imbibe it are demons, Rāknasas and carnivorous black magicians (yātudhāna) who are devoid of the glory (vibhava) of their own true nature. (103-104ab) When the venerable Lord (nātha) and Pārvatī54 were satisfied, seeing (their) great joy, Śrīnātha gave (them) the boon of the heroes’ drink (śrīvīrapāna) that wine (surā) may be (the means by which) this imperishable and supreme bliss is established by yogis in all respects (samantataƒ) in the course of the (repetition of) mantras, worship and sacrifices. (104cd-106ab) There is no success (siddhi) if there is no wine (surā) (to offer) in the sacrifice, the worship of ancestors, at a wedding, on the auspicious occasions (when idols and the like) are installed (pratin˜hā), during the lustration of the diety, fire and the teacher by Yoginīs, ¬nis and Siddhas, when knowledge and wisdom are transmitted, or when there is a great battle between armies.55 (106cd-108ab)

sanskrit: 368 कुमारिकाखण्डः ४१२ ४१६ नित्यं सन्निहिता तस्य पूज्यमाना भवेत् सुरा ॥ १०८ ॥ क्रियाज्ञानविहीनानां भावभक्तिविवर्जिताम् । लौल्यार्थे”३ भिन्नवृत्तीनां अपेया भवते सुरा ।। १०९ ।। नास्तिकाना¨¨ निःसत्यानां भावहीनां तु निर्दयाम्” । गुरुदेवाग्नियोगिन्यामन्त्रसंस्कारवर्जिताम् ॥ ११० ॥ वीरपानान्मयादिष्ट४१ रौरवं नरकं नृणाम् । ।। ।। पतन्ति पशवो४२२ येन कर्मणा नरके ध्रुवम् ॥ १११ ॥ त्रिष्कालज्ञाश्च तेनैव ज्ञानिनश्चोत्पतन्ति हिं । ४२५४२६ देवाग्निगुरुभक्तानां संस्कृतानां तथाणुभिः ॥ ११२ ॥ ।। भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदं सत्यं भविष्यत्यासवं सदा ४२९ । सिद्धद्रव्येण विख्यातं अलिफल्गु च कौलिकम् ।। ११३ ॥ ४३२ •४३३ यदा तदा”” व्रजेत् येषां दूषको नरकं भृशम् । ४३५ तिष्ठते तावद् देवेश यावद् ब्रह्मादिनाष्टकम् ४३९ रसो विष्णुस्तथाधारो ब्रह्मामूर्तिर्महेश्वरः । ॥ ११४ ॥ ।। ।। आनन्दः” कुब्जिका देवी नित्यं समरसेर स्थिता ४३ ।। ११५ ।। मूलनाथो विभूत्वे वै तस्मात् समरसं कुरु । ४४६ यावन्न कुरुते चैक्यं तावत् सिद्धिः कुतो भवेत् ।। ११६ ।। अयष्ट्वा श्रीक्रमं देव अकृत्वा योगितर्पणम् । ४४८ ४५० ४४९ पशुभिः सह संपीत्वा वीराणां नरकं ४५३ भवेत् ४५२ । भवेत् “” ।। ११७ ।। सुरा शक्तिः शिवो‍ मद्यं आनन्द ४५४ मोक्ष उच्यते । चराचरमिदं विश्वमनन्तादि शिवान्तगम् ॥ ११८ ॥ ४५६ •४५७ अशेष५५ षड्विधार्थं तु स्थूल सूक्ष्मं परं च यत् । बिन्दुमात्रप्रदानेन अलिना तर्पितं भवेत् ।। ११९ ॥
english: CHAPTER FORTY-SIX 369 Wine should be always close at hand and respected (pūjyamānā). Wine should not be drunk by those who are devoid of knowledge and ritual (kriyā) and without (deep spiritual) feelings (bhāva) and devotion or by those who, out of greed, lead an immoral life. (It should not be drunk by) atheists, cheats, those devoid of deep feelings or compassion, those who have not been initiated into the mantras of the teacher, god, fire and Yoginīs. I have ordained a terrible (raurava) hell for men (such as these) who drink (the liquor) of Kaula adepts (vīrapāna).56 (108cd-111ab) That action due to which the fettered certainly fall into hell, elevates the wise knowers of the three times.57 (111cd-112ab) Wine will always be the truth that bestows liberation and worldly benefits to those devotees of the teacher, god, and fire who have been purified in this way with its drops. Meat and wine (aliphalgu) are well known as the Kaula substances (dravya) of the Siddhas. (112cd-113) As this is so, he who finds fault (dūnaka) with them will go to a mighty hell and, O mistress of the gods, he will stay (there) for eight of Brahmā's days. (114) VinSu is the juice (rasa), Brahmā is the foundation (ādhāra), the idol (mūrti) is Maheśvara, and the bliss ever present in oneness (samarasa) is the goddess Kubjikā. Mūlanātha is (present) in (its) glorious power (vibhūtva), therefore make (all things) one (samarasa). (115-116ab) As long as (the adept) does not make (all things) one, there is no success (siddhi). O god, drinking with the uninitiated (paśu) without having worshipped the Śrīkrama or offered libation to the yogis (leads to) the hell of (fallen) Kaula adepts (vīra). (116cd-117) Wine (surā) is Śakti, liquor (madya) is Śiva,58 while the joy (of inebriation) is said to be liberation. (118ab) This moving and immobile universe that extends from Ananta to Śiva, the entire sixfold reality (naÆvidhārtha), gross, subtle and supreme, is all lustrated by the offering of just one drop of liquor (ali). (118cd-119)

sanskrit: 370 कुमारिकाखण्ड: ४५८ यज्ञतीर्थतपोदानव्रतचर्यादिकानि च । शतकोटिसहस्राणि ४५९ जपहोमार्चनानि च ।। १२० ।। सर्वे ते हर्षदेवस्य कला नार्हन्ति षोडशीम् । ४६५ इत्युक्त परमेशश्च कृत्वा चानुग्रहं पुरा ।। १२१ ।। कृपया स्वेच्छया ते च तत्रैवान्तरधीयताम् ४६८ ४६६ ४६९ गतेषु तेषु नाथेषु प्रयाताः स्वपुरं सुराः ४७१ परमामृतसंतृप्ता अमरास्तेन ते स्मृता: । ४६७ ४७० ' ।। १२२ ।। अथाष्टाष्टकहीनानां चत्वारि स्वेच्छतः ४७२ कलौ४३ ॥ १२३ ॥ ४७४ व्यतीते लौकिकाब्दानां चैत्रमाश्विनकार्त्तिके । ४७६ ४७८ नवम्यां पूर्णपक्षस्य भूयस्तैस्तु मयाज्ञया ।। १२४ ।। कृत्वावतार श्रीशैले पारिपाऽर्बुदे तथा । क्रमान्नागवरोच्छेषु९ तीव्रवज्रनरोत्तमाः ।। १२५ ।। ४८० मौनमास्थाय सूर्यब्द श्रीक्रमाराधनं प्रति । •४८३ •४८४ ४८५ ४८७ कुलयज्ञं वरं यष्ट्वा परानन्दपुरं पुनः ।। १२६ ।। ४८८ ४८९ प्रयातास्तत्र वै तेषां स्वाधिकारपदे स्थिता: । •४९० ४९१ सद्रहस्य नामानन्दः नामानन्दः ” स्वाधिष्ठानें स्वाधिष्ठाने”२ मुखोत्थितम्”” ॥ १२७ ॥ ४९५ श्रेष्ठमध्यान्तिमानां ९४ च ये जाताः ५ स्वसुतान्वये । दिव्यादिव्ये ९६ विभागेन भविष्यन्ति कलौ युगे ।। १२८ ॥ ५०० पिङ्गेश श्वेतनाथ च क्रूराभ्र मतिविभ्रमम् । ५०९ ५०४ अर्धेन्दुर्मदनोन्मत्तकौलार्क: ०२५०३ कुलभास्करम् ।। १२९ ॥ कौलेश कुलमातङ्ग रुद्रमार्तण्डमेव च । अघोरश्चण्डवेगश्च षष्ठानन्दः ९ खगेश्वरः ।। १३० ।। कुमुदश्चोडदेवश्च रश्मिरूपा व्यवस्थिताः । बीजत्रयविभागस्था: “१३ सर्वज्ञा: १४ सर्वगाव्ययाः ५१५ ५१२ ।। १३१ ।। ।।
english: CHAPTER FORTY-SIX 371 A sacrifice, (any) sacred bathing place (tīrtha), penance, charity, vows, spiritual practice (caryā), thousands of tens of millions of recitations of mantra, fire offerings and acts of adoration, all of these (together) are not worth a sixteenth part of (liquor), the Lord of Joy (Harnadeva). (120-121ab) Once the Supreme Lord had said this and graced them as he chose to do out of the compassion (he felt for them), he disappeared from there. (121cd-122ab) When those Nāthas had left, the gods went to their city. As they are satisfied with the supreme nectar (amrta), they are said to be immortals (amara). (122cd-123ab) The Sixteen Siddhas Now * * * * (?)59 when four years of this world had past freely during the Age of Strife, they again descended (into the world) at my Command onto excellent mountains, on the ninth day of the bright half of the fortnight in Caitra, Aśvina and Kārttika at Śrīśaila, Pāripātra and Arbuda, respectively. (These) best of men (powerful like) intense lightning (tīvravajranarottama) kept silence for a solar year, intent on worshipping the Śrīkrama. Once they had performed an excellent Kula sacrifice, (they) again went to the City of Supreme Bliss60 and there they occupy their own position of authority. The bliss within the (Wheel) of the Self-supported (svādhin˜hāna), which is the true secret, is generated from (their) mouth. (123cd-127) In the Age of Strife, they will belong to their own lineage of (spiritual) offspring of the best, middling and lowest (lineages) (divided) into (two) groups, one divine (divya) and the other human (adivya).61 (128) The Sixteen Divine Siddhas (The sixteen divine Siddhas are) 1) Pi‰geśa, 2) Śvetanātha and 3) Krūrābhra, 4) Mativibhrama, 5) Ardhenu, 6) Madanomattakaulārka, 7) Kulabhāskara, 8) Kauleśa, 9) Kulamāta‰ga, 10) RudramārtaSÆa, 11) Aghora, 12) CaSÆavega, 13) ±a˜hānanda, 14) Khageśvara, 15) Kumuda and 16) OÆradeva.62 They are (all) rays (of the light of the deity) and, omniscient, omnipresent and imperishable, they reside within the division of the three seed-syllables. (129-131)

sanskrit: 372 ५१६ कुमारिकाखण्ड: चराचरस्य विश्वस्य षोडशाधारवत्मगाः । ५१७ दिव्या ह्येते महावीयी आधाराश्चेति विश्रुताः ।। १३२ ।। ते एवापरभेदेन श्रीक्रमज्ञाः समीरिताः । अदिव्ये मानुषे लोके दिव्याज्ञाबलशालिनः ।। १३३ ॥ ५२० ५२१ नरा मार्तण्डरूपेण अज्ञानतिमिरापहाः । ५२४ •५२५ भविष्यन्ति २२ हि मत्यानां तेषां नामानि २३ बोध मे ।। १३४ ।। चन्द्राब्जं वत्सगुल्मार्क: स्तम्भशक्त्यानल परम् । ५२६ कपीसगर्भमातङ्गो २७ वट : १२८ सिंहैकविक्रमम् २९ ।। १३५ ।। ५३१ त्रैलोक्यविरज' षष्ठं श्रीपूपात्मा जयाह्वकम् ५३४५३५ ५३२ । कांसालं त्वभयानन्द ५३३ श्रीभोगरत्नेशः शोभवान् ।। १३६ । श्रीबिम्बविमलानन्द तीक्ष्णाख्यं तीक्ष्णाख्यं ३८ विजयं तथा । वराङ्गरुद्र” वीरेश •५४३ । श्रीधारः केशवेश्वरम् ।। १३७ ।। सहसामलमुद्राख्य वंकविबुद्धडामरम् । । भोजाख्यः १४५ षोडशश्चैव४६ वर्गाद्यं द्वित्रितुर्यकम् ॥ १३८ ॥ ५४८ ५५० षष्ठमेकादशं चान्य सप्तैते ४९ सिद्धनायकाः ज्येष्ठ–ओल्याधिकारस्थाः सप्ताष्टनवमास्तथा ५५१ •५५३ दशमं द्वादशं चान्यं कोटिपूर्व ५३ त्रयोदशम् ।५४ बाल—ओल्याधिकारस्था: ५५ सप्तैते परिकीर्तिताः -५५७ । ५५२ ५५६ ।। १३९ ॥ ।। १४० ।। पञ्चमं मनुसंख्यं च युग्ममेतद् वरानन । मध्यमोल्याधिकारस्थ““ बालसूर्यानलप्रभम् ।। १४१ ॥ ५६२ बहवोऽन्येऽपि° ते चन्द्रबिम्बाद्यास्तत्पुराद्“” बहि: । निर्गत्याज्ञामृतौघेन निमित्तार्थेन धीमताम् ॥ १४२ ॥ ।। ।। इत्येतै: ६५ पुरुषैः६६ सिद्धैः सन्तानत्रयनिर्गतैः१६७ । कृतं दिव्याधिकार वै नानास्थानवराश्रमैः ५६९ ।। १४३ ।।
english: CHAPTER FORTY-SIX 373 They reside on the path of the sixteen Supports (ādhāra) of the moving and immobile universe. These are the divine (Siddhas). They possess great power (vīrya) and are well know as the Supports.63 (132) The Sixteen Human Siddhas These same (Siddhas) according to the other (apara) division, are said to be those who know the Śrīkrama in this profane (adivya) world of men and possess the power of the divine Command. (133) They will be men who, in the form of the sun, will remove the darkness of ignorance (of other) mortals. Learn their names from me.64 (They are) 1) Candrābja (Moon Lotus),65 Vatsa 2) Gulma, Arka (Sun) 3) Stambha, Śaktyānala comes next, (then) 4) Karpāsagarbha (the Cotton Plant), MātaSga (Elephant) 5) Va˜a, Siˆhaikavikrama 6) Trailokya, Viraja (Brilliant) is the sixth, 7) the venerable Pūpātmā,66 Jaya (Victory), 8) Kāˆsāla,67 Abhayānanda (Joy of Fearlessness), 9) Bhoga, Ratneśa (Jewel of Enjoyment), who is beautiful, 10) the venerable Bimba, Vimalānanda (Pure Joy),68 11) TīknSa (Severe), Vijaya (Victory),69 12) Varā‰garudra,70 Vīreśa (Lord of the Heroes), 13) Śrīdhāra,71 Keśaveśvara, 14) Sahasa72 (who is) Amalamudrā, 15) Va‰ka,73 VibuddhaÆāmara (Wizard of the Awakened Worlds) and the one called 16) Bhoja74 who is the sixteenth. (134-138) The one at the beginning of the group, the second, third, fourth, sixth, the eleventh and another. These are the seven leaders of the Siddhas who have authority in the Lineage of the Eldest (jyen˜holi). (139) The seventh, eighth and ninth, the tenth, the twelth and another is the thirteenth who is preceded by millions (ko˜ipūrva).75 These seven are said to have authority in the Lineage of the Child (bāla oli). (140) O handsome one, the fifth and the fourteenth — this is the pair that, shining like the fire and the rising sun (bālasūrya), is in authority in the Middle Lineage (madhyamoli).76 (141) There are many others, including Candrabimba (Lunar Orb) and the rest, who are outside that City. (These teachers) were transported outside by the current of the nectar of the Command (to fulfil) the purpose of the wise. (142) In this way, these accomplished beings who have come from the three lineages (santāna) and whose excellent hermitages are found in many places, have established (their) divine authority (in the world). (143)

sanskrit: 374 कुमारिकाखण्ड: ५७० । एतेषां पुत्रपौत्रादिसन्तानास्त्रिविधा अपि । असंख्याता भविष्यन्ति अदिव्याश्चेतरेतराः ५७३ ५७१ ।। १४४ ।। । एवं ते गगनेशाद्या सृष्टिरेषा ३ कुलान्वये । कृत्वा श्रीमूलनाथस्य लीनाश्चिद्व्योमविग्रहाः ४ ।। १४५ ।। ५७७ द्वात्रिंशाक्षरदेवस्य७५ बहुरूपस्य देहजाः । पञ्चत्रिंश समाख्याताः श्रीनाथा भुक्तिमुक्तिदाः ५७८ कुब्जाद्याप्येवमेवं वै“ योगिन्यः कुलजाव्ययाः ५८३ ५७९ ५८४ ५८१ ।। १४६ ।। । क्रमेण सिद्धनाथाना २ दम्पत्यस्ता इहोच्यते ।। १४७ ।। ज्ञानाम्बा श्रीकुजाम्बा च रौद्राम्बा वामसंज्ञका । ५८९ ५९० ज्येष्ठाम्बा चाम्बिकाम्बा च कामाम्बा सप्तमा स्मृता ।। १४८ ॥ ५९२ ५९४ जालाम्बा' पूर्णसंज्ञा च ओड्डाम्बा दशमां विदुः । गगनाम्बा'९५ महासिद्धरत्नाम्बा पद्मचम्पका ॥ १४९ ॥ ५९७ ५९८ सुरवक्त्रामृताम्बा ँ च तथा ललितभैरवी' । ५९९ ६०० कमलाम्बा शिवाम्बा”” च रामाम्बा कृष्णपिङ्गला ं ॥। १५० ।। चन्द्राम्बा” कल्पविश्वाम्बा २ वटाम्बा गुल्मशेखरा । ६०६ ६०३ स्तम्भाम्बा॰५ विरजाम्बा च रक्ताक्षी कुलशासना ६०४ ६०७ ६११ ।। १५१ ।। लक्ष्म्याम्बा“ सुन्दराख्या च कुटिलाम्बा तथानघ । विकराम्बाथ‘१२ वेगाम्बा ११३ उन्मन्याम्बेष्टकामदा १४ ।। १५२ ।। मोहिन्या च १५ मनोह्लादा इत्येताः परिकीर्तिताः । ६१९ ६१७ परमामृतसंबोधसर्वज्ञा दीपनोद्यताः ।। १५३ ।। दुःखत्रयमहामृत्युपाशौघक्षपणक्षमाः । ६२१ ६२० ६२३ ६१८ अथैषा २९ पूर्वमुद्दिष्टं २२ श्रीनाथानां यथाक्रमम् ।। १५४ ॥ रहस्यं संप्रवक्ष्यामि संज्ञाभेदनिबन्धनम् । येन विज्ञानमात्रेण २४ विधिना पठितेन १२५ च ॥ १५५ ॥ ६२७ सततं २६ श्रीक्रमस्याग्रे आज्ञासिद्धि: प्रवर्तते ।
english: CHAPTER FORTY-SIX 375 Again, their (spiritual) descendents, sons, grandsons and the rest, who are of three kinds (and belong to the transmission) that is human (adivya) and mutual (itaretara),77 will be innumerable. (144) Such is this, your emanation, beginning with Gaganeśa, within the Kula lineage (anvaya). Once (their work) has been done, they dissolve away and (assume) the form of the Void of Consciousness of the venerable Mūlanātha. (145) The Thirty-five Consorts of the Nāthas They are born of from the body of Bahurūpa (the Pluriform One) who consists of thirty-two syllables.78 They are said to be the thirty-five Śrīnāthas79 who bestow liberation and worldly benefits. (146) In the same way the imperishable Yoginīs, Kubjā and the rest, who are born of Kula (number thirty-five). They are the consorts of (these) Siddhanāthas (and there names) are stated here (as follows), in due order. (147) 1) Jñānāmbā (Mother of Knowledge), 2) Śrīkujāmbā (Venerable Mother of Action),80 3) Raudryāmbā (Terrible Mother), 4) the one called Vāmā, 5) Jyen˜hāmbā (the Eldest Mother),81 6) Ambikāmba,82 7) Kāmāmbā (Mother of Passion), who is said to be the seventh. 8) Jālāmbā, the one called 9) PūrSā (Full) and (the wise) know 10) OÆÆāmbā83 to be the tenth84. 11) Gaganāmbā (Mother Sky), 12) Mahāsiddharatnāmbā (Mother of Jewels), 13) Padmacampakā, 14) Suravaktrāmrtāmbā (God Face Mother of Nectar),85 15) Lalitabhairavī, 16) Kamalāmbā (Mother Lotus), 17) Śivāmbā (Śiva's Mother), 18) Rāmāmbā (Rāma's Mother), 19) KrnSapi‰galā (Dark Blue and Tawny),86 20) Candrāmbā (Mother Moon), 21) Kalpaviśvāmbā (Mother of the Universe and Aeons), 22) Va˜āmbā (Best of Mothers), 23) Gulmaśekharā (Bud Crest), 24) Stambhāmbā (Mother Pillar), 25) Virajāmbā,87 26) Raktāknī (Red Eyes) and, 27) Kulaśāsanā. (There are also) 28) Laknmyambā,88 29) the one called Sundarāmbā and 30) Ku˜ilāmbā (Crooked Mother), O sinless one, 31) Vikārāmbā (Deformed Mother), 32) Vegāmbā, 33) Unmanyāmbā (Transmental Mother), who gives what one desires, 34) Mohinyāmbā (Deluding Mother) and 35) Manohlādā (Delight of the Mind). These are who they are said to be.89 (148-153ab) Awakened by the Supreme Nectar they are omniscient. Intent on enlightening (the ignorant),90 they can destroy the great current of the fetters of death and the three (forms of) suffering. (153cd-154ab) The Thirty-five Nāthas Now, in due order, I will tell (you) the secret of the various names of these, the venerable Nāthas mentioned previously. The Command is accomplished (ājñāsiddhi) merely by knowing (this) and reading it constantly in the prescribed way in front of the Śrīkrama. (154cd-156ab)

sanskrit: 376 कुमारिकाखण्ड: ६२९ श्रीविमलात्मजैर्दिव्यै १२८ रश्मिभिः सर्वदेवताः ।। १५६ ॥ ६३१ ६३२ ६३३ शान्त्यातीताध्वगा येन दीक्षिता: कुलशासने । । आद्यं तं विजयं नौमि भक्त्या श्रीनाथभास्करम् ।। १५७ ।। ६३६ शब्दब्रह्मात्मको ३४ योऽसौ ३५ शान्त्यध्वपदवर्तिनाम् । •६३८ अनुग्रहकरं वन्दे सादाख्यं प्रवरं गुरुम् ॥ १५८ ॥ •६३९ ६४० अनन्तमव्ययं ९ कारुण्यानुग्रहे स्थितम् । ६४२ •६४३ ।। विद्यावत्मगतं६४१ रुद्रमनन्तं नमाम्यहम् ।। १५९ ॥ शुभं करोति यो नित्यं प्रतिष्ठान्तरवासिनाम् ६४७ ६४४ ६४८ । वीरमातृगण १४५ रुद्र४६ तं वन्दे शंकरं प्रभुम् ।। १६० ।। निवृत्त्यध्वगत” येन नानारूपावतारकम् ६५० । कृत्वा मायामलं दग्धं श्रीकण्ठं तं नमाम्यहम् ।। १६१ ।। येन दत्ता५१ स्वयं पीत्वा दिव्याज्ञाममृतां सुराम् । ब्रह्माण्डोदरमार्गस्थ तं वन्दे पिङ्गलं विभुम् ।। १६२ ।। ६५४ ६५३ ६५५ ६५६ यः प्रीत्या पूर्वपीठे तु श्रीदेव्या मित्रतां गतम् । ०६५८ ज्ञानार्थी मित्रनाथं त श्रीगुरुं प्रणमाम्यहम् ।। १६३ ।। श्रीमद्दक्षिणपीठाब्जे कुलचर्यव्रतेन तु । ·६६१ कृतं५९ येनाधिकार६६° तं चयीनाथ नमाम्यहम् ।। १६४ ॥ पूर्णगिर्याश्रमे ६३ येन विज्ञाय ं कुलपञ्चकम् । ६६६ •६६७ कृतं षष्ठाधिकार च श्रीषष्ठनाथ नमाम्यहम् ।। १६५ ।। ६६९ महतोड्डामर१६८ रूपमालम्ब्य १९ जगदुद्भवम् ६७२ ६७० । श्रितं श्रीमध्यपीठाब्जे ओड्डीशं तं नमाम्यहम् ।। १६६ ।।
english: CHAPTER FORTY-SIX 377 The Five Siddhas 1) I salute with devotion he who is the first (Siddha), the sun who is Śrīnātha and victory (vijaya) (itself), he who, by means the divine rays born from the venerable pure (reality) (śrīvimala), has initiated all the deities who are on the Path Beyond Tranquillity (śāntyatīta) into the Kula teaching. (156cd-157) 2) I praise Sādākhya, the best of teachers, who is the Word Absolute (śabdabrahman) and bestows grace on those who reside on the plane of reality which is Tranquillity.91 (158) 3) I salute Ananta, the Rudra who is endless, imperishable and abides in compassion and grace on the path of knowledge (vidyāvartman). (159) 4) I salute Lord Śaˆkara,92 the Rudra whose host are the Heroes (vīra) and the Mothers (mātr) and who always does what is auspicious for those who reside within the (force of) the Foundation (pratin˜hā). (160) 5) I salute ŚrīkaS˜ha who has burnt away the impurity of Māyā and, present on the Path of Cessation (nivrtti), has come down (into the world) in many forms.93 (161) The Five Nāthas of the Sacred Seats Pi‰gala 1) I praise the pervasive Lord Pi‰gala who is on the path within the Egg of Brahmā and who, having himself drunk the wine (surā) which is the nectar of divine knowledge, has given it (to others). (162) Mitranātha — Kāmarūpa 2) I, desirous of knowledge, bow to the venerable teacher Mitranātha who, out of love, become friends (mitratāˆ gataƒ) with the venerable goddess (śrīdevī) in the eastern seat.94 (163) Caryānātha — Jālandhara 3) I salute Caryānātha who is established authority in the lotus of the venerable southern seat by (observing) the vow of Kula practice. (164) ±an˜hanātha — PūrSagiri 4) I salute the venerable ±an˜hanātha who, once he had understood the Pentad of Kula (kulapañcaka) in the hermitage of PūrSagiri, established (his) authority in the sixth (nan˜ha) (one).95 (165)

sanskrit: 378 कुमारिकाखण्ड: •६७६ येन॰३ ज्योत्स्नासुधाग्रासात् प्रविश्य पदवीं पराम् । जालभृदग्निसोमार्कनिग्रहानुग्रह कृतम् ।। १६७ ।। कुलकल्पद्रुमच्छायाचन्द्राब्जे चित्तभाश्रमे । ६७७ ६८० ६७८ तीव्रशक्त्याधिकारं तं६७९ वन्दे गगनपादपम् ।। ॥ १६८ ॥ सत्यसंकल्पसन्तानं हि८२ विशुद्धबलेन च । येन कुब्जीकृतं विश्वं नागानां चावलोकनम् ।। १६९ ॥ पञ्चात्मान१८५ महाकुब्जं८६ रत्नेश नौमि शाश्वतम् । ६८८ महापद्मवने सर्वयक्षवीरेशमातराम् ।। १७० ।। ६८९ कृतं येनाधिकारं तं वन्दे श्रीपद्मभास्करम् । ६९० ६९१ । विबुधस्याश्रमे येन राक्षसः गुह्यकैः सह ।। १७१ ॥ दीक्षिताः श्रीगुरुं देववक्त्रं तं प्रणमाम्यहम् । काश्यां श्रीभैरवे यज्ञे क्षेत्रपालाष्टकं तथा ।। १७२ ।। नैमिषे मुनयो यक्षा येन क्रोधावलोकिताः । ६९२ तीव्राज्ञाभैरवाब्जं तं श्रीगुरुं प्रणमाम्यहम् ।। १७३ ।। ६९४ महेन्द्रकमलोद्याने९३ पुरा येन शतक्रतुम् । अभिषिञ्च्य गतं गुह्यं९५ महालक्ष्मीनिकेतनम् ६९७ लीलयानुक्रमे तत्र शोषप्लोषविदारणम् । •७०० ६९६ ७०१ ।। १७४ ।। कीत्यर्थ” सर्ववृक्षाणां पुनराप्यायनं परम् ।। १७५ ॥ कृतं त? कमलार्काख्य श्रीनाथं प्रणमाम्यहम् । ७०५ •७०३ ७०६ पूर्णकालानले ४ स्वौ द्वौ येन दिव्यामृतेन तु ।। १७६ ।। दीक्षितौ तं शिवाम्भोज वन्दे श्रीनाथमव्ययम् । ७०९ त्रिचतुःपथसन्ध्यां तु पदान्ते सर्वदेहिनाम् ।। १७७ ।। ७१० रमते रत्ननाथस्य कारुण्याद् येन नुग्रहम् । •७१३ कृतं तं श्रीगुरु राम आत्मानं प्रणमाम्यहम् ।। १७८ ।। ७०७
english: CHAPTER FORTY-SIX 379 OÆÆīśanātha — OÆÆiyāna 5) I salute OÆÆīśa(nātha) who, assuming the great and excellent (uÆÆāmara) form generated from the universe (jagadudbhava), resides in the lotus of the venerable seat in the centre. (166) The Nine Nāthas 1) I praise Gagana, the tree, who, by imbibing the wine of the Light has entered the supreme path (of realisation) and, having done so, graced and chastized the Fire, Moon and Sun who hold the net (of bondage). (169-170ab) 3) I praise the venerable Padmabhāskara (Lotus Sun) who has established (his) authority over all the Yaknas, Heroes and Mothers in the Great Lotus Forest (mahāpadmavana). (170cd-171ab) 4) I bow to the venerable teacher Devavaktra who initiated the Rāknasas and the Guhyakas in the hermitage of the awakened one (vibudha). (171cd-172ab) 5) I bow before the venerable teacher Bhairavābja whose Command is very powerful (tīvra) and looked with wrath at the Yaknas and the sages in the Naimina (forest) and the eight guardians (knetrapāla) in Kāśī during the sacrifice of the venerable Bhairava. (172cd-173) 6) I bow before Śrīnātha, called Kamalārka, who consecrated Indra (śatakratu) in the lotus garden of Mahendra and then went to Mahālaknmī's secret residence (niketana). There, in due course, in order be glorify (the goddess) (kīrtyartha) he playfully dryed out, burnt and tore apart all the trees and then again (restored them by) the supreme act of nourishment (āpyāyana). english: CHAPTER FORTY-SIX 381 9) I salute KrnSamārtaSÆa (the Black Sun) with devotion, the Nātha who is (like a) black fire. Kāma in Kubjāmraka, KrnSa, the lord of the world, in Dvārakā, GaSādhyakna in Śrīnagari and the two Jitendras in Strīrājya and Malayācala have become his servants. (179-180) The Sixteen Nāthas of the Sixteen Supports97 1) I salute Candrābja98 whose moustache and eyes are brown (pi‰gala) and abides constantly in the first support, ecstatic with the inebriation of the wine of knowledge. (181) 2) I salute Gulmanātha,99 brilliant like ten million moons, whose form is that of a child100 and, white (śveta), resides in the centre of the second hermitage. (182) 3) I salute Stambha101 in the third station of the Self who is the fire of power (śaktyagni) who, (brilliant) like the autumn sky, has lotus eyes and severe (looking) eyebrows. (183) 4) I salute the venerable one called Karpāsa who is the agitation of the intellect (mativibhrama)102 that shines in the lotus of energy of the fourth support and is the light (ābhāsa) that bestows the stream of bliss. (184) 5) I salute Va˜asiˆha who is called Ardhenduvadana (Half-moon Face)103 and is the perpetually manifest ray (of the light of consciousness that shines) in the Lotus of the Sun in the fifth support. (185) 6) I salute Virajeśa who is the ecstatic risen sun of Kaula (the union of Śiva and Śakti) (unmattakaulārka)104 on top of the Five Voids105 in the sixth (support) which is the sixth lotus of Kula. (186) 7) I bow to the venerable Pūpātmā who is Jayānandanātha, the perpetually risen sun of Kula (kulabhāskara)106 within the seventh support. (187) 8) I salute Kauleśa who is Abhayānanda,107 the radiant energy of (divine) sound (dhvani) in the eighth abode of Laknmī, which is the plane where the energies of the Three Abodes (of Fire, Sun and Moon) are consumed (tridhāmakalāgrāsapada). (188) 9) I salute Kulamāta‰ga who is Ratneśa108 in the ninth hermitage. He is inebriated (vikalendriya) with the ecstasy (mada) of the taste of the aesthetic savour (rasa) of the expanse of consciousness. (189)

english: CHAPTER FORTY-SIX 383 10) RudramārtaSÆa109 whose radiance is the great Fire of Time is in the tenth (support). I bow (to him) the venerable teacher Śrībimba called Vimala. (190) 11) In the eleventh hermitage I salute KhaÆga,110 who is called Vijaya. (He is) Aghora who severs the bonds of Karma in the terrible (ghora) world of transmigration. (191) 12) I bow to Śrīnātha, who is Varā‰garudra (otherwise called) Vīreśa, the guardian of the field (knetrapāla), whose form is ferocious (caSÆa) and nature CaSÆavega111 who, having entered the twelfth station of bliss, has brought (all things) under (his) control. (194cd-195ab) 15) I salute Va‰ka, the lord of the clan of the gods (vibudhagotreśa), Śrīnātha Õāmara, the lotus (kumuda) which, brilliant as the sun, is in the lotus of the fifteenth house. Endless, imperishable and the first (pūrva), he is known as Bhojadeva. (196cd-198ab) The body is sustained all around (pari), in due order, by the four, five, six, half of eight and group of five along with the four and by the three, the group of six and by the main group of eight.114 (198cd-199ab) Śrīnātha Pure knowledge (has been revealed) in the venerable sacred seat by the gem which is the Kula Command of the Siddhas as Ānanda and the rest and as the (acts of) chastisement (nigraha) and grace of the universe.115 (199cd-200ab)

sanskrit: 384 ८०३ कुमारिकाखण्डः •८०४ ब्राह्म्यादिसहित” मूल? कुब्जाम्बा चाव्ययं विभुम् ।। २०० ।। श्रीनाथमचलं नित्यं सर्वज्ञत्वादि “ कामदम् । -८०५ वन्दे मूलाधिकारस्थ“ बोधरूपं जगद्गुरुम् ।। २०१ ।। ८०८ इतीदं परमं गुह्यं “ सर्वाज्ञादीप्तिवर्धनम् ८१० ८११ ८०९ । यः पठेन्मानसंयुक्तः कृतमूर्धाञ्जलिः सदा ।। २०२ ।। श्रीमताग्रेऽथवा ” ” सिद्धमण्डलाग्रे क्रमेण तु । ८१३ ।। तस्याज्ञा स्फुरते तीव्रा दुरितौघमहद्भयाः ॥ २०३ ।। व्याधयः प्रलयं यान्ति वशे तिष्ठन्त्यरातयः । ८१९ ८१८ भुक्त्वा श्रीविपुलान् भोगान् परसामान्यतां व्रजेत् ।। २०४ ।। नवलक्षकृताम्नायं विद्यानुष्ठाननिश्चयात् । ८२२ इति सत्यं पुरा प्रोक्तमजेनाव्यक्तमूर्तिना३ ।। २०५ ॥ श्रीषष्ठाख्यं २४ तु यत् सिद्धनाथ२५ तेनावतारिताः । ये च८२६ तेषां प्रमाण २७ वै संज्ञातीतं निगद्यते ।। २०६ ।। शिलाशेखरके पूर्वं पञ्चसिद्धावतारिता: । ८३५ ८३० ८२९ कदम्बगुह्यके चान्ये” पञ्चभिः श्रीपुरे तथा ।। २०७ ।। शतार्धं श्रीकुलूतायां सप्तानां नुग्रहं कृतम् । दशानन्दपुरे ५ श्रीमत्कामरूपे चतुर्दश ।। २०८ ॥ त्रीणि—’७ जालन्धरे विद्यात् तारासंख्यास्तु पश्चिमे । तिथिसंख्यास्तथा ज्ञेया मणिभद्रवटाश्रमे ।। २०९ ।। चतुर्भिर्विरजायां तु हंसद्वारे तु सप्ततिः । ८४४ ८४५ ८४१ ८४३ । वर्षसंख्या महावाटे सिंहले तु शतत्रयम् ।। २१० ।। अट्टहासे शतं सार्धं देवीकोटे शतार्धकम् । अष्टाष्टक¨ पूर्णगिर्ये तदर्धं पूर्णपादये ।। २११ ।। श्रीमत्कोल्लापुरे चान्ये दीक्षिता दशपञ्च च । ८५० ८५१ चत्वारिंशत् “” सतादेष्टे गोकर्णे८५३ पञ्चसप्ततिः बालुकायां तथा देव चन्द्रबिम्बगिरौ शुभे । ८५४ ।। २१२ ।। एकादशार्कसंख्याना नाथेनानुग्रहं कृतम् ।। २१३ ।।
english: CHAPTER FORTY-SIX 385 I praise Śrīnātha (who is this knowledge), the teacher of the universe, the root (Nātha) who is accompanied by Brāhmī and the other (mothers) and who, along with mother Kubjā, is imperishable and pervasive. (I praise him who), immobile and eternal, bestows omniscience and all else one desires and, occupying the position of the root authority (mūlādhikāra), is consciousness.116 (200cd-201) This is the supreme secret, the growth of all the brilliance (dīpti) of the Command.117 The (energy of the goddess's) Command radiates intensely and the current of the mighty fear (of transmigratory existence) is destroyed of one who reads it regularly (sadā) in due order with respect and with hands folded and raised to (his) head in front of the Śrīmata or the maSÆala of Siddhas. (202-203) Diseases are destroyed, the enemies (of the sacrifice) (arāti) are kept under control and, once one has enjoyed the venerable and extensive pleasures of the world (bhoga), one attains supreme universality (sāmānyatā). (204) The teaching the Nine Targets118 is the firm decision to faithfully practice (anun˜hāna) the Vidyā.119 This truth was uttered in the past by the Unborn of unmanifest form.120 (205) The extent (pramāSa) of the (Siddhas) brought down (to earth) by the Siddhanātha called the venerable ±an˜ha(nātha), is said to be beyond number. (206) The Places where Initiates Reside and Received Initiation121 Initially, five Siddhas122 were brought down onto the 1) peak of the Stone, along with five others, in 2) the Kadamba cave and fifty in 3) Śrīpura. 4) Seven were graced in the venerable (town of) Kulūtā, 5) ten in Ānandapura and 6) fourteen in the venerable Kāmarūpa. One should know that there are 7) three in Jālandhara. (Indeed, the Siddhas) in the Western (Tradition) are as many as the stars. (207-209ab) 8) They should be known to be fifteen in the hermitage of the banyan tree (va˜a) (called) MaSibhadra, along with 9) four (others) in Virajā and 10) seventy in Haˆsadvāra, 11) twelve in Mahāvā˜a, 12) three hundred in Siˆhala, 13) one hundred and fifty in A˜˜ahāsa, 14) fifty in Devīko˜a, 15) sixty-four in PūrSagiri, 16) half that (number) in PūrSapādaya (?), 17) there are another fifteen initiates in the venerable Kollāpura, 18) twenty-four in Satāden˜a, 19) seventy-five in GokarSa, O god, (there is) the same (number of adepts) in 20) Bālukā and the Lord (nātha) has graced (adepts) numbering twelve times eleven on the auspicious 21) Candrabimba mountain. (209cd-213)

sanskrit: 386 कुमारिकाखण्ड: यन्नाशौ पश्चिमे तीरे चतुर्भिश्चावलोकिता । ८५९ ८६० ।। कालञ्जरे शताधीर्थं तीव्राज्ञामनुकम्पया ॥ २१४ ।। त्रयोदश बदयीयां शालिग्रामेकविंशति: ' ८६१ ८६५ । कुरुक्षेत्रे शतान्यष्टौ तदर्ध नैमिषे तथा ।। २१५ ।। कन्याकुब्जे४ त्रिपञ्चाशत् सप्त वीराः सुरालये । तत्त्वसंख्या महातीर्थे चित्रकूटे शतद्वयम् ।। २१६ ।। ८६७ एकाशीतिः समाख्याताः त्रिपथाविन्ध्यसंगमे । ८६९ सिन्धुसागरसंघट्टे चतुर्विंशति कीर्तिताः ।। २१७ ।। शतमष्टाधिकं देव सेतुबन्धेऽवतारिताः' । ८७१ ८७० सप्त गोदावरीक्षेत्रे कच्छदेशे च कोङ्कणे ।। २१८ ।। ८७४ क्रमेण चतुराशीतिः चतुर्विंशश्च सप्ततिः । संध्या सप्तत्रिंश स्थाने षट्चत्वारिंशत् कीर्तिता: रुद्रकोट्यां षोडशश्च ९ अयोध्यायां च तत्समाः । कामकोट्यां चतुःषष्टिर्द्विगुणेन तथार्बुदे ।। २२० ।। ८७८ पौण्ड्रवर्धनके चैव काश्यां परापरेऽपि च । उड्रदेशे च गान्धारे पञ्चनद्यां च पुष्करे ।। २२१ ।। उरसायां कलिङ्गे च वर्धमानपुरे तथा । ८८५ पम्पातीरे चलत्यायां सप्तादौ सप्तवृद्धतः ।। २२२ ।। स्थानेष्वेतेषु सिद्धानां नाथेनानुग्रहं“ कृतम् । ।। २१९ ।।
english: CHAPTER FORTY-SIX 387 (The goddess) was seen by four (adepts) in 22) Yannāśi (?) on the western bank. By the compassion of the intense (power of the goddess's) Command, twenty-five (adepts were initiated) in 23) Kālañjara. (There are) thirteen (of them) in 24) Badarī and twenty-one in 25) Śāligrāma, eight hundred in 26) Kuruknetra and half that (number) in 27) Naimina, fifty-three in 28) Kanyākubja and seven Heroes in 29) Surālaya, the number of the Principles in 30) Mahātīrtha and two hundred in 31) Citrakū˜a. (214-216) There are said to be eighty-one where 32) the Ganges (tripathā) meets the Vindhyas and twenty-four where 33) the Indus joins the sea. O god, a hundred and eight were brought down into (the town of) 34) Setubandha, seven in the field of 35) the Godāvarī and eighty-four and ninety-four in the land of 36) Kaccha and 37) KoˆkaSa, respectively. (217-218) There are thirty-seven in 38) Sandhi and there are said to be forty-six in 39) Sthāna. There are sixteen in 40) Rudrako˜i and the same (number) in 41) Ayodhyā, sixty-four in 42) Kāmako˜i, and twice that number in 43) Arbuda. (219-220) 44) PauSÆravardhanaka, 45) Kāśī, 46) Parāpara123 (?), 47) the land of OÆra, 48) Gāndhāra, 49) Pañcanadī, 50) Punkara, 51) Urasā, 52) Kali‰ga, 53) Vardhamānapura, 54) the bank of the Pampā,124 55) Calatyā,125 seven at the begining and increased by seven — in (all) these places the Lord (nātha) has graced Siddhas. (221-223ab)

sanskrit: 388 कुमारिकाखण्ड: षण्णवत्युत्तरे“” गङ्गातीरे श्रीमन्महोदधौ ।। २२३ ।। ८९१ ८९२ श्वेतद्वीपे त्रयस्त्रिंश द्वौ महेन्द्रगिरौ तथा । मलये ९३ वाष्टविंशं वै षट्शतानि हिमालये ।। २२४ ।। चत्वारिंश९७ तथा पञ्च श्रीगिरौ चण्डिकाश्रमे । द्वारिकायां सुरेशान एकाशीत्यधिकशतम् ॥ २२५ ।। स्त्रीराज्ये”” बर्बराख्ये° च मरुभूमौ सुरालये । । त्रयोदश दशाष्टौ ३ च शतमेकाधिकं क्रमात् ।। २२६ ।। ९०४ एकोनार्धशता: सप्त गङ्गातीरेऽवलोकिताः । कृपया परया सम्यक् श्रीनाथेन महात्मना ।। २२७ ।। इत्येते कथिताः सर्वे भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदायकाः । ९०६ व्यक्ताव्यक्तविभागेन दिव्यादिव्यक्रमेण तु ।। २२८ ।। त्रिविधाज्ञाधिकारं वै कृत्यातीता परे शिवे । श्रीनाथ उवाच नैष्ठिकानां च तन्त्रेषु सूचितं वरवर्णिनि ।। २२९ ।। ब्रह्महत्या सुरापानं स्तेयं गर्वं मनोगतम्” । चत्वारि”४ पातकान्येतत्” तत्संयोगी च पञ्चमः ।। २३० ।। ९१६ भवते नारकी देवि मद्यपानकृते सति । ९१८ । भवेत् ।। २३१ ।। कुशाग्रबिन्दुमात्रेण रौरवे पतनं ब्रह्महत्यासमं देवि” मद्यपानमुदाहृतम् । देवि९२१ ९२२ । किं १२३ निमित्तं महादेवि त्वया पीतं महाम्बिके ।। २३२ ।। अस्मिन् तन्त्रागमे” श्रेष्ठा महापुण्यफलोदया । सुरा चैव महेशानि निर्णीता २५ कुलशासने ।। २३३ ॥ ९२७ ९२८ अयं मे२६ संशयोऽद्यापि ७ च्छेतुमर्हसि साम्प्रतम् ।
english: CHAPTER FORTY-SIX 389 There are ninty-six in the north 56) on the banks of the Ganges, thirty- three on 57) Śvetadvīpa in the great ocean, two on 58) mount Mahendra, twenty- eight on (mount) 59) Malaya, six hundred in the 60) Himālaya and forty-five on 61) Śrīgiri in CaSÆikā's hermitage. O Lord of the gods, there are one hundred and eighty-one in 62) Dvārikā and thirteen, eighteen and one hundred and one in 63) Śrīrājya,126 (the land) called 64) Barbara and 65) Marubhūmi, the land of the gods, respectively. The great soul Śrīnātha has rightly gazed upon forty-nine and seven (Siddhas) with supreme compassion 66) on the banks of the Ganges. All of these are said to be the bestowers of (both) liberation and worldly benefits. (223cd-228ab) (Their) authority to command (ājñādhikāra) is of three kinds, divided into manifest (vyakta) and unmanifest, along with the transmission (krama), (both) divine (divya) and human (adivya). (The Command) that transcends (every) goal of action is within Supreme Śiva. (228cd-229ab) The Glory of Wine and Liquor Śrīnātha said: 127O best of women, it is taught (sūcita) in the Tantras of those steadfast in practice (nain˜hika), that the four sins are brahminicide, the drinking of liquor, theft and the pride that resides in the mind along with the fifth associated with that (?). O goddess, one who drinks wine goes to hell. (229cd-231ab) One falls into the Raurava (hell by drinking) merely (the amount contained in) a drop that (drips) from the tip (of a blade of) Kuśa grass. O goddess, drinking wine is said to be as (bad as) commiting brahminicide. (231cd-232ab) O Great Goddess, why do you drink it? O Great Mother, (why) is it taught here in this Tantra and in Kula doctrine (that) wine is the best (of substances) and that it gives rise to the fruit of great merit? Even today, I still have this doubt. Please remove it now. (232cd-234ab)

sanskrit: 390 •९२९ ९३० ९३१ मद्यं २९ किमुच्यते देवि सुरा नाम ९३४ ९३२ एतन्मे तत्त्वतो ब्रूहि यदि तुष्टासि कुमारिकाखण्ड: किमुच्यते ॥ २३४ ॥ वक्रिके । श्रीवक्रा उवाच ९३६ ममाद्यं देवदेवेश परमानन्दलक्षणम् ।। २३५ ॥ •९३८ मद्यं३७ तेन समाख्यातं तव देव प्रकाशितम् । सुरा रसायणं प्रोक्तं परमानन्दनिर्भरम् ।। २३६ ।। ९४१ उमादेहात् समुत्पन्नं शशिमध्याच्च सुन्दरम् । ९४३ समरसे४२ व्यापको देवः परमानन्दलक्षणम्) ९४५ मदिरानन्दमुत्पन्नं तदा मद्यमुदाहृतम् । ९४४ ।। २३७ ।। या सुरा सुन्दरी प्रोक्ता सा च कुण्डलिनी स्मृता ।। २३८ ।। घण्टिकायां भवेत्” ँ नित्यं वारुणी सा परा कला । ९४८ सुरा साध्यात्मिका प्रोक्ता वीराणां देहसंस्थिता ।। २३९ ।। ९५४ यद्” मद्यं तत् परं शौर्य ५१ यत् ५२ शौर्य ५३ तच्च शौर्य तच्च वीरराट् । पीत्वा ५५ यो वीरवृत्तिस्तु आचरेत् सुरसंगमम् ॥ २४० ॥ वीरपानं स्मृतं तेन भुक्तिमुक्तिफलप्रदम् । श्रीमदगिरिवरे दिव्ये कैलासे पर्वतोत्तमे १५९ •९६० मदनोत्सवकाले तु चक्रं संपूजितं पुरा । •९६१ ।। ।। २४१ ।। आदिनाथेन देवेश अष्टाष्टकं महाबलम् ।। २४२ ।। .९६३ तस्मिन् चक्रवरे१६२ दिव्ये १३ परमानन्दमहोत्सवे । चतुःषष्टिस्तु ४ नामानि एकैका या उदाहृता ९६५ ।। २४३ ।।
english: CHAPTER FORTY-SIX 391 O goddess, what is liquor (madya) said to be and what is wine (surā) said to be? O Vakrikā, tell me that in truth if you are satisfied (with me). (234cd-235ab) The venerable (goddess) Vakrā said: O Lord of the god of the gods, it is called liquor (madya) and has been revealed to you, O god, because it is my primary (mamādya) charateristic, namely, supreme bliss. Wine (surā) is said to be the alchemical potion (rasāyaSa) full of supreme bliss. (235cd-236) It is called liquor (madya) because it has arisen out of the bliss of grape wine (madirā) (and because), beautiful, it has come forth from Umā's body and the centre (madhya) of the Moon. It is the god who pervades in oneness (samarasa) (literally `in equalness of flavour') and its characteristic is supreme bliss.128 (237-238ab) The fair lady called Surā (Wine) is also said to be KuSÆalinī.129 Present constantly in the uvula (ghaS˜ikā), she is VāruSī130 (the liquor which is) the supreme energy (kalā) (of the Moon).131 Surā132 resides within the bodies of Kaula adepts (vīra) and is said to be the one to be attained (sādhyātmikā). (238cd-239) Liquor is supreme bravery (śaurya) and bravery is the emperor of heroes. He who behaves as does (a Kaula) hero (vīravrtti) and, having drunk (this liquor), practices union with the gods, (practices) what is said to be the drinking of heroes (vīrapāna), which bestows the fruit of (both) worldly benefits and liberation. (240-241ab) The Sixty-four Yoginīs In the past, the Wheel was worshipped on divine Kailāsa, the venerable and most excellent of mountains, during the festival of Madana (the god of love). O Lord of the gods, the mighty (group of) sixty-four (yogis) resides in that, the divine and best of Wheels, along with the First Lord (Ādinātha), in the great festival of supreme bliss. (Their) sixty-four names are those that have been declared one by one.133 (241cd-243)

sanskrit: 392 ९६६ कुमारिकाखण्डः पीत्वा तु देवतै: सर्वैश्चक्रस्थैश्चतुःषष्टिभिः ९६७ आनन्दितैः पृथक् नाम कृतमानन्दनन्दितैः ९७२ । ९७० वीरपानमलिं चैव खार्जूरं कुम्भकाम्भसा । ९७३ •९७४ ।। २४४ ।। कादम्बरी रुद्र: १३ सिद्धिः चाश्व कौस्तुभसुन्दरम् कौस्तुभसुन्दरम् ।। २४५ ।। ९७६ •९७७ पात्रं पूर्णं पुण्डरीशं ध्वजं गोरोचनं तथा । ९७८ साध्य' व्यापकयोगीन्द्रं ९ नागेन्द्र कर्परं गिरिः ।। २४६ ।। मुक्त चन्द्रकला ज्योति: प्रशमं जगतारकम् ९८३ ९८४ ९८१ । ९८५ मोक्षं शीधुबकौ भाति: मुद्रा ज्ञानशलाकय ।। २४७ ।। अवस्था चोन्मनं भाव“ मन्त्रं पात्रं विमलं पञ्चरात्रं च द्रव्यं सुरगणं समयं पीतरागं च अघोरं तुम्बुरु •९८७ ९८८ कुलेश्वरम् । । तथा ।। २४८ ।। तथा । सिद्धान्तं रुद्रमूर्तिस्थं गन्धर्व शङ्खशुक्तिकम् ॥ २४९ ॥ अधिकारं महारत्नं योगेश्वरं महाकुलम् । •९९१ नटेशं बैन्दवं तार””” योगिनीकमलाननम् ।। २५० ।। घटकोड्डामर भूतिश्चतुःषष्टिरुद्राहृता: । ९९४ ९९३ योगिचक्रे ' स्मृता देव अभिधानाः ९५ परिस्फुटाः ९९७ ९९६ ।। २५१ ।। एतान् ज्ञात्वा पिबेद् देव विमलं कुलगोचरे । अलिविलासभेदोऽय”“ यावन्न ज्ञायते स्फुटम् ।। २५२ ।। तावन्मद्यं न पीतव्य आज्ञाभङ्गः प्रजायते । •९९९ १००१ १००३ श्यामा रक्ता सुरूपाढ्या॰२ गन्धामोदविभूषिता' ।। २५३ ॥ सामृतं न सुरापानं लोके मद्यं प्रतिष्ठितम् । १००५ देवतै ऋषिभि:००४ सिद्धैर्योगिनीयोगिकिन्नरैः ।। २५४ ।। तैस्त्ववधारित पूर्वं मयाद्य प्रकटीकृतम् । ००७ समरसं सुन्दर पानं शेषं मद्यं विडम्बना ' । २००८ ।। २५५ ।।
english: CHAPTER FORTY-SIX 393 (Wine) was drunk by all the sixty-four deities in the Wheel.134 and they were (thereby) made blissful. Delighted with joy, each one gave a separate name (to the sacrificial drink). (244) The Sixty-Four Names of the Sacrificial Drink (There names are as follows): 1) Vīrapāna (Hero's Drink), 2) Ali (Liquor), 3) Khārjūra (Date Wine), 4) Kumbhaka (Jar),135 5) Āmbhas (Water), 6) Kādambarī,136 7) Rudra 8) Siddhi, 9) Aśva (Horse), 10) Kaustubha, 137 11) Sundara (Beautiful), 12) Pātra (Vessel),138 13) PūrSa (Full), 14) PuSÆarīśa (Lord of the Lotus), 15) Dhvaja (Flag),139 16) Gorocana (Musk), 17) Sādhya (Junction), 18) Vyāpaka (Pervader), 19) Yogīndra (Lord of Yogis), 20) Nāgendra (Lord of the Snakes), 21) Karpara (Potsherd), 22) Giri (Mountain), 23) Mukta (Liberated), 24) Candrakalā (Digit of the Moon),140 25) Jyoti (Light), 26) Praśama (Tranquillity), 27) Jagattāraka (Saviour of the World), 28) Mokna (Liberation), 29) Śīdhu 30) Baka (Crane), 31) Bhāti (Splendour), 32) Mudrā, 33) Jñānaśalākā (Scalpel of Knowledge),141 34) Avasthā (State), 35) Unmanabhāva (the Transmental State), 36) Mantra, 37) Pātra (the Drinking Vessel),142 38) Kuleśvara, 39) Vimala (Pure), 40) Pañcarātra (Five Nights),143 41) Dravya (Sacrificial Substance), 42) SuragaSa (Host of Demons), 43) Samaya (Rule), 44) Pīta (Imbibed), 45) Rāga (Passion), 46) Aghora, 47) Tumburu, 48) Siddhānta (Conclusion), 49) Rudramūrtistha (Established in Rudra's Form), 50) Gandharva, 51) Śa‰kha (Conch), 52) Śuktika (Mother of Pearl), 53) Adhikāra (Authority), 54) Mahāratna (Great Jewel),144 55) Yogeśvara (Lord of Yoga), 56) Mahākula, 57) Na˜eśa (Lord of the Dance), 58) Baindava (Belonging to the Drop), 59) Tāra (Star), 60) Yoginī, 61) Kamalānana (Lotus Face), 62) Gha˜aka (Jar), 63) UÆÆāmara (Excellent) and 64) Bhūti (Loot). (These) are said to be the sixty-four. (244-251ab) O god, these names are very clear and are recollected in the gathering of yogis (yogīcakra). O god, one should drink the sacrificial wine (vimala)145 in the field of Kula (only) after they have been learnt. This part (of the teaching) (bheda) (concerns) the joyous sport of the sacrificial liquor (alivilāsa). As long as one does not understand it clearly, one should not drink wine (madya), (otherwise) the Command (of the Goddess) is transgressed. (251cd-253ab) The (goddess) Surā (Wine) is dark blue and red,146 beautiful and possesses a fine aroma. That is nectar, not the drinking that takes place in the world. (253cd-254ab) Today I have clarified what the gods, sages, Siddhas, Yoginīs, yogis and Kinnaras have understood in the past. The drink of unity (samarasa) is beautiful; all other liquor is a deceit. (254cd-255)

sanskrit: 394 सुरतागमकाले तु उत्पन्ना' १००९ कुमारिकाखण्ड: सा रजस्वला । ततः सुरा सा विख्याता सुरसिद्धाभिनन्दिता ।। २५६ ।। १०१० १०११ १०१२ संपूर्ण समया विद्या ११ पात्रस्था चाभिमन्त्रिता' । १०१३ मण्डलाग्रे पिबेद् यस्तु विद्यापीठे गुरोग्रतः ।। २५७ ।। स याति परमं स्थानं कुलानां तारयेच्छतम् । धूपेन च समायुक्तं विप्रूषा तर्पणं यदा' -१०१६ १०१४ ।। २५८ ।। कृतं भक्तिसमायुक्त:. स कुल तारयेच्छतम् । १०१७ अयष्ट्वा श्रीक्रमं देव अकृत्वा तर्पणं यदा ।। २५९ ।। पशुपानविधौ पीत्वा वीराणा १८ नरकं गतिः १०१९ । अन्तरङ्गक्रमे पीत्वा रुद्रत्वं प्राप्यते पदम् ।। २६० ।। यः पिबेत् प्रकटं देव स याति नरकं ध्रुवम् । १०२१ तस्यागम न दातव्यं महाद्रोहो भविष्यति ।। २६१ ।। तेनैव सह संभाषं न कुर्यात् कुलदेशिकः । भवते २२ योगिनीद्रोहो' २३ आज्ञाभङ्गः प्रवर्तते ॥। २६२ ।। मद्यं नाम परं प्रोक्तं समय॰२४ पारमेश्वरम् । असमयिनामिद २५ देव गोपनीयं प्रयत्नतः ।। २६३ ।। १०२८ समयभङ्गेषु॰ २६ दारिद्र्य ७ मरणं गुरुलङ्गनें । १०२९ आज्ञाभङ्गे कुतः सिद्धिर्लङ्घनान्नरक १९ व्रजेत् ।। २६४ ॥ १०३० कृत्वा त्रिवर्तितं मन्त्री क्षमाप्य अलिमण्डलम् । एकाङ्गुल्या प्रदेशिन्या वामहस्तकनिष्ठिका ।। २६५ ।। या मुष्टिस्तत्र' ” बध्वा तु अलिद्रव्यं पिबेत् तत: । दीपकं चरुकं भक्षं कृत्वा पानं पिबेत् तदा ।। २६६ ।। १०३२
english: CHAPTER FORTY-SIX 395 (The goddess), praised by the gods (sura) and Siddhas, is called Surā (Wine) because she arises menstruated (rajasvalā),147 when the good time to copulate comes (suratāgamakāla). (256) The Samayā Vidyā which is completely full and has been invoked (abhimantritā) resides in the (drinking) vessel. He who drinks it in front of the maSÆala in the Seat of Knowledge (vidyāpī˜ha), in the presence of the teacher reaches the supreme Place (sthāna) and saves a hundred Kulas. (257-258ab) If lustration with (just) a drop (of wine) has been offered along with incense, he who has devotion saves a hundred Kulas. O god, the heroes who drink (wine) as the fettered do without first worshipping the Śrīkrama and offering the lustration, go to hell. Drunk in accord with the inner transmission (antara‰gakrama), one attains Rudra's plane. O god, one who drinks openly goes to a lasting (dhruva) hell. (258cd-261ab) One should not allow (such a one) to come (into the ritual enclosure because) he will be one who does great damage. The Kula teacher should not (even) speak with him. If he does so, he does violence to the Yoginīs and the (goddess's) Command is broken. (261cd-262) It is said that the supreme rule of the Supreme Lord's (tradition) (pārameśvara) (is to drink) wine (madya).148 O god, this should be kept secret from those who have not been initiated (asamayin). Poverty is (the consequence of) breaking the Command and death when one disobeys the teacher. If the Command is broken, how can there be success? By transgressing, one goes to hell. (263-264) After the reciter of mantra has rotated (the drinking vessel) three times around the maSÆala,149 he propitiates it with liquor (ali). Then, clenching his fist there (around the cup) with the index finger and the little finger of the left hand (extended), he should drink the liquor that serves as the sacrificial offering (alidravya).150 Having eaten the sacrificial pap (caru) that energizes (consciousness) (dīpaka),151 one should drink (the sacrificial) drink. (265-266)

sanskrit: 396 ०३३ कुमारिकाखण्ड: पुष्पं धूपं प्रदत्वा तु स्वगोत्र ३ सहितैकतः १०३४ । समयपात्रं प्रकर्तव्य ३५ निर्विकल्पेन सुन्दर ।। २६७ ।। एकतः सर्ववर्णानि सदा ३६ चक्रे उपस्थिताः' १०३७ १०४० । चक्राद् बहिर्विनिष्क्रान्ता:१०३८ सर्वे सर्वे०३९ वर्णाः पृथक् पृथक् ।। २६८ ।। तर्जन्या तर्पणं कृत्वा अन्तरिक्षे क्षमण्डले । १०४२ १०४३ सन्धाने ४९ तर्पिता यान्ति तृप्ताः सिद्धिं ददन्ति च ।। २६९ ।। २०४४ मध्यमातर्पणं कृत्वा अन्तरिक्षे खमण्डलें । १०४५ १०४६ पितरः संतर्पिता देव तृप्ता यान्ति परां गतिम् ।। २७० ।। अनामातर्पणं कृत्वा क्रमं च गुरुमण्डलम् । तत् सर्वं तर्पितं तेन त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् ।। २७१ । १०४७ कनिष्ठातर्पणं कृत्वा सिद्धा भैरवमातर: । वीरयोगिनि – आचार्या: १०४८ तृप्ता ०४९ यान्ति' १०५० न संशयः ।। २७२ ।। सर्वे ५१ तृप्यन्ति मनुजा: १०५२ ये सिद्धा मत्यलोकतः । , ०५३ अङ्गुष्ठतर्पण कृत्वा रुद्रास्तृप्यन्ति नान्यथा ।। २७३ ।। देवताश्चैव तृप्यन्ति मातरिभ्यः' समन्विताः । १०५६ १०५४ १०५५ तृप्ता यान्ति न संदेहस्तर्पण कुरु पञ्चधा ।। २७४ ।। खेगती रुद्रसिद्धिश्च अजरामरतां गतिः । सिद्ध्यष्टकं पुरक्षोभं इच्छाकाममवाप्यते ।। २७५ ।। विप्रुषा पदमावेश: ०५९ तर्पणेन कृतेन तु । -१०६० कोटिकोटिफल' तस्य इहलोके ? परत्र च ।। २७६ ।।
english: CHAPTER FORTY-SIX 397 O handsome one, having offered flowers and incense, one should prepare, along with own's (spiritual) clan (svagotra) and free of thought (nirvikalpa),152 the Cup of the Rule (samayapātra). (267) All castes (varSa) always meet together as one in the gathering (of initiates) (cakra). (But) once they quit the gathering, all castes (again) become separate.153 (268) The Five Lustrations (tarpaSa) Having offered a libation with the index finger (pointing) to the sky, the circle of the firmament, (the beings who reside) in the juncture (between heaven and earth) (saˆdhāna) have been offered a libation and, satisfied, bestow success (siddhi). (269) O god, having offered a libation with the middle finger (pointing) to the sky, the circle of the firmament, the manes have been offered a libation and, satisfied, attain the supreme state. (270) Having offered a libation with the ring finger, all the Transmission and the Circle of Teachers has been offered a libation and thus (also) the triple world, with all that moves and is immobile. (271) Having offered a libation with the little finger, the Siddhas, Bhairavas, Mothers, Heroes, Yoginīs and teacher are (all) certainly satisfied. (Along with them) all human Siddhas from the mortal world are satisfied. (272-273ab) Having offered a libation with the thumb, the Rudras are satisfied; (they are not satisfied) in any other way. And, without a doubt, all the deities are satisfied along with the Mothers. (Therefore) perform the libation five times. (273cd-274) The Fruits (In this way) one attains (mystical) flight, Rudra's accomplishment, the immortal state that does not decay, the eight (yogic) accomplishments, the arousal of the (beloved’s) body (puraknobha) and one's cherished desire. (275) One penetrates the (supreme) state with (just one) drop (of wine) and, having offered the libation, one gains countless fruits both in this world and the next. (276)

sanskrit: 398 कुमारिकाखण्ड: इहलोके यशः कीर्तिर्वीरत्व प्राप्यते पदम् । १०६४ दीप्तिश्च भवते देहे ०६३ वशीकरणसंपदः ।। २७७ ।। कामक्रीडाविनोदेन कालो गच्छति तस्य वै । १०६६ यान् यान् वाञ्च्छयते ६५ कामान् तान् तान् लभति पुत्रकः १०६८ परलोकं निर्मलं तस्य मोक्षं गच्छति साधकः । अलिक्रमविधान तु देवतातर्पणादिकम् ।। २७९ ।। •१०७१ कृत्वा पिबेत देवेश परां सिद्धिमवाप्नुयात् । वीरद्रव्यं विना सिद्धिर्न च दृश्यति पश्चिमे ।। २८० ।। तदर्थ॰७३ सिद्धमार्गेऽस्मिन्॰७४ अलिफल्गुरुदाहृतम् । २०७५ । १०७७ १०६७ ।। २७८ ।। विचिकित्सा' न कर्तव्या प्राणै: २०७६ कण्ठगतैरपि ।। २८१ ।। ०७८ अलिना पश्चिमं मार्ग सिद्ध्यते नात्र संशयः । १०७९ १०८० १०८१ नासौ कुलक्रमे शिष्यः' स पशुर्योगिनीकुले' ।। २८२ ।।१०८२ एवं हर्षविहीन तु यो जपेत् पश्चिमं क्रमम्' १०८५ १०८४ । पराङ्मुखं भवेत् तस्य कुलभ्रंश च दारुणम् ।। २८३ ॥ पूजितं निष्फल तस्य भवते नात्र संशयः । ०८७ तस्य दर्शयतेऽज्ञानं न मन्त्रं न च मण्डलम् ।। २८४ ।। न क्रमं न कुलं कौलं रहस्यं तु प्रगोपयेत् । १०८९ यागभूमौ प्रवेश तु न दद्याच्च कदाचन' परिहार्य प्रयत्नेन मशक ९० परिवर्जयेत् । प्रस्तारमागम तस्य न दर्शेत९२ कदाचन •१०९१ सर्वशङ्काविनिर्मुक्तो वीरपानाभिनन्दकः । १०९४ १०९३ ।। २८५ ॥ ।। २८६ ।। ।। २८७ ।। स एव योग्यतामेति पश्चिमे कुलशासने ' पशुत्वं च स्मृता शङ्का न पशुः प्राणिषु क्वचित् ।
english: CHAPTER FORTY-SIX 399 He attains fame and acclaim in this world and the status of a Hero. (He experiences) intense energy (dīpti) in (his) body and (obtains) the wealth of mastery (over all things). He spends his time in the play of pasionate love (kāma). (That spiritual) son (putraka) gets whatever he desires. The next world (to which he is destined) is pure and the adept (sādhaka) attains liberation. (277-279ab) O Lord of the gods, one should drink (only after) having completed the prescribed procedure for the liturgy of the sacrificial liquor (alikrama), namely, the libation of the deities and the others. (In this way) one attains supreme success (siddhi). (279cd-280ab) No success is visible in the Western (Tradition) without (drink), the (sacrificial) substance Heroes (vīradravya) (offer). On this Siddha Path that substance (artha) is called `meat and wine' (aliphalgu). One should not feel doubt (vicikitsā)154 (in any circumstance about offering it) even when (one's) vital breaths are (at one's very) throat. The Western Path is accomplished by means of liquor (ali) — there is no doubt about it! (280cd-282ab) He who repeats mantras but does not in this way possess the joy (harna)155 (that comes from the sacrificial drink) is a fettered soul in the Yoginīkula; he is not a disciple belonging to the Kula transmission (kulakrama). The Western Transmission is averse (parā‰gmukha) to him and he suffers a terrible fall from the Kula. (282cd-283) What he has worshipped is certainly fruitless for him. Ignorance is shown to him, not mantra nor the maSÆala, not the Transmission, nor the Kula or Kaula. (Indeed) one should keep the secret hidden (from him). (284-285ab) Never allow (him) to enter the sacrificial ground (yāgabhūmi). Having abandoned (him) with effort, one should avoid (him) like a gnat. One should never show him the scripture (āgama) or the sacred grid (prastāra). (285cd-286) Only he who is free of all doubts and praises the drinking of Heroes becomes fit (to be a part) of the Western Kula teaching. The fettered state is said to be doubt (śa‰kā).156 (In reality), there is no fettered soul anywhere amongst living beings. (287-288ab)

sanskrit: 400 कुमारिकाखण्ड: १०९८ पशुभाव परित्यज्य कुलकौलं समभ्यसेत् ।। २८८ ॥ कुलकौलपदें प्राप्ते कुतः शङ्का कुतो मलम् । विचरेत् स्वेच्छया मन्त्री न भयं भवसागरे ॥ २८९ ॥ ११०० एकपात्रं न कर्तव्यं यदि साक्षात् कुलेश्वर: । ११०१ मन्त्राः पराङ्मुखा यान्ति विघ्नानि च पदे पदे ।। २९० ।। शशाङ्कमध्यगा तन्वी १०२ उन्मना मनवाहिनी' निरानन्दपदे लीना सा सुरा न सुरा सुरा ११०७ ११०४ ११०३ । ।। २९१ ।। मया च गोपित०५ मार्ग न बाह्ये प्रकटीकृतम् । मानुषा नैव जानन्ति तेन ते पशवः स्मृताः' सर्वदेवर्षिसंघैश्च गुह्यकैः सिद्धकिन्नरैः । मयापि धारिता”०९ कण्ठे तथा नागगणैर्वरै: ११०८ ।। २९२ ।। ।। २९३ ।। १११० १११२ सुरा सुरतमानन्द १९१९ सुरा कामाख्यसंभवा' । सुरा सुरतकाले तु सुचक्रं योगिनीस्थितम् ।। २९४ ।। कर्णिकाया च या वामा पराभामृतवाहिनी । -१११३ सा सुरा देहजा श्रेष्ठा नित्यानन्दकरी शुभा ।। २९५ ॥ १११४ -१११५ 'तया' पूज्य क्रमं कौल १६ सुखविज्ञानमुद्रया १११७ । तृप्यते परमं ब्रह्म ११९ पशुमध्ये न कारयेत् ॥। २९६ ।। तद् रहस्यं सदा गोप्यं गोपनात् कौलिनी सिद्धि: ११२३ ११२२ विद्यासमयसंयुक्तः यः पिबेन्मुद्रया युतः ।। २९७ ।। मण्डलाग्रे तु ता१२४ पीत्वा विद्यापीठस्य चाग्रतः । स याति परम१२५ स्थानं कुलानां तारयेच्छतं ।। २९८ ।। ।
english: CHAPTER FORTY-SIX 401 (Thus) abandoning the feelings of the fettered state (paśubhāva), one should practice Kula and Kaula. Once one has attained the plane of Kula and Kaula, where is doubt? And where is impurity? The reciter of mantra moves (freely) according to his own desire. (For him) there is no fear in the ocean of phenomenal existence. (288cd-289) (Even) if one is Kuleśvara (himself), directly visible, one should not dine with others (who belong to a different tradition) (ekapātraˆ na kartavyam).157 The mantras (of one who does so) become averse (to him) and (he encounters) obstacles at every step. (290) The slender (beautiful young) woman who resides in the centre of the Moon is the Transmental (unmanā) who transports the mind. Merged in the plane of the Bliss of Stillness (nirānanda),158 she is (the goddess) Wine (Surā).159 (Mere) wine is not (the true) wine. (291) I have hidden (this) path. It has not been revealed outside (the circle of initiates). People do not know this and so they are said to be fettered souls. All the troupes of gods and sages, Guhyakas, Siddhas, Kinnaras and the excellent hosts of Nāgas drink their fill (of wine) as I myself do.160 (292-293) Wine (surā) is the joy of sex (surata). Wine is born of what is called passion (kāmākhya). During sex, wine is the (fluid) in the beautiful Wheel (sucakra) within the Yoginī.161 The woman (vāmā) who is in the calyx (of the Wheel) and transports the nectar of the Supreme Light is the wine born in the body. It is most excellent, gives eternal bliss and is auspicious.162 (294-295) One should worship the Kaula Transmission with that (wine) by means of the Gesture of Blissful Consciousness (sukhavijñāna). (In this way) the Supreme Brahman is satisfied. (296abc) One should not cause this to be done in the midst of the uninitiated (paśu). That secret should always be kept hidden. By hiding it, (one achieves) Kaulinī Siddhi. If one who is linked to the Samayā Vidyā drinks (wine making the ritual) gesture, having drunk it in front of the maSÆala and the sacred seat of wisdom (vidyāpī˜ha), he attains the supreme place (sthāna) and he saves a hundred Kulas. (296d-298)

sanskrit: 402 कुमारिकाखण्ड: आत्मक्रमं सुसंज्ञात्वा ११२७ ११२६ ततः पानं समाचरेत् । पात्र सूर्योदयं ध्यायेत् मन्त्रं चन्द्रोदयं पिबेत् ।। २९९ ॥ तन्मध्ये चिन्तयेद् बिन्दुं पद्मरागसमप्रभम् -११२९ -११३० ११२८ । । परामृतसुसंपूर्णी २९ कला सप्तादशीं पिबेत् ॥ ३०० ॥ ११३४ महाभैरवतेजो १३२ वै१३३ तत्कलागलितामृतम्' । -११३५ ११३६ तन्मद्य देवदेवेश न यद् द्राक्षेक्षुसंभवम् ।। ३०१ ।। योगपानं पिबेन्मद्यं परावस्था च मैथुनम् । नादबिन्दुः परं मांस योगी योगेन भक्षयेत् ॥ ३०२ ॥ ११३८ नादेनानन्दचित्तेन स्वबुद्ध्योदधिमन्थनम् । ११४१ शून्यनेत्रप्रकर्षोऽयं यत्तद्धौत• रसायणम्' ॥ ३०३ ॥ नैवेद्य १४२ मानसं कार्य११४३ आनन्द ११४४ पानग११४५ प्रिये । ११४८ । ।। विद्यात् कमलभ्रूमध्ये४६ क्षेत्रे”४७ श्रीबिन्दुभैरवीम् ।। ३०४ ।। परविज्ञानतिलके”४९ उदयं मन्त्रकोटिषु' । ११५० एतद् देव तवाख्यात“ विक्षेपानन्दमुत्तमम् ।। ३०५ ।। सर्वसिद्धिकरं देव ज्ञात्वा सर्वं समाचरेत् । ११५३ ११५२ इत्याद्यावतारे महामन्थानभैरवयज्ञे अन्वये सप्तकोटिप्रमाणे मेरुमार्गविनिर्गते” लक्षपादाधिके विद्यापीठमार्गे विमलषट्कनिर्णये १३ कादिभेदे आज्ञापारमेश्वरे स्वामिनीमते श्रीचतुर्विंशत्सहस्रसंहिताया ४ अव्वाक्रमभाषिते१५५ विक्षेपा– धिकारमाहात्म्यवर्णने १५६ क्रमोदयो नामानन्दः ।। ४६ ।।
english: CHAPTER FORTY-SIX 403 Once he has understood his own Transmission (ātmakrama) well, (the initiate) should practise drinking (pāna). He should contemplate the cup as the dawning Sun and the mantra as the dawning Moon and (then) drink. He should imagine that the Drop, the colour of a ruby, is in between them. Drink the (energy of this), the seventeenth digit (of the Moon), completely full of the Supreme Nectar. (299-300) The nectar that flows from that energy (kalā) is the radiant power (tejas) of the Great Bhairava. O Lord of the god of the gods, that is (the true spiritual) liquor (madya), not that produced from grapes and sugar cane.163 (301) Drink the wine (madya) that is the drink of Yoga. While sexual intercourse (maithuna) is the Supreme State. (The couple) Sound and the Drop (nādabindu) is the supreme meat (māˆsa) the yogi should eat by means of Yoga.164 (302) The ocean of one's own intellect is churned by (divine) Sound (nāda), that is, the blissful mind (ānandacitta). This is the excellence of the Eye of the Void namely, that the alchemical potion (rasāyaSa) is washed by that. (303) One should make a mental food offering (naivedya). O dear one, (spiritual) bliss is in the drink. One should know the venerable Bhairavī of the Drop (bindu) in the field in the lotus between the eyebrows. The arising (of the deity) within tens of millions of mantras takes place when the mark (tilaka) of supreme consciousness (on the forehead has been made).165 (304-305ab) O god, this, the most excellent bliss of emission (viknepa),166 has been explained to you. O god, it gives rise to all (forms of yogic) accomplishment. Do everything (only) once this has been understood. (305cd-306ab) This is the (forty-sixth) chapter which is the emergence of the transmission (kramodaya) with regards to the description of the Glory of Emission (viknepādhikāramāhātmya). It belongs to the primordial descent into the great sacrifice of the Churning Bhairava in the tradition (anvaya) that consists of seventy million (verses) that has emerged on the Path of Meru and (extends) for more than a hundred thousand quarter (verses). It is on the path of the Seat of Knowledge (vidyāpī˜ha) and is the ultimate purport of the Pure Six Thousand (verses) (vimalana˜ka) in the division beginning with `Kā' in the venerable scripture of twenty-four thousand (verses) (known as) the Svāminīmata of the Supreme Lord's command as uttered within the Tradition of the Mother (avvākrama).

sanskrit: सप्तचत्वारिंशानन्दः श्रीनाथ उवाच हर्षदेवस्य माहात्म्य' विधानं च यथाक्रमम् । ज्ञातमद्य स्फुतं भद्रे वटुकं च न मे श्रुतम् ॥ १ ॥ किं तस्य वटुकत्वं हि कुत्रोत्पन्न' वरानने । किं तेन पूजितेनैव कथं बलिनिवेदनम् ।। २ ।। ७ एतन्मे वद देवेशि ध्यान पूजा यथाक्रमम् । श्रीवक्रा उवाच' षण्मुखो वटुकेन्द्रस्तु मम पुत्रो महाबलः ॥ ३ ॥ अधिकार मया दत्तं समस्ते' कुलशासने । १३ स्वामिना च महात्मना बलिभाग प्रगृह्यते ॥ ४ ॥ यावन्न दत्तं वटुकें तावन्नैव कुलाग । १७ कपिलोग्रमहारूप जटाजूट तु धारिणम् ॥ ५ ॥ पिङ्गाक्षं दण्डहस्तं च सर्पीभरणभूषितम् । नानासंविघ्नसंघातं पुरतः परिभावयेत् ।। ६ । श्रीनाथ उवाच वटुकस्य विधानं तु मया ज्ञातं कुलेश्वरि । अपरं श्रोतुमिच्छामि क्षेत्रपालागमं यथा ॥ ७ ॥
english: CHAPTER FORTY-SEVEN The Description of the Practice of the Rule The Visualized Form of Va˜uka Śrīnātha said: O auspicious one, today I have clearly understood the greatness of (wine) the God of Joy (Harnadeva) and the prescribed procedure concerning it in due order. But, I have not heard about (the procedures concerning) Va˜uka (the Child). What is his condition as a child? O fair faced one, where did he originate? What is the purpose of worshipping him? How is animal sacrifice (bali) offered (to him)? O mistress of the gods, tell me this, (his) visualised (form) (dhyāna) and rite of adoration, in due order. (1-3ab) The venerable (goddess) Vakrā said: The Lord Va˜uka has six faces. Greatly powerful, he is my son. I have given (him) authority over all the Kula teaching. The great souled Lord accepts (his) part of the animal sacrifice (bali). It is not offered to the Kula scripture if it has not been (first) offered to Va˜uka. (3cd-5ab) He is big, fearsome and tawny, (his) hair is matted and (his) eyes are brown. He carries a staff in his hand and is adorned with snakes as ornaments. He overcomes the mass of the many obstacles before (him).1 (5cd-6) The Fifty Guardians of the Field (Knetrapāla) Śrīnātha said: O Kuleśvarī, I have understood the procedure prescribed for Va˜uka. I want to hear something else, namely, the tradition (āgama) concerning the guardians of the field (knetrapāla). (7)

sanskrit: 406 श्रीवक्रा उवाच २२ कुमारिकाखण्डः अधुना शृणु वक्ष्यामि महावीरेन्द्रवन्दित । यथा ते प्रतिबुध्यन्ति वर्णराशिं वदाम्यहम् ।। ८ ॥ तेषां“ नामानि वक्ष्यामि एकैकस्य पृथक् पृथक् । अधुना आसुरिश्चैव इन्द्रगर्भस्तथा परः ।। ९ ॥ ईश्वर उग्रतेजश्च ऊष्माकरो” रिपुघ्नकः । निरीहश्च” तथा देव लिप्ताङ्गो लीनमस्तकौ ॥ १० ॥ एकाम्रकस्तथा ऐन्द्र ओघवाहस्तथापरः । औषधिस्तम्रवर्णश्च विसर्गख्यः परोऽनघः ॥ ११ ॥ कन्थकारश्च गोपालोऽपस्मरश्च तथापरः । ४१ व्योमश्च वक्रनाम च च्छेदको जन्मदाहकः ।। १२ ।। ऋषिश्च” औत्तरो” टङ्कठोऽण्डदेहश्चण्डवरः” । ५० दृढकर्णेण चोत्तानः पाण्डुदीमनमेव च ॥ १३ ॥ धर्मारम्भो नलो नाम पलितान्तोऽथ पुंस्कृतः” । बृहद्वक्षो भवाण्डश्च मतोऽह्लादो यमान्तकः ॥ १४॥ रक्ताक्षो लम्बबाहुश्च वक्षायतः” शशिस्तथा” । षठः५३ समाधिर्हंसाख्यः क्षपान्तकस्तथापरः ।। १५ ।। एते वै क्षेत्रपालाश्च कौलनामा: प्रकीर्तिताः । असंख्याताश्च देवेश ज्ञातव्याः साधकोत्तमैः ॥ १६ ॥ ५६
english: CHAPTER FORTY-SEVEN 407 The venerable (goddess) Vakrā said: O you who are praised as the great lord of heroes, now listen as I explain (this to you). I will tell (you) how they awaken the aggregate of letters. I will now tell you their names, each one separately. (8-9ab) 1) Āsuri, then 2) Indragarbha (Containing Indra), 3) Īśvara (Lord), 4) Ugratejas (Ferocious Energy), 5) Ūnmākara (Warm Form), 6) Ripughnaka (Destroyer of Enemies), 7) Nirīha (Desireless) and, O god, 8) LiptāSga (Smeared Limbs), 9) Līna (Merged) 10) Mastaka (Head), 11) Ekāmraka, 12) Aindra and then 13) Oghavāha (Transport of the Current), 14) Aunadhi (Medicinal Herb), 15) TamravarSa (Copper Colour), the one called 16) Visarga (Emission) who is supreme, 17) Anagha (Sinless), 18) Kanthakāra (the Patch Quilt Maker), 19) Gopāla (Herdsman) and then 20) Apasmara, 21) Vyoma (Sky), the one called 22) Vakra (crooked), after which comes 23) Cchedaka (Splitter), 24) Janmadāhaka (Burner of Re-birth), 25) ¬ni (Sage), 26) Auttara (Northern), 27) Ta‰ka˜ha (Axe), 28) ASÆadeha (Egg Body), 29) CaSÆavara (Most fierce), 30) Uttāna (Expanded) along with 31) DrÆhakarSa (firm Ear), 32) PāSÆu (White), 33) Dāmana (Subjugation), 34) Dharmārambha (Beginning of Dharma), 35) Nala, 36) Palitānta (End of Wrinkles), 37) Puˆskrta (Man Made), 38) Brhadvakna (Broad Chest), 39) BhavāSÆa (Egg of Phenomenal Being), 40) Mata (Doctrine), 41) Ahlāda (Joy), 42) Yamāntaka (Destroyer of Death), 43) Raktākna (Red Eyed), 44) Lambabāhu (Long Arms), 45) Vaknāyata (Wide Chest), 46) Śaśi 47) Śa˜ha (Cheat), 48) Samādhi (Concentration), the one called 49) Haˆsa (Gander) and then 50) Knapāntaka (Destroyer of Darkness). (9cd-15) These, indeed, are the guardians of the field (all of) whom are said to have Kaula names. O Lord of the gods, the best of adepts should know that they are without number. (16)

sanskrit: 408 कुमारिकाखण्ड: नीलाञ्जननिभाः सर्वे रक्तान्तायतलोचनाः । ।। उन्मत्ता विह्वला:“ सर्वे पिबन्ति मदिरासवम् ॥ १७ ॥ कपालेन विचित्रेण मुण्डमालैरलङ्कृताः” । ६१ महाशवशिराम्भोजमालिनो योगिनीप्रियाः ॥ १८ ॥ प्रेतस्कन्धसमारूढा वीरेशा वीरवन्दिता: । ६३ ६२ बलिप्रदाने पूजायां सर्वे ते वरदायकाः ।। १९ ॥ यावन्न ज्ञायते देव क्षेत्रपालविधानकम्¨ । तावद् विघ्नानि भूयन्ते साधकानां न संशयः ॥ २० ॥ श्रीनाथ उवाच क्षेत्रपाला मया ज्ञातास्त्वत्प्रसादेन ६ भैरवि ६७ । अधुना श्रोतुमिच्छामि शिष्याणां तु हिताय वै ।। २१ ।। दीक्षितस्य सुशिष्यस्य नाममाला कथं वद । ७० श्रीवक्रा उवाच ७२ ७४ शासने३ दीक्षितानां तु शिष्याणां भक्तितत्पराम् ।। २२ ।। अभिधानं यथा तेषां कर्तव्यं च तथा शृणु ७५ ७६
english: CHAPTER FORTY-SEVEN 409 They are all like dark blue collyrium and their eyes are long and red inside. They are ecstatic (unmatta) and, troubled (by passion), they all drink the wine of grapes. (17) They are adorned with garlands of human heads and a beautiful (vicitra) skullcap. The lotus garland they wear on their heads is made of (the heads of) Brahmin corpses (mahāśava) and they are dear to the Yoginī. (18) Praised by the heroes, they are their lords and are seated on the backs of ghosts. When, in the course of worship (pūjā), animal sacrifice (bali) is offered, all of them bestow boons.2 (19) O god, there is no doubt that as long as the ritual procedure concerning the guardians of the field is unknown, (even) adepts are faced with (great) obstacles (20) Initiatory Names Śrīnātha said: O Bhairavī, by your grace I have known (who) the guardians of the field are. Now in order to benefit (our) disciples tell (me) the list of names (that may be given to) an initiated disciple. (21-22ab) The venerable (goddess) Vakrā said: Listen to the names (the teacher) should give to devout disciples initiated into the teaching.3 (22cd-23ab)

(Thus), O god, I have told you (their) letters and names. They should not be told or given (freely). (I have) revealed them out of love for you. I was not (the first) to declare them but (I) have heard (them) from the mouth of Himavat. english: CHAPTER FORTY-SEVEN 413 The venerable (goddess) Vakrā said: O god, listen, I will explain the practice of the Rule. The list of (possible) names (that can be given to) an initiated disciple has been revealed. After this, one should make him hear the Rule (in the way) I am about to explain (to you).4 (26cd-27) This is the (forty-seventh) chapter called the Description of the Practice of the Rule (samayācāra). It belongs to the primordial descent into the great sacrifice of the Churning Bhairava in the tradition (anvaya) that consists of seventy million (verses) that has emerged on the Path of Meru and (extends) for more than a hundred thousand quarter (verses). It has been brought (down to earth) into the first sacred seat along the path of the Seat of Knowledge (vidyāpī˜ha). It is the ultimate purport of the Subsequent Six Thousand (verses) of the Pure Division (vimalabhedottarana˜ka) in the division beginning with `Kā' in the venerable scripture of twenty-four thousand (verses) (known as) the Svāminīmata of the Supreme Lord's command as uttered within the Tradition of the Mother (avvākrama).

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER THIRTY-ONE 1. Similar definitions of initiation are found in virtually all the manuals and Āgamas of the Siddhānta and indeed in Tantras of all schools. Most of these definitions are in the form of didactic etymologies of the roots dā ‘to give’ and kna ‘to destroy’. Abhinavagupta also says that these are the defining characteristics of initiation (dānaknapaSalaknaSā dīknā PTv p. 14). Similarly, Knemarāja defines initiation as ‘the destruction of the fetters and the bestowal of Śiva’s plane’ (comm. SvT I p. 13). Brunner has collected examples of such definitions from the Siddhānta Āgamas (see SŚP III p. 3-4). Four out of five of them agree with our text that what is given (dīyate) by initiation is the essence of knowledge. Similarly, what is destroyed is bondage. This is variously described as the ‘cage of sin’ (Suprabheda, caryāpāda, 4/1cd), the three impurities (Cintya, T. 14, p. 338, AVS, T. 7, p. 77), the latent trace of karma (Mrgendra, kriyāpāda, 8, comm. on the first verse) and that of the fetters (comm. SvT 5/88a). It thus purifies the Self (Mrgendra ibid.) and bestows knowledge (AVS ibid.). Abhinavagupta quotes a similar verse from the Siddhāntāgamas which says: ‘Initiation is said to possess the attributes of giving and destroying. It gives the essence of knowledge and destroys all impurity by piercing (the soul) with awakened consciousness (bodhānuvedha)’ (PTv p. 14). The Kaula Tantras agree with the Siddhānta. The KaulārSavatantra declares: ‘As the touch of purified and processed mercury changes iron into gold, so does the soul touched by initiation become Śiva . . . Initiation burns away all Karma. It severs the bond of Māyā and bestows the attainment of supreme knowledge. The adept is thus freed from the seeds of Karma (dagdhabīja) and attains Śivahood’. All Śaiva and Kaula schools agree that the individual soul acquires knowledge to the degree in which he is purified of the fetters that limit his consciousness. This is the function of initiation. As Knemarāja explains: ‘The one Great Light of the blissful Bhairavic fire burns the series of forests of evil bonds, by virtue of the activity of the knowledge (imparted by) initiation’ (SvT intro. verse to chapter 4). Higher spiritual states are attained according to the degree in which the soul is purified. Thus Abhinava states that: ‘initiation is a process whereby the principles of existence are purified (thus) it is the means of attaining Śivahood’ (TS p. 3). Jayaratha explains that it is ‘a process of imparting real knowledge and preceptorial instruction that removes the bondage of the fetters. Such benediction and benevolent action is called initiation’ (TĀ vol. I (KSTS), p. 80). Initiation is not only essential in order to practice the recitation of mantras or perform rituals, it is also a prerequisite for the practice of Yoga (na cādhikāritā dīknāˆ vinā yoge ‘sti śāˆkare — comm. TĀ 4/42). However, although the Kashmiri teachers agree that initiation is essential, they also maintain that it may take place through direct insight into the nature of

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER THIRTY-ONE 36 within mantra in the sphere of Sound. Then once known at the End of Sound, that is called `recollection' (smaraSa). `Recollection' is said to be Śakti who `comes and goes'. At the end of Śakti is the subtle, supreme energy (kalā) and that is Nectar (amrta). It is beyond merger, formless and known of itself (svayaˆvedyā) by desisting from thought. O goddess, it has no characteristic, no mark, it is not destroyed nor does it grow; it is neither black nor white, it is devoid of night and day, sandhyā, ayana, vinuva and saSkrānti. Consciousness arises once one has known the condition (gati) of all states. O beloved, this is the Kaula Umāmaheśvara. By repeating the Moving One 100,000 one certainly flies up into the air. Motion (calā) is said to be power uttered by the (reality) which is the mark (of consciousness). She is said to be Mālinī who is without letters (avarSā) and conjoined to them. Once she is associated with the individual parts (pada of the mantra), O fair faced one, she is without number. (KMT 5/92-100ab) 63. The word ‘piSÆa’ literally means a ‘conglomeration’ or ‘ball’ and so, by extension, a ‘body’. I suppose piSÆa here means the kulapiSÆa, that is, the aggregate of fifty letters that make up the body of Kula. Thus the ‘belly of the body’ is the Yoni full of the phonemic energies of Speech (see above 2/34cd- 35ab). 64. See ±SS 3/48 ff. concerning the many evils of this, the Age of Strife. Cf. above, 6/175-177ab and below 69/24-25ab where we are told that the kingdom of the barbarians will be in the North. It is clear that the reference here is to Muslim rule. See Dyczkowski 1986: 9-11 and 98 and discussion in intro. vol. 3, p. 297 ff..
