english: CHAPTER SIXTY-EIGHT 337 One should perform the worship of the Transmission (krama), repetition of mantra and Yoga by means of this body, as one contemplates up to the end of (all) the planes (of existence), beyond that inner mental organ. (21) (Anyone) anywhere who does not possess (knowledge of) the visualized form of (the goddess) Kujā and does not have (access) to the tradition of (the goddess) Kujā (but nonetheless) worships the Transmission, is a fettered and impure soul. (22) For such a one, the Vidyā and the KramamaSÆala — all is useless and the hereafter is uncertain. As long as one does not worship (and serve) the Kula, how can one have (the experience of) pervasion within (this), the Śāmbhava Kula? (23-24ab) The Sūtra concerning Liberation (muktisūtra)15 The venerable (god) Kaulīśa said: O mistress of the God of the gods, I have heard the entire purport of the scriptures. I now wish to hear the teaching of the Sūtra concerning Liberation (muktisūtra), merely by knowing which one is freed from the bondage of phenomenal existence. (24cd-25) The venerable (goddess) Kubjikā said: O Lord of the gods, I will tell (you) a very lucid path to liberation. You should keep it extremely hidden and it should not be given to (just) anybody. (26) The Sixteen Mata Tantras (The Mata Tantras are): the Picumata Tantra, the Siddhayogeśvarīmata Tantra, the Śivādūtīmata Tantra, the Vāmeśvarīmata Tantra, the Sundarīmata Tantra, the Ratnasundarikāmata Tantra, the Mātrmata Tantra, the Rūpikāmata Tantra, the Sārasvatamata Tantra, the MaSgalāmata Tantra, the Śikhottaramata Tantra, the fine Mālinīmata Tantra, the great Ambāmata16 Tantra, the Khecarīmata Tantra, the Bhairavīmata Tantra, and the venerable Kulālikāmata Tantra.17 The Matas (common to) the three lineages (oli) make a group of six * * * * * which is clear. (Then there are) the five independent (Tantras) concerning the Krama and the five causes (kāraSa)18 that are above - such are your sixteen Matas. (27-32ab)

sanskrit: 338 कुमारिकाखण्ड: १७१ ।। ३२ ।। १६३ स्फुट क्रमाधिकाराणि निरालम्बानि पञ्च च ।। ३१ ।। १६४ कारणाः पञ्च ऊध्वस्था: ६५ एवं ते मतषोडश १६७ १६९ १६६ । आद्यारभ्य समनान्ते स्वे स्वे तत्त्वे तु व्यापकाः सकलावरणे शम्भो ते समनावधिस्थिताः । ७५ १७२ महच्छब्दमत:¨३ पूर्वं विमलं षट्कनिर्णयम् ।। ३३ ॥ पराषट्कावतार तु जात्युत्तीर्णं हि षड्विधम् । महामायोदरातीतं तन्त्रस्योपरि सर्वदा ॥ ३४ ॥ १७८ उलीना पश्चिमाम्नायं स्वाधिकारं क्रमोदयम् । १७९ a मायातीतं समनोवै अंशके ९ प्रथमोदय' -१७९b १८२ ।। ३५ ।। अवतारं पुरा जात भेदें मन्थान भैरवे । शाम्भवाज्ञाविनिष्क्रान्त कादिभेदं सतार्णवम् ।। ३६ ।। येन विज्ञातमात्रेण सर्वज्ञत्वं युगे युगे । १८७ १८८ खण्डत्रयविधानज्ञ: ँ चतुःपादक्रियावित् तु ।। ३७ ।। १९० कादिभेदक्रमे युक्तः स भवेन्मतबोधक: ९९ मन्त्रमण्डलनिर्मुक्तो” योगभ्रष्टः स९३ विज्ञेय:' १९५ १९४ । आकाशे कुसुमं यथा । आज्ञाचक्रविनिर्मुक्त: षोढाशक्तिविवर्जितः १९८ १९७ संसारे वर्तते भूय:”“ संसारान्न” निवर्तते । अदत्वालि विधानेन समयाज्ञाविवर्तित : २०२ २०३ २०१ भुञ्जते सततं यस्तु भुञ्जते नरकत्रयम् । ।। ३८ ।। । ॥ ३९ ॥ ।। ४० ।।
english: CHAPTER SIXTY-EIGHT 339 Starting from the beginning up to the end of the Equal One (samanānta) they (each) pervade their own (corresponding) (metaphysical) principle. O Śambhu, established up to the end of the Equal One (samanā), (they are present) in all the spheres (of existence) (sakalāvaraSa).19 (32cd-33ab) The Supreme Scripture After that (comes) the Great Sound (mahacchabda). It is the teaching concerning the first pure group of six (na˜kanirSaya), which is the descent of the Hexad of the Supreme (parāna˜ka)20 which is beyond the six types (of Vedic syllables) (jāti).21 Beyond the belly of Mahāmāyā, it always stands above the Tantra.22 (33cd-34) Of the lineages (uli), it is the Western Tradition, the arising of the Transmission (kramodaya) which is authoritative in itself. Beyond Māyā, it is the first emergence (prathamodaya) within (the Transmental) aspect (of the deity) which is above the Equal One. (35) The descent (of the teaching) has taken place in the past within the division (of the tradition called) Manthānabhairava (the Churning Bhairava). It is the division beginning with `KĀ',23 the ocean of truth, that has emerged from Śiva's Command (śāmbhavājñā), merely by knowing which (initiates attain) omniscience in every Age. (36-37ab) The one who knows the methods prescribed in the three sections (of the Manthānabhairavatantra)24 and the ritual (kriyā) of (its) four parts and is intent on the transmission (krama) (taught) in the division beginning with `KĀ', is one who awakens to the teaching (mata). (37cd-38ab) The Sūtra concerning the Observance of the Rule (samayānun˜hānasūtra)25 One who does not have mantra or (know) the maSÆala should be known to be one who has fallen from Yoga. (His practice is as ineffective) as a sky-flower. Devoid of the Wheel of the Command (ājñācakra)26 and (Vāgbhava) the energy of the six (noÆhāśakti),27 he goes on living in the world of transmigration again (and again) and he does not quit it. (38cd-40ab) One who is devoid of the Command of the Rule and has not offered wine (to the deity) in the prescribed way and is constantly indulging in worldy experience (bhuñjate), (eventually helplessly) suffers (bhuñjate) the (agony of the) three hells. (40cd-41ab)

sanskrit: 340 कुमारिकाखण्डः २०४ स्नानत्रयविनिर्मुक्तो यस्तु पूजयते क्रमम् ॥ ४१ ॥ समयात्मा महामूढो भुञ्जते नरकत्रयम् २०७ २०६ । गायत्रीत्रयनिर्मुक्तो विद्यातद्ग्रहवर्जित २८ ॥ ४२ ॥ षडुत्थमण्डलोत्तीर्ण:०९ संसारान्न निवर्तते । •२११ २१० सु–उल्यां”” गुरुगुह्यं तु निर्बीज पूजयेत् तु यः २१४ २१६ संसारे वर्तते भूयः ४ संसारान्न ५ निवर्तते । २१८ २१३ ।। ४३ ।। कादिभेदक्रमेऽयुक्तः”७ खटिकाद्वारवर्जितः ।। ४४ ।। प्रस्तारषोडशोत्तीर्णः१९ अधिकारान्न मुच्यते । .२२० उन्मनादिक्रमेणैव यावत् श्रीनाथचिञ्चिणी श्रीनाथचिञ्चिणी २२१ । ४५ ॥ पुष्पसंकेतकं शम्भो अज्ञात्वा नैव” मुक्तिभाक् । समयानुष्ठानसूत्रम् २२३ श्रीनाथ उवाच कथं २२४ बौद्धे २२५ च देवेश च देवेश २५% आरहन्ते कथं कथम् ।। ४६ ॥ २२७ वैष्णवे तु कथं सौरे २२६ शैवे मुक्तिः कथं कथम् । वामदक्षिणमार्गेषु कथं च २२८ २२९ २३० मालिनीकुले ॥ ४७ ॥ मुक्तिमार्गं त्रिके देवि कथं नित्याक्रमेषु च । २३२ ।। कथं मुक्तिस्त्रिखण्डाख्ये कालिकायाः क्रमे कथम् ।। ४८ ।।
english: CHAPTER SIXTY-EIGHT 341 One (who belongs to) the Rule (but), greatly deluded, cause the Transmission to be worshiped without having taken the three baths (at the three times of day) suffers (the pain of) the three hells. (41cd-42ab) He who is devoid of the three Gāyatrī (mantras) (uttered at the three times of day), the Vidyā and Tadgraha and (considers himself to have mastered and be) beyond the maSÆala generated from the six (parts), does not get out of the world of transmigration. (42cd-43ab) He who belongs to a good lineage (uli) (but) does not worship the teacher's secret (deity) with the (prescribed) seed (syllables) remains in the world of transmigration and does not leave it. (43cd-44ab) One who is not intent on the Krama (taught in the Manthānabhairavatantra of) the division beginning with `KĀ' and is devoid of the (sacred) chalk (kha˜ikā)28 (with which the grid of letters is drawn that is) the door (which gives access to the mantras) and is beyond the sixteen grids (prastāra) (of letters),29 is not freed from (the lower levels of) responsability. (44cd-45ab) O Śambhu, without having known the Convention of the Flower (punpasaˆketaka) that extends in due order from the Transmental (unmanā) up to Śrīnātha and CiñciSī, one is not liberated.30 (45cd-46ab) (This is) the Sūtra concerning the Observance of the Rule (samayānun˜hānasūtra). The Consecration of Yoga: The Hierarchy of the Traditions and the Stages of Realisation31 Śrīnātha said: How is liberation amongst the Buddhists and, O lord of the gods, amongst the Jains (ārahanta), the VainSavas, the worshippers of the Sun (saura) and the Śaivites? How is it on the paths of the Right and the Left and in the Mālinī Kula? O goddess! how is the path to liberation in (the teaching of the) Trika? And (how is it) in the transmissions of the (goddess) Nityā? How is liberation in the (scripture) called TrikhaSÆa (`the one having three sections')32 and in Kālikā’s Krama?33 (46cd-48)

sanskrit: 342 कुमारिकाखण्डः २३३ मुक्तिर्वै अमरिकाम्नाये तथा श्रीवक्रिकामते । २३६ २४० । तस्य३४ ऊध्वे२३५ यतो नास्ति मुद्रा मण्डलकं क्रमम् ।। ४९ ।। तदेच्छा २३७ शाश्वती २३८ व्याप्तिः सावधिः २३९ परिकीर्तिता तत्राधो—आगमा चैव यावद् बौद्धं तु दर्शनम् ॥ ५० ॥ यतस्तद् बुद्धितत्त्वं तु न सा मुक्तिस्तु सावधिः । • २४५ २४३ २४९ ।। ।। २४४ तेषां निरवधि: २४६ प्रोक्ता २४७ शान्ते २८ त्वात्मनि संस्थिता ॥ ५१ ॥ २५० संतोषेण' तु ये नष्टा अहंकारेण तु २५१ गर्विताः । तदा तेषां पुनर्जन्म संसारो न २५२ निवर्तते २५३ ॥ ५२ ॥ एवं मुक्तिस्वरूपेण कुजान्ते५४ भावयेत्५५ सदा । इति संक्षेपत:५६ प्रोक्तं देहियोगाभिषेचनम् श्रीकौलिन्युवाच ५८ अतिप्रश्नोत्तर५९ गुह्यं त्रिदशैरपि दुर्लभम् । । ॥ ५३ ॥ कथयामि निःसंदिग्धं° तव स्नेहेन कौलिकम् ॥ ५४ ॥ २६१ .२६२ २४ a धरातत्त्वात् पुरुषान्तं ऊध्वे २३ माया तु विज्ञेया । सत्त्वशुद्धात्मरूपा च अष्टवर्गक्रमे स्थिता ।। ५५ ।। २६४ २६६ तदूव६५ ईश्वरं तत्त्वं तस्योध्वे तु सदाशिवम् । २६७ । शिवं तस्योपरिस्थं तु व्योमव्यापी निरञ्जनम् ।। ५६ ।। इत्यार्णव महादण्डं शिवाद्यवनिगोचरम् •२७३ । तस्योध्वे २७२ पञ्चधा शाक्त ध्वनिरूपादितः क्रमात् ॥ ५७ ॥ दण्ड¨५ । २७४ समनावधिपर्यन्तं तावद् दण्डं महोदयम् ।
english: CHAPTER SIXTY-EIGHT 343 Liberation is indeed (to be found) in the tradition (āmnāya) of (the goddess) Amarikā (the Immortal One) and in the venerable Vakrikāmata. As there is no Krama, Mudrā or maSÆala above it, then the will, which is perpetual pervasion, is said to be `with limit' (sāvadhi).34 There, below are the traditions (āgama) (that are progressively inferior) up to the system (darśana) of the Buddhists. As (the latter corresponds to) the principle of the intellect, that liberation is not ‘with limit’.35 (49-51ab) The (liberation) they possess (although) located within the tranquil Self is said to be limited (niravadhi). Those who are destroyed (and fall from the path) by being satisfied (with merely this level of attainment), arrogant with pride, are then reborn and the world of transmigration does not cease. One should always contemplate (the reality) within (the goddess) Kujā in this way as the essential nature of liberation. The consecration (abhinecana) of the Yoga of the embodied soul has thus been explained in brief. (51cd-53) The Three Sticks The venerable (goddess) Kaulinī said: The answer to (this) question is extremely secret and hard to get even by the gods. (But) because of (my) love (for you) I will tell you (about this) Kaula (reality) which is free from doubt.36 (54) (The lowest level extends) from the Earth principle up to the Person. One should know that above that is Māyā. It is the pure Self of sattva (the quality of purity)37 and is (located) in the sequence of the eight classes (of the letters of the alphabet). (55) Above that is the Īśvara principle and above that (the principle of) Sadāśiva. Śiva, stainless (nirañjana), is above that, pervading the Sky (of pure consciousness) (vyomavyāpin). (56) This is the Ocean, the Great Stick, the field of which (extends) from Śiva (up to) the Earth. Above that is the fivefold empowered (nature) (which extends) from the Resonance (dhvanirūpa) onwards, in due order, up to the Equal One (samanā). Such is the (second) Stick, the Great Arising (mahodaya). (57-58ab)

sanskrit: 344 कुमारिकाखण्ड: २७६ •२७७ कलातीतं परानन्दं तृतीयं दण्डनायकम् ॥ ५८ ॥ भरणाद् भैरवाकारं शाम्भवं दण्डमुच्यते । २७९ १२८० एवं दण्डत्रय७८ ज्ञात्वा तस्य ऊवे निरामयम् ।। ५९ ।। एवं व्याप्य स्थितं शान्तं सर्वज्ञं सर्वगं परम् । २८२ २८३a द्विविधा तु स्मृता मुक्तिः सावधि: २ ज्ञेयवेदिनाम् निरवधिस्त्वन्या २८४ मुक्ति: क्रियाज्ञानविदात्मनाम् । ।। ६० ।। प्रथमा ८५ पौरुषं तत्त्वं २६ मायातत्त्वं द्वितीयका ८७ ।। ६१ ।। २८८ २८९ तृतीया शुद्धविद्या च चतुर्थी ईश्वरोपरि । २९२ पञ्चमी सदाशिवान्ते” षष्ठी मुक्ति: शिवावधि: ॥ ६२ ॥ शक्त्यान्ते२९३ सप्तमी प्रोक्ता समनान्ते तथाष्टमी । च२९८ ।। ६३ ।। दशैका९४ मुक्ति:९५ क्लिन्नान्ते त्रिखण्डान्ते च द्वादशी २९९ ३०१ ३०२ त्रयोदशी च कल्पान्ते आद्यन्ते तु चतुर्दशी । त्रिपञ्चमी कुजान्ते तु द्वाचत्वारिंशती पुरे ३०५ ३०४ ॥ ६४ ॥ निष्कला या परा विद्या निरौपम्या षडक्षरा । सकले ६ षोडशी प्रोक्ता मुक्तिरेषा प्रकीर्तिता ।। ६५ ।। ३०७ स्थिता षोडशभेदैस्तु ं निरवधित्वे“ व्यवस्थिता । ३१० तस्यान्ते सा परा मुक्ति: शून्यान्ते तु लयं गता ।। ६६ ।।
english: CHAPTER SIXTY-EIGHT 345 Beyond the units of energy (kalā) is supreme bliss which is the Master of the Sticks (daSÆanāyaka), the third. (This) Stick is said to be Śiva's plane (śāˆbhava) and (its) form is Bhairava because it fills (all things) (bharaSa). (58bcd-59ab) Once one has known the Three Sticks in this way, (one realises) the (supreme) faultless (reality) above that and, having thus pervaded (all things), it abides tranquil, omniscient, omnipresent and supreme.38 (59cd-60ab) Liberation With and Without Limit Liberation is said to be of two kinds. (There is one) `with limit', which is that of those who who know (the ultimate reality) that should be known. The other is the liberation that is `without limit'. It is (the state) of those who know the scriptures (jñāna) and (the correct performance and full experience of) ritual (kriyā). (60cd-61ab) The first (type of liberation corresponds to the realisation of the true nature of) the principle of the Person and the second to the principle of Māyā. The third is Śuddha Vidyā (Pure Knowledge), the fourth is above Īśvara, the fifth is within Sadāśiva while the limit (avadhi) of the sixth (degree of) liberation is Śiva. The seventh is said to be within Power (śakti) and the eighth in the Equal One (samanā).39 (61cd-63ab) The eleventh (degree of) liberation (occurs) within the (goddess) Klinnā (the Wet One) and the twelfth within (the goddess) TrikhaSÆā (Three Parts). The thirteenth (is attained) at the end of an Aeon (kalpānta) and the fourteenth at the beginning and end (of one). The fifteenth (takes place) within (the goddess) Kujā in the City of the Forty-two (syllable Vidyā).40 (63cd-64) The incomparable and supreme Vidyā of Six Letters (is located therein) and is the (aspect) without parts (ninkalā). The sixteenth (energy of the Moon) (noÆaśī) is said to be (within the aspect) which has parts (sakala) and that is extolled as (ultimate) liberation. (65) She is established within (the liberated condition) without limit with (her) sixteen divisions. Supreme liberation (is attained) in the end of that when she dissolves away into the Void. (66)

sanskrit: 346 कुमारिकाखण्ड: अन्तःशून्यात्मिका”” शक्ति: शून्ये शून्यत्वमागता५ । यदा न किञ्चिद् विद्येत सावधिः परिकीर्तिता ।। ६७ ।। ३१६ तस्य ऊध्वे” परं भावं भावातीतं परं पदम् । मन्त्रध्यानविनिर्मुक्त”” मुद्राक्रमविवर्जितम् ।। ६८ ॥ ३२१ परान्तं तु निराधार सर्वध्यानविवर्जितम् । यागक्रियासमुत्तीर्णं बिन्दुभेदविवर्जितम्” ।। ६९ ।। करणत्रयनिर्मुक्तं हेयोपादेयवर्जितम् । अस्तिनास्तिविनिर्मुक्त” अवस्थानन्दवर्जितम् ।। ७० ।। निस्तरङ्गं परं शान्तं निरानन्दं निराश्रयम् । परशून्यं महाशून्यं परान्तं शाम्भवं पदम् ३२५ ।। ७१ ।। •३२६ मुक्तिमार्गं द्विधा भिन्नं साकार तु निरञ्जनम् । ३२८ उपर्युपरिसंस्थस्य साकारस्य न निश्चयम् ।। ७२ ।। यदा शून्यावधिर्नास्ति अस्वतन्त्र तदा भवेत् । कथं धत्ते परां मुक्तिं यावत् शून्यावधिर्न” हि । ।। ७३ ।। I अन्वयावधिः३ शून्यान्ते परे प्राप्ते निरामये ५ । अन्वयज्ञानमाश्रित्य३५ पराषट्के तु साधिते ।। ७४ ।। ३३७ यावदोवे ३९ परे जन्म मन्त्रमार्गे महेश्वर ३४९ । ३४२ तावत् तु शाश्वती‍ मुक्तिरवधिरेषा प्रकीर्तिता ३४४ ।। ७५ ।। एवं मुक्तिस्वरूपं तु शून्यतत्त्वादि पौरुषम् । पौरुषं शून्यमाख्यातं माया तस्यैव शून्यता ।। ७६ ।।
english: CHAPTER SIXTY-EIGHT 347 She is the power which is the inner Void who, within the Void, has become emptiness. If one knows nothing, then she is said to be `with limit'.41 (67) Above that is Supreme Being, while the Supreme Plane is beyond (phenomemal) being. It is devoid of mantra, meditation, mudrā and the Krama. (68) (Located at the ultimate) extremity of the supreme (reality), it is free of supports and all meditation. It is beyond the sacrificial rites, free of the divisions of the Point (bindubheda),42 devoid of the three instruments (of mantra) and (of all that) should be taken up or abandoned. (69-70ab) Free of being and non-being, it is devoid of the (various forms of) bliss (pertaining to the series of yogic) states. Waveless and supremely tranquil, it is the Bliss of Stillness (nirānanda),43 free of support. It is the Supreme Void, the Great Void, the extremity of the supreme (reality), (in short) the Śāmbhava plane. (70cd-71) The path to liberation is of two kinds, namely, With Form (sākāra) and Stainless (nirañjana). (The path) With Form developes increasingly upwards and does not reach an ultimate conclusion (niścaya). (72) If (a sphere of reality does not) culminate in the Void, it is not free (and independent) (asvatantra).44 How can it give supreme liberation if (it) does not terminate in the Void? (73) The culmination (avadhi) of the tradition (anvaya) is (realised) within the Void, when the supreme, faultless (reality) has been attained, (that is,) when having taking the support of the knowledge (transmitted by the) tradition, the group of six of the Supreme (goddess) (parāna˜ka) has been attained. (74) O Maheśvara! Liberation is permanent to the degree in which one is born into the superior (reality) above (the other ones) on the Path of Mantra.45 (This kind of liberation) is said to be ‘with limit'.46 (75) Such is the liberation pertaining to 1) (the principle of the) Person and commencing with the Void. (Indeed), the Void is said to be that of the Person and 2) Māyā is its emptiness. (76)

sanskrit: 348 कुमारिकाखण्ड: तथेश्वरं भवेच्छून्य ततः शून्यं सदाशिवम् । शिव३४६ सर्वगतं शून्यं नादान्तं शून्यमुच्यते ।। ७७ ।। ३४९ कारणं व्यापिनी शून्यं समना तस्य शून्यता । भैरवान्तं स्मृतं शून्यं शून्यं वै भैरवीपदम् ।। ७८ ।। वीरावलीपदं शून्यं कालिकाक्रम शून्यता । ·३५१ ३५२ ३५० ३५३ शून्यममरिकाम्नायं कुजान्ता यस्य शून्यता ।। ७९ ।। द्विचत्वारिंशतीशून्य संचरान्ते ५५ ह्यधिस्थितम् ५६ । ३५७ तत्रोध्वे परं शून्यं निस्तरङ्गं तु शाम्भवम् ।। ८० । ३५८ मन्त्रविद्याविनिर्मुक्तं हेयोपादेयवर्जितम् । •३६० ३६१ कुजान्ते त्ववधि: ३५९ प्रोक्ता मन्त्राणां नास्ति संग्रहम् ॥ ८१ ॥ तदधो निरवधिस्तु`‍ संबन्धमुत्तमोत्तरम् । ३६४ ३६५ मन्त्राणां तु यदा जातं षड्विधाज्ञा महत्परा ॥ ८२ ॥ •३६६ शान्तेच्छा कारणं शून्यं शून्याम्नायमिदं स्फुटम् । स्थितं षोडशभेदैस्तु तस्यावधिर्न विद्यते ।। ८३ ।। •३६८ यदा ध्यानात्मक६७ भाव मन्त्रमुद्राविभेदितम् । ३७० ३७१ जाप्यार्चनरतं नित्यं मोक्षमेतन्निरवधिः ।। ८४ ।। स्थिता पौरुषतत्त्वादि शान्तेच्छा यावत् कारणम् । अस्वतन्त्र७२ समाख्यातं ध्यानत्यागे ३ विनश्यति ॥ ८५ ॥ मन्त्रत्यागं॰ विना शान्तं मुमुक्षूणां तु दुर्लभम् । ३७६ यत् तच्छान्तं परं शून्यं सर्ववयववर्जितम् ॥ ८६ ॥ ३७७ ३७८ यत् तत् स्थानं कुले ध्यानं मुद्रामन्त्रा लयं गताः ।
english: CHAPTER SIXTY-EIGHT 349 Similarly, 3) Īśvara is the Void and the (principle of) 4) Sadāśiva is the Void. 5) Śiva is the omnipresent Void and 6) the End of Sound is (also) said to be the Void. (77) 7) The cause which is the Pervasive One (vyāpinī) is the Void. 8) The Equal One (samanā) is its emptiness. 9) The Void is said to be within Bhairava. 10) The Void is indeed the plane of Bhairavī. 11) The plane of the line of Heroes (virāvalī) is the Void and 12) the Kālikākrama is (its) emptiness. 13) The tradition of (the goddess) Amarikā (the Immortal) is the Void and 14) its emptiness is within (the goddess) Kujā. 15) The Void (of the goddess who is the Vidyā of) Forty-two (syllables) is established at the end of (the fettered soul’s) wandering (saˆcara). 16) The supreme Void which, waveless, is the Śāmbhava (plane), is there above.47 (78-80) Free of mantra and Vidyā, it is devoid of (all that needs to be) taken up or abandoned. The culmination (avadhi) of (all) mantras is said to be at the extremity of (the goddess) Kujā (kujānta),48 (where there is) no accumulation (saˆgraha) (of anything). (81) Below that is (the form of liberation corresponding to the reality) `without limit'. When the relationship between the mantras (is ordered in such a way) that the subsequent one is higher than the preceding, (then) the sixfold Command is (realised to be) eminently supreme. (82) The tranquil will is the (primal) cause which is the Void. This is clear teaching concerning the Void (śūnyāmnāya). Established with (its) sixteen divisions, it has no limit.49 (83) If a meditative state of being obtains, associated with mantra and Gesture, that form of liberation, which is constantly intent on the repetition of mantra and worship is `without limit'. It abides as the tranquil will that extends from the principle of the Person up to the (primal) cause. (84-85ab) (The sphere of existence) that is said to lack autonomy (asvatantra)50 is destroyed when meditation is abandoned (upon reaching the supreme state). Without abandoning mantra, it is hard to attain the tranquil (reality that is the goal) of those who desire liberation. (85cd-86ab) That tranquil (reality) is the supreme Void, free of all constituent parts. Within Kula, that place (sthāna) is (where) meditation, Gestures and mantras have dissolved away. (86cd-87ab)

sanskrit: 350 कुमारिकाखण्ड: पूजाजाप्यविधान” च द्रव्यानुष्ठानपञ्चकम् आज्ञाक्षोभलयं यत्र अणिमादिगुणाष्टकम् । ३८० ।। ८७ ।। भूत्यागं धारणावेधं मुद्रास्फोटादिप्रत्ययम् ।। ८८ ।। अतीतानागतं चैव वर्तमानं चिरायुष्यम्” । यदा न विद्यते यत्र तन्मोक्षं शाश्वतमजम् ।। ८९ ।। इच्छान्ते तु ध्रुवं शान्तं यत्र सर्वे लयं गताः । सावधिस्तु समाख्याता स्वतन्त्रं सर्वतोमुखम् ।। ९० ।। ३८७ प्राप्तत्यागं यदा नास्ति नान्यं भवति किञ्चन । ३८८ •३८९ प्रभुत्वं सर्वजन्तूनां शान्तमित्यक्षरं द्वयम् ।। ९१ ॥ तावत् क्रिया:” प्रवर्तन्ते दर्शनानां पदे पदे ९२ । तावदाक्रम्य९३ मन्त्राणां क्रियायुक्तिर्विधीयते ॥ ९२ ॥ परान्ते तु पदे प्राप्ते क्रियाज्ञानी निवर्तते । ३९६ तावत् ज्ञानक्रियाव्याप्तिर्निरवधि: ५ परिकीर्तिता ॥ ९३ ॥ यावन्न९७ सावधिं प्राप्य शान्तावस्था प्रपद्यते । •४०० तत्क्रियाज्ञानरहितं” कुजान्तं शाम्भवं पदम् ।। ९४ ।। तथान्तरहितं‍ ज्ञानं क्रियामार्गेण विद्यते । •४०४ शान्तं ज्ञानं क्रियाहीनं पूजा ध्यानं न विद्यते ।। ९५ ।। क्रियाज्ञानेन अभ्यासादिच्छातीतः प्रवर्तते । सिद्धमार्गप्रपन्नानां ै अन्ते ज्ञेया तु सावधि: ४०७ ।। ९६ ।। ४०१
english: CHAPTER SIXTY-EIGHT 351 The group of five, namely, the rite of adoration, the repetition of mantra, the prescribed (rites), the (sacrificial) substance and attendance (on the diety), (also cease there) where the disturbance brought about by the Command comes to an end. The eight (yogic) powers (guSa), including the ability to make oneself small at will (aSima) and the rest, (the power of) flight, the piercing by means of concentration (dhāraSāvedha), (every) sign of accomplishment (pratyaya), such as the (power to cause) explosions by gesturing (mudrāspho˜a), the past, future and present, longevity - when and where (all this) does not exist, that liberation is unborn and eternal. (87cd-89) The tranquil and stable (dhruva) (reality is attained) when desire ceases; where all things have dissolved away. (That is) said to be (the form of liberation) `with limit'. (It is the reality that is) free (svatantra) and omnipresent. (90) If that which has been attained (is never again) abandonded (and lost) and nothing else at all exists, (one has attained reality) which is the power (prabhutva) of all living beings (expressed by) the two syllables `tran-' and `-quil' (śānta).51 (91) The rites (kriyā) of (the various) schools (darśana) operate at every step and, as long as one has reached only a certain level (tāvat) (literally, `this much'), the practice of mantras is required. (But) once the plane which is the extremity of the supreme (reality) (parānta) has been attained, the knower of action quits (the world of transmigration) (nivartate). (92-93ab) The pervasive presence of knowledge and action is said to be `without limit' until the tranquil condition prevails once the (liberation) `with limit' has been attained. Devoid of that knowledge and action, the Śāmbhava plane is (located at the) extremity of (the goddess) Kujā. (93cd-94) Again, the knowledge without end is obtained by means of the path of action. Tranquil knowledge is devoid of action - there is no meditation or rite of adoration. (95) (The reality) beyond desire arises by practicing with knowledge of (inner) action (kriyājñāna). At the end (the liberation) of those who are intent on the path of the Siddhas should be known to be `with limit'. (96)

sanskrit: 352 कुमारिकाखण्ड: सा च सोपानशक्तिस्तु अजान्ते” अनुगम्यते । सोपानेन विना”? मुक्तिः शून्यमार्गे ? तु दुर्लभा ।। ९७ ।। सावधिस्तु क्रमान्ते वै शून्यान्ते तु लयंगता । कन्दुकं तु यथा गच्छेन्मुष्टिना तु समाहतम् ॥ ९८ ॥ आकाशं गहनं५ यस्मान्मिथ्याचारेण साधकः । ४१६ ४१७ ४१८ ४१९ तद्वत् सावधिमोक्षान्ते निराचारपदे स्थित: ।। ९९ ।। •४२० आमूलाद् यावत् शाखाग्र कर्कटो ४१ वोपसर्पति४२२ । तथा श्रीश्रीक्रमं प्राप्य परान्तमनुवर्तते ।। १०० । ४२३ साधकः सर्वभावज्ञो बौद्धमार्गीदितः क्रमात् । ४२४ । आरुहेत् क्रमशो मूर्ध्नि बहुजन्मान्तरेष्वपि ॥ १०१ ॥ कुजाम्नायपदं प्राप्य परान्ते तु लयं व्रजेत् । ४२६ न तस्य पुनरावृत्तिरधो २५ जन्मनि जन्मनि ॥ १०२ ॥ बौद्धशास्त्रादितः सर्वं यावत् कुलालिकामतम्” । ४२९ । अन्योन्यगुणयोगेन यस्य क्रिया निवर्तते ॥ १०३ ॥ सावधेस्तु पदं प्राप्य क्रिया तस्य निवर्तते । ।। । तावत् क्रियारूढो” मन्त्री वृक्षन्यानेन कर्कटः ।। १०४ ।। मन्त्रातीतपदं प्राप्य४३३ तदा शास्त्रं४ परित्यजेत् ५ । ४३६ । साकारस्य विनाशोऽस्ति मुद्रापञ्चक्रमेण तु ॥ १०५ ॥ निराकारस्य शान्तस्य मुक्तिरित्यक्षरद्वयम् । ज्ञात्वा सकलसारं‍ तु परित्यजेत् ।। १०६ ।।
english: CHAPTER SIXTY-EIGHT 353 The power of the ladder (that leads to liberation) is understood (only) at the end of the Unborn. Without a ladder, liberation is hard to attain on the path of the Void. (The liberation) `with limit' has dissolved away at the end of the Krama within the Void. (97-98ab) Stages of Realisation: The Hierarchy of Teachings Just as a ball struck by the fist goes (up) into the vast (gahana) sky from that (place below), similarly, the adept resides on the plane beyond the bounds of scriptural injunction (nirācāra) at the end of the liberation `with limit' by virtue of (his) deceitful practice (mithyācāra) (by which he cheats bondge). (98cd-99) Or else, just as a Karka˜a plant creeps (upwards) from the root to the top of the branches (of a tree), similarly, once (the initiate) has obtained the venerable Śrīkrama, he (goes on) to reach the extremity of the supreme (reality). (100) The adept who knows all the states of being should gradually ascend in stages from the Buddhist path onwards to the top, even if (this takes place) in the course of many lives. (101) Once attained the plane of (the goddess) Kujā's tradition, he dissolves away at the extremity of the supreme (reality). He does not return again below, life after life. (102) He whose action and every (teaching) from (that of) the Buddhist scriptures up to the Kulālikamata has ceased by the mutual conjunction (yoga) of (their) qualities, (all) his (remaining) action ceases once obtained the plane (of liberation) `with limit'. The reciter of mantra is mounted on action to this extent (as is the) Karka˜a plant according to the maxim of the tree (and the creeper entwined around it). (In short), once attained the plane beyond mantra, one should then abandon scripture. (103-105ab) (The aspect) 'with form' is destroyed by the sequence of the five Gestures. The two lettered (word) 'mukti' (i.e. liberation) (refers to the reality) of the tranquil (aspect) without form. Once know the essence (of the deity) with form (sakala) * * * * one should abandon (it). (105cd-106)

sanskrit: 354 कुमारिकाखण्डः ४४० । न जन्मैके भवेद् व्याप्तिः परे४२ शान्ते निरामये । शास्त्रव्याप्तिविधानेन‍ मुक्तिमार्गमतः परम् ।। १०७ ।। ४४४ ज्ञात्वा सम्यग्विधानेन तदा ऊध्वगति: ५ भवेत् ४६ । •४४८ बौद्ध बुद्धिपदं मोक्षं आरुहन्तं गुणत्रयम्॥ १०८ ॥ ४४९ प्रधानं वेदवादीनां चतुर्वेदविदात्मानाम् ” । •४५० पौरुषं सौरवादीनां सांख्यानां परमं पदम् ।। १०९ ।। मौशलायुधहस्तानां मायातत्त्वं परं पदम् । शुद्धज्ञानमया विद्या वैमलानां परं पदम् ॥। ११० ।। अष्टप्रमाणवेदज्ञा५३ लाकुलार्थविशारदाः ४५४ । व्रते पाशुपते चैव ऐश्वरं परमं पदम् ।। १११ । •४५७ नवनित्यागमज्ञानां५६ शिवतत्त्वं परं पदम् । ४५९ ४५८ तदूवे कारणाः पञ्च त्यक्त्वा ऊर्ध्व ४६० तु४६१ भैरवम् ।। ११२ ।। ४६५ । साष्टतन्त्रतान्त्रिकानां४६२ नित्यानन्द४६३ प ४६४ पदम् परं समनान्तकलातीतं वामदक्षिणसंस्थितम् ।। ११३ ॥ पंक्तिक्रमेण मोक्षोऽस्ति सत्यं नास्त्यत्र संशयः । ४६७ तस्य ऊर्ध्व पराषट्कं उपर्युपरिसंस्थितम् ।। ११४ ।। ·४६९ षडारं प्रथमं भेद‍ भैरवाख्यं द्वितीयकम् । वीरावली तृतीयं तु चतुर्थं कालिकाकुलम् ॥ ११५ ।। ततस्त्वाद्यावतारं तु तस्य ऊध्वमनाहतम् ।
english: CHAPTER SIXTY-EIGHT 355 Pervasion in the supreme, tranquil and flawless (reality) is not (achieved) in one lifetime. The path to liberation beyond this (is formed) by the prescribed method, namely, the pervasion of (all) the scriptures (in such a way that every scripture marks a place along the path). (107) Once known correctly by means of the prescribed method, (the adept) then moves along the upper path. Buddhist liberation corresponds to the plane of the intellect, (that of the) Jains, the three qualities. (108) Fundamental Nature (is the highest level) of those who adhere to the Veda and know the four Vedas. (The principle) of the Person is the supreme plane (pada) for the votaries of the Sun and and the followers of the Sāˆkhya. (109) The principle of Māyā is the supreme level for (the Pāśupatas) who carry a club in (their) hands as a weapon. The Vidyā consisting of pure knowledge is the supreme plane for the Vaimala (Pāśupatas). (110) Īśvara's plane is supreme for those who know the doctrine (veda) of the eight authorities (pramāSa) and, well versed in the teachings (artha) of Lākula, are (dedicated) to the Pāśupata vow. (111) The Śiva principle is the supreme plane for those who know the scriptures of the Nine Nityās. Above (these) are the (PraSavas, that is, the) five causes. Having abandoned (these also), Bhairava is (attained) above (them). (112) Eternal bliss is the supreme plane of the Tāntrikas who follow the Sān˜a Tantra.52 (The reality) established in the (Tantras) of the right and the left is beyond the energy at the end of the Equal One. Liberation takes place according to the (place one is) in the serial order (of the teachings of the various schools). This is the truth and there is no doubt here (about this).53 (113-114ab) Above that comes Parāna˜ka (the parts of which are) arranged in a hierarchy. The first division is the Six Spokes (naÆāra), the second is the one called Bhairava, Vīrāvalī (the Line of Heroes) is the third, the fourth is the Kālikākula,54 then comes the Primordial Descent (ādyāvatāra) and above it, Unstruck Sound.55 (114cd-116ab)

sanskrit: 356 कुमारिकाखण्ड: श्रीमत्कुलालिकाख्यं ? तु जातिभेदेन साम्प्रतम् तेष्वासौ आदिभेदं तु क्रमत्रयविवर्जितम् । तस्य ऊध्वे४७५ कादिभेदं सप्तकोटिप्रमाणकम् सूत्रसंग्रहमाख्यातं आदिनाथावतारितम् । ४७७ ४७६ ४७३ ।। ११६ ।। ।। ११७ ।। प्रधानं सर्वतन्त्राणां सप्तकोट्या विनिर्गतम् ॥ ११८ ॥ तत्सारं कोटिपादं तु लक्षपादाधिकं ततः । प्रमाणं सर्वशास्त्राणां विशेषं पश्चिमान्वये ॥ ११९ ॥ मयावतारितं तुभ्यं महाकुलालिकामतम् । क्रमोदय८२ समासेन मुद्रापीठोपरिस्थितम् ।। १२० ।। मन्त्रविद्यासमुत्तीर्णं जातिभेदविवर्जितम् । रजमण्डलनिर्मुक्त८५ सर्वध्यानविवर्जितम् ।। १२१ ॥ तन्त्राचारविनिर्मुक्त ँ साधिकार“ त्रयोलिषु । । सारात् सारतरं तस्माद्” दुग्धाद्” घृतमिवोद्धृतम् ।। १२२ ।। •४९१ जिनसंख्यागमं मूलं मूलान्वयक्रमागतम् । खण्डत्रयं”? पराषट्कं विशेषाज्ञावधिष्ठितम् ।। १२३ ।। •४९३ सिद्धसन्तानसंकाशं महाक्रमस्य शासनम् । ४९४ शुद्धात्मकस्य सिद्धस्य पूर्णिमान्ते स्थितस्य च ।। १२४ ।। प्रस्तारषोडशोत्तीर्णं ९५ आद्यपीठे तु उद्धृतम् ४९६ ४९७ शाम्भवं सरहस्यं तु आख्यातं तन्नपुंसकम् उत्तमं सर्वमार्गीणां बौद्धशास्त्रादितः क्रमात् । । ।। १२५ ।।
english: CHAPTER SIXTY-EIGHT 357 Kulālikā's Scripture and its Divisions56 Now (I will talk about the scripture) called the venerable Kulālika according to the division of (its various) types (jātibheda).57 (116cd) 1) Amongst them, the first division is devoid of the three Transmissions (krama).58 2) After that comes (tasya ūrdhve) the division beginning with `KĀ' the extent of which is seventy million (saptako˜i) (verses). It is called the `collection of Sūtras' and it has been brought down (into the world) by the First Lord (Ādinātha). It has emerged as the seventy million (verses) and is the main one of all the Tantras. (117-118) 3) The essence of that (is the scripture of) two and a half million (ko˜ipāda) (verses). 4) Then comes (the scripture consisting of) 125,000 verses. Amongst all the scriptures it is the (greatest) authority (pramāSa) and is particularly special in the Western Tradition. (119) 5) I have brought down (to earth) for you the great Kulālikāmata.59 It is, in short, the arising of the Transmission (kramodaya) and it stands above the Sacred Seat of Gesture (mudrāpī˜ha). Beyond mantra and Vidyā, it is free of the types (jātibheda)60 and the sphere of rajas and it is free of all (forms of) meditation, the practice of Tantra (tantrācāra) and it has authority in the three Lineages (oli). The essence of the essence, it is like clarified butter taken from the milk (of the scriptures). (120-122) The scripture numbering twenty-four (thousand verses) is the root. It has come down through the transmission of the root tradition (mūlānvayakrama). (Consisting of) three sections (khaSÆa), it is the Parāna˜ka (Parā's Group of Six) and is sustained by a special Command. (123) (This is) the teaching of the Great Transmission (mahākrama), luminous (saˆkāśa) with the Lineage (santāna) of the Siddhas. (It is the teaching) of the pure Siddha who resides at the end of the Full Moon. (124) Extracted in the First Sacred Seat, it is beyond the sixteen grids (prastāra) (of letters). That is the Neuter (absolute), said to be the Śāmbhava (plane) with (its) secret.61 It is the best of all paths beginning, in due order, with the Buddhist. (125-126ab)

sanskrit: 358 कुमारिकाखण्ड: •४९९ मालिनीविजयं कृत्वा यावच्छास्त्रं नपुंसकम् ।। १२६ ।। तावत् तेषां तु ते जाता भेदे भेदे पृथक् पृथक् । स्वस्थाने भवते मुक्तिर्मुनीना तु कुलान्वये महाक्रमपरस्यापि पदान्ते तु परं लय । ५०४ । ५०२ ।। १२७ ।। सावधिर्मुक्तिमार्गेऽस्मिन् कुजाम्नाये तु साधिते ।। १२८ ।। बौद्धमारहन्तं वेदं सौरं सांख्य च वैष्णवम् । योगव्रत च विमलं तथा पाशुपतं महत् ॥ १२९ ॥ शैवं तस्य विशेषं तु भैरवाष्टकनिर्णयम् । -५१० पराषट्क कुजान्तं च उपर्युपरिसंस्थिताः ।। १३० ॥ बौद्धशास्त्रमारहन्त १ तस्माद् वैदिकदर्शनम् । •५१२ वेदशास्त्रात् परं सौर“?? सौरात् सांख्य ३ च वैष्णवम् ।। १३१ ।। -५१५ योगशास्त्रं च बहुधा ततस्तूव महाव्रतम् । तस्माच्च वैमलं सारं प्रमाणाष्टौ च लाकुलम् ॥। १३२ ।। •५१६ ततः पाशुपत प्रोक्तं तस्माच्छैवमनेकधा १७ ' अतः परं तु स्वच्छन्द निष्कलं सकलं ततः ।। १३३ ।। बहुरूपमघोरीश“”” व्याधिभक्षं च भैरवम् । । चन्द्रगर्भं तु° विज्ञानं तुम्बुरुं चामृतेश्वरम् ।। १३४ ॥ ·५२१ क्रमेणापि षडर्थं स्यान्मालिनीविजय कुलम् । ऊध्वे५२२ क्लिन्नान्वयं योगं तस्यातीतं परं पदम् ।। १३५ ।। वीरावलीकुलाम्नायं अपरं कालिकाक्रमम् । ५२३ ततः कुलकपाटं तु आद्यमध्वानशासनम् ॥ १३६ ॥
english: CHAPTER SIXTY-EIGHT 359 The Hierarchy of Scripture and Teachings The Mālinīvijaya (Tantra) was created first of all, (and then the others) up to the scripture (concerning the) Neuter (absolute). They have arisen individually, in each of their (various) categories (of scriptures). The liberation of (those) sages who belong to the Kula tradition is in (accord with their) own level (of attainment) (svasthāna). Once the (teaching of) Kujā’s tradition has been attained, the supreme merger (occurs) at the end of (all the) levels in the case of one who is intent on the Great Transmission on this path of liberation `with limit'. (126cd-128) (The forms of liberation corresponding to the various schools) are arranged in an ascending hierarchy, (as follows):62 the Buddhist, Jain and Vedic (form of liberation), that of the Sun worshippers, the Sāˆkhya, the VainSava, (that of the) Vow of Yoga, the Vimala, the great Pāśupata, the Śaiva and the (liberation that is achieved by applying the) teaching of the group of eight Bhairava (scriptures) which is a special (Śaiva teaching), and (then) finally, (the teaching of the Tantras of the goddess) Kujā which is the Parāna˜ka, the Hexad of the Supreme (goddess). (129-130) (At the bottom is) the Buddhist scripture, (then comes that of) the Jainas and then the Vaidika school (darśana). The Saura (scripture of those who worship the Sun) is higher than the Vedic. Higher than the Saura (scripture) is the Sāˆkhya, the VainSava and the Yogaśāstra, which is of many kinds. Above that is (the Pāśupata scripture concerning) the Great Vow (mahāvrata). After that comes that the essence of the Vimala (school of the Pāśupatas) and the eight authorities (pramāSa)63 of the Lākula (Pāśupata). Then the Pāśupata is said (to come next) after which comes the Śaiva (scripture), which is of many kinds. (131-133ab) Higher than that (the scripture of) Svacchanda, who is (both) formless (ninkala) and with form (sakala), (also called) Bahurūpa, Aghorīśa, Vyādhibhakna (the Devourer of Disease) Bhairava, Candragarbha, and Vijñāna. (After Svacchanda’s scriptures come those of) Tumburu and Amrteśvara and (then), in due order, comes Trika (naÆardha) which is the Mālinīvijayakula. Above that (comes) the Yoga of the tradition of (the Goddess) Klinnā (the Wet One), beyond that is the supreme plane. Another is the tradition of the Vīrāvalī Kula and the Kālikākrama. Then (comes) the Door of Kula (Kulakapā˜a), which is the first teaching of the Path (adhvānaśāsana).64 (133cd-136)

sanskrit: 360 कुमारिकाखण्ड: ५२४ तत`४ एवं कुजाम्नायं हितार्थ“ शुद्धकौलिकम् । ५२६ तस्योध्वे तु निरानन्दं शान्तमित्यक्षरद्वयम् ।। १३७ ॥ ५२८ शाम्भवं शाश्वतं २७ मोक्षं क्रियाजालविवर्जितम् । मन्त्रोपदेशरहितं' •५२९ ।। १३८ ।। ५३१ ₹५३० प्राप्य सर्वावस्था भविष्यति । ५३३ बौद्धशास्त्रात् समारभ्य यावत् काद्यं नपुंसकम् ।। १३९ ।। परान्तमनुगच्छेत'' मन्त्रत्यागेन सर्वदा । ५३६ मुक्तिविशेषणमस्मिन्'३ ऊध्वाभ्यन्तरमद्वयम् ।। १४० ।। मुक्तिसंग्रहसूत्रेद कादिभेदात् परं नहि । ५३८ विदित्वा ज्ञायते मुक्तिः शास्त्राम्नाायेन” नान्यथा वेदसिद्धं पशोश्चोर्धव४९ ऊध्व ५४२ वामे ५४० ।। १४१ ।। ५४३ शुत्व । वामदक्षिणमार्गे तु दक्षिणाम्बिकनिर्णये ॥ १४२ ।। ।। ५४४ तं तु योभ्यर्त्तवे लीन ज्योति श्रीवक्रिकामते ४५ (?) । नातः परतरं किञ्चिदित्याज्ञा पारमेश्वरी ।। १४३ ॥ इत्याद्यावतारे महामन्थान भैरवयज्ञे अन्वये ४६ सप्तकोटिप्रमाणे मेरुमार्गविनिर्गते महामन्थानभैरवयज्ञे ५४७ लक्षपादाधिके आद्यपीठावतारिते विद्यापीठमार्गे विमलभेदोत्तरे षट्कनिर्णये कादिभेदे आज्ञापारमेश्वरे स्वामिनीमते श्रीचतुर्विंशत्सहस्रसंहिताया ४९ अम्बाक्रमभाषिते ५० ५५१ मुक्तिसंग्रहसूत्राधिकारो नामानन्दः ।। ६८ ।।
english: CHAPTER SIXTY-EIGHT 361 Then, in the same way, comes the tradition of the (goddess) Kujā, the pure Kaula (tradition that has been revealed) for the benefit (of the world). Above it is the Bliss of Stillness (nirānanda), (denoted by) the two syllables ‘tran-‘ and ‘— quil’ (śānta).65 (137) (That is) the eternal Śāmbhava liberation, free of the net of action and devoid of (any) teaching concerning mantra * * * * * * the universal state (sarvāvasthā) will prevail once (it) has been attained. (138-139ab) One should reach the culmination of the supreme (level of existence) (parānta) by constantly (and progressively) abandoning the mantras starting (with those of) the Buddhist scripture up to the Neuter, which is (the tradition) beginning with `KĀ'. The unique feature of liberation in this (tradition) is that it is the nondual (reality) at the very end, which is above (all others). (139cd-140) This is the Sūtra of the Compendium of Liberation. There is nothing higher than the division beginning with `KĀ'. One knows (what true) liberation is having learnt it by means of the scriptural tradition; not in any other way. (141) What is accomplished by the Veda is above (that of the scripture) the fettered soul; (of a Buddhist or a Jain) * * * * above on the left * * * (?) on the path of the left and the right in the teachings of the mother of the right. (142) * * * * * (?) the light in the venerable Vakrikāmata. There is nothing higher than this: this is the Command of the Supreme Goddess. (143) This is the (sixty-eighth) chapter named concerning the Sūtra of the Compendium of Liberation. It belongs to the primordial descent into the great sacrifice of the Churning Bhairava in the tradition (anvaya) that consists of seventy million (verses) that has emerged on the Path of Meru and (extends) for one hundred and twenty-five thousand (verses). It has been brought (down to earth) into the first sacred seat along the path of the Seat of Knowledge (vidyāpī˜ha). It is the ultimate purport of the Subsequent Six Thousand (verses) of the Pure Division (vimalabhedottarana˜ka) in the division beginning with `KĀ' in the venerable scripture of twenty-four thousand (verses) (known as) the Svāminīmata of the Supreme Lord's command as uttered within the Transmission of the Mother (ambākrama).

sanskrit: ऊनसप्ततितमानन्दः श्रीनाथ उवाच त्वं गुरुर्मम देवेशि अहं तव विचारणें' । रुद्रभैरववीराणां एषा आज्ञा न कस्यचित् ॥ १ ॥ मम मित्रत्वभावेन' कारुण्येन प्रकाशितम् । श्रीवक्रा उवाच ४ आज्ञापितस्तदा' देवः' आज्ञापरिग्रह प्रति ॥ २ ॥ श्रीकण्ठस्य महावृद्ध' दत्त' कृतयुगे क्रमम् । १७ प्रभवे वत्सरे मासे श्रावणे त्वसिताष्टम्याम् ॥ ३ ॥ बालस्यौल्यवतार तु ततस्त्रेतायुगे पुनः । २३ २४ दुर्वासस्य तु देवेश” ओड्डीशस्य त्वनुग्रहम् ॥ ४ ॥ .२८ २९ दत्तमोडामर तस्य क्रमं वीरावली स्फुटम् । वैशाखे त्वसिताष्टम्यां प्रमोदे” हितवत्सरे ॥ ५ ॥ द्वापरे षण्मुखस्यापि दत्तमाज्ञा त्वनुग्रहम्” । कौमाराख्यं व्रत दत्तं श्रीवत्से त्वसिताष्टम्याम् ।। ६ ।। चैत्रमासे मध्यमोल्यां” अवतारं युगे युगे । विदितं षष्ठनाथेन” ततः कलियुगे पुनः ॥ ७ ॥
english: CHAPTER SIXTY-NINE Conclusion The Siddhas, the Time of their Attainment and their Sacred Seats Śrīnātha said: O Mistress of the gods, you are my teacher (of the Tantra) and I am yours with regards to the reflection (vicāraSa) (on its meaning). Neither Rudra, Bhairava, the Heroes or anyone (else) possess this Command. (All this has been) revealed (to me) by virtue of your compassionate friendship towards me.1 (1-2ab) The venerable (goddess) Vakrā said: Then the god was permitted to receive the Command and the Great Transmission of the Aged (mahāvrddhakrama) was given to ŚrīkaS˜ha in the Krta Age during a Prabhava year2 in the month of ŚrāvaSa on the eighth of the dark lunar fortnight. (2cd-3) Then the descent of the Lineage of the Child (bāla oli) took place again in the Tretā Age. O Lord of the gods, (this is) the grace (given to) Durvāsa and OÆÆīśa. The immortal transmission of OÆa, which is the lucid (teaching of) the Vīrāvalīkrama, was given to him in the beneficial year of Pramoda3 on the eighth day of the dark lunar fortnight of the (month of) Vaiśākha. (4-5) In the Dvāpara Age, the Command, which is grace, was also given to ±aSmukha (Kārttikeya - the Six Faced One) (in the form of) the Vow called Kaumāra during the lunar asterism of Śrīvatsa on the eighth day of the dark lunar fortnight in the month of Caitra. (In this way the teaching has) descended into the Middle Lineage (madhyamoli) in each (Dvāpara) Age and was learnt by ±an˜hanātha.4 (6-7abc)

sanskrit: 364 कुमारिकाखण्ड: ४६ नन्दिरुद्रस्य सा आज्ञा” चर्याीनाथस्य त्वनुग्रहम्” । करोत्याज्ञा स्वयं सम्यक् ज्येष्ठानुक्रमयोगतः ॥ ८ ॥ ज्येष्ठोल्यामवतारं तु एवमोलिक्रमत्रये । ५२ ५० चतुर्थ सर्वसाधारं निरंशपदसंस्थितम् ।। ९ ॥ वीरावलीक्रम + ३ नाथ एवं क्रमचतुष्टयम् । ५७ ५५ ६५ .४८ भविष्ये ६ पञ्चमं नाथ कलौ अन्ते न संशयः ।। १० ।। क्षयसंवत्सरे जाते? शिवरात्र्यां चतुर्दश्याम् । श्रीमत्पिङ्गलरुद्रस्य मतङ्गीशात्मकस्य च ॥ ११ ॥ ६७ .६८ आज्ञासंक्रमण कृत्वा दत्तं तस्यापि खेचरम् । क्रम मूलान्वयं सारं दिव्यलिङ्गाद् विनिर्गतम् ।। १२ ।। लिङ्गोल्यामन्वय” सर्वं युगान्ते संभविष्यति । पञ्चानां युगनाथानां” आदिनाथ तु भैरवम् ।। १३ ॥ नवात्मानन्ददेवेश विद्याराजेश्वरेश्वरम् । ७९ श्रीकुजेच्छासमुत्पन्न श्रीकुजेश महात्मनः ॥ १४ ॥ कुचन्द्रशेखरो ं नाम समनान्ताद् विनिर्गतः” । ८२ .८३ इत्युत्सङ्गावतारं तु चन्द्रद्वीपे कुलाम्बिके ।। १५ ॥ इच्छानाथं स्थितं ह्येकं” आज्ञासिद्धैस्तु¨ पञ्चभिः । ८७ ९२ तेषां मध्यादोलित्रये अधिकारे स्थितास्त्रिभिः ँ ।। १६ ।। श्रीकण्ठ“ एष भगवान् मैत्रीभाव ं कृते गतः” । कामरूपे स्थितो यो” हि जन्तूनां तारणार्थतः ९६ ॥ १७ ॥
english: CHAPTER SIXTY-NINE 365 Then again in the Age of Strife, that Command belongs to Nandirudra5 and grace (was given to) Caryānātha. (Then) correctly and in accord with the Transmission of the Aged, the Command spontaneously gives rise to the descent (of the teaching) into the Lineage of the Aged in this way within the transmission of the three lineages. (8-9ab) The fourth (descent) is common to all and is located on the plane without parts (niraˆśa). O Lord, (it is) the Vīrāvalīkrama (the Transmission of the Line of Heroes).6 Such is the Fourfold Transmission (kramacatun˜aya). (9cd-10ab) In the future, at the end of the (Age of) Strife there will certainly be a fifth Lord (nātha). (His coming will take place) in the year (called) Knaya7 on the fourteenth (of the dark lunar fortnight) on Śiva's Night. Having transmitted the Command to the venerable Pi‰gala Rudra, who is Mata‰gīśa, the Transmission of the Skyfarer (khecara) was also given to him. (10cd-12ab) (This is) the Root Tradition (mūlānvaya), the essence (of it all) that has emerged from the Divine Li‰ga. At the end of the Age all the tradition (anvaya) will arise in the Lineage (oli) of the Li‰ga.8 (12cd-13ab) Out of the five Lords of the Ages, the First Lord (ādinātha) is Bhairava. He is the Lord of the gods (who delight in) the bliss of Navātman, the Lord of the lords of the king of Vidyās. (13cd-14ab) The venerable Kujeśa, born from the Great Self by the will of the venerable (goddess) Kujā is (the Bhairava) called Kucandraśekhara who has emerged from the extremity of the Equal One (samanā).9 (14cd-15ab) O Mother of Kula! This is the descent onto the Island of the Moon (of the god who) is united (with you) (utsa‰gāvatāra). The Lord of the Will (icchānātha) abides (thus) as one (accompanied) by the five Siddhas of the Command. (15cd-16ab) Kāmarūpa Three amongst them are established in authority in the three lineages (oli). This, the Lord (bhagavat) ŚrīkaS˜ha who feels loving friendship (maitrībhāva) (towards the goddess and the world)10 in the Krta Age, is the one who resides in Kāmarūpa in order to save living beings.11 (16cd-17)

sanskrit: 366 ९७ कुमारिकाखण्ड: पुरन्दरः ँ स भगवान्“ ओडुनाथः त्रिते युगे । १०५ जालन्धरे स्थितो यो हि वीराणां सिद्धिदायकः ॥ १८ ॥ श्रीकुमारः स भगवान् षष्ठनाथस्तु द्वापरें ०७ । पूर्णगिय स्थितों यो हि योगिना योगसिद्धिदः ११२ ॥ १९ ॥ नन्दिरुद्रः स”३ देवेश चर्यानाथः कलौ युगे । श्री ॐकारे १५ स्थितो१६ यो १७ वै१८ भोगमोक्षप्रदायकः ।। २० ।। १२१ १२२ दक्षिणाशा गतो यो हि श्रीमच्चन्द्रपुरे गृहे । युगान्ते पिङ्गलो नाम मतङ्गीशो महाबल: ।। २१ ।। आज्ञाहेतोस्तिस्रपीठे” पञ्चमं सिद्धनायकम् । १२५ •१२७ व्यापकं च१५ नवात्मानं अनादियुगसंस्थितम् ।। २२ ।। कुचन्द्रशेखरानन्द चन्द्रपीठे जगद्गुरुम् । १३० श्रीमित्रनाथादिसिद्धौघ” चन्द्रद्वीपाद् विनिर्गतम् ।। २३ ।। पश्चिमे” सिद्धसन्तान'३ पूर्वसन्तानवर्जितम्” । पश्चिमे तु युगे देव म्लेच्छराज्ये च उत्तरे ।। २४ ॥
english: CHAPTER SIXTY-NINE 367 Jālandhara Purandara is the Lord (bhagavat) OÆunātha12 in the Tretā Age who resides in (the sacred seat of) Jālandhara and bestows accomplishment (siddhi) to the Heroes. (18) PūrSagiri The venerable Kumāra is the Lord (bhagavat) ±an˜hanātha in the Dvāpara (Age) who resides in PūrSagiri and bestows success in Yoga to (true) yogis. (19) OÆÆiyāna O Lord of the gods, Nandirudra is Caryānātha (the teacher) in the Age of Strife who resides in the venerable (seat of) the letter O¤13 and bestows liberation and worldly enjoyment. (20) Tisra He who went to the southern quarter in the House of the venerable City of the Moon at the end of the Age is Pi‰gala who is the very powerful Mata‰gīśa. He is the fifth leader (nāyaka) of the Siddhas who, at (the goddess's) Command, (resides) in the sacred seat (called) Tisra. (21-22ab) Candra Kucandraśekharānanda, the bliss of the universe, (resides) in the sacred seat of the Moon. All pervasive, he is Navātman who is established (there) from beginningless aeons.14 (22cd-23ab) The current of Siddhas, beginning with the venerable Mitranātha, has emerged from the Island of the Moon.15 The lineage (santāna) of Siddhas in the (Tradition of the) West, is devoid of the previous lineage (pūrvasantāna).16 O god, it has (arisen) in the last (paścima) Age when the kingdom of the barbarians is in the north. (23cd-24)

sanskrit: 368 कुमारिकाखण्ड: १३७ a १३७b इतरे गुरुशिष्ये तु लोभमोहवशं गते । १३८ आज्ञावेशे ८ गते क्षीणे अधिकारे क्षयं गते ।। २५ ।। अवतारं करिष्येऽहं पञ्चमे पीठनायके । सिद्धस्तत्र मतङ्गीशः श्रीमातङ्गीसमन्वितः तत्रारभ्य महापूजा भविष्यति चतुष्टये । १४४ १४२ ।। २६ ।। इदं तथ्यं मया प्रोक्तं चतुर्विंशत्सहस्रकें ।। २७ ।। श्रीमत्कुमारिकाखण्डे षट्साहस्रे मतोत्तमे । । आदौ कुमारिकाखण्डं सिद्धखण्डं द्वितीयकम् ॥ २८ ॥ तृतीयमादिखण्डं तु चतुष्पादाः क्रमाद् विभो १४८ । । वृक्षोऽय” कुब्जिकादेव्याश्चतुर्विशत्सहस्रकम् ।। २९ ॥ शेषराजस्य हस्ते तु स्थापितं कारणार्थः । उक्तं देव्या'५१ त्विदं वाक्यं इदं यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः ।। ३० ।। तस्य अनुग्रह दास्ये वेधमाज्ञासमन्वितम् । तस्य'५३ देयमिदं शास्त्रं सामध्ये ५४ प्रकटीकृते ।। ३१ ।। नागराजेन शिरसा धृतमादेशपूर्वकम् । ततस्तु“ विश्वदेवेन सिद्धनाथेन भैरव ।। ३२ ।। आनीतोऽनुग्रहाथीय भक्तानां ताणीय च । ॐकारे तु महापीठे सिद्धयोगिन्यलंकृते ।। ३३ ॥ कनकमञ्जरी नाम” योगिनी च महाबला । स्थापित६२ तद्गृहे ज्ञानं कृत्वा समयपूर्वकम् ॥ ३४ ॥
english: CHAPTER SIXTY-NINE 369 When other teachers and (their) disciples have come under the sway of greed and delusion and the penetration of the Command (ājñāveśa) has ceased and authority come to an end,17 I will descend into the fifth lord of the sacred seat. (25-26ab) The Siddha there is Mata‰gīśa who is accompanied by the venerable (goddess) Māta‰gī. There will be a great rite of adoration beginning from there in the fourth (Age). (26cd-27ab) The Scripture of Twenty-four Thousand Verses I have spoken this truth in the venerable Section Concerning the Virgin Goddess (consisting of) six thousand verses (which is a part of the scripture of) twenty-four thousand (verses), the best of Matas.18 (27cd-28ab) In the beginning comes the Section Concerning the Virgin Goddess. The Accomplished Section (SiddhakhaSÆa) is the second one. The third is the First Section (ĀdikhaSÆa) and, O pervasive one, there are four parts (pāda) in due order.19 (28cd-29ab) This is the Tree of the goddess Kubjikā, namely, (the scripture of) twenty- four thousand (verses). It was placed in the hands of King Śena to serve as the cause (of liberation). (29cd-30ab) The goddess has said: “I will give the one who correctly understands this (my) grace and (the initiation by) piercing endowed with the Command.” (30cd-31ab) This scripture should (only) be given to one when (his) ability (to grasp and apply it) has become clearly evident. The king of the snakes sustains it with (his) head in accord with the orders (given to him by the goddess). (31cd-32ab) Then, O Bhairava, in order to grace and save the devotees (of the goddess), Siddhanātha, the god of all (viśvadeva), brought it into the great seat of the letter O¤ adorned with Siddhas and Yoginīs. The powerful Yoginī, Kanakamañjarī by name, (also) placed knowledge in that House in accord with the Rule. (32cd-34)

sanskrit: 370 कुमारिकाखण्ड: नाभिवर्तिरहीका ३ च वज्रसन्धि:१६४ कपाटयो: । १६५ संकेतान् वेत्ति योऽप्यत्र तस्य देय कुलागमम् ।। ३५ ।। अन्यथा नैव दातव्यमित्याज्ञा पारमेश्वरी । इत्याद्यावतारे महामन्थान भैरवयज्ञे अन्वये सप्तकोटिप्रमाणे मेरुमार्गविनिर्गते लक्षपादाधिके आद्यपीठावतारिते विद्यापीठमार्गे ६८ विमलभेदोत्तर— १७० षट्कनिर्णये कादिभेदे आज्ञापारमेश्वरे स्वामिनीमते चतुर्विंशत्सहस्रसंहिताया आम्बाक्रमभाषिते' श्रीमत्कुमारिकाखण्डं समाप्तं ।। ६९ ।। लक्षकोटिप्रमाणं तु मतं वै पारमेश्वरम् । एतस्मादुद्धृतं सारं सप्तकोटिप्रमाणतः ।। १ ॥ •१७४ सप्तकोट्या : ३ सारतरं लक्षपादाधिक ततः । १७६ एतस्मात्” सारतर ं स्याच्चतुर्विंशत्सहस्रकम् ॥ २ ॥ त्रिभिः खण्डैः कुजेशान्या मित्रस्यैव प्रकाशितम् । १७९ १८१ १७८ नन्दन्तु कुलयोगिन्यो नन्दन्तु कुलपुत्रकाः ॥ ३ ॥ नन्दन्तु” श्रीकुलाचर्या ये चान्ये कुलदीक्षिताः ।
english: CHAPTER SIXTY-NINE 371 The Wick of the Navel is the female serpent and the Conjuction of the Thunderbolt (vajrasandhi) of the two door panels.20 The Kula scripture should be given to one who knows the conventions here also. Otherwise it should not be given - this is the Command of the Supreme Goddess. (35-36ab) The venerable Section Concerning the Virgin (Goddess) is finished. It belongs to the primordial descent into the great sacrifice of the Churning Bhairava in the tradition (anvaya) that consists of seventy million (verses) that has emerged on the Path of Meru and (extends) for one hundred and twenty-five thousand (verses). It has been brought (down to earth) into the first sacred seat along the path of the Seat of Knowledge (vidyāpī˜ha). It is the ultimate purport of the Subsequent Six Thousand (verses) of the Pure Division (vimalabhedottarana˜ka) in the division beginning with `KĀ' in the venerable scripture of twenty-four thousand (verses) (known as) the Svāminīmata of the Supreme Lord's command as uttered within the Tradition of the Mother (ambākrama). The scripture (mata) of the Supreme Lord (pārameśvara) extends for a million million (verses) (laknako˜i). The essence extracted from this extends for seventy million verses (saptako˜i). The essence of the (scripture of) seventy million (verses consists of) one hundred and twenty-five thousand quarter (verses). The essence of that is (the scripture of) twenty-four thousand verses. It was revealed by (the goddess) Kujeśī to Mitra in three sections. May the Kula Yoginīs rejoice! May the sons of Kula rejoice! May the teachers of Kula rejoice and all others who have been initiated into the Kula!

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER FORTY-EIGHT 1. The passage up to verse 45 is also found in the SiddhakhaSÆa (KuKh 48/2-45 = SKh 5/26-71; see notes to the Sanskrit text and concordance for details). In the SKh it is introduced with the statement that this is another teaching concerning the Kramasūtra. The passage that precedes it there concludes with the statement: ‘the Kramasūtra that has come down through the transmission of the root lineage has been explained.’ (kramasūtraˆ samākhyātaˆ mūlānvaya- kramāgatam | SKh 5/25ab). However, at the beginning of that passage it is referred to as the ‘PūjākhaSÆa’ (athāntaraˆ pūjākhaSÆaˆ prārabhyate tad yathā | ibid. 5/1cd). Thus, the PūjākhaSda of the SKh consists of two Kramasūtras. The first part of the second one corresponds to verses 2 to 45 of this chapter. Again, according to the colophon of the entire passage of the SKh, containing both Kramasūtras, it is called the DaśaughakramanirSayasūtra, just as the following one is called Dvādaśaughanityakramasūtra. It ends with the statement: O Śambhu, he who knows this Kramasūtra is a (true) teacher (kramasūtram idaˆ śambho yo jānāti sa deśikaƒ [g: deśika] || ibid. 5/123cd). As the whole chapter is called the Kramasūtra, it appears that initially this was all that it contained and that the Sūtra of the Teaching (upadeśasūtra), which begins with verse 50 and continues to the end, was added later. Here, in our text, the goddess declares that she will expound the Sūtra of the Rite of Adoration (pūjāsūtra), which is the name of the first long section of the SKh that deals with ritual procedure. Thus the SKh (1/1ab) begins: Now I will tell (you) the teaching of the Pūjāsūtra. (athātaƒ [g: aˆthātaƒ] saˆpravaknyāmi pūjāsūtrasya nirSayam [g: nirnarSSayaˆ] |) The reason for this cross-identification is probably due to the version of the SKh that the redactor used as his source. Of the three MSs of the SKh that have been recovered, MS K repeates a part of this passage towards the beginning of the SKh (see details in the notes to the Sanskrit edition). It is possible that the manuscript of the SKh with which the redactor of the KuKh was working included the Kramasūtra in the place it is found in MS K, that is, inserted in the Pūjāsūtra. Note also that the Sanskrit of the first line of the verse we are examining, which contains the reference to the Pūjāsūtra, is clumsy and not quite correct. This may well be because the redactor mistakenly thought that the Kramasūtra was the Pūjāsūtra and altered his text accordingly. Note also that the first part of chapter 50 below, which is called Śrīkramasūtra, and the second half of chapter 49 (from about verse 50 onwards) are embedded in the continuation of the second Kramasūtra of the SKh. The entire section of the SKh corresponding to the first half of this chapter, the second half of the next and the first part of chapter 50 of our text is a single coherent whole. english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER FORTY-EIGHT 21 the inner Triangle. They have two names: 1) BrahmākhaSÆa — StutikhaSÆa 2) VinSukhaSÆa — MātrkhaSÆa 3) RudrakhaSÆa — MantrakhaSÆa. As sacred seats are located on the corners of the Triangle, it is natural to associate them with the parts of the Vidyā, as we do in fact find in the SKh: Thus the Samayā Vidyā is in the three seats, (present there) in due order. The StutikhaSÆa is in Kāmākhya, the MātrkhaSÆa is in PūrSagiri, and the MantrakhaSÆa is UÆyāSa or else, Laghvī (is there) according to (her) desired form. tato vai samayāˆ vidyāˆ trinu pī˜henv anukramāt [g: pī˜hesva-] || stutikhaSÆaˆ tu kāmākhye mātrkhaSÆaˆ tu pūrSake [kh: mūrtake] | mantrakhaSÆaˆ tathoÆyāSe [k: tatho prāSe] laghvī vā kāmarūpataƒ || SKh 5/99cd-100 We are told below (50/31cd-2) the three places in the body onto which these three sections are projected. english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER FORTY-NINE 1. The rest of this chapter is reproduced and briefly glossed in the SamP (fl. 11b-13a) where it is called the Dhyānasūtra. The variants have been noted in the critical apparatus of the edition. 2. SamP: (The reference to) the Gesture of the Rule (indicates the other) gestures including that of the Yoni and the rest. The lotus posture and the other (postures) are assumed by arranging the two feet (in various ways). A soft seat is made from soft cloth and the like. Having reached the (inner) seat which is the place of the foundation, that is, the feet. Having visualized the Yantra, the practicioners of mantra worship (it). It is visualized by those who identify with the body in their own body and is (then) worshipped. The visualization, for those who are comfortable with both (inner and outer worship), is of two kinds, namely, within the Yantra and inwardly (in the body). Being a yogi, one should visualize it through the practice (caryā) of Yoga. samayamudrā yonimudrādayaƒ | pādadvayaven˜anena [-yena] padmāsanādi | mrdvāsanaƒ [mrddhāsanaƒ] komalavāsādiracitaƒ | ākramyeti āsanārthaƒ | sutalaƒ pādaƒ | mantropāsakā [-kair] yantraˆ [yantre] dhyātvā pūjayanti | dehābhimānībhiƒ svadehe dhyātvā pūjitam [-tāƒ] | ubhayānukūlakairubhayam dhyānaˆ dvividhaˆ yantrastham antaraˆ ceti yogī bhūtvā yogacaryayā dhyāyet | 3. The word ‘sutala’ is an architectural term that denotes the foundation of a large building. 4. The Bell is the uvula at the back of the throat (normally called ghaS˜ikā lit `little bell’. It is also Unstruck Sound; cf. 49/12cd-13. 5. SamP (One who is) ecstatic and inebriated is ecstatic with wine (knībonmatto madirāmattaƒ). Cf. 46/302-304. 6. According to Monier-Williams the adjective jun˜a- means: pleased, propitious; liked, wished, loved, welcome, agreeable, usual; frequented, visited, inhabited; swept over (by the wind); afflicted by; served, obliged, worshipped; practiced; furnished with, possessed of; the remanents of a meal; jun˜i (f.): love service, favour, satisfaction. Thus as ‘jun˜a’ the goddess is ‘propitious’, ‘agreeable’ and ‘loving’. At the same time, as a caSÆālinī, she is an outcaste woman who is so impure and low in social status that she is free to eat the remanents of other peoples’ meals — their ‘jun˜a’. Kubjikā, who receives and consumes offerings that are normally considered to be impure and polluting, is thus outwardly like her, even as she inwardly transforms pollution into nectar. In this form she governs the Lineage of the Eldest. As Māta‰gī, the Sweeper, another low caste woman, she presides over the Lineage of the Youth. That form is described below at the beginning of chapter 66. In the form described in chapter 29 she governs the Lineage of the Child. That one is also linked to pollution

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER FIFTY 1. A few of the first thirteen verses of this chapter are drawn from the Kramasūtra of the SiddhakhaSÆa, which our text refers to here simply as the ‘sūtra’. See note at the beginning of chapter 48 and Sanskrit edition for details. These verses outline how the Krama of Twenty-eight divisions is projected onto the body. The Krama of Twenty-eight (an˜aviˆśatikrama) is the one taught in the KMT and the ±SS. The main Krama of YKh (1) consist of twenty-seven mantra (see above note to 3/52cd-53ab). The KuKh presents a variety of Kramas, but as a whole follows YKh (1) and accepts the Krama of Twenty-seven (saptaviˆśatikrama) to be the main one. This is further evidence that the part of the text in common with the SKh is drawn from it. 2. Mukundarāja quotes the passage from 50/4ab to the end of this chapter in full and calls it the Pūjāsūtra. 3. In the SKh the following two lines (i.e. SKh 5/79cd-80ab), which frame the context there, precede this section: One should worship the GurumaSÆala with flowers along with scent and water (argha) five times and then Olinātha in the middle of the directions. gandhārghasaˆyutaiƒ (k g: -tai) punpaiƒ (g: punpai) pūjayed gurumaSÆalam || pañcadhā madhyato diknu olinātham ataƒ param | This is followed by the corresponding line to this one which reads: One should worship the line of teachers up to the name of one’s own (teacher) to the north of him. tasyottare (kh: -ttāra) gurupa‰ktiˆ (k: guruˆ-) svanāmāntaˆ prapūjayet | 4. The projection and worship of the units of the Krama taught here takes place progressively down the body. We may presume, therefore, that the sacred seats, which constitute the first group of four of the Krama, are worshipped in the Triangle in the End of the Twelve. 5. english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER FIFTY 42 15. KuKh 50/25cd-30ab = KM 25/90cd-95 = TS 15/62cd-67. These verses are drawn either from the KMT or from the TS, which is their original source. The context where these verses appear in the KMT and the TS is the Vidyāvrata which requires the adept to wander to the sacred sites projected into the soul of the inner wayfarer. 16. See note to 48/85cd-86 for a table of correspondences. 17. After Mukundarāja has quoted this, the Pūjāsūtra, in full he goes on to say: One should worship the deity of a particular place in one's body after having visualized it (there). All the groups of deities mentioned in the MBT should be worshipped in their respective places in one's own body or else in images of the deities or in a Yantra. The general form of the mantra used to worship these deities begins with the Five PraSavas and the rest, the name of the deity comes in the middle and it ends with `I worship the sandals'. The ritual begins with the worship of the door, this is followed by the purification of the elements (of the body), the deposition, the installation of the deity and its visualization, the worship of the attendant deities and the main deity, the offering of the offerings, the repetition of the (deity's) mantra, hymns, animal sacrifice, the offering of lamps at night and the dismissal of the deity. This is the overall pattern in all the Tantras. There are differences according to the practice of one's own particular Kula, country (deśa) and time. But although there are such differences (nonetheless true initiates) worship with pure feelings (bhāva). arthaƒ | svadehe vā tatsthānadevatāˆ dhyātvā pūjayet | athavā tattatsthānenu devapratimāsu yantre vā taduktaśenadevagaSāśca maˆthānoktā [-ktāƒ] sarve pūjyāƒ | pūjāyāˆ prakāraƒ | pañcapraSavādikena nāmamadhyena pādukānte pūjayāmīti pūjayet | vāmacāreSa tatra paramparā | ādau dvārapūjā bhūtaśuddhiƒ nyāsaƒ prāSapratin˜hā dhyānaˆ parivārārcane mūladevapūjā upacārārpaSam japastavaƒ paśuyāgaƒ rātrau dīpārpaSavisarjanamiti sarvatantrasaˆgatiƒ | svakulācārato deśācārataƒ kālācāraśca bhedatve.api śuddhabhāvenārcayanti | iti mukundatantrite manmthānācāre pūjāsūtrārthasaˆknepaƒ |

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER FIFTY-ONE 1. These lines appear at the beginning of the Gurukramādhikārasūtra found in chapter 22 of YKh (1) (22/25cd-45ab) from which it draws its name. The rest of that sūtra explains them as follows: Brahminicide, the drinking of wine, theft, sex with the teacher's consort, and incitement or association with these sins (saˆyogin) are said to be the five great sins according to the Siddhānta. Brahminicide, the drinking of wine, theft, and sex with the teacher's consort — these, excluding incitement or association with them, are the four sins according to (the teachings of the Tantras of the) North. The drinking of wine, theft, and sex with the teacher's consort — is said to be the triad of the (Tantras of the) South. Now I will tell you the two of the East. The two sins (there) that are hard to bear are the drinking of wine and sex with the teacher's consort. In the Three Lineages in Kujā's tradition no atoning penance is possible for the abduction of the teacher’s consort. (This sin persists), undestroyed, birth after birth. There are four types of violence to which the teacher may be subject that brings about the fall of all (and anybody who does it to him) but especially those who have (pledged to follow the teachings of the) Hermitage in the Western (tradition). In increasing order (of gravity) the fourfold sin of violence to the teacher (found) in the disciple is (violence to) the teacher's Command, the teacher’s substance, the teacher’s task and the teacher’s woman. Great acts of disrespect and the like are bound with the bonds of aversion. Freed from such violence to the teacher, one is not stained by other sins. brahmahatyā surāpānaˆ [k, gh: -na; ‰: surā * naˆ] steyaˆ gurva‰ganāgamam [k, kh, gh: gurvveganāmaˆ; ‰: gurvaganāgamaˆ] || etāni pātakāny āhus tatsaˆyogī [k: -nyāhutat-] ca pañcamam | ete pañca mahāpāpāƒ [k, kh, gh: -pā] siddhānte saˆprakīrtitāƒ [gh: -tā] || brahmahatyā surāpānaˆ steyaˆ gurva‰ganāgamam [gh: gurve-; ‰: gurvaganā- gamaˆ] | catvāraś cottare [k, kh: -ścoˆtare] pāpās tatsaˆyogivivarjitāƒ [k, kh, gh, ‰: -tā; ‰: -yogavivarjitā] || surāpānaˆ [k, kh, gh: -pāna] tathā [k, kh, gh: mathā] steyaˆ gurustrīgamanaˆ tathā | dakniSaˆ ca trikaˆ [‰: ni *] proktaˆ dvikaˆ [k, kh, gh: dvike] pūrve [k, kh: dvikaˆ; gh: pūrva] bravīmy aham [kh: vravī * haˆ] || gurva‰ganā surāpānaˆ dvike pāpāni [‰: śrāpāvi] duƒsahāƒ [k, kh: -hā; gh: -dā; ‰: * sahā] | ulitraye [‰: * licaye] kujāmnāye [k, gh: -ya] gurustrīharaSena [k, kh, gh:

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER FIFTY-THREE 1. This is the second of two Santānasūtras. The first is in chapter seventeen. This one, which is also called the Prajñāsūtra (which may be its original name) claims to present the ‘hidden meaning’ (gūÆhārtha) of the Santānasūtra. Even so, Mukundarāja prefers to comment only on the first one. The contents of the two sūtras partly coincide throwing light on each others’ meaning when they do so. The reader is referred back to the notes of chapter seventeen where they are compared. This Santānasūtra is also found in YKh (2) (24/15cd-30) with which it has been collated. The Śrīsantānasūtra in chapter seveneteen defines sixteen 'conventions' (saˆketa), which are all briefly redefined in this version of the Santānasūtra. They are (each entry is followed by the verse numbers of chapter seventeen where it appears): 1) The Path of Meru (16-19); 2) The Deity of the Lineage (20-25); 3) and 4) Oˆkāra and the Two Siddhas (26-28ab); 5) The Cave Dwelling (28cd-29); 6) The Kadamba Tree (30-31); 7) The Convention of the Lion (32-3); 8) The House of the City of the Moon (34); 9) The Division of the Churning Bhairava (35-6ab); 10) The Clan (36cd- 39); 11) The Sign of Accomplishment (40-43ab); 12) Authority (43cd-44); 13) Brahmā’s Stone of Birth (45-46ab); 14) Persistence in Kāmarūpa (46cd-47cd); 15) Fame and the Tamarind Tree (48); 16) The Ocean (49) and Conclusion (50-56). 2. Cf. 17/16-19 (1); 17/20-25 (2); 17/26-28ab (3, 4) and 17/28cd-29 (5). 3. The two Flowers are Śakti as CiñciSī and Śiva as Śrīnātha (see intro. vol. 2, p. 410-411 and 39/52) represented by the letter Kha and Ma, respectively. The former is the Void of the Yoni (= unbounded Emptiness) that represents Mālinī, the deity of the lineage and the latter the Point (= transdimensional Emptiness) in the centre. embodied in the Bhairava of Knowledge — the First Teacher. The two combine to form the Path of Meru, that is, the tradition and its teachings. The twelfth Jewel is the letter E, which represents the ‘body’ of the Triangle. From the triangular Path of Meru emerge the six deities of the Hexagram who govern all the groups of six that form the Krama. 4. The ‘garden’ — udyāna — is the seat OÆÆiyāna, which houses the Point in the centre. The Void of the Li‰ga is the Cave (58/7cd-8ab) above the Half Moon (see 58/7). 5. Cf. below, 58/64cd-65ab and note 60. 6. Cf. 17/30-31 (6) and 17/32-33 (7); see also note to 5/70-71 and 58/64cd- 67ab. The Kadamba Tree is the seed-syllable Vidyā of the goddess, whose energy is the Command of realization that pervades it. This Tree is the Lion and the goddess who lives in it is the lioness. 7. Cf. 17/34 (8), 17/35-6ab (9) and 17/36cd-39 (10).

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER FIFTY-FOUR 1. The Five PraSavas are presented in code in 8/92cd-105ab and are related to the sacred seats in 8/111cd-113. See notes there for a table of correspondences that combines the data in this chapter and there. 2. The Yoni in this case is located in the genital centre. 3. This should be the second PraSava, which is located in the navel, not the third. The location of the third one is not mentioned here. Presumably, it is the heart centre. 4. See 6/183cd-184ab. 5. This PraSava is called Bhairavī Vidyā above in 8/104cd-105. 6. 4. Table of Correspondences of the Five PraSavas and the Sacred Seats PraSava Colour Seat Location Age Sign First (Vāgbhava) White Kāmarūpa Centre of Yoni Krta Arousal (knobha) Second Morning sun Jālandhara Navel - Paralysis (stobha) Third Yellow PūrSagiri (Heart) - Throb of Bliss (ghūrSi), Arousal of the Body (puraknobha) Fourth Black Tisra Throat End of Kali Invisibility, Controlled Possession (vaśyāveśa) King Bhairava Red Udyāna Between the eyebrows - Yogic Sleep (yoganidrā) It is not possible to establish which Ages correspond to the sacred seats. Udyāna is normally the seat of the Krta Age, but this has been taken over by Kāmarūpa. As usual, the text here says that Tisra is the seat that manifests at the end of the Kali Age. Normally, however, it is the fifth seat and Kāmarūpa, which is generally said to be the fourth one, is the seat of the Kali Age. As the change in the order of the seats has disrupted the usual correspondences, it is not possible to determine which Age Udyāna belongs to in this setup. One wonders why this has taken place. Is it because a need was felt to relate Vāgbhava to Kāmarūpa? Cf. above 9/20. 7. Concerning these eight yogic powers see above note to 4/41cd-42 and 8/123-124. 8. The Vidyā of the New Moon is Kubjikā’s Samayā Vidyā. It becomes the Vidyā of the Full Moon by adding the Five PraSavas to it in the beginning in the forward order and at the end in the reverse order.

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER FIFTY-FIVE 1. This sūtra describes how the maSÆala of the Transmission of the Eldest should made and worshipped. It basically consists of the core of the SaˆvartāmaSÆala. The sandals of the god, which symbolize Śiva and Śakti, are Śrīnātha in the centre. Around them is the usual downward facing triangle in the corner of which are three sacred trees. Outside the Triangle is a Hexagram on the corners of which the six Yoginīs (here called ‘Mothers’) starting from Õākinī are worshipped. The Five PraSavas are projected into the area around the Hexagram (perhaps two on each side and one above). Their locations in the maSÆala represent the Five Voids within five Wheels (cakra) in the body. All this is contained within a square, outer enclosure. 2. The Circle of the Yoni is the Wheel of the Self-supported (svādhin˜hāna). See above 21/35-36. 3. The Five Voids are within five of the Wheels in the subtle body. In order to make five fit into the usual group of six, MaSipura, the Wheel in the navel, has been omitted. Similarly, above in 21/35-36, in order to accommodate the Five Elements into the Six Wheels, Viśuddhi, the Wheel in the throat centre has been omitted (cf. also note to 25/2-3ab). Here the Wheels are listed from the top down, whereas the PraSavas to which they correspond have been listed from the bottom up in the sūtra of the previous chapter. Each Wheel contains one of the Five PraSavas, that together constitute the Five-syllable Vidyā. Just as the energies of the nine letters of Navātman (HSK±MLVRYŪ¤) are considered to be a Void (µ fol. 84a) because of their essentially transcendental, conscious nature, similarly the Five PraSavas are Five Voids in the centre of the five Wheels in the body. The Five Voids are described in detail in notes to 25/39cd-40 in a different, although not incompatible, way. Cf. below (59/83) where we read that ‘space has become fivefold by the countless divisions of the one.’ 4. 5. Table of the Locations of the Five Voids and the PraSavas Location of the Void Age PraSavas Wheel of the Drop (between the eyebrows) Elder (vrddha) Sadāśiva The Pure Wheel (in the throat) Brother (bhrātr) Īśvara Heart Father (pitr) Rudra Circle of the Yoni (in the genitals) Grandfather (pitāmaha) VinSu Foundation of the Root (in the base of the spine) Greatgrandfather (prapitāmaha) Brahmā

According to the NT (7/31-32ab) says that the Place of Birth, the Root, the Belly of the Fish, the Fivefold Place and the Tortoise are all names for Mūlādhāra. Knemarāja explains that it is called the Tortise because its shape is like a tortoise. Externally, the ‘tortoise seat’ is where the officiant sits when he performs the rite. See above note 17 to 48/20-21ab. 7. YKh (2): The (sacrificial) meat is (placed) on the left in the north. 8. According to the version in YKh (2) the meat offering is placed on the left. Perhaps that is meant here. 9. Concerning the Three Trees see 46/21cd-26 and notes. We are there that the three trees are in the three corners of the downward facing triangle in the centre of SaˆvartāmaSÆala. The Kadamba tree is in the front corner, while the Bilva and Ciñcā are in the right and left ones, respectively. 10. See below, chapter sixty-three.

english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER FIFTY-SEVEN 1. This chapter of the KuKh is the same as chapter thirty-six of YKh (1). 2. Concerning these eighteen see above 2/20-26 and notes and intro. vol. 2, p. 582 for a chart of the names of these eighteen found in this chapter and those there. When the names differ, they are noted in brackets next to the headings. 3. See note to 59/4. 4. At the lower, immanent level, the goddess has a form, although, of course, it is not a physical one. All the states and energies in the sphere of her emanation, including the highest most subtle energies and principles, are ‘forms’ of the goddess. Thus each one of these eighteen energies are aspects of the one supreme energy, namely, the Transmental. Although ordered in a ‘sequence’ — krama — they are equally the same energy which is the goddess who leads directly to the supreme state in which she is immersed. From one point of view the Transmental is the cosmogonic will, which is the energy and source of emanation — the Yoni — that issues forth as the Divine Current in all its phases and aspects. From another point of view, it is the energy of the one transcendental being. As such it is ‘established in the Void’. Here the Transmental is the goddess ‘devoid of form’. Or, to be more precise, her form has been ‘nivartita-‘ that is, ‘suppressed’, ‘brought to an end’ or ‘turned away’. She is the supreme transcendental reality from which, as the Upaninad says, mind, ‘turns away’ (nivartate) because it cannot reach it. Thus the Transmental — unmanī — ‘beyond mind’ is ‘established in the Void’ of the absolute, transcendental reality from which mind ‘turns away’ and ceases. The second account (57/58) stresses, as does this one, that the Transmental is the pure consciousness which is deity immersed in the contemplation of its supremely blissful nature. Ineffable oneness, all duality, including the identity of the Transmental itself dissolves away into this Bliss. 5. The second account of this aspect of the Transmental stresses its immanent pervasive nature (57/59). Extending from Śiva to Earth it spans the entire range of immanence, the sacred and profane, even as it maintains its grounding in its essential transcendental nature. Māta‰gī, the Sweeper who is not bound by the dichotomy of pure and impure, represents this condition well. Thus in the first phase, although the Transmental has emerged from pure transcendence beyond the opposites, its transcendental nature dominates, in this phase, the aspect of immanence in which the Transmental is ‘the abode of (all that is) emitted’. Māta‰gī is Jun˜acaSÆālī (49/36), the form of the goddess described above in chapter forty-nine. 6. Mālinī resides in the End of the Twelve. english: NOTES OF THE TRANSLATION OF CHAPTER FIFTY-SEVEN 94 serpent on which he rests, became the rope, In this case, the rope is the female snake KuSÆalinī, who embodies Time. Thus, above we are told that, moving in SunumSā, the Cavity of Space between the breaths, ‘slender, her limbs beautifully variegated by time and moment, she awakens to (ultimate) reality’ (KuKh 2/5) (cf. above 2/4cd-6ab). 67. Concerning Matsyendranātha as a fisherman, see intro. vol. 2, p. 321 and TĀ 1/7. 68. The Couple pulsate with the bliss of the rhythmn of their union at the ‘supreme limit’ of immanence that borders on the sphere of transcendence. In the downward flow they lead out to emanation; in the upward flow they are the way into the Divine Current that streams through and up into the liberated Śāmbhava state. At each phase of the flow union takes place between the goddess of that phase and her Lord. These conjunctios are aspects of the one culminating conjunctio that takes place at the end of the series between Śrīnātha and the Goddess where immanence flows out of transcendence. This reflects in its turn the total oneness at the beginning of the series where the polarities are perfectly fused and hence do not manifest. These pairs are worshipped together as a couple in the mantras that invoke each phase. Thus the names of the latter are listed next. 69. See above, 2/27 and note. 70. Each of the eighteen phases is the goddess and so is both a Flower and the Flower. Each is an aspect of the Command which is transmitted from ‘Flower to Flower’. See above 57/49cd-50ab.
